events.title: Reclaiming our Democracy and Economy from AI moderated by Jackie Fielder
events.location: Medicine for Nightmares, 3036 24th St, San Francisco, CA 94110
events.description: Join moderator Supervisor Jackie Fielder for an evening exploring how we, as everyday people, can take back our economy and democracy from artificial intelligence. We will explore what we even mean when we talk about “AI,” whether we’re in an AI bubble, the impacts of AI, whether we should be afraid of AI, and who’s behind the AI hype. This panel is jam-packed with women authors whose books have inspired critical conversations about AI and the tech sector at large: Dr. Alex Hanna, co-author of The AI Con, Wendy Liu, author of Abolish Silicon Valley, and Tamara Kneese, author of Notes Toward a Digital Workers’ Inquiry. Wendy Liu made a career switch from software engineer to writer, a move that was sparked by reading lots of books at a time when her startup was tanking. Now she mostly writes about the horrors of Silicon Valley and why tech workers need to organise. She is the author of Abolish Silicon Valley. Dr. Alex Hanna is a writer and sociologist of technology, labor, and politics. She is the Director of Research at the Distributed AI Research Institute (DAIR). Her work examines how new computational technologies--such as AI and machine learning--exacerbate racial, gender, and class inequality through their data practices and effects on labor. With Emily M. Bender, Dr. Hanna is the co-author of The AI Con (Harper, 2025), a book about AI and the hype around it. They also run the Mystery AI Hype Theater 3000 series, playfully and wickedly tearing apart AI hype on their livestream and podcast. She also works in the area of social movements, focusing on the dynamics of anti-racist campus protest in the US and Canada. She holds a BS in Computer Science and Mathematics and a BA in Sociology from Purdue University, and an MS and a PhD in Sociology from the University of Wisconsin-Madison. Dr. Tamara Kneese is a Senior Research Scientist at Partnership on AI and a Practitioner Fellow at the University of Virginia's Environmental Institute. She is the author of Death Glitch: How Techno-Solutionism Fails Us in The Life and Beyond (Yale University Press 2023) and co-author (with Capacitor Collective) of Notes Toward a Digital Workers' Inquiry (Common Notions 2025). Supervisor Jackie Fielder is a Mission renter, public bank organizer, former city commissioner and educator, and climate and environmental justice advocate. Jackie got her start in the #NoDAPL movement by organizing for divestment from the Wall Street banks financing the Dakota Access Pipeline. In 2017, she co-founded the San Francisco Defund DAPL Coalition and the San Francisco Public Bank Coalition to start the nation’s first city-owned bank to support small businesses, affordable housing, and renewable energy. She’s the proud granddaughter of Mexican immigrants and Native American grandparents and a citizen of the Three Affiliated Tribes of North Dakota, with Two Kettle Lakota and Hidatsa descent. She graduated from Stanford University in 2016 with a Bachelors of Arts in Public Policy and a Masters of Arts in Sociology.

events.description: Contemporary jazz icons · In 2024, Jay Beckenstein and the band started their observation of the 50th anniversary of the band. What started as a diversion, something that was just for fun (and twenty-five cents at the door), continues its evolution into 2025. It began inauspiciously when Beckenstein and a few musician friends in Buffalo, NY, organized a get-together on their shared night off from working in bands that actually made money. It was a simple, humble idea with a name that was likewise simple and humble, “Tuesday Night – Jazz Jam”. Fast forward 50 years, and this jazz supergroup has released over 30 albums, garnering gold and platinum along the way. They’ve played over 10,000 concerts on six continents. events.description: Contemporary jazz icons · In 2024, Jay Beckenstein and the band started their observation of the 50th anniversary of the band. It began inauspiciously when Beckenstein and a few musician friends in Buffalo, NY, organized a get-together on their shared night off from working in bands that actually made money. It was a simple, humble idea with a name that was likewise simple and humble, “Tuesday Night – Jazz Jam”. Fast forward 50 years, and this jazz supergroup has released over 30 albums, garnering gold and platinum along the way. They’ve played over 10,000 concerts on six continents. Spyro Gyra has maintained its standards of excellence, and that has sustained them on the “A list” of live attractions in jazz for 50 years.

events.title: Night Watch // Gregory Rick
events.location: Johansson Projects, 2300 Telegraph Ave, Oakland
events.description: Johansson Projects presents Night Watch, a striking exhibition of paintings and works on paper by Gregory Rick that boldly reimagines history painting through the fractured lens of contemporary life. Apocryphal yet deeply referential and incisive, Rick’s compositions collapse past events with biblical and mythological imagery, art-historical allusions, and capitalist spectacle into hypersaturated scenes that are at once facetious and unsettling. A burning cross, a feline maw, a tree of serpents, and tigers charging toward machine-gun fire populate a world where violence–and communal acts of resistance–appear both ancient and immediate. Figures clad in Fila jackets, yellow Hokas, and other recognizable markers of contemporary consumer culture anchor these frenetic compositions in the present. As a veteran, citizen, and subject, Rick draws upon collective memory to confront the cognitive dissonance of navigating everyday life amid recurring cycles of violence, surveillance, and oppression. In works such as Night Watch (We Got Us), Rembrandt’s civic militia meets Picasso’s Guernica, transforming the historical tableau into a contemporary cry for help and vision of mutual aid. A few of the works are painted and collaged on silk mesh, their transparencies exposing the layers of their construction and underscoring history itself as an unstable, assembled narrative. In Night Watch, Rick contends with what it means to stay woke and on watch in the 2020s. Night Watch runs from September 30 to October 31, 2026 with an opening reception Friday, October 2 from 5-8pm.

events.title: NEW DATE: Garrison Lovely - Obsolete
events.location: Book Passage Ferry Building 1 Ferry Building San Francisco, CA 94111
events.description: Is AI a bubble or humanity's last invention? An existing harm or an existential threat? Obsolete cuts through the hype and false binaries to answer all the AI questions you have, while raising some you probably aren't prepared for. The richest companies in history are racing to build a machine that replaces human labor-- all of it . And, as this provocative new book insists, the only surefire way they won't succeed is if we stop them. Many today don't get further than seeing AI as a boondoggle--a new shiny object for techno-capitalists to sink their cash into as we barrel toward climate disaster. Obsolete takes those concerns seriously, but implores us to keep our eye on the ball: the attempt to render you obsolete . The scale of their project has no real precedent. What we think of as big--the Gilded Age monopolies, the Manhattan Project, the Apollo program--doesn't even come close to capturing its size. Almost none of us wants this vast transformation to succeed. Yet we're letting it proceed virtually unabated. Why? Because we don't know it's happening, we don't believe it will work, or we don't think we can stop it. Obsolete takes on all three. AI expert and journalist Garrison Lovely's debut is a refreshing reset on an AI debate in which basically everyone is getting some big things wrong. With deep access to top researchers, advocates, and industry insiders, Obsolete offers a new way to think about the technology and a plan for deciding its future democratically. Garrison Lovely is a freelance journalist based in Brooklyn, known for his cover stories in The Nation (“Confessions of a McKinsey Whistleblower”) and Jacobin (“Can Humanity Survive AI?”), as well as writing in The New York Times, BBC, Nature, MIT Technology Review, Bloomberg, Foreign Policy, TIME, The Guardian, The Verge, and elsewhere. He was previously a reporter in residence at the Omidyar Network and is the author of Obsolete, a Substack on the political economy of artificial intelligence. Lovely’s work has been translated into five languages and cited by The New Yorker, The Atlantic, ProPublica, and others. events.title: SHAAN MERCHANT: SURVIVOR LEGENDS
events.location: Books Inc. Palo Alto, 855 El Camino Real, Palo Alto, CA 94301
events.description: The tribe has spoken: Journalist, cultural critic, and lifelong Survivor fan Shaan Merchant will be at Books Inc. Palo Alto for a reading and signing of his new book, Survivor Legends: The Players Who Changed the Game (Unofficial & Unauthorized)! About the book: A deep dive into the players who shaped Survivor—and how their stories helped define reality TV. [Book not endorsed by or affiliated with any creator or producer of the show] For more than 25 years, Survivor has reigned supreme as one of the most influential shows on American television. Each season, castaways from across the country arrive on a secluded island with the same ultimate goal: to outwit, outplay, and outlast for the $1 million prize. The game is physically grueling and psychologically unforgiving. While the structure of the game remains familiar, what has made Survivor endure—and evolve—is the players at the center of the it. Survivor Legends tells the stories of the players who left an indelible mark on the series, through narrative profiles that revisit the show’s most influential figures. From early rule-breakers and strategic innovators like Richard Hatch and Cirie Fields, to unlikely heroes and enduring icons, like Parvati Shallow and Mike White, these players didn’t just change how the game was played—they shaped how audiences understood competition, character, and authenticity. Through their stories—who was celebrated, who was vilified, and how those judgments shifted—this book offers fresh insight into beloved contestants while revealing how American ideas about identity, morality, and power have changed across a quarter century of reality television. Featuring exclusive interviews from players including Sandra Diaz-Twine, Tyson Apostol, John Cochran, Carolyn Wiger, and more, Survivor Legends is a vivid, player-centered portrait of one of television’s most enduring cultural phenomena. Based in New York City, Shaan Merchant is a journalist, cultural critic, and lifelong Survivor fan. His work has been featured in the New York Times, Slate, Salon, Washington Monthly, Condé Nast Traveler, Insider, Philadelphia Inquirer , and more.

events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: Learn how to turn your expertise into a clear, compelling nonfiction book that reaches the people who need it most. "A smart and stylish guide to writing and publishing a nonfiction book." — Kirkus Reviews. Whether you're a consultant, coach, educator, healthcare provider, or entrepreneur, writing a book can expand your influence and help more people benefit from your ideas. The Complete Expert-to-Author Guide provides a practical, step-by-step roadmap for moving from concept to finished manuscript without getting stuck along the way. Written by veteran editors and book coaches Marisa Solis and Elizabeth Dougherty, who have guided hundreds of nonfiction books from idea to publication, this hands-on guide walks you through every stage of the writing process with clarity and confidence. Here’s what makes The Complete Expert-to-Author Guide an essential resource: • A Clear Road Map for Writing Your Book: Follow a proven framework that takes you from initial idea to completed manuscript with manageable, actionable steps. • Designed for Experts and Professionals: If your profession involves helping people improve their lives, turn your knowledge into an advice-based nonfiction book. • 25 Practical Exercises and Writing Tools: Writing prompts, preformatted templates, and market analysis exercises help you clarify your message and stay focused. • Structure Your Book with Confidence : Develop your advice-based book’s premise, fine-tune your framework, and strengthen your table of contents upfront—making writing faster and less stressful. • Navigate the Publishing Process: Write a book proposal, explore publishing paths, and build the platform needed to reach your audience. If you’ve been thinking about writing a book but aren’t sure where to start or how to finish, The Complete Expert-to-Author Guide gives you the structure, strategy, and support to bring your book to life. Marisa Solis is a book coach, developmental editor, and cofounder of Book Structure Pros, a boutique editorial services company. Since her start in travel guidebook publishing in 1999, she has worked on more than 500 nonfiction books. Her specialties are self-help and wellness. Marisa lives in Los Angeles. Elizabeth Dougherty is a book coach, developmental editor, and cofounder of Book Structure Pros. She has worked in publishing since 1988 and was an executive editor at Weldon Owen. Her focus is on parenting, health and wellness, and women’s leadership. Elizabeth holds a master’s from Northwestern’s Medill School of Journalism and lives in Palo Alto, California. events.title: Lucille Lang Day's "THE COSMOS AND ME"
events.location: Mrs. Dalloway's, 2904 College Ave, Berkeley, CA 94705
events.description: Poet Lucille Lang Day shares her latest collection of heartfelt and timely poems. Join us at Mrs. Dalloway's Bookstore on Thursday, October 1 at 6:30 PM when poet and author Lucille Lang Day comes to the store to present her lastest collection The Cosmos and Me: New and Selected Poems . Lucille will be joined by Denise Low and will sign copies of her book after the presentation. The Cosmos and Me by Lucille Lang Day is an opus of a life spent pursuing wonder, justice, love, and of course, poetry. In these poems that span over fifty years, Day invites the reader to consider the larger questions of existence and meaning alongside the small joys of the everyday, with poems on the universe alongside poems that consider red shoes or a lost necklace, poems set in outer space alongside poems set in the backyard. Lucille Lang Day is unafraid to ask and to answer the hard questions, to bear witness to our times, be they beautiful, tragic, or both. As California Poet Laureate emeritus Dana Gioia puts it: “Full of both intellect and emotion, The Cosmos and Me lives up to its large and lofty title.” LUCILLE LANG DAY is a poet, author, editor, and children's book author with numerous published books to her name. Her memoir, Married at Fourteen: A True Story, received a PEN Oakland/Josephine Miles Literary Award and was a finalist for the Northern California Book Award in Creative Nonfiction. Her writings have appeared widely in newspapers, magazines, and anthologies. www.lucillelangday.com DENISE LOW, former Poet Laureate of Kansas, is author of House of Grace, House of Blood (U. of Arizona Pr., KAC Nelson Award); the memoir Turtle's Beating Heart: One Family’s Story of Lenape Surviva l (U. of Nebraska Pr.); Casino Bestiary (Spartan), Jigsaw Puzzling (Meadowlark Press , KAC Coffin Award), essays, and others. She is an Academy of American Poets guest editor for the 2026 Poem-A-Day series. At Baker University she teaches in the Business and Professional School. Low programs Indigenous Voices for the Sonoma County arts organization The 222. www.deniselow.net

events.title: Adrianna Adarme Author Talk • A Cozy Kitchen Cookbook: 100 Easy, Comforting Recipes for Every Mood and Desire
events.location: Omnivore Books on Food, 3885a Cesar Chavez St, San Francisco, CA 94131
events.description: Adrianna Adarme is the creator of A Cozy Kitchen, a beloved food platform with a community of over a million followers, and the bestselling author of The Year of Cozy . She’s also a contributor to New York Times Cooking . She lives in Los Angeles with her family and her mischievous corgi, Amelia. Violet Witchel is a content creator with more than 3 million followers on social media. She has been featured in Bon Appétit, Martha Stewart, Food & Wine, and TODAY and had a recent profile in Forbes. In the past year, Violet has been travelling the country popping up, launched her social series The Sunday Stock, and has been writing her top ranked Substack. She lives in San Francisco. A Cozy Kitchen Cookbook - The mastermind behind A Cozy Kitchen presents 100 easy, approachable recipes for quick weeknight meals, Peruvian and Colombian family recipes, and comforting baked goods—all using common ingredients and uncomplicated techniques. To Adrianna Adarme, “cozy” isn’t just about comfort—though, yes, comfort is very much invited. It’s also about ease, intention, and beauty. Cozy is food that tastes good, looks good, and makes you want to tie on an apron even when you’re still wearing your pajamas. A Cozy Kitchen Cookbook is a celebration of mood-based cooking. Of cozy cravings. Of trusting yourself enough to say: “What do I actually want to eat right now?” and then making it happen without any stress. Whether you’re in lazy mode, party mode, I-just-need-to-get-dinner-on-the-table mode, or all three in the same week, the 100 recipes in this book contain the solution. Each chapter sets a vibe and a pace. Some recipes are slow and meandering, like The Fluffiest Cinnamon Rolls with Cream Cheese Icing —perfect for when you want to lose track of time and end up with a kitchen full of warmth and sugar. Others are built for speed and ease, like the One-Pan Shrimp Orzo , which exists for those weeknights when your brain is a little fried but you still want something that tastes like you tried. Drawing from her Peruvian and Colombian heritage, Adrianna also includes traditional staples like Saucy Beef Empanadas and Aguadito (aka Peruvian Chicken Soup) which feel like a love letter directly from her family's recipe collection. There’s no one way to get cozy. Some days, it’s about standing at the stove while something bubbles away and makes your whole home smell like comfort. Other days, it’s assembling something unfussy and eating it cross-legged on the couch. Regardless of mood, A Cozy Kitchen Cookbook will leave you feeling nourished, grounded, and a little more at home with yourself.

events.title: ENTRE DIENTESJAWS[tiburón]— Bay Area Launch with translators Dora Prieto and Daniela Rodríguez Chevalier
events.location: Medicine for Nightmares, 3036 24th St, San Francisco, CA 94110
events.description: Something toothy is coming to Medicina. Join translators Dora Prieto and Daniela Rodríguez Chevalier, with special guests Román Luján and Hugo García Manríquez, for an evening of poetry with bite, celebrating Xitlalitl Rodríguez Mendoza’s JAWS [tiburón], translation out now from Cardboard House Press (2026). What happens when the shark gets tired of being the villain? When it splits into a chorus of workers who have bills to pay? When jaws starts sounding suspiciously like yo ? Moving between ocean and office, Hollywood horror and everyday survival, this darkly comic collection sinks its dientes into work, language, and the business of staying alive. Come for poems, stay until your teeth get pointy and a fin cuts the moon in two. DORA PRIETO is a Mexican and Canadian poet and translator whose life and work have an unruly relationship to geography. She is a 2025–27 Wallace Stegner Fellow at Stanford and has held residencies at Hedgebrook and the Banff Centre. She is the co-translator of JAWS [tiburón] by Xitlalitl Rodríguez Mendoza (Cardboard House Press, 2026). Her work has appeared in Best New Poets 2025 , Catapult , and Maisonneuve , and she won the 2025 Bronwen Wallace Award for poetry. She is a co-founder of El Mashup Collective, and her practice moves across poetry, translation, textiles, and visual forms. Daniela Rodríguez Chevalier Born in Cuernavaca, Mexico ✿ city of eternal Spring ✿ and raised in el Distrito Federal, Daniela Rodríguez Chevalier writes and translates from unceded Coast Salish territories (Vancouver, BC). Her work has appeared in PRISM International, Volume, Discorder and carte blanche. She is part of eclectic artist collectives mim and El Mashup, Festival Coordinator and programmer at the Vancouver Latin American Film Fest, and co-host of Vivaporú on CiTR 101.9FM. Foodie who shelves books and binds them too. Ocean child. She has felt the presence of a shark stirring nearby waters. Dani has two feisty gorgeous dachshunds, Xoco and Rol. @la.tacodelic Román Luján is a Mexican poet, scholar, and literary translator based in the Bay Area. He is the author of several poetry books in Spanish, including Sánafabich, where he explores a poetics of anti-assimilation by examining the history of violence (material and symbolic) on both sides of the US-Mexico border. His work, translated into English, German, and Finnish, has been awarded three national poetry prizes in Mexico. Imagenigma, his first full poetry collection translated into English, will be published by Cardboard House Press. He teaches in the Department of Spanish and Portuguese at UC Berkeley. Hugo García Manríquez,. Two of Hugo's most recent translations into Spanish are two anthologies he edited and translated. One of the San Francisco Bay poet Jack Spicer, “After Lorca and other poems” and the other by English poet Sean Bonney, titled “The Language of barricades”. His latest poetry collection is Lo común, translated and published by Cardboard House Press as Commonplace. Dora @primadora_ Dani @la.tacodelic Xitlalitl @pollitaconpapos Cardboard House Press @cardboardhousepress

events.title: 9th Ave: Tomas Moniz with Miah Jeffra
events.location: Books on the Park on 9th Avenue, 1231 9th Ave., San Francisco, CA 94122
events.description:
Join us on Thursday, October 1 at 7pm for the launch of Tomas Moniz's latest novel, The King of Aloe Vera, with Miah Jeffra at 9th Ave!

You can preorder The King of Aloe Vera through Sep. 29, 2026 and receive a signed copy and other perks!

Free to Attend, Please RSVP
Mask Encouraged for In-Person Attendance
Or Watch on YouTube Live/Link Available Soon

About The King of Aloe Vera
An elderly man has just a month to leave his home. A young woman from his neighborhood is soon to be unhoused. Slowly but surely, the two form an unlikely yet transformational friendship in this warm and funny novel about love and community.

Rey, a widower of 10 years, has lived on the same block in San Francisco’s Mission District for most of his life. He has watched his city transform as he becomes ever more set in his ways. Now he spends most of his time volunteering at the library, where he is determined to educate everyone who comes through the library doors and where his co-workers tolerate him though secretly hoping he’ll retire. It’s at the library where he meets Q, on probation, post breakup with her girlfriend and dealing with a troubled family, who keeps littering cigarette butts on the steps. As Rey tries to decide what to do with the rest of his days, literally counting them off and cutting his remaining ties, Q begins to insert herself into his world in a way that he can’t deny.

With a story about Latinx identity, intergenerational friendship, and chosen family, set over the course of a month, Tomas Moniz takes us on a journey through senior dance classes, illegal bike trips over the Bay Bridge, and fair housing rallies. And as the days tick down, Rey and Q find themselves leaning on each other for answers on how to find community and purpose, make amends, and process grief. Equally funny and tender, The King of Aloe Vera delights in how we choose to live, and live out, our lives.

About Tomas Moniz
Tomas Moniz is a Latinx writer living in East Oakland, CA. His debut novel, Big Familia, was a finalist for the 2020 PEN/Hemingway and a Lambda Literary Award. His second novel, All Friends Are Necessary, won the 2024 California Golden Poppy Award. He teaches at Berkeley City College, the Antioch MFA program and St. Mary's College. He has stuff on the internet but loves penpals: PO Box 3555, Berkeley CA 94703. He promises to write back.

events.location: Bookshop West Portal 80 West Portal Ave San Francisco, CA 94127
events.description: Bookshop West Portal will be welcoming poet D.A. Powell, who is leading a San Francisco Poetics class with University of San Francisco students. On October 1st, the class will take place at Bookshop West Portal. The class will include a poetry reading, learning about Bookshop West Portal and the literary history of that part of the city, and some general discussion. Benjamin Gucciardi, author of the West Portal poetry collection and Shelley Wong, author of As She Appears will also be joining. This class will not only include the students from D.A. Powell's class but it is open to the public! You are encouraged to sit in and participate in the class to learn about our neighborhood and hear from poets who wax lyrical about our very own West Portal. About the Poets D. A. Powell is the author of five collections, including Useless Landscape, or A Guide for Boys, which received the National Book Critics Circle Award in poetry. His honors include two Northern California Book Awards, the Kingsley Tufts Poetry Prize, the Shelley Memorial Prize from the Poetry Society of America, and the John Updike Award in Literature from the American Academy of Arts & Letters, as well as fellowships from the National Endowment for the Arts and the Guggenheim Foundation. Originally from San Francisco, California, Benjamin Gucciardi is the author of Arguments (Persea Books, 2026) winner of the 2025 Lexi Rudnitsky Editor’s Choice Award and West Portal (University of Utah Press, 2021), winner of the Agha Shahid Ali Prize in Poetry. His poems appear in American Poetry Review , Kenyon Review , Poetry Magazine , On Being’s Poetry Unbound , and elsewhere. Shelley Wong is the author of As She Appears (YesYes Books), longlisted for the 2022 National Book Award and winner of a 2023 Lambda Literary Award and the 2019 Pamet River Prize. Her poems have appeared in American Poetry Review, Best American Poetry, Kenyon Review, and New England Review. A Kundiman and MacDowell fellow, she lives in San Francisco.

events.title: VINCENT INGALA
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: One of the most exciting artists to emerge this past decade · Declared by Jazziz Magazine as “one of the most exciting artists to emerge this past decade,” Vincent Ingala remains an unstoppable and ever-adventurous creative force in urban contemporary jazz, with a total of nine #1 Billboard hits, twenty-two Top 10 singles, and more to come from his latest release and 8th studio album, Escape With Me on Shanachie Entertainment. Upon exploding onto the scene in 2010 with his independent, critically acclaimed debut album North End Soul at the age of 17, Vincent was already a seasoned performer, developing somewhat of a cult following in his home state of Connecticut during his high school years with his compelling one man show. That fan base grew exponentially across the U.S. – and in Europe, thanks to supportive online outlets – with his breakthrough single and Top 15 Billboard track “It Is What It Is.” Eleven years after the first time he earned Billboard’s designation as Smooth Jazz Artist of the Year , the saxophonist, multi-instrumentalist, composer, producer and long-beloved entertainer achieved this accolade again in 2023 upon the success of his hit singles “Ridin’ the Wave” and “Shadow Dancer,” the latter of which stayed at #1 on the Smooth Jazz Airplay chart for three weeks. Vincent’s unique dual ability to electrify fans while connecting emotionally with them has made him one of the genre’s most popular touring artists. He draws the audience in and makes them part of an exciting musical experience that bridges the gap between the music of his father’s R&B, funk, and soul collection (which Vincent grew up heavily immersed in) and Vincent’s own crisp grooves, well-executed horn lines, and horn-drenched melodies. Just as he plays every instrument on his self-produced albums, he fronts his explosive band by providing the audience with a well blended show of sax, guitar, drums, and vocals. The in-demand recording artist continues to make his mark with a signature music blend of energetic smooth jazz grooves, infused with soulful, old-school retro vibes. His versatility on multiple instruments makes him sought after both live and as a producer in the studio.

events.title: Hiromi & Kazunori Kumagai
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
Virtuoso pianist Hiromi returns to the Miner stage with four exclusive nights with projects ranging from solo to trio.

She kicks off her residency with remarkable duo evening with Japanese tap dance master Kazunori Kumagai, revisiting their ongoing collaboration that goes back to their showstopping debut performance at the 2011 Tokyo Jazz Festival.

Moving to New York at age 19 to immerse himself in tap culture, Kumagai is a veteran of Ted Levy and Savion Glover’s “Funk University” — the training ground for the landmark musical Bring in da Noise, Bring in da Funk — and studied with the late legend Gregory Hines. After moving back to Japan, Kumagai built on his affinity for jazz with the iconic Japanese trumpeter Terumasa Hino and opened his own studio in Japan in 2008. He was selected as one of the “100 Most Influential Japanese People” by Newsweek Japan and appeared as a solo performer at the Opening Ceremony of the 2020 Summer Olympics in Tokyo. He and Hiromi first toured Japan together in 2018.

Hiromi’s work in a duo setting has always been a hallmark of her career, in which the limitlessly talented pianist can play off their shared energy, taking both artists to new heights of creativity.

Personnel: Hiromi (piano); Kazunori Kumagai (dancer)

events.title: Cyrille Aimée
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Joe Henderson Lab
events.description:
Winner of the Sarah Vaughan International Vocal Competition, Cyrille Aimée truly has jazz in her blood. Raised by a French father and Dominican mother in the northern French town of Samois-sur-Seine – the last home of Roma jazz giant Django Reinhardt – Aimée found inspiration in the music of Reinhardt and the freedom of the gypsy lifestyle, singing on street corners during travels across Europe. Winning the Montreux Jazz Festival Vocal Competition in 2007 helped finance her self-produced debut album, and finishing as a finalist in the 2012 Thelonious Monk International Jazz Vocal Competition elevated Aimée’s visibility to a global level as a major new figure in jazz. A performer possessed of an infectious joy, lightness of touch and deep feeling for the lyric, Aimée released her breakout 2014 hit on Mack Avenue, It’s a Good Day, mixing Roma jazz inspirations, bossa nova, flamenco and the Great American Songbook.

A relocation to Costa Rica and new motherhood have instilled a fresh inspiration in Aimée, and for these performances, she performs a cross-section of her wide-ranging repertoire including music from her latest Whirlwind release, à Fleur de Peau and live session, Cyrille Aimée: 4.24.

Personnel: Cyrille Aimée (vocals)

events.location: inStudio with Empowerment Avenue, 473 25th St., Suite A, Oakland
events.description: The Distance Between: Traveling Beyond Count Time Program & Event Overview Currently on view at Empowerment Avenue’s inStudio in Oakland, The Distance Between: Traveling Beyond Count Time brings together stories told through the work of Black currently and formerly incarcerated artists. Their work traces histories of enslavement and confinement alongside the realities of incarceration today, while carrying memory, endurance, and imagination toward something beyond them. Together, these works invite us to explore the space between captivity and liberation, to see differently, and to imagine a world beyond systems of punishment. Friday, October 2 | 1:00–9:00 PM 1:00 PM | Gallery Opens Empowerment Avenue’s inStudio will open its doors at 1:00 PM, inviting visitors to experience The Distance Between: Traveling Beyond Count Time and spend time with the work throughout the afternoon. Live at inStudio 6:00 PM | Panel Discussion: Black Yearning for Freedom At 6:00 PM, we will gather for a conversation exploring a continuing Black yearning for freedom and the ways artists carry memory, history, our bodies, and our imaginations onto canvas and paper. Moving between histories of enslavement and confinement and the realities of incarceration today, the conversation will consider art as a place to hold these experiences while also imagining beyond them. What does it mean to create from within systems of confinement without allowing confinement to define the limits of the imagination? What can Black creative practice teach us about freedom, possibility, and the worlds we have yet to make? The conversation will feature exhibition artists Ray Williams Jr. and Alvin Smith, alongside exhibition co-curator De’jon Joy. The discussion will be moderated by Milan Drake, Community Design Lead at the Hasso Plattner Institute of Design at Stanford University (the d.school). 7:00 PM | Live Performance by Inertia the Artist Following the conversation, Inertia the Artist will offer a live performance in the gallery. Inertia the Artist is an Oakland-based vocalist, loop artist, facilitator, and somatic psychotherapist whose soulful music and sound work center healing, transformation, and social change. The performance extends the evening’s exploration beyond the visual, bringing voice, sound, body, and collective experience into the exhibition space.

events.title: Eriq La Salle with Dave Clark - Laws of Solomon
events.location: Book Passage Ferry Building 1 Ferry Building San Francisco, CA 94111
events.description: Propulsive and deeply human, Laws of Solomon is a story of redemption, found family, and the cost of choosing compassion in a brutal world. In saving Gaby, Solomon may finally discover whether peace is something a man like him can earn—or something he must sacrifice everything to protect. Eriq will be joined in conversation by Dave Clark, an Emmy Award-winning television journalist, professional announcer, emcee, speaker, interviewer, and community advocate with more than five decades of broadcasting experience. "Beautiful and heartbreaking." — Walter Mosley "An amazing read!" — S.A. Cosby "Lush and brutal, a poem hiding out as a novel." — Rachel Howzell Hall "La Salle writes with verve." — Dennis Lehane Redemption isn't given. It's fought for. After years of violence, Solomon leaves the brutal backdrop of New York and its underworld to find peace in California where he settles for the quiet life of a gardener defined by routine, restraint, and a fragile kind of peace that had alluded him. Having been a former child soldier, mercenary, and hit man, he is determined to put his past behind him. But as violence erupts on the grounds he tends, his hard-won tranquility shatters when he encounters a young boy named Gaby whose life is in danger. Protecting the child pulls Solomon back into a world he swore he'd buried. As they set out on an unexpected journey, hunted by men who will stop at nothing to get what they want, Solomon must confront not only the threat closing in but the darkness he carries within. Propulsive and deeply human, Laws of Solomon is a story of redemption, found family, and the cost of choosing compassion in a brutal world. In saving Gaby, Solomon may finally discover whether peace is something a man like him can earn—or something he must sacrifice everything to protect. Eriq La Salle brings readers into the world of his acclaimed Martyr Maker series with this standalone novel—the perfect entry point for readers new to La Salle's writing. Actor. Director. Producer. Author. ERIQ LA SALLE is best known to audiences for his portrayal of Dr. Peter Benton on the ground-breaking medical drama ER. Other notable acting appearances include Coming to America, One Hour Photo, and Logan. La Salle received his formal training from Juilliard and NYU’s Tisch School of the Arts. La Salle has built a prolific career behind the camera as well, directing and executive producing for Law & Order, On Call, FBI, Chicago PD, among others. After decades of success in the entertainment industry, La Salle launched his highly personal and award-winning Martyr Maker series. With these novels, he brings an unusual new depth and emotion to the traditional procedural thriller. Find Eriq online at iameriqlasalle.com, on Instagram @eriqlasalle and TikTok @eriqlsalleauthor Dave Clark is an Emmy Award-winning television journalist, professional announcer, emcee, speaker, interviewer, and community advocate with more than five decades of broadcasting experience. Since 2007, he has served as a morning news anchor for KTVU TV Channel 2 in the San Francisco Bay Area, where viewers know him for his credibility, warmth, and steady presence. His on-camera presence reflects journalistic authority and genuine human connection. Beyond the anchor desk, Dave hosts KTVU’s “Talk of the Town,” where he interviews newsmakers, artists, business leaders, and community voices. His commanding voice and engaging style have made him a sought-after master of ceremonies, narrator, and speaker. Dave serves as an Advisory Board Member for Joshua’s Gift and Director of Media & Community Relations for The Vibrancy Foundation™. He and his wife, artist and entrepreneur Lucretia D. Clark, share a deep commitment to community, culture, and service. events.title: Under The Thumb
events.location: Werkshack, 481 25th Street, Oakland
events.description: This group exhibition at Werkshack Studios brings together four artists to explore themes of oppressive systems, power, and control through glass and mixed media. Working across diverse techniques including fusing, painting, stained glass, cast glass and more, each artist brings a distinct perspective to the ways power shapes our lives and communities. Glass becomes both medium and metaphor: beautiful yet fragile, transparent yet obstructive, resilient yet vulnerable. Together, the works examine how systems of power are experienced differently across individuals and groups, inviting us to consider who holds power, who is affected by it, and what it means to resist, endure, or transform it. events.title: Kiliii Yuyan - Guardians of Life
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: Based on the work of award-winning National Geographic photographer Kiliii Yüyan, Guardians of Life takes readers on a transformative journey to people living in relationship with their ancestral homelands while upholding the sovereign rights of Indigenous peoples to care for their lands and waters. This book seeks to build a movement that broadly benefits and sustains life on Earth for everyone. There is a critical yet underrecognized role that Indigenous peoples around the world have played—and continue to play—in sustaining biological and cultural diversity. As the biodiversity and climate crises converge, the time to support Indigenous leadership is now. This rich, in-depth, storytelling initiative is based on growing global recognition of the critical role Indigenous peoples play in sustaining biological and cultural diversity, as well as adapting to and abating climate change. This book, Guardians of Life , is based on the work of award-winning National Geographic photographer Kiliii Yüyan , and will take readers on a transformative journey to places and people living in relationship with their ancestral homelands. Vivid portraits of Indigenous men and women, youth and elders, hunters and farmers, spiritual leaders and craftsmen will reveal their ways of knowing and taking care of the land. These are concepts and skills that have been taught for generations and are based on a foundational veneration for life— which is at the heart of caring for a living planet. This reflects a holistic and broad approach to sustainability, including language, art, and ceremony as ways to maintain human-environment relations. These place-based stories and imagery are complemented by an introduction by Gwich’in supermodel and activist Quannah Chasinghorse . Essay contributions come from award-winning writer Charles C. Mann , author of 1491 , and award winning author, Indigenous peoples' ally, and National Geographic Explorer, Gleb Raygorodetsky . This book upholds the inherent sovereign rights of Indigenous peoples to care for their ancestral lands and waters , and seeks to build a movement that would broadly benefit and sustain life on planet Earth for all. “Indigenous peoples have mastered the art of living on Earth without destroying it. They continue to teach and lead by example. We must heed these lessons, if we want our grandchildren to have a future.” — Jon Waterhouse, S'klallam, Chippewa-Cree "A visually dazzling and deeply informative collection that will linger with readers long after the last page." -- Kirkus Reviews (starred review) "Both breathtaking and intimate. . ." -- Foreword Reviews (starred review) KILIII YÜYAN: Photographer and National Geographic Explorer Kiliii Yüyan brings to life stories from the Arctic sea ice, beneath the waves, and within the heart of human communities. Of Chinese and Nanai/Hèzhé (East Asian Indigenous) descent, he works through a cross-cultural lens, exploring how humanity lives in relationship with land and sea. His photography and storytelling appear in National Geographic , TIME , Vogue , WIRED , and other major publications. In 2023, Kiliii was honored with the Eliza Scidmore Award for Outstanding Storytelling , one of National Geographic ’s highest recognitions. His work has been recognized by Pictures of the Year , Leica Oscar-Barnack , PDN , and ASMP , and is held in museum collections across the U.S. Kiliii has taken the stage at TEDx , toured with NatGeo Live , and now keynotes through Changemaker Talent , sharing the human stories behind his images. events.title: City Arts & Lectures @ Sydney Goldstein Theater - Kyle MacLachlan in conversation with Jesse Hawthorne Ficks
events.location: Sydney Goldstein Theater
events.description: Event location: Sydney Goldstein Theater, 275 Hayes St in San Francisco. Black Bird Bookstore will be the onsite bookseller at this event. In his upcoming debut memoir Fictional Selves, cultural icon Kyle MacLachlan looks back at his off-beat journey in Hollywood. From his debut in David Lynch’s Dune, to his award-winning performance as as Special Agent Dale Cooper in Twin Peaks, to his recent viral social media stardom, MacLachlan reveals his complex relationship with fame, his relationships with iconic actors, and everything he learned along the way. Kyle MacLachlan has built a fascinating acting career, performing in everything from David Lynch’s Twin Peaks to the adaptation of the video game Fallout. In the process, he has become a beloved cultural icon. MacLachlan’s 1984 film debut was the starring role in Lynch’s Dune. He would go on to work with the experimental director on multiple projects, including the classic film Blue Velvet. For his performance as Special Agent Dale Cooper in Twin Peaks, MacLachlan won a Golden Globe and gained international fame. Over the next few decades, MacLachlan brought his unique talent to a wide variety of movies, including The Doors, Showgirls, and the live-action adaptation of The Flintstones. MacLachlan also became a sought after guest star for popular television shows, including How I Met Your Mother, Law & Order SVU, Sex and the City, and Portlandia. More recently, he has gained a new group of fans through his award-winning performance in the show Fallout and the crime comedy show The Lowdown. When not acting, MacLachlan co-founded the winery Pursued by Bear, co-created the podcasts What Are We Even Doing? and Varnamtown, and became a viral session on TikTok and Instagram. In his upcoming debut memoir Fictional Selves, MacLachlan looks back at his off-beat journey in Hollywood. Through beautiful storytelling, MacLachlan traces his many iconic roles, his relationship with fame, and his iconic artistic collaborators, revealing details of his career and the lessons he has learned over the past fifty years. Jesse Hawthorne Ficks is the Film History Coordinator at the Academy of Art University in San Francisco, a member of the San Francisco Bay Area Film Critics Circle, and has been a guest professor at Chapman University. He is Film Festival Critic for 48 Hills and is a frequent co-presenter with local festivals, including the San Francisco International LGBTQ+ Film Festival, hosted by Frameline. For 25 years, Ficks has curated and hosted MOViES FOR MANiACS, “a film series celebrating underrated and overlooked cinema, in a neo-sincere manner.” A limited number of tickets include a copy of MacLachlan’s new book, Fictional Selves. If your ticket comes with a book and you are unable to attend this event, please call Black Bird Bookstore at (415) 742-5203 to arrange for pick-up. Books are available for you to collect at 4541 Irving Street in San Francisco up to 7 days following the event. Photo by Sophy Holland

events.title: Cyrille Aimée
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Joe Henderson Lab
events.description:
Winner of the Sarah Vaughan International Vocal Competition, Cyrille Aimée truly has jazz in her blood. Raised by a French father and Dominican mother in the northern French town of Samois-sur-Seine – the last home of Roma jazz giant Django Reinhardt – Aimée found inspiration in the music of Reinhardt and the freedom of the gypsy lifestyle, singing on street corners during travels across Europe. Winning the Montreux Jazz Festival Vocal Competition in 2007 helped finance her self-produced debut album, and finishing as a finalist in the 2012 Thelonious Monk International Jazz Vocal Competition elevated Aimée’s visibility to a global level as a major new figure in jazz. A performer possessed of an infectious joy, lightness of touch and deep feeling for the lyric, Aimée released her breakout 2014 hit on Mack Avenue, It’s a Good Day, mixing Roma jazz inspirations, bossa nova, flamenco and the Great American Songbook.

A relocation to Costa Rica and new motherhood have instilled a fresh inspiration in Aimée, and for these performances, she performs a cross-section of her wide-ranging repertoire including music from her latest Whirlwind release, à Fleur de Peau and live session, Cyrille Aimée: 4.24.

Personnel: Cyrille Aimée (vocals)

events.title: THE CURTIS FAMILY C-NOTES
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Funk, soul, and R&B, mixed with elements of jazz and gospel harmony · As seen on America’s Got Talent, Season 16, The Curtis Family C-notes are on tour promoting their 3rd album, Awaken III. Since their AGT appearances, they have done television commercials for JCPenney, ads for Fluevog, and have played sold-out shows at iconic venues like Yoshi’s, the Blue Note, the Fox Theatre, and the Concord Pavilion. The band of multi-instrumentalists is made up of the entire family: Papa C, Mama C, and their 5 children, Zahara, Nile, Isis, Kiki, and Phoenix. The Curtis Family has also played and performed with icons like, Jon Batiste, El DeBarge (of the iconic Debarge family), Lenny Williams (former lead singer of Tower of Power), opened for Juan Escovedo (of the famed E Family), Lalah Hathaway, opened the 50th annual Stone Soul Concert at the Concord Pavilion, toured the country playing historical venues, the Lincoln Theatre in D.C., the Blue Nile in New Orleans, and The Bitter End in New York, where the family recorded a live album, to be released in the Fall of 2026. The Curtis Family’s goal is to use their growing platform to highlight the disparities that adversely affect marginalized communities in San Francisco through their non-profit, Passing The Torch, where they bring the whole family, seniors, and the youth together through music. Maestro Curtis and his wife Nola are proud faculty members of the San Francisco Community Music Center, where all 5 of their children are also students; they all take pride in being a part of an institution that ensures high-quality music education is accessible to people of all ages, backgrounds, and abilities, regardless of financial means.

events.title: Hiromi
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
No pianist alive imbues the solo piano format with more explosive virtuosity or thrilling unpredictability than Hiromi Uehara – a GRAMMY-winning artist the All Music Guide calls “one of the most remarkable pianists of the past half century.” For the second night of her 2026-27 residency, Hiromi brings her inimitable fire and passion to this solo performance.

Debuting with the Czech Philharmonic at 14, the Hamamatsu, Japan native was mentored by Chick Corea and Ahmad Jamal early in her development, signing her first record deal with Telarc before graduating from Boston’s Berklee College of Music. Blending a foundation in classical repertoire with a deep feeling for the jazz tradition, she’s collaborated with Corea and Stanley Clarke, led 17 albums including her latest releases with her Sonicwonder quartet and a live duo session with legendary singer, songwriter, and pianist Akiko Yano.

But it is the solo recital that allows Hiromi to follow her creative muse unadorned and explore without restriction — a format memorialized on her superlative 2019 Concord Jazz solo album, Spectrum, a recording intended to be a celebration of the instrument’s full potential. Of that aim, DownBeat says “few documents testify more powerfully than Spectrum.”

Personnel: Hiromi (piano)

events.title: Snarky Puppy
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Paramount Theatre, Oakland
events.description:
The five-time GRAMMY-winning juggernaut Snarky Puppy returns to Oakland’s Paramount Theatre for a highly anticipated performance.

“An exultant throwdown of smart danceability” (Village Voice), Snarky Puppy isn’t exactly a jazz band. It’s not a fusion band or a jam band. It’s probably best to take Nate Chinen of The New York Times’ advice, as stated in an online discussion about the group, to “take them for what they are, rather than judge them for what they’re not.”

The global collective which features a revolving cast of up to a dozen musicians makes what it likes to call “music for your brain and booty.” Led by bassist and composer Michael League, the band features a rotating lineup of world class instrumentalists whose résumés boast work with stars like Erykah Badu, Marcus Miller, Justin Timberlake, Roy Hargrove, Snoop Dogg and John Mayer.

Their 2022 recording, Empire Central, received a well-earned GRAMMY win for Best Contemporary Instrumental Album at the 66th awards ceremony — their fifth win in as many nominations — and was inspired by the band’s formative home of Dallas, blending their whirlwind jazz-ified funk with elements of Southern rock, electric blues, classic soul, slinky R&B, and modern gospel.

The group’s most recent album, 2025’s Somni, created in collaboration with the acclaimed Metropole Orkest, expands the band’s boundary‑blurring sound with lush orchestral textures and deep grooves. Hailed as “a sweeping, cinematic evolution of the band’s groove-driven aesthetic” (DownBeat), the project pairs League’s expansive compositions with the orchestra’s rich sonic palette.

Personnel: Michael League (bass); Others TBA

events.title: John Baccigaluppi - Making Music
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: John Baccigaluppi discusses Making Music , in conversation with SASAMI Groundbreaking conversations with the music producers behind the most successful recording artists on the planet, collected from Tape Op magazine “ Tape Op magazine is a font of information and great stories about the craft and history of making records. It’s about making music from the microphone up.” —Brian Eno (David Bowie, U2, Talking Heads) John Baccigaluppi will be joined in conversation with musician SASAMI. THIS BOOK IS A COLLECTION OF INTERVIEWS with people who have made records with some of the biggest names in music. Along the way, they might be engineering the recordings, picking the songs, guiding the singers, picking the best takes of songs, balancing egos, fixing the lyrics, booking the studio time, buying lunch, playing instruments, pushing artists further, writing or cowriting the songs, selecting the musicians to use, overseeing the mixes, and many other tasks. Making records is always a combination of many skills and goals, and the producer needs to have what it takes to make the session productive and the music compelling. In this book, interviewees include people who have worked with the Beatles, the Rolling Stones, Public Enemy, Taylor Swift, Doja Cat, Bob Dylan, P!nk, U2, Peter Gabriel, Emmylou Harris, Willie Nelson, Wu-Tang Clan, David Bowie, T.Rex, Johnny Cash, the Moody Blues, Aretha Franklin, Amy Winehouse, Paul McCartney, Dolly Parton, Duran Duran, the Replacements, Christina Aguilera, Alicia Keys, Kendrick Lamar, Tom Petty, Thin Lizzy, and Sabrina Carpenter. And that’s just the beginning of the credits these producers—Brian Eno, Finneas, Glyn Johns, Hank Shocklee, Jack Antonoff, Joe Boyd, Jon Brion, Lee Scratch Perry, Lynda Perry, Mark Ronson, RZA, Sasami, Steve Lillywhite, Susan Rogers, Sylvia Massy, T Bone Burnett, and many others—collectively hold. All of these interviews come from the pages of Tape Op magazine, founded in 1996 by editor Larry Crane. Over the last thirty years, along with publisher John Baccigaluppi, Tape Op has become the world’s deepest archive of conversations about the art and science of recording music, and is still an active, print-based magazine with the highest circulation of any recording magazine in the world. “Tape Op is always full of joy for me. Real people making real music with real tools and very, very little snobbery. Old and new equally valued.” —Pete Townshend (The Who) “Tape Op is, without question, the leader in its field.” —Glyn Johns (Rolling Stones, The Who, The Beatles, Led Zeppelin) “What a wild ride Tape Op has been on! You’ve helped the music community in so many ways.” —Don Zientara (Inner Ear Studio, Fugazi, Minor Threat) “I’ve pretty much read every issue of Tape Op magazine since I’ve known of its existence many years ago. Tape Op is my inside track on the people who make the music that lives on my stereo. These are my heroes and my peers.” —Joe Chiccarelli (White Stripes, Elton John, Beck, U2, the Killers) ABOUT THE EDITORS LARRY CRANE (not appearing) was a home recordist and member of the band Vomit Launch in the 1980s before he moved to Portland, Oregon, where he opened a studio and founded Tape Op magazine in 1997—initially photocopied and hand-stapled. Crane’s Jackpot! recording studio has hosted R.E.M., Sonic Youth, Eddie Vedder, Pink Martini, Spoon, Death Cab for Cutie, and Built to Spill, and he has worked with Elliott Smith, the Go-Betweens, the Decemberists, Sleater-Kinney, Jenny Lewis, Quasi, She & Him, M. Ward, Moon Duo, Team Dresch, Stephen Malkmus, Jolie Holland, Jason Lytle, and the Walkabouts. JOHN BACCIGALUPPI is a producer, engineer, and studio owner; he met Larry Crane when he produced Vomit Launch’s third and fourth albums. He came aboard Tape Op in 1999 as the publisher, designer, and co-owner. Since then, Tape Op has become the largest-circulation recording magazine in the world. Baccigaluppi currently runs Panoramic House Studio and has worked with My Morning Jacket, Devendra Banhart, Kurt Vile, Cate Le Bon, Hurray for the Riff Raff, Feist, Deftones, Thee Oh Sees, Ty Segall, 7 Seconds, and Little Wings. Crane and Baccigaluppi have worked with some of the most important artists of the last thirty years, while also running a magazine that discusses the art of making records. events.title: inStudio: The Distance Between: Traveling Beyond Count Time
events.location: inStudio with Empowerment Avenue, 473 25th St., Suite A, Oakland
events.description: Program & Event Overview Currently on view at Empowerment Avenue’s inStudio in Oakland, The Distance Between: Traveling Beyond Count Time brings together stories told through the work of Black currently and formerly incarcerated artists. Their work traces histories of enslavement and confinement alongside the realities of incarceration today, while carrying memory, endurance, and imagination toward something beyond them. Together, these works invite us to explore the space between captivity and liberation, to see differently, and to imagine a world beyond systems of punishment. Saturday, October 3 | 12:00–5:00 PM 12:00 PM | Gallery Opens On Saturday, inStudio will reopen for an afternoon of art, conversation, and community. Open Flow: Community Dialogue Throughout the afternoon, exhibition co-curators De’jon Joy and Christine Lashaw will host an open-flow community dialogue inside the gallery. Rather than a traditional panel, the gathering will create space for visitors to move through the exhibition, ask questions, sit in conversation, and reflect together on the histories, ideas, and possibilities held within the work. Currently incarcerated participating artists will also call into the gallery at various points throughout the day, creating opportunities for visitors to hear directly from artists whose work they are encountering on the walls. The weekend invites audiences not simply to view the exhibition, but to spend time inside its questions: to consider what we have inherited, what we have normalized, and what becomes possible when Black artists are given space to imagine beyond captivity.

events.title: Book Event with Mahmoud Khalil
events.location: First Congregational Church of Oakland
events.description: Join AROC Action and the Center for Constitutional Rights for a conversation with Palestinian organizer and writer Mahmoud Khalil on political repression, Palestine solidarity, and the fight against authoritarianism in the United States and around the world. The discussion will mark the publication of Khalil’s first book, No Land to Stand On: Notes from Detention , a memoir drawing on his prison diary and recounting his arrest, incarceration, separation from his family, and continuing struggle against deportation. The book can be purchased for a discount with your ticket, or separately at retail value by clicking below. In March 2025, federal immigration agents arrested Khalil, a lawful permanent resident and prominent participant in the Palestine solidarity movement at Columbia University. He was held in immigration detention for 104 days while the federal government sought to deport him. Khalil continues to face removal proceedings while pursuing multiple legal challenges related to his arrest, detention, and targeting. In 2026, the Center for Constitutional Rights filed a lawsuit on his behalf challenging his detention and alleging a coordinated effort by government officials and far-right and pro-Israel groups including the Heritage Foundation, Betar, and Canary Mission to punish and intimidate Palestinian rights advocates. His case raises urgent questions about the collaboration of private and state actions to use immigration law, surveillance, institutional power, and state repression against political dissent. At a moment of expanding executive authority and intensified attacks on protest movements, this conversation will explore what Khalil’s experience reveals about the broader struggle to defend civil liberties, confront authoritarianism, and protect movements organizing for Palestinian freedom and collective liberation. Hosted by AROC Action and the Center for Constitutional Rights, the event will bring together Khalil’s personal story, his ongoing legal battles, and a wider conversation about how movements can resist political repression while continuing to organize for justice. Doors open at 12:30pm. Book signing will take place from 12:30pm to 1pm. Event will run from 1pm to 3pm. No one turned away for lack of funds. events.title: Désirée Zamorano with Linda González & Jennifer Nguyen - Amarisa's Cooking Pot
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: Amarisa’s Cooking Pot: Tales of Life in All Its Wonders is a riveting collection whose worlds collide and connect between the fantastic and the ordinary. Désirée Zamorano allows readers to explore this question beautifully, and memorably, long after the last page is turned. Désirée will be joined in conversation by Linda González, the author of Rest Like a Giant Tree , and Jennifer Nguyen, the soon-to-be author of Everything is Fine . Amarisa’s Cooking Pot: Tales of Life in All Its Wonders is a riveting collection whose worlds collide and connect between the fantastic and the ordinary. Startling in their breadth and depth, these stories range from the quietly desperate to the gloriously fantastical, representing Mexican American culture among the characters who are guided by gifts of enchantment or confronted with illusory events shaped by deeply human and enlightening emotions. Each story is dedicated to capturing something ineffable, an emotional truth, a moment of beauty or realization, a moment of calm, or a spark of fury. What does it mean to be alive in a capricious world? Désirée Zamorano allows readers to explore this question beautifully, and memorably, long after the last page is turned. “Zamorano’s collection of stories is a medley of surprises, heartbreak, and triumph. In these tales, Zamorano offers a feast both magical and stark, interweaving miracles and realities of working-class daily life amid the bonds of family—mothers and sons, daughters and grandmothers, lovers snatching tenderness in ambiguous spaces—and with deft language and precise, evocative style, lays open the complicated webbing connecting this community.” —Marcela Fuentes, author of Malas, Reforma National Book Award winner “How deft, vibrant, and heartfelt these stories are. I love the way they slip, subtly, from quiet domesticity to magic, then back again; I love even more how often the conduit for those shifts is a perfectly imagined mundane detail, such as an inherited cooking pot or a mother's shed strands of hair. And when these stories offer glimpses of wonder, they do so in order to give Zamorano's characters justice that the world denies them.” —Holly Goddard Jones, author of Antipodes: Stories and Girl Trouble: Stories In addition to her short stories, ranging from the gritty to the fantastical, Désirée Zamorano is also the author of the groundbreaking family saga, historical fiction novel Dispossessed . Her highly acclaimed literary novel, The Amado Women was re-released September 2025. An award-winning and Pushcart prize nominee short story writer, her work is an exploration of where cultures collide and connect and a representation of her Mexican American demographic. A selection of her work can be found in Alta , The Kenyon Review Online and Akashic’s South Central Noir . She is the senior fiction editor for Silk Road Press, and, up until the Eaton Canyon Fire, lived in Altadena for 26 years. Linda González (she/ella) is the author of four non-fiction books and has published many essays. Her most recent essay collection is Rest Like a Giant Tree: Be Happy in the Midst of So Much . She works tirelessly to write and support writing that enriches the current canon of literature, challenging the narrative that she cannot include Spanish in her work without explaining or italicizing it. She works with BIPOC (Black, Indigenous, and People of Color) writers to claim their voice. She currently lives in Pt. Richmond, the unceded land of the Ohlone nation. Jennifer Nguyen is a non-fiction writer based in Oakland, California. Her first book of personal essays, entitled Everything is Fine: Vietnamese American Notes , will be published in 2028. She is currently working on a book about abolishing institutional philanthropy, the field in which she works. She still types two spaces after every period and does not intend to stop. events.title: Real Social Connections
events.location: 550 Laguna St, San Francisco + Full Studio
events.description:
🌿 Description
Beyond small talk, social scripts, and the pressure to be a certain way.
An immersive half-day exploration of movement, playfulness, touch, authentic relating, and meaningful conversation in a trauma-informed space.

🌿 About This Gathering
Meaningful connection rarely happens by accident. It tends to emerge when we feel safe enough to slow down, be ourselves, and meet one another with curiosity.
This gathering is an invitation to explore what helps genuine connection emerge - not by performing, saying the "right" thing, or following a script, but by creating the conditions where we can be more present, playful, and authentic with ourselves and others.
At the heart of this gathering is a simple idea: connection deepens when we feel safe enough to be seen and expressed -not just the polished parts of ourselves, but also the parts we might usually hide or hold back. Through movement, play, somatic awareness, and guided conversations, we'll explore what happens when we let ourselves show up more fully and meet one another more deeply.
This is an evolving exploration of connection, community, and play. I'm excited to create a deep experience together and to see what becomes possible when we give ourselves more space to be ourselves and meet one another more fully.
My hope is that you'll leave with a deeper sense of connection to yourself and others, and maybe even with a new friend or two.

🕰 Flow / Schedule


💫 Who This Is For
This gathering is for anyone who longs for more genuine connection. It’s especially for people who sometimes struggle to connect, fit in, or feel like they truly belong; for those who appreciate a slower pace when getting to know others; and for anyone curious about moving beyond small talk, social performance, or the feeling that they need to say the “right” thing or show up in a certain way.
Rather than trying to “get connection right,” we’ll explore what naturally allows connection to emerge—through presence, play, movement, and authentic conversation.
Whether you're outgoing, introverted, or somewhere in between, you'll be invited to participate at your own pace. No previous experience is needed: just come as you are.

👥 Facilitator
Simone Giacometti is a somatic practitioner, psychedelic integration guide, and facilitator passionate about helping people heal, grow, and connect more deeply with themselves and others.
Originally trained as a scientist, Simone spent years working at the intersection of biology, technology, and program management before transitioning into healing work. Today, he supports people through one-on-one sessions that weave together trauma-informed healing, somatic practices, inner exploration, and psychedelic integration work to help people reconnect with themselves and grow into greater authenticity.
His group facilitation draws on somatics, authentic relating, nervous system awareness, and play to create spaces where people can slow down, be themselves, and feel more at home with others. (This gathering is fully substance-free and centered on movement, conversation, and connection.)

Learn more about Simone and his work at healwithsimone.com

events.title: Artists’ Reception – Julie Engelmann, Amos Goldbaum, Liv Losee-Unger, Fernanda Martínez, & Deirdre Weinberg
events.location: Manna Gallery, 473 25th St., Oakland
events.description: Meet the artists of Big, Small, and Everything In Between and celebrate this group exhibition featuring five Bay Area muralists. Join us for an afternoon gathering and a closer look at how these artists bring the color, energy, and visual language of their public work into the gallery’s intimate setting. Free and open to the public. Julie Engelmann, based in Half Moon Bay, works across murals, paintings, and digital illustration. Using media ranging from acrylic on canvas to spray paint on large walls, she creates highly detailed and often surrealistic imagery, frequently drawing on historical themes and using color and composition to create new visual possibilities. Amos Goldbaum is a San Francisco–based visual artist known for his signature line drawings, which span canvases, large-scale murals, prints, and apparel. Inspired by the places and everyday scenes around him, his work combines multiple viewpoints, angles, and moments in time into cohesive compositions connected by a singular line. His murals can be found throughout the San Francisco Bay Area and in cities around the world, including New York, Los Angeles, Seattle, Tokyo, and Kathmandu. Liv Losee-Unger is a Bay Area muralist known for vibrant, nature-inspired, and community-centered art. With more than sixty public artworks completed across the United States and abroad, her detailed and colorful murals transform spaces through stories of flora, fauna, femininity, and human connection. Fernanda Martínez is an Oakland-based painter, muralist, and sculptor whose vibrant, expressive work draws from memories and observations of nature. Born and raised in Mexico City, she moved to the Bay Area in 2015, where she has developed an experimental and intuitive practice exploring the emotional depth of color, form, pattern, and texture. Her work spans painting, sculpture, murals, and public art, transforming her distinctive visual language across two- and three-dimensional forms. Martinez has exhibited her paintings and sculptures in galleries and has collaborated on numerous public art projects for businesses, nonprofit organizations, and community-focused and affordable housing developments. Deirdre Weinberg is a multidisciplinary artist with deep ties to the San Francisco Bay Area, working across murals, public art, and studio practice. Her evolving work currently focuses on climate change, using a limited black-and-white palette to explore landscapes, seascapes, and airscapes with a sense of urgency and starkness. Whether creating work in public spaces or the studio, Weinberg seeks to build community, connect with viewers, and inspire conversation, reflection, and new perspectives. events.title: Fear Not – William Rhodes Artist’s Talk with Gospel Choir Performance
events.location: Transmission Gallery, 770 West Grand Ave., Suite A, Oakland
events.description: Please join us for William Rhodes’ talk with gospel choir performance by the Dr. George W. Davis Senior Center Choir, music conductor and leader Kenneth Little Saturday, Oct 3rd starting at 2 pm This is part of a series of NEXUS SFBay events including the Caleb Dowdell performance with his piece, Our Prism of Dreams, starting at 1:30 pm just downstairs at Gearbox Gallery, performance about 15 minutes. William’s talk starts at 2 pm upstairs with the Dr. George W. Davis Senior Center Choir closing out the event with a Gospel Choir performance. See one or both at that galleries at 770 West Grand Ave in Oakland. More about Fear Not, William Rhodes’ solo exhibition at Transmission Gallery: William Rhodes’s sculptures on view incorporate objects that have been used, inherited, discarded, or found with elements he has carved himself. Trained early on as a furniture maker, he combines hand carved figures, flames and snakes with objects collected from a family home, photographs, hardware, tools, and other remnants of everyday life. Neon words signal from some pieces. The resulting works resemble shrines or memorials, but they remain grounded in the ordinary. Religious symbols appear alongside household objects. A photograph might be surrounded by carved waves, tools, hardware, animals, or religious symbols. A suitcase can become an architectural space. A toilet becomes the base of an unexpected monument. Things with little apparent value are carefully incorporated into elaborate constructions, their histories becoming part of the work. ​ Rhodes is equally interested in people; family, mentors, and leaders, as well as those who have been overlooked or treated as disposable, recognizing and elevating their presence in his work. By giving attention to these lives, enshrining and revering them, he considers how value is assigned and who gets remembered. The title Fear Not appears in the work as both a phrase and a kind of instruction. It can be read in relation to the religious imagery that runs throughout the sculptures, but it also takes on a morepersonal meaning. To look closely at lives and objects that are easily dismissed is, in its own way, an act of resistance to that dismissal.

events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: A groundbreaking, multilayered mind-body-spirit approach to empowerment and healing. In this transformative guide, revered psychologist Laurel Parnell presents Multidimensional Integrative Healing (MDIH)—a powerful new method developed to help readers reclaim their True Self when traditional recovery isn't enough. “ Come back to the version of who you know yourself to truly be. ” If you've ever experienced a pivotal life event that felt as though it broke you apart and left you struggling to recover, Dr. Parnell understands. After the tragic death of her son, when expert knowledge in trauma recovery wasn't enough to reclaim her True Self, she embarked on a journey that led to the development of a whole new approach. Through this comprehensive guide—integrating transpersonal psychology, Eastern spiritual practices, and energetic traditions—readers learn to: Access resources that can be called on for help when needed Engage energetic sovereignty to stand in your own power Release energies that simply do not belong to you Align with inner knowing and innate healing intelligence Explore five dimensions of reality: physical, emotional, psychological, somatic, and spiritual Dr. Parnell writes, “MDIH recognizes there are different dimensions of reality that exist and can be accessed for healing.” Instead of remaining stuck in old patterns or limiting beliefs, discover how to use these dimensions to move toward wholeness, reclaiming the version of yourself you know you were meant to be. This book guides you to find resources, engage your sovereignty, and finally release what isn't yours. “ Wise and visionary. Laurel is a pioneer in healing and includes the essential dimension of the sacred that has been missing for so many. ” ―Jack Kornfield, author of A Path with Heart and All in This Together “ Releasing What Isn’t Yours invites us to explore the many layers of experience that often go unrecognized in everyday life—and in psychotherapy—yet influence us in profound ways. Laurel Parnell is our deeply insightful, wise, and courageous guide whose devotion to healing and illuminating the truth are revealed in this inspirational personal and professional journey to uncover the ways we are inextricably connected across time and space. When these energy patterns go unrecognized, we may become stuck in the chaos and rigidity of the impaired integration of unresolved trauma. Introducing us to the origins and practical steps of her approach of Multidimensional Integrative Healing, the chapters of this book provide useful ways of understanding layers of experience—whether they are mechanisms or metaphors of the mind—that we can tap into to cultivate post-traumatic growth and resilience in our liberated lives. ” ―Daniel J. Siegel, MD, New York Times -bestselling author of Aware and Mind Laurel Parnell, PhD , is the executive director of the Parnell Institute and the developer of Attachment-Focused EMDR, Resource Tapping, and Multidimensional Integrative Healing. A clinical psychologist and expert in trauma recovery, she has trained thousands of clinicians in the United States and abroad. She is the author of several books, including Attachment-Focused EMDR, A Therapist's Guide to EMDR, and Rewiring the Addicted Brain. Find the author at www.drlaurelparnell.com or on social media.
