events.title: WILL DOWNING
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: They say a man’s “ soul ” is his spiritual essence. Life’s twists and turns can lift that soul high into the sky or send it crashing to the ground below. Unfortunately, 2023 started with the latter for Will Downing, following the unexpected and soul-crushing loss of his daughter, Aron Siobhan Downing, in January. As a father, he was devastated…heartbroken. As an artist, he sought solace and comfort through his craft…facing the hurt head-on and exploring multiple themes of love to begin the healing. Persevering through the pain, Downing is poised to finish the year with his soul rising…literally! The Prince of Sophisticated Soul is ready to share his 7- song masterclass in triumph over tragedy, Soul Rising ! Celebrating an insane 35 years in the “ bizness ” and 27 Albums to his credit, Will Downing will not be stopped! Flexing on his international appeal, the lead single "What Part of My Love" shot to the top of the UK Soul Chart Top 30 and parked there. Those who no longer listen to new releases as the collective work it was intended to be should make an exception in this case. Although not a "concept" album, the pieces of Soul Rising fit together beautifully as a single statement and should be enjoyed as such. We all know about the smoothness, but there's a brand-new kind of...Dare I say..."Funkiness", that I think is here to stay! You (and your speakers, Headphones) etc….. will feel the difference right off the jump, with the lead-off cut, “Closer to Me”, when that bass and drum start hitting a little differently. The familiar writing and production tandem of Downing and guitarist Randy Bowland turns the heat up a bit from their usual formula. With keyboardist Mike Logan Sr. and background vocalist Ms. Monet rounding out the groove, I dare you not to move somethin'! House of Love, another Downing/Bowland collab, gives me "Maze" vibes, however unintended, but that's never a bad thing! To the extent that over the last 4 decades, these two surviving entities may have directly or indirectly influenced each other, I'll welcome that musical baby into the fold every time with open arms and ears. Make no mistake...Will Downing didn't forget the "smooth" that made the Man the Myth the Legend! Nor did he abandon his world-famous knack for what he affectionately calls "interpretations" of classic hits. He plucked an absolute diamond of a gem from arguably one of the finest early 70's albums, The Stylistics, Round Two, and their hauntingly enchanting, “You're As Right As Rain”! If you've ever "slow-dragged" with a blue light in the basement, you will be transported to afros, platforms, bell-bottoms, and Brut cologne...if you know you know, but I digress. In addition to assistance from long-time collaborator Ronnie Foster, Downing recruits the sweet trumpet of solo Artist and one-half of 90's duo Imprompt2, Johnny Brit t, to seal the vibe. Soul Rising then takes a solemn turn to the heart and very "Soul" of this release. Downing, maybe for his own well-being, had to stare his tragedy down squarely and turn art into therapy. “Till We Meet Again” serves as a father's sweet hand-off to God to care for his angel Siobhan, until they're joined again divinely as father and daughter in heavenly reward. An unimaginable undertaking for a parent attempting to channel pain into art. The song is introduced by the actual last New Year's Day voicemail exchanged by Downing and Siobhan, which contains no hint of the drama to unfold just 10 days later. Downing makes the song a true family affair, with daughter Aja and wife Audrey Wheeler Downing lending their supportive voices. A passionately moving, albeit gut-wrenching tribute, but well done. Given that dynamic, it's understandable that the final three tracks all lean into a theme of "Love". Starting with the aforementioned smash, “What Part of My Love”, but pivoting back to that new "funk" vibe with “Love You Right”, this time with Hubert Eaves IV joining the revival. An intentional sequence, I would think, to lift and restore the spirit of Soul Rising ! I think the final cut, “Love of A Lifetime”, as a message, speaks simultaneously of what we seek in both a personal relationship and the love of a father to a child. Maybe that wasn't the intent, but given the circumstances, I heard both. Love is love! Family…, Will Downing dug deep for this one. Even down to the Album cover, an original piece of artwork by Frank Morrison. Realize, recognize, and appreciate a real man, a real artist, and a real father with his Soul Rising !

events.title: Gary Wolf with Kevin Kelly - The Quantified Self
events.location: Book Passage Ferry Building 1 Ferry Building San Francisco, CA 94111
events.description: Science has given us tools and methods that allow us to observe things that were once imperceptible—and this book shows what we can learn when we use them to look at ourselves. “This book is a perfect roadmap to how to actually do personal science… [It outlines] what one needs to do to [answer] questions that matter… whether about a chronic degenerative disease or some other challenge.” - Eli Pollard, renowned patient advocate and Executive Director, World Parkinson Coalition Written by science journalist Gary Wolf, co-founder of the Quantified Self movement, this book teaches readers how to use proven scientific methods to answer their own health questions. At a time when trust in expertise is fractured and people are divided not just politically but over how to know what’s true, The Quantified Self makes the case that science belongs to everyone—and proves it by putting the method in the reader’s hands. Wolf teaches ten reasoning patterns adapted from the history of scientific practice and illustrates them with dozens of personal narratives. Across chapters on pain, mood, cognition, sleep, digestion, heart health, and hormones, readers learn a practical method for answering the health questions that matter most to them. “This book is a gift to anyone who has ever wanted to take their life seriously as a site of learning. It is a profoundly practical, clear, kind, hard-earned manual for self-research, and a foundational starting point for current and future health scientists.” - Eric Hekler, PhD, Professor of Public Health and Design, UC San Diego “You are in charge of your own well-being. That could sound like a threat, but it’s really a promise. What is important to you? What mystery are you trying to solve? What’s a hunch you want to test? Quantified Self: Learning to Observe will give you the tools, language, and strategies you need to reason your way to a better life.” - Susannah Fox, author of Rebel Health: A Field Guide to the Patient-led Revolution in Medical Care and former CTO of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services "Most self-tracking books promise miracles. This one promises something more useful: a method. These experts have distilled nearly two decades of the Quantified Self community into a working guide for asking better questions about your own body and getting answers. The quietly radical claim here — that careful observation, not better sensors, is what turns data into understanding — will be useful to everyone trying to learn more about their health." - Harlan M. Krumholz, MD, founder of the Yale Center for Outcomes Research and Evaluation and author of The Expert Guide to Beating Heart Disease Gary Wolf writes about science and technology. A former executive editor of Wired Digital and contributing editor at Wired magazine, he cofounded the Quantified Self movement in 2008. His first book, The Quantified Self: Learning to Observe , will be published by Workman in October, 2026. He currently works with the Personal Science Research Group to build tools, develop methods, and publish case studies that support small scale empirical science. He lives in Berkeley, California. Kevin Kelly is Senior Maverick at Wired, an award-winning magazine he co-founded Wired in 1993. He is co-chair of The Long Now Foundation , a membership organization that champions long-term thinking. He is founder of the popular Cool Tools website, which has been reviewing tools daily for 20 years. He is also the author of multiple best-selling books about the future of technology. His newest is Excellent Advice for Living , a book of 450 modern proverbs for a pretty good life. He is best known for his radical optimism. Gary Wolf - photo courtesy of the publicist; Kevin Kelly - photo credit: Christopher Michel Event details: This event will be hosted by Book Passage at our Ferry Building store. Free Admission / Open Seating There will be a signing line or meet and greet following the presentation.

events.title: Strategy as an Emotional Act: An Interactive Practice for Changemakers #SFTechWeek
events.location: 550 Laguna St, San Francisco + Full Studio
events.description:
What becomes possible when you design with emotions at the center, not around them?
Most systems change work is technically significant but often lacks an intentional emotional foundation. This 2-hour session treats that as a design challenge. We give you the tools, the frameworks, and the constraints. You bring the real material: your own experience of doing this work, the relational dynamics inside your teams, and the systems you're trying to change.
We move through four design layers: what you're actually feeling, what that creates between people, what emotional conditions make systems genuinely generative, and what all of it means when AI is part of the design.
What you'll takeaway:
Learnings on the language and embodiment of emotions.
Tangible relational tools that you can take back to your org.
Connection that can only come when you lead with vulnerability and emotion.
This event is a part of #SFTechWeek—a week of events hosted by VCs and startups to bring together the tech ecosystem. Learn more at www.tech-week.com.

events.title: Nik Sharma Author Talk • Fundamentals of Flavor: 100 Recipes for the Science of Better Cooking
events.location: Omnivore Books on Food, 3885a Cesar Chavez St, San Francisco, CA 94131
events.description: Nik Sharma is the bestselling author of cookbooks celebrated for blending culinary science with deeply personal storytelling: Season, The Flavor Equation, and Veg-Table. A former molecular biologist, Sharma brings a unique lens to the kitchen, where flavor is both a feeling and a formula. He serves as Editor in Residence at America's Test Kitchen, where he hosts the James Beard nominated YouTube show Flavor Forward with Nik Sharma, is a co-host of the show In the Test Kitchen on Netflix, and is a cast member on America’s Test Kitchen show on PBS. Sharma is the creator of the award-winning blog Nik Sharma Cooks (formerly A Brown Table), and his writing and photography have been featured in The San Francisco Chronicle, The New York Times, The Guardian, and The Wall Street Journal, among others. He lives in Los Angeles, California, where he's always dreaming up his next recipe. Paolo Lucchesi is the editorial director of Resy. Prior to Resy, he worked at the San Francisco Chronicle and Eater, both as an editor and reporter. He has written several books, including “ Flour + Water: Pasta ” and “ A Burger to Believe In .” He lives in San Francisco. Fundamentals of Flavor - Building on the science-forward thinking of The Flavor Equation and the accessibility of his award-winning Veg-Table , Nik Sharma’s latest cookbook brings fascinating technical know-how to exciting everyday recipes. In these pages, Sharma explores the four powerful elements of nature and their profound influence on how we cook, delving into such topics and dishes as: Fire: How caramelization deepens the flavor of Caramelized Shallot and Feta-Labneh Dip Earth: How salt's minerality brings crispness to Salt-Baked New Potatoes with Gochujang Vinaigrette Air: Why drying out cookie dough results in perfect Extra Rich Chocolate-Cinnamon Crinkle Cookies Water: Why sous vide is the best way to cook a hearty, tender loaf of Icelandic Rye Bread And much more. With more than 150 evocative photographs and 20+ infographics that simplify scientific principles for visual learners, this is a beautiful, foundation-building reference book for home cooks who approach their meals with a hunger for knowledge and big flavor.

events.title: Jonah Raskin, Marc Zegans, Larry Beckett read some of their poetry, and Jonah introduces his latest book
events.location: Bird & Beckett Books & Records, 653 Chenery Street, San Francisco
events.description: Jonah Raskin introduces his most recent book of cultural writings, Keeping the Beat (Regent Press, 2026), a collection of original, groundbreaking reviews and essays about the writers of the Beat Generation, plus their contemporaries and fellow travelers. Jonah’s five and a half decades’ output of short and long-form literary/cultural criticism and journalism has traced three-quarters of a century of outsider American socio-political life, with an eye on the American imperial project that frames it. Lately, he’s also produced a fair amount of poetry. Jonah will bring some of his poems to the table to join with poets Marc Zegans and Larry Beckett, who will present some of their own poetry, principally recent work. Larry will also sing a poem of Paul Verlaine, in his own translation, accompanying the poem/song on piano. The Book of Immaculate Perception / Madrigals is a tête-bêche (flip book) by Marc Zegans and Larry Beckett in which two poem cycles, “Madrigals” by Beckett and “The Book of Immaculate Perception” by Zegans can be read from their respective fronts-to-backs in a single spine format. The project developed when Marc sent Larry the manuscript for “The Book of Immaculate Perception,” a micro-chap tracing the circle from raw awareness through life mediated by language to simple awareness regained, and Larry, responding enthusiastically, shared with Marc a thematically resonant series of madrigals inspired by his daughter that trace the life arc forward from conception. The confluence between these poem-cycles extends beyond shared narrative lines to independently formed yet common imagery and complementary methods of composition. In each body of work, you will find compactness of speech, form that liberates line, and an easy flow from poem-to-poem that animates and enriches the experience of reading these two sets of poems in each other’s company. Larry Beckett’s poetry ranges from songs to blank sonnets and 100-page narrative works. His lyric, “Song to the Siren,” is a modern standard. In the years since, he’s written the postmodern epic, “American Cycle,” including the long narratives Paul Bunyan, Wyatt Earp, Amelia Earhart, and he has reinvented Sonnets. “The Book of Merlin” is a recovery and translation of the 6th-century Brythonic poet, and “Romances Without Words / In Solitary” is the first translation of the prison manuscript of Paul Verlaine. “Beat Poetry” is a study of the poets and poetry of the fifties San Francisco Renaissance. These madrigals are to a child from conception on. They’re dedicated to his daughter, Susannah Beckett. Marc Zegans’s seven collections of poems include Lyon Street (Bamboo Dart Press, 2022) and The Snow Dead (Červená Barva Press, 2020). Ghost Book (Kite String Press, 2024), a fine art photo book collaboration with photographer Tsar Fedorsky, is held in the special collections of the Boston Athenaeum, the Getty Research Institute, Yale University’s Haas Family Arts Library, Haverford College, the Peabody Essex Museum, and others. Marc reviews poetry for Liberated Words in his column, “On the Cutting Edge.” Films based on Marc’s poems appear regularly at festivals around the world. He lives by the coast in Northern California.

events.title: !Laloismo! A poetic and musical reimagining of the lyrics  of Lalo Guerrero
events.location: Medicine for Nightmares, 3036 24th St, San Francisco, CA 94110
events.description: Tonight four pochos from different corners and dimensions of Aztlan come together for a poetic and rasquache reimagining of the lyrics of foundational Mexican American singer songwriter Lalo Guerrero. Featuring pendejadas, poetics, y musica from Marisol Medina-Cadena, Louis “El Panadero” Gutierrez, soledad con carne, and Josiah Flores. MC’d by the Pocho poeta Josiah Luis Alderete. This evento is part of the Lalo Guerrero Legacy Festival happening at the Freight and Salvage on November 6th and 7th and is also a PBS(Pocho Broadcasting Company) production. Louis “El Panadero” Gutierrez is a 24th street organic intellectual, Mission poet, and neighborhood archivist. His familia has owned the iconic La Reyna Bakery for over 40 years. Marisol Medina-Cadena is a fourth generation Californian; Bay Area on her mom’s side and LA County on her pop’s side. She is a San Francisco based comedian and storyteller by way of the dirty D, aka Pasadena, California. When she's not being a sad clown she's doing boring things like research and collecting intel of all things pochismo and San Pancho. As a proud member of (PBS) the Pocho Broadcast Service, she takes her duty very seriously to make audiences he-he and ha-ha. soledad con carne is an intergalactic Chicanx punk poet. They are a poet of the root that cracks the concrete on occupied Fernandeño-Tataviam Land: otherwise known as the San Fernando Valley. Part-time poet turned melodic storyteller, Chicano singer/songwriter Josiah Flores puts music to the parts of life most tend to hide from. From the foothills of south San Jose to the foggy avenues of San Francisco, he calls the Bay Area his home. Influenced by the likes of Stoney Edwards, Freddy Fender, and Willie Dunn, if one were to sit in a dimly-lit corner of their local watering hole, hunched over a beer, they would find Josiah’s songs sitting down next to them.

events.title: Dr. Shefali - Raising Conscious Daughters & Raising Conscious Sons (SF)
events.location: Walt Disney Theater 104 Montgomery Street Presidio San Francisco, CA 94129
events.description: Please join us in celebration of bestselling author Dr. Shefali and her compassionate and insightful new books, Raising Conscious Daughters & Raising Conscious Sons. Dr. Shefali will be joined by her co-hosts: Shirin Aryanpour, the founder of Illuminate Her Path, with more than 16 years of experience as a physical therapist, and Geno La Placa, an Executive Leadership and Life Coach, Speaker, and Retreat Facilitator specializing in emotional and intuitive leadership. “In this insightful and compassionate book, Dr. Shefali helps parents understand the immense pressures girls face today... A timely and important book for every parent of girls.” — Dr. Laura Markham, author of Peaceful Parent, Happy Kids Raising Conscious Daughters by bestselling author Dr. Shefali is a powerful wake-up call, a hands-on guide, and a pathway forward to reclaim how daughters are seen, supported, and raised in the 21st century. Something unprecedented is unfolding in the inner lives of our girls today. On the surface, they are excelling and achieving in ways that would seem unimaginable to previous generations. Yet beneath this success lies a far more urgent and unsettling truth: Girls are unraveling at alarming rates. Anxiety, perfectionism, and self-harm are surging, exposing a devastating paradox between the confident, high-achieving facade the world applauds and the fragile, unmoored self that struggles silently within. In a digital age that commodifies attention, comparison, and worth, this inner fracture is no longer slow or subtle. Into this urgent moment comes Raising Conscious Daughters , the groundbreaking new book from clinical psychologist and bestselling author Dr. Shefali, founder of the revolutionary Conscious Parenting movement. Drawing on real-life clinical cases, interviews with children and parents, and deeply practical, prescriptive guidance, Dr. Shefali offers a radical reorientation of how we understand girls today. In this book she shows parents how to raise daughters who: Trust their inner voice Set boundaries with confidence and clarity Stay emotionally connected to their authentic self At a time when girls appear more capable than ever yet feel more fragile within, Raising Conscious Daughters stands as a one-of-a-kind guide for helping them grow into empowered, worthy and resilient beings. "Wise, compassionate, and enormously relevant, this book offers parents a powerful new framework for raising emotionally healthy, resilient boys.” — Dr. Laura Markham, author of Peaceful Parent, Happy Kids Raising Conscious Sons by bestselling author Dr. Shefali is a clarion call, a practical resource, and a hopeful invitation to radically reimagine how boys are understood, nurtured, and raised in the 21st century. Boys today are standing at a critical crossroads unlike any generation before. They are bombarded with impossible and contradictory mandates: Be tough but never vulnerable; be sensitive but never weak; be strong but never domineering. Caught between these warring expectations—and shaped by a digital world that amplifies comparison, disconnection, and performative identity—boys are now experiencing an unprecedented crisis of masculinity, marked by alarming rates of suicide, aggression, isolation, and apathy. In Raising Conscious Sons , clinical psychologist and bestselling author Dr. Shefali—founder of the revolutionary Conscious Parenting movement—offers a bold and urgently needed map for helping boys reclaim their sense of purpose and their capacity to engage meaningfully with life. Drawing on real-life clinical cases, interviews with children and parents, and practical, prescriptive guidance, she shows parents how to raise sons who: Feel emotionally secure and connected to their inner world Develop confidence grounded in integrity rather than dominance Step into purpose with clarity, empathy, and self-discipline At a time when boys are flooded with messages about masculinity yet lack guidance on how to embody it, Raising Conscious Sons stands as a one-of-a-kind guide for helping them stay emotionally connected, authentic and grounded in who they are. Dr. Shefali is a clinical psychologist, a New York Times bestselling author, and the founder of the Conscious Parenting movement, redefining how families understand selfhood, connection, and the inner life of children. She works where psychology meets consciousness, tracing the hidden forces that shape identity, relationships, and the way we inhabit the world. Trained at Columbia University, she has spent decades guiding families to move beyond patterns of control and fear toward presence and authenticity. Her work brings Western psychology and Eastern wisdom into lived practice, creating a path for children—and the adults who raise them—to know themselves fully. Shirin Aryanpour (Founder, Illuminate Her Path) Bio: Shirin Aryanpour is the founder of Illuminate Her Path, an impact-driven platform and community devoted to empowering women through wellness, connection, and authentic sisterhood. With more than 16 years of experience as a physical therapist, Shirin has guided individuals of all ages and backgrounds on their journeys toward healing and well-being. A two-time breast cancer thriver, her personal healing journey deepened her commitment to women's health, equity, and empowerment. Geno La Placa (Executive Coach & Mentor) Bio: Geno La Placa is an Executive Leadership and Life Coach, Speaker, and Retreat Facilitator specializing in emotional and intuitive leadership. A former hedge fund CFO and due diligence expert, she brings extensive executive and financial experience to her transformational coaching work. Geno holds certifications from the Berkeley Executive Coaching Institute, Dr. Shefali's Conscious Parenting Method™, and Dr. Gabor Maté's Compassionate Inquiry. Her work integrates neuroscience, NLP, somatic psychology, emotional intelligence, and intuitive intelligence to help leaders develop greater clarity, confidence, and purpose. events.description: King Lear by William Shakespeare Directed by Michael Socrates Moran Music composed by Paul Dresher Presented by Oakland Theater Project & New Performance Traditions In the twilight of his rule, a king sets out to divide the kingdom among his three daughters. events.title: Dorothy Lazard at Clio's!
events.location: Clio’s Books, 353 Grand Avenue, Oakland, CA 94610, Oakland, CA
events.description: Behind the Desk at the Main. · Join Heyday for another installment of Heyday Presents , an ongoing conversation series presented in collaboration with Clio's Books. Over the course of her 20-year-tenure at the Oakland Public Library’s flagship branch—known as “the Main”— Dorothy Lazard built a career helping residents connect with the city’s past and present, eventually becoming the keeper of Oakland’s local history archives. In her new book, Behind the Desk at the Main , published by Heyday, Lazard offers an insider’s look at the modern American library. Through personal stories and decades of experience, Lazard demystifies the work of librarians and reveals how libraries serve as vital hubs—and defenders—for knowledge, connection, and civic life. She will be joined in conversation by East Bay Yesterday host and producer Liam O'Donoghue . Dorothy Lazard was born in St. Louis and grew up in San Francisco and Oakland. A librarian for forty years, she joined the staff of the Oakland Public Library in 2000. From 2009 until her retirement in 2021, she was the head librarian of OPL’s Oakland History Center, where she encouraged people of all ages and backgrounds to explore local history. Lazard's first book, What You Don't Know Will Make a Whole New World , was the 2023 recipient of the Oscar Lewis Award in Western History from the Book Club of California. She lives in Oakland. Liam O’Donoghue is the host and producer of the East Bay Yesterday podcast and co-creator of the Long Lost Oakland map. He also writes a monthly feature about the East Bay for SF Gate. His journalism has appeared in outlets such as KQED, Oaklandside, Berkeleyside, Mother Jones, Salon, and elsewhere. In 2018, he was honored by the East Bay Express as “the best journalist-turned-historian” and presented with a “Partners in Preservation Award” from Oakland Heritage Alliance. O’Donoghue’s quotes on Oakland-related issues have appeared in media outlets including New York Times and Washington Post. About Heyday Heyday is an independent nonprofit publisher specializing in publications that explore California's natural history, art and culture, Indigenous perspectives, and social justice. This series is part of our Heyday Presents program. Heyday Presents features Heyday authors in conversation with notable luminaries and thought leaders. Heyday Members receive free VIP access to Heyday Presents program and a curation of our top new releases, among a host of other perks. Heyday members and Clio's members receive free admission!

events.title: Janaki Sandy Gaal's "SOULFUL SANCTUARIES"
events.location: Mrs. Dalloway's, 2904 College Ave, Berkeley, CA 94705
events.description: Learn to create a garden that is a sanctuary for peace, reflection, & spiritual growth with this guide to mindful gardening & sacred spaces. Join us at Mrs. Dalloway's Bookstore on Thursday, October 8 at 7:00 PM when author & gardener Janaki Sandy Gaal comes to the store to present her new book S oulful Sanctuaries: Cultivating Sacred Spaces . She will be joined in con In Soulful Sanctuaries , Janaki Sandy Gaal—known as “The Rose Lady”—invites readers to reimagine gardens of any size as places of renewal, healing, and connection to the natural world. Blending practical gardening wisdom, meditative practices, and heartfelt storytelling, this richly photographed book offers a meaningful approach to cultivating an outdoor space that feels personal, restorative, and spiritually alive. Drawing on decades of experience as an organic gardener, garden designer, and consulting rosarian, Janaki shares guidance on organic gardening, year-round cultivation, and creating garden altars that reflect each reader’s own intentions and beliefs. Featuring photography by her daughter, Rebecca Gaal, Soulful Sanctuaries is both an inspiring guide and a keepsake gift book rooted in family, beauty, and spiritual practice. Here’s what makes Soulful Sanctuaries meaningful: • Mindful Gardening for Every Space: Helps readers turn gardens of any size into places to slow down, reconnect, and cultivate meaning. • Practical Organic Gardening Wisdom : Includes sustainable practices, year-round cultivation, and insights from Janaki’s experience as a consulting rosarian. • Spiritual Practices Made Personal: Offers meditative practices, intention-setting, and guidance for creating garden altars. • A Beautiful Keepsake Gift Book: Rebecca Gaal’s photography creates an immersive experience for gardeners, spiritual seekers, and anyone seeking a more restorative living space. Soulful Sanctuaries is a mindful gardening book and spiritual gardening guide for readers interested in sacred spaces, organic gardening, garden sanctuaries, meditation, and connecting more deeply with nature. JANAKI SANDY GAAL is an author, educator, gardener, and longtime student of Ram Dass. An organic gardener, garden designer, and consulting rosarian, she has dedicated her life to relieving suffering—from her early work as an ICU nurse to opening her garden to the public. Through writing and teaching, Janaki explores the connection between spirituality, nature, and everyday life, encouraging reflection, presence, and healing through simple practices such as gardening, cooking, and connecting with the natural world. She lives on Maui, Hawaii, surrounded by ʻohana. REBECCA GAAL is a creative strategist and visual storyteller whose work bridges environmental science, public health, and visual communication. A Fujifilm X Photographer, her work has been exhibited and published internationally by The Nature Conservancy, The American Scholar, Harvard University Center for the Environment, Adobe, and the National Institutes of Health. She is Director of Partnerships at the Santa Barbara Wildlife Care Network and Executive Producer of Wild Rescue, an IMAX 3D film exploring the intersection of wildlife and human worlds. She lives in Ventura, California.

events.title: WILL DOWNING
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: They say a man’s “ soul ” is his spiritual essence. Life’s twists and turns can lift that soul high into the sky or send it crashing to the ground below. Unfortunately, 2023 started with the latter for Will Downing, following the unexpected and soul-crushing loss of his daughter, Aron Siobhan Downing, in January. As a father, he was devastated…heartbroken. As an artist, he sought solace and comfort through his craft…facing the hurt head-on and exploring multiple themes of love to begin the healing. Persevering through the pain, Downing is poised to finish the year with his soul rising…literally! The Prince of Sophisticated Soul is ready to share his 7- song masterclass in triumph over tragedy, Soul Rising ! Celebrating an insane 35 years in the “ bizness ” and 27 Albums to his credit, Will Downing will not be stopped! Flexing on his international appeal, the lead single "What Part of My Love" shot to the top of the UK Soul Chart Top 30 and parked there. Those who no longer listen to new releases as the collective work it was intended to be should make an exception in this case. Although not a "concept" album, the pieces of Soul Rising fit together beautifully as a single statement and should be enjoyed as such. We all know about the smoothness, but there's a brand-new kind of...Dare I say..."Funkiness", that I think is here to stay! You (and your speakers, Headphones) etc….. will feel the difference right off the jump, with the lead-off cut, “Closer to Me”, when that bass and drum start hitting a little differently. The familiar writing and production tandem of Downing and guitarist Randy Bowland turns the heat up a bit from their usual formula. With keyboardist Mike Logan Sr. and background vocalist Ms. Monet rounding out the groove, I dare you not to move somethin'! House of Love, another Downing/Bowland collab, gives me "Maze" vibes, however unintended, but that's never a bad thing! To the extent that over the last 4 decades, these two surviving entities may have directly or indirectly influenced each other, I'll welcome that musical baby into the fold every time with open arms and ears. Make no mistake...Will Downing didn't forget the "smooth" that made the Man the Myth the Legend! Nor did he abandon his world-famous knack for what he affectionately calls "interpretations" of classic hits. He plucked an absolute diamond of a gem from arguably one of the finest early 70's albums, The Stylistics, Round Two, and their hauntingly enchanting, “You're As Right As Rain”! If you've ever "slow-dragged" with a blue light in the basement, you will be transported to afros, platforms, bell-bottoms, and Brut cologne...if you know you know, but I digress. In addition to assistance from long-time collaborator Ronnie Foster, Downing recruits the sweet trumpet of solo Artist and one-half of 90's duo Imprompt2, Johnny Brit t, to seal the vibe. Soul Rising then takes a solemn turn to the heart and very "Soul" of this release. Downing, maybe for his own well-being, had to stare his tragedy down squarely and turn art into therapy. “Till We Meet Again” serves as a father's sweet hand-off to God to care for his angel Siobhan, until they're joined again divinely as father and daughter in heavenly reward. An unimaginable undertaking for a parent attempting to channel pain into art. The song is introduced by the actual last New Year's Day voicemail exchanged by Downing and Siobhan, which contains no hint of the drama to unfold just 10 days later. Downing makes the song a true family affair, with daughter Aja and wife Audrey Wheeler Downing lending their supportive voices. A passionately moving, albeit gut-wrenching tribute, but well done. Given that dynamic, it's understandable that the final three tracks all lean into a theme of "Love". Starting with the aforementioned smash, “What Part of My Love”, but pivoting back to that new "funk" vibe with “Love You Right”, this time with Hubert Eaves IV joining the revival. An intentional sequence, I would think, to lift and restore the spirit of Soul Rising ! I think the final cut, “Love of A Lifetime”, as a message, speaks simultaneously of what we seek in both a personal relationship and the love of a father to a child. Maybe that wasn't the intent, but given the circumstances, I heard both. Love is love! Family…, Will Downing dug deep for this one. Even down to the Album cover, an original piece of artwork by Frank Morrison. Realize, recognize, and appreciate a real man, a real artist, and a real father with his Soul Rising !

Come meet thoughtful people, slow down for a moment, and leave feeling clearer, more grounded, and better ready to keep building ambitious things.

events.title: Tiffany Austin
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Joe Henderson Lab
events.description:
sings Carmen McRae’s Carmen Sings Monk

“One of the country’s best jazz singers” (KQED Arts), Bay Area-based vocalist Tiffany Austin honors Thelonious Monk’s birthday with her take on the legendary Carmen McRae’s iconic 1990 album saluting Monk and his timeless compositions.

An L.A. native, Austin spent five years in Japan as a singer before moving to the East Bay in 2009 to study at the UC Berkeley School of Law. During her studies, the pull of music was too strong to ignore, and she earned a full scholarship to the California Jazz Conservatory (formerly known as the JazzSchool), where she worked extensively with renowned Brazilian pianist Marcos Silva.

Recorded live for the Novus label at San Francisco’s Great American Music Hall in 1988, Carmen Sings Monk was one of the final albums McRae completed in her lifetime, receiving a GRAMMY nomination for the vocalist and featuring a stunning lineup of greats including longtime Monk saxophonist Charlie Rouse, saxophonist Clifford Jordan, pianist Larry Willis, bassist George Mraz, and drummer Al Foster. With titles changed due to copyright restrictions, the songs were adapted with lyrics by Jon Hendricks, Abbey Lincoln, Mike Ferro, and Sally Swisher, and have become the definitive versions of Monk’s compositions with vocals, particularly McRae’s luminescent takes on “Ruby, My Dear” (“Dear Ruby”), and “Rhythm-A-Ning" (“Listen to Monk”).

Personnel: Tiffany Austin vocals; Others TBA

events.title: Kurt Elling & The Yellowjackets
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
Modern jazz giants Kurt Elling and The Yellowjackets make their joint debut on the Miner Auditorium stage in tribute to the groundbreaking fusion of Joe Zawinul and Wayne Shorter’s Weather Report.

There is simply no artist in jazz having more fun than vocalist Kurt Elling. Over the past decade, the 17-time GRAMMY Award nominee (and two-time GRAMMY winner) has cut loose, following his quicksilver muse wherever it flows. Whether he’s reinventing pop and rock hits with guitar wizard Charlie Hunter, crooning standards with the New York Philharmonic and Germany’s WDR Big Band, or thriving in the volatile fray of the Branford Marsalis Quartet, Elling has been seizing any interesting opportunity to stretch his wings.

One of his latest flights is a project with The Yellowjackets featuring his lyrics for seminal Weather Report compositions by Shorter and Zawinul. A brilliant wordsmith, Elling introduced several of the pieces with the SFJAZZ Collective last year. With The Yellowjackets he soars into the universe of fusion’s definitive band, transforming beloved instrumental pieces into enthralling songs. It’s a powerhouse collaboration that captures the celestial explorations, deep funk, world rhythms, and extended forms that made Weather Report a creative juggernaut.

Personnel: Kurt Elling (vocals); Bob Mintzer (tenor and soprano saxophone, EWI); Russell Ferrante (keyboards); Dane Alderson (bass); Will Kennedy (drums)

events.title: Angela Johal: Intersecting Colour
events.location: Slate Contemporary Gallery, 5510 College Ave, Oakland
events.description: Join us at SLATE Contemporary Gallery on Saturday, October 10 from 4-6pm for an artist reception in celebration of our newest exhibition, “Angela Johal: Intersecting Colour.” This exhibition invites viewers to explore how hue and tone interact across vividly painted color fields. Johal approaches each painting as a puzzle to solve, seeking balance among dichotomous realms—physical and spiritual, light and dark, vivid and subdued—creating compositions that reveal how each color shifts, responds to, and is transformed by those around it. Steeped in color theory, Johal’s work is deeply informed by the human eye’s natural passage through dimension. This exhibition features abstracted geometric compositions that, when meditated on, transform into natural landscapes, animal-like forms, and shifting light.

events.description: $12 adv / $15 door Co-presented with Left Margin Lit and Vintage Berkeley Back by popular demand, with an all-new lineup! Sex and death are central human concerns, but older women poets often find themselves silenced or sidelined on the first of these subjects. Here, in an event curated by Rebecca Foust, five women aged 40 and better—Mahogany L. Browne, Prageeta Sharma, Jen Siraganian, Melissa Stein, and Barbara Jane Reyes—will share frankly erotic work that refuses to be muted or mooted and makes a bulwark of bodily sensuality against death, time, and our aging selves. Alongside the reading, emceed by poet Tracey Knapp, winemaker Emily Fernwood will be on site to introduce Osa Major wines, which will be available for purchase by the glass. events.description: King Lear by William Shakespeare Directed by Michael Socrates Moran Music composed by Paul Dresher Presented by Oakland Theater Project & New Performance Traditions In the twilight of his rule, a king sets out to divide the kingdom among his three daughters. But in mistaking flattery for love, Lear’s foolish choices usher in a new reign of domination, cruelty and collapse. As a self-styled “bastard” sets out to upend the ruling order, Lear must confront his own part in the kingdom’s downfall. Can he transform in time to reclaim what is sacred before the clown show becomes the new order? events.title: Tiffany Austin
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Joe Henderson Lab
events.description:
sings Carmen McRae’s Carmen Sings Monk

“One of the country’s best jazz singers” (KQED Arts), Bay Area-based vocalist Tiffany Austin honors Thelonious Monk’s birthday with her take on the legendary Carmen McRae’s iconic 1990 album saluting Monk and his timeless compositions.

An L.A. native, Austin spent five years in Japan as a singer before moving to the East Bay in 2009 to study at the UC Berkeley School of Law. During her studies, the pull of music was too strong to ignore, and she earned a full scholarship to the California Jazz Conservatory (formerly known as the JazzSchool), where she worked extensively with renowned Brazilian pianist Marcos Silva.

Recorded live for the Novus label at San Francisco’s Great American Music Hall in 1988, Carmen Sings Monk was one of the final albums McRae completed in her lifetime, receiving a GRAMMY nomination for the vocalist and featuring a stunning lineup of greats including longtime Monk saxophonist Charlie Rouse, saxophonist Clifford Jordan, pianist Larry Willis, bassist George Mraz, and drummer Al Foster. With titles changed due to copyright restrictions, the songs were adapted with lyrics by Jon Hendricks, Abbey Lincoln, Mike Ferro, and Sally Swisher, and have become the definitive versions of Monk’s compositions with vocals, particularly McRae’s luminescent takes on “Ruby, My Dear” (“Dear Ruby”), and “Rhythm-A-Ning" (“Listen to Monk”).

Personnel: Tiffany Austin vocals; Others TBA

events.title: Kurt Elling & The Yellowjackets
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
Modern jazz giants Kurt Elling and The Yellowjackets make their joint debut on the Miner Auditorium stage in tribute to the groundbreaking fusion of Joe Zawinul and Wayne Shorter’s Weather Report.

There is simply no artist in jazz having more fun than vocalist Kurt Elling. Over the past decade, the 17-time GRAMMY Award nominee (and two-time GRAMMY winner) has cut loose, following his quicksilver muse wherever it flows. Whether he’s reinventing pop and rock hits with guitar wizard Charlie Hunter, crooning standards with the New York Philharmonic and Germany’s WDR Big Band, or thriving in the volatile fray of the Branford Marsalis Quartet, Elling has been seizing any interesting opportunity to stretch his wings.

One of his latest flights is a project with The Yellowjackets featuring his lyrics for seminal Weather Report compositions by Shorter and Zawinul. A brilliant wordsmith, Elling introduced several of the pieces with the SFJAZZ Collective last year. With The Yellowjackets he soars into the universe of fusion’s definitive band, transforming beloved instrumental pieces into enthralling songs. It’s a powerhouse collaboration that captures the celestial explorations, deep funk, world rhythms, and extended forms that made Weather Report a creative juggernaut.

Personnel: Kurt Elling (vocals); Bob Mintzer (tenor and soprano saxophone, EWI); Russell Ferrante (keyboards); Dane Alderson (bass); Will Kennedy (drums)

events.title: Artist Talk – Patricia Guthrie: Get Up Stand Up
events.location: Mercury 20 Gallery, 475 25th Street, Oakland
events.description: One purpose of art is to support and communicate political messages. Using color, letters, and shapes, Patricia Guthrie’s abstract quilts deliver political messages relating to the government, international relationships, and global warming. She creates artwork using cotton fabric, wool batting, dyes, and machine stitching. Bio: After retiring as a professor and department chair of Human Development and Women’s Studies at California State University East Bay, Patricia Guthrie decided to actively engage in the visual arts. She began taking community-based art classes: drawing, photography, quilt making, and printing on fabric. Quilt making and all its aspects has become her passion. Guthrie hopes her quilts encourage viewers to move beyond art that is merely pleasing to the eye to seek a deeper meaning. Her work has been shown nationally and internationally including Schweinfurth Memorial, Art Center, Auburn, New York; International Quilt Museum, Lincoln, Nebraska; Philadelphia Museum of Art, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania; and Tuch + Technik Museum, Neumunster, Germany. This is Guthrie’s second solo show at Mercury 20 Gallery. Gallery Hours: Friday and Saturday, 12 – 5 pm (and by appointment) Opening Reception: Saturday, September 12, 3 – 5 pm ﻿Oakland Art Murmur / First Friday: October 2, 5 – 9 pm

events.title: Angelica Page - Bountiful: Growing Up with Geraldine Page
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: An intimate examination of Oscar Award-winning film and stage actress Geraldine Page, written with compassion and honesty by her only daughter, Angelica Page. Bountiful: Growing up with Geraldine Page is the first book about legendary screen and stage actress Geraldine Page, presenting a one-of-a-kind look at her body of work and private life. Includes insider stories of her stage and film career (nominated for four Tony Awards and eight Academy Awards, Oscar winner for The Trip to Bountiful ), her relationships with other renowned actors including her husband and Angelica’s father Rip Torn, Actors Studio founder Lee Strasberg, and her interactions with other legends including James Dean, John Wayne, Jackie Kennedy, and many more. Angelica Page, daughter of Geraldine and Rip Torn, skillfully weaves in stories of her own coming of age: being mesmerized by her mother’s stage performances as a child and a rebellious young adult; learning to swim in Grace Slick’s guitar-shaped pool; enduring a chaotic home life, immersing herself in the 1970s and 80s NYC underground of CBGBs, Max’s Kansas City, and the Mudd Club. This is as much a theatrical history lesson as a first-person survival guide to life in the fast lane. A love song sung by the daughter of a remarkable artist who should not be forgotten any time soon. Includes more than 40 rare photos from family archives. “A definitive memoir by a brilliant actress about a truly beloved American actress, mother and hero.” —Elizabeth Ashley, actor “Supercharged with boundless talent, emotion and at times unrequited love, Angelica Page’s portrait of the great Geraldine is one for the ages.” —Sandra Bernhard, actress “Be warned, this book is dangerous; it can make you regret never having lived through the thrilling, dangerous times Geraldine Page lived in and partly created. In these trying times, she is an important reminder of the potential of the individual, in art and in life.” —F. Murray Abraham, actor Angelica Page is an American actress, director, producer, and writer and the only daughter of legendary actors Rip Torn and Geraldine Page. She has appeared frequently onstage on- and off-Broadway, earning an Outer Critic’s Circle nomination for best Solo Performance, the Helen Hayes Award for Best Actress, and the New York People’s Choice Award for Best Supporting Actress. She is the creator of the critically acclaimed one-woman show Turning Page on which Bountiful is based. When not touring the US, she lives in Mexico. Angelica Page - photo courtesy of the publicist Event details: This event will be hosted by Book Passage at our Corte Madera store. Free Admission / Open Seating There will be a signing line or meet and greet following the presentation.

events.title: Heather Hardcastle - The Flour Craft Bakery & Cafe Cookbook
events.location: Ferry Building Foodwise Classroom San Francisco, CA 94111
events.description: Meet & Greet Book Signing Only • SF Ferry Plaza Market 11:00 AM PT Food Demo // 11:30 AM PT Book Signing Please join us for a special meet and greet signing event with Heather Hardcastle, following her Foodwise demo at the Ferry Plaza Farmers Market. Gluten free as it should be--fresh, simple, and for the whole family,--The Flour Craft Bakery & Cafe Cookbook includes seventy-five impeccable, seasonal recipes for every time of day. The Flour Craft Bakery & Cafe Cookbook empowers readers with simple and approachable recipes for mouthwatering cakes and cookies, pastry and savory bakes, everyday treats and holiday centerpieces, plus fresh salads and soups--all naturally gluten free. 75+ recipes cover breakfast, brunch, lunch, teatime, and dessert, from coffee cakes to focaccia, scones to tartines. Heather Hardcastle combines alternative flours including rice, millet, nut flours, and starches to achieve a perfect crumb and oven-fresh texture. Flour Craft breaks down the process in an approachable way, teaching readers how to combine a few key flours in the correct proportions to yield excellent results every time. The cornerstones of the book are the "Master Recipes," classics of baking to be practiced and adapted. The full Flour Craft experience is brought to life for the reader with a glossary of ingredients and terms curated to build confidence for bakers of all skill levels. “We can finally enjoy renowned Flour Craft Bakery & Cafe’s recipes at home. This beautiful book is full of breads, cakes, and pastries I cannot wait to make, not only for those who eat gluten-free but for everyone else too.” —Aran Goyoaga, author of Cannelle et Vanille "I’ve savored many gluten-free focaccia slices, sourdough waffles, and sweet treats at Flour Craft Bakery & Café over the years. I’m thrilled that I can finally make every recipe in my own kitchen! Heather reveals her baking secrets in this gorgeous book furnished with luscious photographs and recipes that everyone will love—whether they eat gluten-free or not." —Alanna Taylor-Tobin, author of Alternative Baker "Heather's passion for fresh, uncompromisingly delicious cooking and baking has made her gluten-free bakery and cafe a favorite among Northern California food lovers. This book brings the magic home, allowing even beginner cooks to recreate the wonderful flavors of Flour Craft in their own kitchens." —Erika Lenkert, Editor-in-Chief, GFF Magazine "For those who are searching for gluten-free dessert recipes on a regular basis, Flour Craft's cookbook is a treasure trove of information." —SAN FRANCISCO CHRONICLE Heather Hardcastle understood where gourmet GF was headed before everyone else. In the early 2000s, diagnosed with gluten intolerance, and passionate about food and cooking, Hardcastle left her well-established career and enrolled at the Culinary Institute of America, determined to learn the nuances of great pastry and solid classical technique. Her dream was always to turn her passion and knowledge into a thriving business, creating delicious, high-quality gluten-free baked goods. In 2013, she opened the first Flour Craft Bakery. events.title: April Snow, LMFT - Big Feelings, Big Joy
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: “My purpose in writing this book is not only to teach you what high sensitivity is—because it’s so much more than what people assume—but also to show you that, contrary to what you may have thought, this trait can be an immense gift. It’s not just big messy emotions, getting lost in your head, or being flooded with anxiety. Highly sensitive people are the emotional leaders, healers, problem solvers, and changemakers of the world.” — Excerpted from BIG FEELINGS, BIG JOY by April Snow, LMFT In BIG FEELINGS, BIG JOY: The Essential Practices to Reclaim Your Strengths as a Highly Sensitive Person , licensed psychotherapist and sensitivity expert April Snow delivers a practical and empowering toolkit for Highly Sensitive People (HSPs) to embrace their sensitivity and chart their own path to joy. Drawing from her clinical experience with thousands of HSPs and her own life as a highly sensitive person, Snow makes it clear that sensitivity is a core part of who you are—something to value and nurture, not change. Through simple language and relatable stories, this book offers a three-part framework rooted in self-acceptance and honors sensitivity as a gift that can bring meaning, creativity, and a deep sense of connection. In BIG FEELINGS, BIG JOY , readers discover key practices and insights to help them understand their needs, manage overstimulation, and embrace their sensitive nature with confidence: Honor your sleep and downtime: Learn why HSPs need more rest than most and discover simple changes to your daily routines and environment for optimal restoration. Tend to your nervous system: Practice easy strategies to manage overstimulation, navigate emotional lows, and regain a sense of calm and clarity. Set boundaries with compassion: Gain tools for advocating for your needs in relationships, work, and daily interactions—so you can protect your energy without guilt. Embrace sensitivity as your strength: Experience how sensitivity can fuel creativity, intuition, deep empathy, and meaningful connections. With this book, April Snow encourages readers to confidently honor their needs, celebrate their sensitivity, and build a life that reflects their true selves—full of joy, balance, and deeper connection. "A warm and wise book that offers a fresh take on sensitivity and what it means to navigate the world as a highly sensitive person. Grounded, practical, and deeply validating, it will resonate with anyone who has ever felt they experience life more intensely than those around them." - Tom Falkenstein, psychotherapist and author of The Highly Sensitive Man " Big Feelings, Big Joy is a must-read for any highly sensitive person who is tired of being told to "grow a thicker skin." Snow gives you practical tools to honor your nervous system and step into sensitivity as the superpower it can be. With the book's blend of wisdom and warmth, I know it's one I'll be recommending for years to come." - Melody Wilding, LMSW, author of Trust Yourself: Stop Overthinking and Channel Your Emotions for Success at Work " Big Feelings, Big Joy is a must-read for HSPs ready to reclaim the gifts of being sensitive. As an HSP myself, life can feel like a lot, and I’ve often wished I could turn my sensitivity off. This book is a refreshing reminder of the ways sensitivity can enrich our lives, especially when it’s understood and supported. April gets it—she brings both personal and professional experience together in a way that feels validating and hopeful, with practical strategies readers can actually use to thrive." - Sharon Martin, DSW, LCSW, author of The CBT Workbook for Perfectionism and The Better Boundaries Workbook April Snow, LMFT, is a licensed psychotherapist, author, and consultant. She specializes in working with highly sensitive people to help calm the storm of overload, guilt, and self-doubt to allow their innate sensitive strengths to shine through. Deeply committed to changing the narrative of what it means to be highly sensitive, April supports HSPs around the world through her Sensitive Circles community, Sensitive Sessions workshops, and Sensitive Stories podcast. In addition to Big Feelings, Big Joy she has written Find Your Strength: A Workbook for the Highly Sensitive Person. April holds a Master’s Degree in Integral Counseling Psychology and is a Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist in California where she lives with her wife. In her free time she enjoys being at the beach, curled up in bed, on her yoga mat, spending quality time with her nieces and nephews, or seeing live music. events.description: Please join us for a reading by Laurie McAndish King from her new book, Wild Thing, I Think I Love You! This event is organized by the Left Coast Writers and hosted by Book Passage. Wild Thing, I Think I Love You! is a journey into the complicated, surprising, and often intimate connections between humans and wild animals. From close encounters in the field to quieter moments of recognition, these essays explore what draws us to the wild—and what happens when habitat recedes. Hunt for renegade she-lizards in the Chiricahua Wilderness Learn about the “Dogs Saving Cats” program to help save cheetahs Track Namibia’s rare black rhino—and learn why “dehorning” backfired By turns curious, funny, and deeply felt, Wild Thing, I Think I Love You! explores connection, responsibility, and the enduring allure of the wild. "Whether she's describing a thrilling adventure with massive beasts of the jungle or experiencing a moment of awe in a butterfly sanctuary, the work is captivating ... entertaining ... Engaging and packed with countless intriguing factoids about the natural world." -Kirkus Reviews (Recommended review) "Our Verdict: GET IT" "The Bald Eagles of Klamath Basin have been called the greatest gathering of eagles outside of Alaska. And King has done the hard work for you-rousing before dawn, wearing five layers of insulation to fend off the icy air ... The best thing about King's essays is that you already know Laurie. She is your pal, your sister, your shadow-person who does the adventure with you and then says just the thing you wish you'd said." -Allen Fish, Director, Golden Gate Raptor Obvservatory "King's powerful piece on saving wild elephants is a moment you should not miss-even if it hurts." -Natalie Lefevre, Editor, Ethical Traveler Laurie McAndish King is an award-winning writer whose subjects include a one-legged toucan, an elephant orphanage, the alleged medicinal qualities of rhino horn, and the basics of eagle sex. King’s essays and photography have appeared in Smithsonian magazine, the Washington Post , the San Francisco Chronicle Magazine , Travelers’ Tales’ The Best Women’s Travel Writing , Lonely Planet’s The Kindness of Strangers , and other magazines and literary anthologies. King’s three books of travel stories—insightful, poignant and often quite funny—are celebrated for the way they inspire and entertain readers. Her latest book, Wild Thing, I Think I Love You: Curious Encounters with Wildlife around the World , is due out in September, 2026. events.title: Artist Talks: Present Figures – Curated by Laura Malone
events.location: Mercury 20 Gallery, 475 25th Street, Oakland
events.description: Laura Malone, Carnivale, Oil on Linen, 60” x 48”, 2021, Photo courtesy of the artist Present Figures brings together five California painters whose works exist within the figurative language of portraiture, simultaneously expanding and disrupting it. Centered around themes of intimacy, boundaries, and embodied emotion, each artist takes an individual approach to media, scale, and the capacity of the human form to be both a site of identity and a vessel of metaphor. Engaging in profound considerations of what it is to be human—our physicality, sense of self, relationships, consciousness, and creativity, these artists invite us to engage with these shifting, eternal questions and reflect on our own experiences—be they practical, peaceful, disturbing, humorous, fragmented, spiritual, or otherworldly. As individuals, choices that begin with who and what to portray later manifest in stylistic and material communiquès that boldly and poetically reveal themselves to the world. Collectively, the psychologically charged spectrum of the group reminds us of the myriad ways our sentience can be narrated. Like Anais Nin said, “We don’t see things as they are, we see them as we are.” Bio: With Present Figures, Laura Malone expands her practice to curation. Malone invited four artists to show alongside her, chosen for their unique and diverse approaches to representing the figure: two Southern California artists — Cindy Craig and Shannon Rae Fincke — and two from the Bay Area — Nina Katz and Heidi Brueckner. Collectively their work has been shown across the globe in Europe, Asia, and the United States. Malone’s artwork was featured in The Crocker Kingsley National Art Competition and included in “Disrupted Realism,” juried by John Seed, who wrote the book of the same name. Malone currently resides in Oakland, CA and has been a member of Mercury 20 since 2023. Gallery Hours: Friday and Saturday, 12 – 5 pm (and by appointment) Opening Reception: Saturday, September 12, 3 – 5 pm ﻿Oakland Art Murmur / First Friday: October 2, 5 – 9 pm

events.title: Artist Talk – Tara Esperanza: Close to Home
events.location: Mercury 20 Gallery, 475 25th Street, Oakland
events.description: Tara Esperanza, Guardians, 2026, acrylic-on-panel, 20” x 16”, Photo courtesy of the artist Whether painted in California or Oaxaca, the works in Close to Home begin with the same impulse: to slow down and look closely. Working on a more intimate scale than in her previous work, Tara Esperanza found herself drawn to quiet moments of observation, where familiar plants reveal unexpected beauty through color, form, and light. Created between two places that have become part of her life, these paintings are less about geography than about attention. Though rooted in different landscapes, each painting is shaped by the same curiosity and sense of wonder inspired by the resilience and sculptural elegance of plants. For many years, succulents have been Esperanza’s way of exploring themes of adaptation, diversity, and endurance. Through this body of work, the smaller scale invites viewers to slow down, look closely, and discover that what is closest to us often has the most to reveal. Bio: Tara Esperanza resides in Oakland, California, where succulents thrive year-round. When she is not painting, she enjoys running and capturing images that later inspire her work. Esperanza earned a BFA in Painting, graduating cum laude from the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, and studied plein air painting in Brittany, France. A representational painter inspired by nature, she has dedicated years to portraying the remarkable beauty and diversity of succulents. She has been a member of Mercury 20 Gallery in Oakland, CA, since 2020. Her work has been shown at the Women’s United Art Movement Virtual Gallery, as well as numerous group exhibitions. In 2025, Esperanza received Best of Show at the Annual National Juried Painting Exhibition at Emerald Springs Art Center in Oregon. Her paintings have been featured in Create! Magazine, New Visionary Magazine, and other publications, and are held in private collections throughout the United States. events.title: Paul Sussman's DID SHE REALLY SAY TANTRUM YOGA
events.location: San Francisco
events.description: Opening Reception September 26 (Please do not bring infants to the show) The world is reeling towards chaos! Wars! Fires! Corruption! The Death of Democracy! It’s an all-out Emergency!!! THIS TIME IS DIFFERENT! This isn’t just a blurb – ask around. It’s time to get out of denial, stare down the grim reality, and… party ? There’s nothing like an encounter with a mysterious stranger at a party: take a risk, lay yourself bare, and – just maybe – find a tiny bit of hope and laughter amidst the chaos. And so many questions along the way! Starting with something safe… “Can we just not… like… talk about Fascism?” “Is the right to eat beef really in the 2nd Amendment? “ If you make it past the chit chat, the questions go deeper: “Maybe it’s time to drop the whole notion of Reality?” “Is it already too late?” And eventually… “Why the two of us, right here, right now?” “What’s next?” Paul Sussman’s latest creation tosses us into the center of the swirl, and offers us lifelines to laugh, to cry, to hope, and to act. “One of the most authentic presentations of humanity I’ve ever seen” “Paul has entered some other zone… of deep thoughtfulness and connection.” ” I laughed, I cried, and I left carrying so much to think about. The way you wove together themes of grief, anger, and how we’re all navigating this moment in time was powerful and deeply resonant.” “You have outdone yourself in this medium –your depth and candor, scope from the personal to the epochal, agile shifting from gentle or scathing satire to the existentially terrifying. I am stunned into silence pondering the implications you invite audiences to consider for this moment.” “You avoid easy answers and platitudes. The threats and the stakes in play have an urgency and brutality that you confront head on, with humility and honesty.” “I loved, loved, loved, your show. Such courageous saying out loud all the things we think, and in such a funny way. Thank you” “This show was so great — so of the moment, so hilarious and at moments horrific at once. Bravo!” Paul Sussman has written and performed a series of solo pieces through the eyes of Neanderthals, road-ragers, insects, Anabaptists, cannibals, and others who persist in the search for meaning. He’s entertained and provoked in theater festivals from Fundy to Fresno. Paul developed his unique approach to melodrama and farce through decades of work in financial management with Bay Area nonprofit organizations. “Did She Really Say Tantrum Yoga ?” is his third full-length solo show (following “The Wrong Kind of Pessimism” and “Beyond Belief”), entitling him to refer to himself in the third person. Sussman has worked for over 40 years to champion affordable housing development in San Francisco and received the Catherine A. Baur Lifetime Achievement Award from the Non-Profit Housing Association of Northern California in 2017. David Ford (director) has been collaborating on new and unusual theater for three decades and has been an artist-in-residence at The Marsh for most of that time. events.description:
The National Book Award finalist and New York Times bestselling author of Pachinko returns with a breathtaking contemporary epic

Co-presented with Kearny Street Workshop

Once comfortably middle class in Korea, John and Helen Koh and their three children—Bo, DH, and Mido—find their lives upended, first by a shocking betrayal by John’s oldest friend, then by the 1997 Asian financial crisis. Desperately striving to regain their footing, they leave Seoul for Sydney and eventually settle in Southern California—where new vistas of opportunity open up for the children as their parents, strangers in a strange land, must adjust to a new life in which their experience and education mean little.

In American Hagwon, Min Jin Lee has crafted an unforgettable, panoramic novel where the smallest of gestures can have enormous repercussions, where the bonds of family and of memory twist and fray but rarely break, and where willful self-sacrifice—for the benefit of loved ones and even strangers—is a kind of prayer. In conversation with Andrew Sean Greer. Doors at 6:00pm. $15 gen adm / $45 with signed book

events.title: Queen Budapest
events.location: Balboa Theatre, 3630 Balboa St, San Francisco, CA 94121
events.description: On July 27, 1986, Queen performed the largest-ever stadium concert at the Népstadion in Budapest in front of 80,000 ecstatic fans. The concert was part of the famed Magic Tour, which was the last time the band toured with lead singer Freddie Mercury. Now, this original concert film has been beautifully rescanned and remastered in 4K alongside a dynamic new audio mix, featuring many of Queen's favorite tracks— "Bohemian Rhapsody,” "Crazy Little Thing Called Love," "I Want To Break Free” and "We Are The Champions." With three years to go before the fall of the Berlin Wall, this was the first Western rock concert performed in a stadium behind the then Iron Curtain. It was of such significance to the Hungarian authorities and film industry that a group of the country’s top film cameramen and technicians were brought together to film it for posterity. Be transported to San Francisco’s Fillmore District—beginning in the present day, where the echoes of a once-thriving Black neighborhood still shape the streets. From there, Every Saturday Night pulls audiences back into the 1950s, the vibrant “Harlem of the West,” when the Fillmore pulsed with jazz, community, and possibility.

events.title: RISING - Susan Edsall's Buen Camino
events.location: San Francisco
events.description: Susan has a perfect life, a perfect love, and perfect happiness. When she suddenly undergoes an unexpected loss, her perfect life ends. Consumed by excruciating pain, she finds it impossible to imagine any future worth living. Until, on an ordinary trip to the grocery store, she hears The Voice. The trouble is, Susan doesn’t believe in Voices. And yet, when The Voice tells her to walk the Camino de Santiago in Spain, she obeys despite knowing nothing about this ancient pilgrimage. With only her pack and her pain, Susan begins a journey through unrelenting rain and temperatures that rarely get above 50 degrees. With the help of some improbable Spiritual Guides, a little bit of magic, and the Camino itself, Susan must face her past to have any hope of creating her future. Alone on stage, she becomes 23 characters to take the audience on her solitary walk through 540 miles of rain, resentment, and redemption. Buen Camino is a moving story about grief leading to surrender, and ultimately to freedom. A published writer, performer, and career consultant, Susan Edsall grew up in Montana and now lives in Kailua Kona, Hawaii. Author of the forthcoming novel Bitterroot , she has also written two memoirs, Into the Blue: A Father’s Flight and a Daughter’s Return and Saved . She premiered Buen Camino at the SOLO STARS Series in Los Angeles in December 2024, winning their Encore Award. Susan brought the show to United Solo on 42nd Street in New York City in March 2025 and the Hollywood Fringe Festival in June 2025. Buen Camino enjoyed a full run with Gilded Balloon at the 2025 Edinburgh Festival Fringe. She also performed at the Philadelphia Fringe and in several theaters in Vermont. events.title: Goldenvoice Presents USA & Canada Tour 2026 Palace with Rollo Doherty
events.location: The Warfield, 982 Market St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description:
PALACE ARE BACK WITH “KID” AND MASSIVE TOUR OF USA + CANADA

Palace have been making music together for over a decade. What started out as carefree jam sessions between Leo Wyndham, Rupert Turner and Matt Hodges in an airless studio in North London has burgeoned into a project that has amassed a global audience more akin to a community than a fanbase.

Their early EPs - Lost In The Night (2014) and Chase The Light (2015) - were recorded in the band’s beloved aforementioned studio, The Arch, and established a DIY ethos that remains intrinsic to the spirit of the band to this day. Four albums followed; So Long Forever (2016), Life After (2019), Shoals (2022) and Ultrasound (2024): each one a musical exploration of a particular feeling in a particular place during a particular time; ranging from grief and the loss of a relationship to the emergence of new love and light. Consequently, it's not easy to sonically classify Palace. Their sound varies from the atmospheric and ethereal to the more grounded notes of Blues and Americana, yet in every song there is still something remarkably identifiable as Palace: an ineffability to the feelings conjured up by the music. In a word, transcendent. Perhaps it is this feeling of transcendence which resonates so deeply with their supporters; loyal fans who, by the time Palace had made their Coachella debut in 2024, welcomed them home to a sold-out show at London’s Hammersmith Apollo.

In early 2025, Palace took a career leap that harkens back to their DIY origin. They released the Greyhound EP on their own label, Palace Presents - a collective they'd started in 2016 as a monthly night at The George Tavern in East London, which had quietly grown into something more intentional. A positive and protected space as Leo described it, away from the usual constraints of the music industry. The EP followed a sold-out run across the USA and Canada to growing crowds of dedicated fans.

Kid was released in April 2026, together with the announcement of a 30 date tour of the USA and Canada in the Fall of 2026, culminating in a show at the Greek Theatre in Los Angeles. “Kid is about longing for a child an ocean away. It’s the ache we feel for our people when we’re separated from them. It doesn’t feel like a sadness or heaviness, but more an affirmation of that love, a primal release sung into the sunset as the road flies by."

The journey from an airless studio in North London to the Greek Theatre in Los Angeles is a long one, and by doing things their way, Palace have managed to arrive still recognisably, unmistakably themselves

events.title: Marcus Shelby New Orchestra
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
To celebrate Thelonious Monk’s birthday — an SFJAZZ tradition — Marcus Shelby and his New Orchestra honor the large ensemble work of the iconoclasic jazz legend with special guests including pianist Cyrus Chestnut, saxophonist Sarah Hanahan, and vibraphonist Warren Wolf.

Bassist, composer, arranger, educator and bandleader Marcus Shelby is a figure synonymous with Bay Area jazz and the spirit of collaboration. A recipient of the Charles Mingus Scholarship, Shelby attended Cal Arts and studied with Charlie Haden and James Newton while working simultaneously with the all-star jazz ensemble Black/Note, who released a series of highly regarded albums in the 1990s. Since moving to the Bay Area, he has led a highly regarded jazz orchestra and numerous small groups, with large-scale commissions focused on the history, present, and future of the African-American experience.

On what would have been Monk’s 109th birthday, Shelby and his band evoke the spirit of the pianist’s 1959 classic The Thelonious Monk Orchestra at Town Hall and 1964’s Big Band and Quartet in Concert. Piano great and Monk disciple Cyrus Chestnut sits center stage, joined by Sarah Hanahan — a major new voice on saxophone — along with the SFJAZZ Collective’s Warren Wolf, who has a deep connection to Monk’s singular songbook.

events.title: The Commons Public Hours ☕
events.location: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco + Full Space
events.description:
🎉 Public Hours at the Commons 🎉
Every Sunday, the Commons opens to the public — no membership required. Come co-work, connect, create, or just explore the space at your own pace. ✨
🕘 When: Every Sunday, 9 AM – 10 PM
📍 Where: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco (corner of Hayes & Laguna, basement level)
RSVP and we'll email you your entry code ahead of time — so you can let yourself straight in when you arrive.
──────────────────────────────
🧭 A self-guided day
Public Hours are self-guided — come in, settle in, and make the space your own. Weekends are usually unstaffed, so there's no check-in desk or guided tour. Our members are glad to answer questions about the space; for anything else — including guided tours, which we don't offer as drop-ins — email hello@thesfcommons.com ahead of time.
──────────────────────────────
🔭 Getting in
Your entry code comes by email. Once you RSVP, we'll send you a personal QR code — that's your key for the day. Keep it handy on your phone (and check spam if you don't see it).
Find us. We're at 540 Laguna St, on the corner of Hayes & Laguna. Head down the stairs beside Earthbody to the basement level — that's the Commons.
Scan your QR code at the reader to unlock the door. Hold your phone just below the Kisi reader by the door and it'll let you in.
Your access stays active all day, 9 AM – 10 PM, so you can come and go freely.
Can't find your code on the day? No problem — scan the QR posted on the door to check in and get a fresh one on the spot.
We're shoes-off 🧦 — please clean up after yourself, including dirty dishes and mugs, and use only the front entrance. Trouble getting in? Email hello@thesfcommons.com.




The Commons is a modern-day town square for communal meaning-making, personal discovery, and self-expression in the heart of San Francisco. Apply to become a member here__.

She has Inside Weather of her own. And with Fluff beside her, she learns to find her way back to just right. A warm, hand-painted picture book for children ages 4–10, Hazel and Fluff gently introduces breath, stillness, and self-regulation through the magic of clouds, color, and one unforgettable friendship. Because every child deserves to know — the sun is always there. Even behind the clouds. About the Author Cheryl is an artist, author, and passionate believer in every child. For over twenty-five years she has worked alongside children who learn and feel differently. She lives and works in the San Francisco Bay Area, where she paints landscapes and skies, and spends her days helping extraordinary children discover who they are meant to become.
