events.title: Jean-Baptiste Phou: Coming Out of My Skin
events.location: Telegraph Hill Books, 1501 Grant Ave, San Francisco
events.description: FREE, $10-$15 suggested donation Part of Words Around the World Sponsored by Center for the Art of Translation Co-presented with Villa Albertine Having grown up as a Cambodian immigrant in France, Jean-Baptiste Phou has long explored the challenges and contradictions of the Asian diaspora experience throughout his artistic career. However, up until now, he’s always been careful not to raise issues of sexuality—in particular, his homosexuality. In his recent memoir, Coming Out of My Skin, the artist shifts his focus to examining the role his ethnic origin has played in the construction of his sexual identity and his romantic relationships in a predominantly white environment. An astute observer of the various ways in which his body has been perceived, Phou asks: how does a marginalized person develop emotionally and build, reclaim, and express their sexuality? How does this inform the experience of a queer Asian person navigating predominantly white cultural spaces? In conversation with César Cadabes, Artistic Director for the GLBTQ Asian Pacific Alliance (GAPA) Theatre. Doors at 6:30pm

events.title: Lalo Guerrero Listening Party and Platica with Jesse "Chuy" Varela
events.location: Medicine for Nightmares, 3036 24th St, San Francisco, CA 94110
events.description: Join us tonight for a listening party and platica celebrating the music of foundational Mexican American singer/songwriter Lalo Guerrero hosted by the Bay’s favorite DJ Jesse “Chuy” Varela! Chuy will be playing us some of his favorite Lalo rolitas for us, as well as discussing the importance of Lalo’s legacy in the Latine musical cannon. Jesse ‘Chuy’ Varela serves as Program and Music Director at KCSM JAZZ 91, the Bay Area’s Jazz radio station. 2025 marks Chuy’s 42nd anniversary in radio. He has worked at KBBF – Santa Rosa, KPFA – Pacifica Radio in Berkeley, KJAZ Radio in Alameda, KBRG – Spanish Language Radio - San Jose, and KCSM JAZZ 91 , as well as a news reporter/stringer for National Public Radio, Latino USA, Radio Bilingüe , and other radio entities. He has served as a consultant for the Smithsonian Institute in Washington DC, Oakland Museum of California, The DeYoung Museum in San Francisco, Grammy Museum in Los Angeles, SFJAZZ, and numerous other organizations. Varela is also a freelance journalist who has written for the San Francisco Chronicle, The Eastbay Express, Latin Beat Magazine, Jazz Times Magazine, El Tecolote Newspaper, and numerous other publications as well as writing liner notes for Verve Records, Concord Records, Arhoolie Records, High Tone Records , and other numerous indie labels. Varela has lectured and taught at UC Berkeley, UC Santa Cruz, Stanford University, City College of San Francisco, The International Association of Jazz Educators Conference, The University of the Sagrado Corazon in Puerto Rico, Habana Jazz Festival, The Kiwanis Club of Oakland , and numerous other schools and organizations. He also serves on the board of directors of The Oaktown Jazz Workshop, a jazz education program for young people in Oakland, as well as a mentor for The Berkeley High School Jazz Band Honors Project. Currently Jesse ‘Chuy;’ Varela hosts The Latin Jazz Show on Sundays from 2pm-6pm and Jazz In The Afternoon Mon.-Weds, 2pm-6pm. In May 2024, Jesse ‘Chuy” Varela celebrated 40 years hosting The Latin Jazz Show, which he began hosting at KJAZ in 1984. This event is part of the Lalo Guerrero Legacy Festival happening at the Freight & Salvage on November 6th & 7th.

events.title: Picturing the Past: Graphic Novelists on History and Memory
events.location: Mrs. Dalloway's, 2904 College Ave, Berkeley CA 94705
events.description: FREE, $10-$15 suggested donation Sponsored by Berkeleyside Through memoir, history, fiction, or a combination, these four talented creators use cartoons to give readers a vivid glimpse into the past. Frederick Noland shares the epic story of Major Taylor, the “world’s fastest man,” a global cycling sensation despite the incessant racism the Black athlete encountered. In Armaveni, Nadine Takvorian draws on her own family history to relate the heartbreaking history of the Armenian genocide. Emil Wilson’s The Nightingales blends fact and fiction in a personal story of the 1980s AIDS crisis. And Maria van Lieshout’s graphic novel Song of a Blackbird pairs the stories of two Dutch teens, one contemporary and one bearing witness to Nazi atrocities. Brief visual presentations will be followed by a conversation led by graphic memoirist Briana Loewinsohn. Doors at 6:30pm.

events.title: Nathaniel Philbrick's The Rush: California Gold, the Civil War, and the Making of the Modern World
events.location: Bookshop West Portal 80 West Portal Ave San Francisco, CA 94127
events.description: Bookshop West Portal will be welcoming Pulitzer Prize finalist and National Book Award winner Nathaniel Philbrick , author of In the Heart of the Sea, Why Read Moby-Dick, and Mayflower . Philbrick will discuss his new book, The Rush: California Gold, the Civil War, and the Making of the Modern World , a thrilling and detailed deep dive into a remarkably formative time in California's and our country's history. Paced like a novel and from a myriad of perspectives, you won't be able to put this one down! Lee Bruno , local historian, journalist, and author of Misfits, Merchants, and Mayhem: Tales from San Francisco’s Historic Waterfront, 1849–1934, will be in conversation with Philbrick. About the Book: National Book Award winner and Pulitzer Prize finalist Nathaniel Philbrick, author of In the Heart of the Sea and Mayflower , reveals how California's Gold Rush forged the modern United States--and lit the long fuse to civil war In January 1848, a carpenter spotted flecks of gold in a shallow stream at Sutter's Mill in California--triggering the greatest voluntary migration in U.S. history and jolting a fragile republic already sliding toward crisis. In The Rush , Nathaniel Philbrick transforms the Gold Rush from a tale of sudden riches into the origin story of America's modern contradictions: capital consolidated at dizzying speed, democracy in thrall to private power, xenophobia weaponized in the name of liberty--and a stubborn belief in the American experiment that refuses to die. This is the story of a nation tearing at the seams--a republic tested by its own ideals. From the feverish gold-mining camps of the Sierra Nevada mountains to the wharves and vigilance committees of San Francisco, Philbrick renders a combustible, all-world society: Chilean brothers reinventing themselves to outrun prejudice; Native communities navigating dispossession and violence; the merchant-showman Samuel Brannan, drawn into the center of early vigilantism; and the politicians vying for control of California's future--the ambitious free-soil political boss David Broderick, who squared off against William Gwin, the Southern power broker intent on tilting the state toward slavery and the Confederacy. Not until a year after the outbreak of the Civil War, when President Lincoln signed legislation that would unite the nation east to west by building a transcontinental railroad, was California's loyalty secured. Philbrick follows the gold as it moves from riverbed to countinghouse to the halls of power, revealing how vigilantism hardened into law and how debates over slavery in the West tipped the balance in Washington. The result is a clear, human story of how a scramble for wealth reshaped ideas of freedom, labor, and belonging--and how California's rise helped push a fractured nation toward war. The Rush is alive with characters whose choices still reverberate: a searing, panoramic epic that captures both the fury and the promise of America. About the Author: Nathaniel Philbrick is the author of In the Heart of the Sea , winner of the National Book Award; Mayflower , finalist for the Pulitzer Prize; Valiant Ambition , winner of the George Washington Prize; Bunker Hill , winner of the New England Book Award; Travels with George ; Away Off Shore ; Second Wind ; Sea of Glory ; and The Last Stand . Lee Bruno is an author and journalist. His most recent book is Misfits, Merchants, and Mayhem: Tales from San Francisco’s Historic Waterfront, 1849–1934 , winner of the 2019 Independent Book Publisher Benjamin Franklin Gold Medal for History. His first book, Panorama: Tales from San Francisco’s 1915 Pan-Pacific International Exposition, was published in 2014. Bruno is a frequent contributor to the San Francisco Historical Society's quarterly journal, The Argonaut. He has reported on business, technology, and science with writings appearing in various national and international publications. He has lived in San Francisco for more than forty years, raising a family of four sons with his wife and enjoying open-water swims with the eccentrics at the South End Rowing Club.

events.title: DAMIEN ESCOBAR
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: One of the most influential and impactful violinists in modern history · Hailed as one of the most influential and impactful violinists in modern history, two-time Emmy award-winning artist Damien Escobar has spent nearly two decades cementing his legacy as the “King of Strings”. He’s inspired listeners, broken barriers, and created a blueprint for other contemporary violinists who aspire to top the charts and make their way onto main stages around the world. And his work is just getting started. The Jamaica, Queens native, who is known for his charisma, sincere humility, and undeniable talent, has always believed the key to his success is rooted in his humble beginnings. It is the main source that keeps him connected to his fans and cultivates his unending love for performing. And if you’ve heard his story, you know that Escobar’s journey after Juilliard (from which he graduated at the age of 12) wasn’t easy! But his passion and vision took him from playing for straphangers on NYC subways to serenading everyone from Oprah to the Obamas while achieving several lifetime goals in between— including an NAACP award nomination, topping the 100 Billboard charts, and selling 1M+ records. In 2023, Escobar sold out venues across the nation with his “Victory Lap” tour — an inspiring experience intended to empower audiences to celebrate their lives and all they’ve overcome. Escobar has a lot to celebrate on his musical journey, with his song “Taboo” earning the #1 song in the country and topping the Billboard charts, as well as the release of his highly anticipated album, Gemini. Escobar is letting it be known that his reign as the King of Strings will not cease. He’s on a mission to prove there’s astonishing power in instrumental music, and he intends to motivate listeners and make an impact on mainstream music like never before. With the release of his studio album, “Gemini”, Escobar is showing no signs of slowing down.

events.title: Our Loving Companions (San Francisco)
events.location: San Francisco
events.description: Our Loving Companions is a groundbreaking immersive theater experience celebrating the beautiful bond at the heart of pet ownership. A bond strong enough to propel us through deeply painful loss, time and again. Over 90 minutes, audiences journey through the laughter, devotion, inexplicable joy, and grief that define our relationships with our animal companions. Most shows will have a facilitated discussion afterwards for those who desire to partake. A portion of each $100 Companion Circle Ticket is donated to Bay Area animal charities to support animals in need. “The Bridge” by Jay Cross “What We Know” by Stephanie Weisman “A Dog Dreams” by Jeffrey Fisher Smith ”A Little Bird Told Me” by Marilyn Anderson “Must Love Pitbulls” by Jenny Mead “Tomorrow” by Alan Stewart “Outside the Box” by Emily Turner “A Good Dog” by Laura Neill “Ellie’s Goodbye” by Leslie Corn “Like a Dog”by Anya Martin “For The Love Of Buddy” by Dyanna Morrison “Roll Over, a monologue from the cat’s point of view” by Tommy Our Loving Companions is the result of a shared artistic vision between Grief Dialogues founder Elizabeth Coplan and co-producer and playwright Alan Stewart . Recognizing the need for an animal-centered immersive experience, Coplan envisioned a space that honors the distinct and deeply personal nature of the creatures who share our homes, our routines, and our unconditional love. Stewart, a producer, playwright, Dramatist Guild Foundation Fellow, and former trustee of San Francisco’s Magic Theatre, brings a distinctive artistic voice shaped by his first career as a veterinary internist and a lifelong belief in the human-animal bond as a language of the heart. Together, they create theater that invites audiences not only to witness grief, but to experience it in a way that clarifies, deepens, and transforms. As founder and Artistic Director of The Marsh, Stephanie Weisman brings a deep appreciation for work that blends storytelling with emotional truth, making her collaboration with Our Loving Companions a natural and meaningful fit. She is delighted to welcome Grief Dialogues to both The Marsh San Francisco and Berkeley—spaces long dedicated to bold, intimate, and transformative performance. Through hundreds of productions each year, alongside classes, youth programs, and live music, The Marsh has become a home for stories that matter. Stephanie’s own work in grief-centered theater, including her play 180 Days, To Die. To Live. , reflects that same commitment to exploring life’s most tender moments with honesty and care. And at home, her own loving companions—Marsh mascots Marsha and Junior—are never far from heart, a daily reminder of the deep bonds this experience so beautifully honors. Under the consulting direction of Dani Davis , Our Loving Companions living, immersive theatrical experience invites audiences to move through a curated landscape of short plays, poetry, music, sculpture, shared reflection, and personal stories. Blending warmth, tenderness, reverence, and moments of gentle humor, the production explores death, loss, and remembrance through what follows the final goodbye…the empty leash, the quiet food bowl, the space at the foot of the bed. Each performance is carefully choreographed behind the scenes to create an atmosphere fostering connection, validation, and collective witnessing for those grieving animal companions. In a culture where pet loss is sometimes dismissed as “lesser,” this experience affirms that love is not measured by species, and grief is not ranked by hierarchy. Michael Bud serves as Creative Producer and Director of Design for Our Loving Companions , shaping the audience experience from arrival through reflection. Working across promotion, staging, production design, and visual storytelling, he translates the project’s artistic and emotional vision into a cohesive immersive environment. His role supports both the creative flow of each performance and the deeper intention to witness, honor, and hold space for those mourning the loss of cherished animal companions. Pamela Hollings (she/they) is a theater-maker, working as a director, dramaturg, educator, actor, deviser and writer, depending on the project. Her career has focused on developing new work; working with playwrights as both director and dramaturg and as a devisor of new work, often site-specific. She is an ensemble member of Aviva Arts (formerly foolsFURY) where most recently they served as a co-writer, dramaturg and performer for Burning Wild a climate catastrophe devised piece performed outdoors in both Sonoma County and San Francisco. She was the Curation & Education Director at 3Girls Theatre, and the Board Chair (2013-2021), as well as an ensemble member (2018-2022) of foolsFURY Theater and the former Artistic Managing Director of both The Yat/Bentley Centre for Performance, SF Bay Area and Soup Kitchen Theatre, Melbourne, Australia. They trained in Theatre Direction at Australia’s National Institute of Dramatic Art (NIDA) whose distinguished alums include Cate Blanchett, Sara Snook, Baz Luhrmann and many more. Pamela is also a breath practitioner / voice teacher working at the intersection of theatre, education, ritual and somatic wellness. Anna Takayo Walden is a San Francisco-based theatre artist, AEA actor, and the Founding Artistic Director of San Francisco Classical Theatre, a site-specific classical theatre company that launched in June 2026 with a sold-out inaugural reading of Chekhov’s The Seagull directed by Carey Perloff. She is a Directing Fellow at Oakland Theatre Project, a member of the Actors Reading Collective, and Associate Artistic Director of Hawaii Public Theatre. As a director, Anna is drawn to work that lives in the body and in space — theatre that asks audiences not just to watch, but to feel, move, and reckon. Her practice is rooted in classical text, physical theatre, and ensemble, with a particular interest in immersive and site-specific forms that dissolve the boundary between story and world. As a performer, Anna’s credits span classical theatre companies across the United States and internationally, She holds an MA in Acting from the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art in London and an MFA in Classical Acting from The Shakespeare Theatre Company at George Washington University, Please read our Health, Safety and COVID-19 Information Our commitment to our patrons

events.title: Every Saturday Night
events.location: A.C.T., 415 Geary St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description:
Be transported to San Francisco’s Fillmore District—beginning in the present day, where the echoes of a once-thriving Black neighborhood still shape the streets. From there, Every Saturday Night pulls audiences back into the 1950s, the vibrant “Harlem of the West,” when the Fillmore pulsed with jazz, community, and possibility.

Following two Black boys—one in each era—the musical explores home, belonging, and resilience, revealing how the Fillmore’s past and present are connected by displacement, gentrification, and the enduring fight to stay rooted in the community.

Inspired by true events, this boisterous and heartfelt new work commissioned and presented by San Francisco Bay Area Theatre Company (SFBATCO) celebrates a historic neighborhood while asking urgent questions about who gets to remain in the city today.

events.description: A Word for Word and Z Space production · Stories by E.L. Doctorow & Tatyana Tolstaya Presented by Word for Word and Z Space Directed by Rotimi Agbabiaka In “Assimilation” by E. L. Doctorow, Ramon is offered a promotion and cash which could pay for grad school – if he agrees to enter a green-card marriage with his boss’s niece. When he agrees, he gets more than he bargained for. “Smoke and Shadows” by Tatyana Tolstaya centers on a Russian professor living in the U.S., navigating her professional life, her intimate relationships, and the mysteries of culture. Told with Tolstaya’s sharp, restrained wit, the story zeros in on the experience of living in a new culture, and the confusions and imbalance that can cause. What does it mean to assimilate? These two writers offer two very different perspectives.

events.description: The Cornley Polytechnic Drama Society is back, and this time they’re taking on Peter Pan . It’s their most ambitious production yet, complete with flying rigs, sword fights, and a very real crocodile problem. What could possibly go wrong? As technical mishaps pile up and tempers flare, the cast battles to keep the show on track while everything around them spectacularly falls apart. Lines are forgotten, scenery refuses to cooperate, and rivalries spill onto the stage in real time. From the creators of The Play That Goes Wrong , this riotous comedy delivers nonstop mayhem, perfectly timed chaos, and the kind of theatrical disaster you have to see to believe.

events.title: Oaklando
events.location: The Dawn Club, San Francisco
events.description: What do you get when you fuse the spicy grooves of Afro-Peru with that funky sound of Oaktown? A ground-breaking, new, energetic genre with distinctive rhythms and innovative melodies that will inspire you to hit the dance floor. Oaklando is the brainchild of SF native Patrick Morehead, the composer and keyboardist who’s played with such talents as Karl Perazzo, Steve Turre, Jerry Gonzalez, and Benny Valarde. Conceived at the Patio de Ochun Studios, with drummer Josh Jones (of Omar Sosa) bassist David Pinto (of Susana Baca) and cajon player Juan Medrano Cotito (of Susana Baca) Oaklando was engineered by multi-grammy winner, Greg Landau (of David Byrne fame), and became a recipient of the prestigious Music in Place Grant. Oaklando has regular performances at Local Edition, Lakehouse Jazz, Elevation LVK, and Zeitgeist. Along with Morehead, Cotito and Jones include Charlie Gurke (sax), Chloe Scott ( flute) Pedro Rosales (cajon/vocals) vocalist Marina Lavalle (Peru Negro) with guest appearances on the first recording ‘Lima Oakland’ by NY jazz phenom Yosvany Terry. Check out the newest single OAKLANDO on all platforms Oaklando is honored to present the highly acclaimed Dawn Club with its fusion of Afro-Peruvian rhythms and funky jazz dub.

events.title: Alicia Dattner's Small Batch Artisanal Comedy
events.location: Berkeley
events.description: Opening Reception September 19 (Please do not bring infants to the show) Balinese scooters. Portuguese military installations. Brazilian waxes. Indian ashrams. Serbian kitesurfers. A secret tantra party. A deadbeat baby daddy. A planetary death doula. A Rube Goldberg joke factory. The last plane to Lisbon before the world shuts down. Safety-ism. Presbyopia. Cyborgs. Incels in service to the Goddess. Shade grown coffee. Ego dissolution Cervical orgasms. And the slow realization that enlightenment doesn’t get you very far. Alicia Dattner’s new show is farm-to-funnybone, post-apocalyptic, biodynamic artisanal comedy — for the spiritually adventurous and existentially exhausted. Raised in an extremely liberal branch of Judaism known as an ashram (that’s a joke), Alicia’s spiritual roots – and propensity for poking fun at them – go deep. Alicia did her first standup set at 18 and graduated from Hampshire College with a degree in standup comedy and filmmaking. Mentored by several talented comedians over the years, including W. Kamau Bell (CNN, FX), Eugene Mirman (Flight of the Conchords), and Bill Santiago (Comedy Central), she’s been rocking clubs like The Improv and Gotham Comedy Club, playing in San Francisco, New York, London, Hollywood, Honolulu, Bali, and Bombay. She’s performed with Ali Wong, Maria Bamford, Moshe Kasher, Arj Barker, Marc Maron, and many more luminaries. Please read our Health, Safety and COVID-19 Information Our commitment to our patrons

events.title: Zaccai Curtis Sextet
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Joe Henderson Lab
events.description:
For these two nights, pianist Zaccai Curtis leads a fiery sextet reviving Afro-Cuban bebop. His 2024 release Cubop Lives! reimagines jazz history with bold, modern swing, winning a GRAMMY for Best Latin Jazz Album. Born in New York and raised in Hartford, Connecticut, Curtis grew up immersed in jazz, Afro-Caribbean rhythms, and the rich musical traditions of his Puerto Rican and African American heritage. A student of Jackie McLean’s Artists Collective, he developed into a pianist and composer celebrated for combining technical brilliance with deep rhythmic sophistication.

Over the years, Curtis has collaborated with major artists including Eddie Palmieri, Brian Lynch, Christian Scott, Donald Harrison, and Santana, while also building a celebrated musical partnership with his brother, bassist Luques Curtis. Together, they co-founded the Truth Revolution Recording Collective and have become leading voices in contemporary Latin jazz.

Cubop Lives! pays tribute to the explosive fusion of bebop and Afro-Cuban music pioneered by Dizzy Gillespie, Chano Pozo, and Mario Bauzá, while showcasing Curtis’ dynamic working sextet. Featuring Luques Curtis, Willie Martinez III, Camilo Molina, and Reinaldo de Jesús, the ensemble delivers electrifying performances filled with rhythmic fire, virtuosity, and joyous improvisation.

Personnel: Zaccai Curtis (piano); Others TBA

events.title: Lila Downs
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
With “a stunning voice, a confident multicultural vision grounded in her Mixtec Indian roots” (LA Times), Lila Downs is one of Latin America’s most influential voices - an artist with a singular sound, magnetic stage presence, and recognized with multiple GRAMMY and Latin GRAMMY Awards, including the recipient of the 2026 Latin GRAMMY Lifetime Achievement Award. With her new album Cambias mi Mundo (You Change My World), she returns to the Miner stage for four nights after her hugely successful run of Día de los Muertos performances at the Paramount. The album marks a return to her essence: deeply committed to global causes, passionate, intimate and celebratory.

She made her major label debut with 1999’s jazz-informed La Sandunga, and her contributions to the 2002 Frida Kahlo biopic Frida elevated her status to that of a major international star. Downs has become recognized worldwide as a global ambassador for Mexico’s folkloric traditions and champion for the preservation of native Mexican culture, recording songs in indigenous Mayan, Nahuatl, Trique, and Purépecha languages.

Rooted in Oaxaca and shaped between Mexico and the United States, she weaves Mexican tradition with jazz, cumbia, folk, and contemporary rhythms. Her music is both celebration and conscience; she turns each concert into a gathering—intimate, fearless, and deeply human.

Personnel: Lila Downs (vocals); Josh Deutsch (trumpet, keyboards); George Saenz (trombone, accordion); Rafael Gomez (guitars); Luis Guzman (bass, synthesizer); Sinuhe Padilla (jarana, bajo, zapateado); Lautaro Burgos (drums); Nakeiltha Cambpell (percussion)

events.title: DAMIEN ESCOBAR
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: One of the most influential and impactful violinists in modern history · Hailed as one of the most influential and impactful violinists in modern history, two-time Emmy award-winning artist Damien Escobar has spent nearly two decades cementing his legacy as the “King of Strings”. He’s inspired listeners, broken barriers, and created a blueprint for other contemporary violinists who aspire to top the charts and make their way onto main stages around the world. And his work is just getting started. The Jamaica, Queens native, who is known for his charisma, sincere humility, and undeniable talent, has always believed the key to his success is rooted in his humble beginnings. It is the main source that keeps him connected to his fans and cultivates his unending love for performing. And if you’ve heard his story, you know that Escobar’s journey after Juilliard (from which he graduated at the age of 12) wasn’t easy! But his passion and vision took him from playing for straphangers on NYC subways to serenading everyone from Oprah to the Obamas while achieving several lifetime goals in between— including an NAACP award nomination, topping the 100 Billboard charts, and selling 1M+ records. In 2023, Escobar sold out venues across the nation with his “Victory Lap” tour — an inspiring experience intended to empower audiences to celebrate their lives and all they’ve overcome. Escobar has a lot to celebrate on his musical journey, with his song “Taboo” earning the #1 song in the country and topping the Billboard charts, as well as the release of his highly anticipated album, Gemini. Escobar is letting it be known that his reign as the King of Strings will not cease. He’s on a mission to prove there’s astonishing power in instrumental music, and he intends to motivate listeners and make an impact on mainstream music like never before. With the release of his studio album, “Gemini”, Escobar is showing no signs of slowing down.

events.description: Barely Legal presents The Rocky Horror Picture Show at the Phoenix! Film screening with live shadow cast · The Rocky Horror Picture Show is a 1975 musical comedy film that parodies science fiction and horror films. With a screenplay written by Richard O'Brien and Jim Sharman, the film features Tim Curry, Susan Sarandon and Barry Bostwick. The film is based on the British musical stage production The Rocky Horror Show. The film is considered a cult classic and a midnight movie, although it is widely known by mainstream audiences and has a large international following. RHPS was the first movie from a major film studio—20th Century Fox—in the midnight-movie market. The movie is one of the most well known and financially successful midnight movies. It is the longest running theatrical release in film history. More than 30 years later it is still in limited release in cinemas around the world. In 2005, the film was selected for preservation in the United States National Film Registry by the Library of Congress as being "culturally, historically, or aesthetically significant".

events.title: The Commons Public Hours ☕
events.location: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco + Full Space
events.description:
🎉 Public Hours at the Commons 🎉
Every Sunday, the Commons opens to the public — no membership required. Come co-work, connect, create, or just explore the space at your own pace. ✨
🕘 When: Every Sunday, 9 AM – 10 PM
📍 Where: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco (corner of Hayes & Laguna, basement level)
RSVP and we'll email you your entry code ahead of time — so you can let yourself straight in when you arrive.
──────────────────────────────
🧭 A self-guided day
Public Hours are self-guided — come in, settle in, and make the space your own. Weekends are usually unstaffed, so there's no check-in desk or guided tour. Our members are glad to answer questions about the space; for anything else — including guided tours, which we don't offer as drop-ins — email hello@thesfcommons.com ahead of time.
──────────────────────────────
🔭 Getting in
Your entry code comes by email. Once you RSVP, we'll send you a personal QR code — that's your key for the day. Keep it handy on your phone (and check spam if you don't see it).
Find us. We're at 540 Laguna St, on the corner of Hayes & Laguna. Head down the stairs beside Earthbody to the basement level — that's the Commons.
Scan your QR code at the reader to unlock the door. Hold your phone just below the Kisi reader by the door and it'll let you in.
Your access stays active all day, 9 AM – 10 PM, so you can come and go freely.
Can't find your code on the day? No problem — scan the QR posted on the door to check in and get a fresh one on the spot.
We're shoes-off 🧦 — please clean up after yourself, including dirty dishes and mugs, and use only the front entrance. Trouble getting in? Email hello@thesfcommons.com.




The Commons is a modern-day town square for communal meaning-making, personal discovery, and self-expression in the heart of San Francisco. Apply to become a member here__.

events.title: Sandy Walker - My Deepest Desire
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: My Deepest Desire is a poetic short story about the yearning to live and love fully, free from the burden of loss and tragedy. Written by the late Tamiki Hara and presented by the award-winning artist Sandy Walker. My Deepest Desire is Tamiki Hara’s final work, published posthumously after his tragic suicide in 1951. A short yet grippingly moving meditation on the desire to live a different, fuller life, free from pain, isolation, and the intrusively haunting experience of tragedy, it is a demonstration of how dreams, memories, and traumatic despair intertwine inside a person’s psyche. Artist’s Preface In 1982 my friend Alan Gussow initiated the Shadow Project in New York City. It grew each year to where people in more than one thousand locations worldwide, on the anniversary of the bombing of Hiroshima, participated by painting the outlines (shadows) of humans and animals on streets and sidewalks each year for all to see early in the morning as they got up and went to work. My wife, dancer and choreographer Ellen Webb, and I, in about 1985, participated in our small community in the North Cascades National Park of Washington state. Then around 1988, Ellen and I were in central Wyoming when we heard that Paul Tibbets, the pilot of the Enola Gay (the plane that carried the bomb) was speaking in Casper. We were stunned and appalled by what he said. This led us to collaborating on an evening length performance at the Cowell Theater in San Francisco near the 50th anniversary of the bombing. Tibbets’ words were at the heart of the performance. During our research for the performance, I read this work of poet Tamiki Hara, which conflates the loss of Tamaki’s wife before the bombing with the experience of the bombing and its aftermath as he struggled to make sense of life. I was deeply moved by this work and resolved to make an artwork around it. Over a long time I carried it with me. One dark night I found the images, or I could say they found me, in the in the form of these ink drawings. After that time, it still took me years (over 25 years in all) to bring the text together with the images. Finally, I determined to handwrite the words as if I were Tamiki. The project has rested with me in this form as a loose portfolio until Lynne Elizabeth saw it, and later asked if New Village Press could publish it, not with my handwriting but with a typeset text opposite the drawings. I am thrilled that Tamiki Hara’s writing can have more life, especially in this new translation by Liza Dalby. We also offer the Japanese text at the end. – Sandy Walker "Tamiki Hara, a Hiroshima atomic bomb survivor, activist and poet/writer, living under the U.S.–led Allied Occupation’s control of speeches and publications, wrote about his own confusion, outrage, love and solitude. In spite of the oppressive environment, he repeatedly asserted that what he desired more than anything else in the world was a new world where the dignity of each and every human being was respected and protected, allowing peace to prevail." ~Setsuko Thurlow (born Nakamura Setsuko), a hibakusha and leading figure of the International Campaign to Abolish Nuclear Weapons "Devastated by the atomic blast in Hiroshima, and following his wife’s passing, the prolific poet and novelist, Tamiki Hara (1905–1951), expresses his helpless sorrow, loneliness, and despair in an extremely imaginative way. Shingan no Kuni ( My Deepest Desire ), drafted shortly before his suicide, is a most tragic narrative taken from the pages of Japanese literature. This book provides readers with a trio of Liza Dalby’s elegant translation of the sensitive original, along with an amazing set of ink drawings by Sandy Walker committed to denounce nuclear bombs." ~Kazuaki Tanahashi, author of Painting Peace: Art in a Time of Global Crisis "The depth of Tamiki Hara's heart is so exquisitely expressed that I was brought to a state of wonder and awe. His quietly inventive meditations, memories and dreams are a true gift from the poet who, despite the personal and global tragedy he endured, still could say, ‘I want to live as innocent as a bird until the moment death snatches me up.’ The combined boldness and sensitivity of Sandy Walker's ink drawings dance across the imagination, startling in their nakedness—a perfect accompaniment to Liza Dalby's pristine translation of Hara's final work." ~Peter Levitt, author of Fingerpainting on the Moon: Writing and Creativity as a Path to Freedom Artist Sandy Walker is a painter, printmaker and visual artist. He is the recipient of the prestigious Isadora Duncan Dance Award for Visual Design, and his work is in the collections of many museums, including the Museum of Modern Art, the Metropolitan Museum of Art, and the Whitney Museum in New York, the Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco, and the Smithsonian American Art Museum in Washington, D.C. A catalogue raisonné of his woodblock prints was published by Cicero Books in 2026. Walker lives and works in Oakland, California. Sandy's website: https://sandywalker.com Tamiki Hara was a Japanese writer and poet. Born in Hiroshima, he lived through the atomic bombing in 1945. In the years preceding his death, Tamiki Hara wrote about the destruction he witnessed in autobiographical short stories and poems, making him a known figure in the atomic bomb literature genre. Liza Dalby is an anthropologist specializing in Japanese culture. Her nonfiction books, Geisha and Kimono, have become classics, and her best-selling historical novel, The Tale of Murasaki has been translated into nine languages. Dalby’s memoir, East Wind Melts the Ice, is a gardener's diary and an enlightening excursion through cultures east and west. Dalby lives in Berkeley, California. Sandy Walker - photo courtesy of the author Event details: This event will be hosted by Book Passage at our Corte Madera store. Free Admission / Open Seating Books are available for purchase in-store or over the phone! Give us a call at (415) 927-0960 to order your copy ahead of the event. There will be a signing line or meet-and-greet following the presentation.

Beginning in the present—at a writing residency in the aftermath of this success—How to Exi(s)t unpeels the layers between present and past in bursts of brief poetic essays. Unsparing, even caustic in its insistence on racism as a dominant note of American life, but marked by surprising tenderness and humor, How to Exi(s)t is a compelling portrayal of Tran’s pedagogical philosophy as well as an interrogation of a poetic language that conceals as much as it reveals. events.title: Laura Cunningham - A State of Change
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: ​A State of Change is a magnificently illustrated classic of California natural history, now updated in a long-awaited reissue by artist-naturalist Laura Cunningham. "I wouldn't be the artist-author I am today without A State of Change . I consider Cunningham's work to be an original inspiration for all that I do." --Obi Kaufmann Originally published in 2010, A State of Change: California’s Forgotten Landscapes by Laura Cunningham is widely considered a classic text of California natural history. Returning to print in a fully restyled package in fall 2026, this updated edition includes expanded content, Cunningham’s original oil paintings and field sketches, and a contemporary design that offers readers a firsthand look at pre-colonial California and the immense biodiversity that once reigned. Melding science, Traditional Ecological Knowledge, stunning landscapes and species portraiture, artist-naturalist Cunningham takes a multi-field perspective to reenvision the West as it once was, before centuries of settlement reshaped the land and its native wildlife. Compiled over decades, A State of Change (on sale October 13, 2026) draws from fieldwork spanning the state and beyond, Indigenous oral histories and interviews with tribal elders, scientific research in biology and paleontology, and years of artistic study. This deep time exploration of Old California throws into stark relief the engineered landscapes we know today and the diminution of biodiversity already millennia in the making. “This book is my life’s work trying to understand California in the past so that we can protect and help restore the natural and cultural landscapes of this precious state into the future,” says Cunningham, whose acclaimed original publication garnered a California Book Award, a Northern California Book Award, was declared a Best Book of the Year by East Bay Express, and a finalist for Foreword’s Book of the Year. Cunningham’s original publication predicted the explosive development of megafires in California and reacquainted readers with species long since absent from the landscape—from the extinct flightless marine diving goose to the Golden State’s banner grizzly, last seen a century ago. The 2026 edition of A State of Change reflects watershed ecological developments since the book’s original publication. These include the comebacks of California wolves and condors, the resurgence of salmon populations under tribal stewardship, and the gradual reimplementation of Indigenous fire management. Cunningham also challenges popular ideas about regenerative agriculture and livestock grazing, pointing toward pathways to restore native grasslands that underpin the state’s ecosystems. Learning about the plight of species in the past has kindled Cunningham’s lifelong passion for saving species for the future—and with this galvanizing and visually immersive text she aims to alight a kindred spark in the reader. “This wonderful book is a vivid reminder of how things began, and also as a vision of the rich and beautiful world we can work toward in our shared future,” says author Kim Stanley Robinson, “One of Heyday’s best.” "This wonderful book is a vivid reminder of how things began, and also as a vision of the rich and beautiful world we can work toward in our shared future." -- Kim Stanley Robinson "This brings a lost world straight back to life--and one hopes it will help us work to restore it in the real world." -- Bill McKibben Laura Cunningham is an artist-naturalist and award-winning author of A State of Change: California's Forgotten Landscapes. Cunningham studied paleontology and biology at the University of California, Berkeley. She has worked field biology jobs for the California Department of Fish and Game, the United States Geological Survey, and various universities, gaining experience with such species as Owens Valley pupfish, salmon and steelhead trout, Yosemite toads, Panamint alligator lizards, and tule elk. Simultaneously, she taught herself the arts of sketching and oil painting and pursued studies of California's historical ecology. She currently works in the conservation nonprofit field. Her studio is next to Death Valley National Park along the Amargosa River. events.title: Carrie Powell - The Midlife Edit
events.location: Book Passage Ferry Building 1 Ferry Building San Francisco, CA 94111
events.description: The Midlife Edit is a practical, judgment-free guide to decluttering and organizing—praised by Publishers Weekly as "a smart and simple approach to a daunting task"—that helps you manage your home without the pressure to become a minimalist. “But… it feels wrong to throw it away!” If that thought has ever stopped you from decluttering, you’re not alone. By midlife, most homes are filled with decades of belongings—your own, your children’s, and often your parents’ too. The result? Overwhelm, decision fatigue, and a home that no longer fits your next chapter. What You’ll Learn: A step-by-step decluttering system designed specifically for midlife and beyond How to handle sentimental items without guilt or regret Simple strategies for downsizing, organizing, and letting go How to overcome the emotional blocks that make decluttering feel impossible Practical methods to reduce clutter and maintain an organized home long-term Why This Book Is Different: Focuses on real-life decluttering , not unrealistic perfection Tailored for midlife, empty nesters, and retirement planning Combines mindset shifts + actionable organizing techniques Helps you prepare your home—and life—for what’s next Written by professional organizer Carrie Powell, this guide gives you the tools to reclaim your space, reduce stress, and move forward with clarity. Start decluttering today—and make space for the life you actually want. "So much stuff accumulates by midlife, but if you’re ready for a reset, Carrie will help you take control of your life for good. In this no-nonsense but encouraging book, you’ll learn how to make swift decisions while honoring memories—so your time can be spent living rather than managing things." —Laura Vanderkam, author of Big Time: A Simple Path to Time Abundance " The Midlife Edit is a beautiful reminder that letting go isn’t loss, it’s making space for what truly matters. This book gently guides you to release the excess and step into your next chapter with clarity, purpose, and peace." —Nikki Boyd, organizing expert & author of the Beautifully Organized s eries "The result is a smart and simple approach to a daunting task." —Publishers Weekly Carrie Powell is a professional organizer and decluttering coach. As a midlifer and almost-empty nester, she draws on her personal experience and that of hundreds of clients to inform her approach to midlife decluttering. She has witnessed (and coached!) countless transformations that have changed lives for the better. She found organizing and coaching as a career in midlife, after spending 30 years in Fashion Merchandising at Nordstrom. Even though her own home is organized, a pandemic-fueled decluttering frenzy led to a newfound appreciation for the art of curating a lifetime of possessions and its impact on the next chapter of her life. Her coaching is rooted in habits, mindset shifts, and building the muscle to break down overwhelm. events.title: Our Loving Companions (San Francisco)
events.location: San Francisco
events.description: Our Loving Companions is a groundbreaking immersive theater experience celebrating the beautiful bond at the heart of pet ownership. A bond strong enough to propel us through deeply painful loss, time and again. Over 90 minutes, audiences journey through the laughter, devotion, inexplicable joy, and grief that define our relationships with our animal companions. Most shows will have a facilitated discussion afterwards for those who desire to partake. A portion of each $100 Companion Circle Ticket is donated to Bay Area animal charities to support animals in need. “The Bridge” by Jay Cross “What We Know” by Stephanie Weisman “A Dog Dreams” by Jeffrey Fisher Smith ”A Little Bird Told Me” by Marilyn Anderson “Must Love Pitbulls” by Jenny Mead “Tomorrow” by Alan Stewart “Outside the Box” by Emily Turner “A Good Dog” by Laura Neill “Ellie’s Goodbye” by Leslie Corn “Like a Dog”by Anya Martin “For The Love Of Buddy” by Dyanna Morrison “Roll Over, a monologue from the cat’s point of view” by Tommy Our Loving Companions is the result of a shared artistic vision between Grief Dialogues founder Elizabeth Coplan and co-producer and playwright Alan Stewart . Recognizing the need for an animal-centered immersive experience, Coplan envisioned a space that honors the distinct and deeply personal nature of the creatures who share our homes, our routines, and our unconditional love. Stewart, a producer, playwright, Dramatist Guild Foundation Fellow, and former trustee of San Francisco’s Magic Theatre, brings a distinctive artistic voice shaped by his first career as a veterinary internist and a lifelong belief in the human-animal bond as a language of the heart. Together, they create theater that invites audiences not only to witness grief, but to experience it in a way that clarifies, deepens, and transforms. As founder and Artistic Director of The Marsh, Stephanie Weisman brings a deep appreciation for work that blends storytelling with emotional truth, making her collaboration with Our Loving Companions a natural and meaningful fit. She is delighted to welcome Grief Dialogues to both The Marsh San Francisco and Berkeley—spaces long dedicated to bold, intimate, and transformative performance. Through hundreds of productions each year, alongside classes, youth programs, and live music, The Marsh has become a home for stories that matter. Stephanie’s own work in grief-centered theater, including her play 180 Days, To Die. To Live. , reflects that same commitment to exploring life’s most tender moments with honesty and care. And at home, her own loving companions—Marsh mascots Marsha and Junior—are never far from heart, a daily reminder of the deep bonds this experience so beautifully honors. Under the consulting direction of Dani Davis , Our Loving Companions living, immersive theatrical experience invites audiences to move through a curated landscape of short plays, poetry, music, sculpture, shared reflection, and personal stories. Blending warmth, tenderness, reverence, and moments of gentle humor, the production explores death, loss, and remembrance through what follows the final goodbye…the empty leash, the quiet food bowl, the space at the foot of the bed. Each performance is carefully choreographed behind the scenes to create an atmosphere fostering connection, validation, and collective witnessing for those grieving animal companions. In a culture where pet loss is sometimes dismissed as “lesser,” this experience affirms that love is not measured by species, and grief is not ranked by hierarchy. Michael Bud serves as Creative Producer and Director of Design for Our Loving Companions , shaping the audience experience from arrival through reflection. Working across promotion, staging, production design, and visual storytelling, he translates the project’s artistic and emotional vision into a cohesive immersive environment. His role supports both the creative flow of each performance and the deeper intention to witness, honor, and hold space for those mourning the loss of cherished animal companions. Pamela Hollings (she/they) is a theater-maker, working as a director, dramaturg, educator, actor, deviser and writer, depending on the project. Her career has focused on developing new work; working with playwrights as both director and dramaturg and as a devisor of new work, often site-specific. She is an ensemble member of Aviva Arts (formerly foolsFURY) where most recently they served as a co-writer, dramaturg and performer for Burning Wild a climate catastrophe devised piece performed outdoors in both Sonoma County and San Francisco. She was the Curation & Education Director at 3Girls Theatre, and the Board Chair (2013-2021), as well as an ensemble member (2018-2022) of foolsFURY Theater and the former Artistic Managing Director of both The Yat/Bentley Centre for Performance, SF Bay Area and Soup Kitchen Theatre, Melbourne, Australia. They trained in Theatre Direction at Australia’s National Institute of Dramatic Art (NIDA) whose distinguished alums include Cate Blanchett, Sara Snook, Baz Luhrmann and many more. Pamela is also a breath practitioner / voice teacher working at the intersection of theatre, education, ritual and somatic wellness. Anna Takayo Walden is a San Francisco-based theatre artist, AEA actor, and the Founding Artistic Director of San Francisco Classical Theatre, a site-specific classical theatre company that launched in June 2026 with a sold-out inaugural reading of Chekhov’s The Seagull directed by Carey Perloff. She is a Directing Fellow at Oakland Theatre Project, a member of the Actors Reading Collective, and Associate Artistic Director of Hawaii Public Theatre. As a director, Anna is drawn to work that lives in the body and in space — theatre that asks audiences not just to watch, but to feel, move, and reckon. Her practice is rooted in classical text, physical theatre, and ensemble, with a particular interest in immersive and site-specific forms that dissolve the boundary between story and world. As a performer, Anna’s credits span classical theatre companies across the United States and internationally, She holds an MA in Acting from the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art in London and an MFA in Classical Acting from The Shakespeare Theatre Company at George Washington University, Please read our Health, Safety and COVID-19 Information Our commitment to our patrons

events.title: Obi Kaufmann with Victoria Schlesinger - California Inside Out
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: In a provocative new work blending manifesto, philosophy, and ecological inquiry, the bestselling California Field Atlas series creator challenges readers to reimagine humanity's relationship with the living world. Obi Kaufmann will be joined in conversation by Victoria Schlesinger, the editor-in-chief of Bay Nature. This fall, award-winning creator of the California Field Atlas series, Obi Kaufmann, publishes his most probing and philosophical book to date: California Inside Out: Mapping an Ecology of Mind(on-sale: October 6, 2026). With this compact, pocket-sized volume, the San Francisco Chronicle and Los Angeles Times bestselling author recenters radical kinship with the more-than-human world, advancing an environmental worldview rooted in the recognition of nature’s agency and humanity’s inseparable relationship to place. Part manifesto, part lyrical meditation, California Inside Out interrogates the stories that estrange people from the living systems that surround them and searches for new language capable of restoring that connection. Kaufmann challenges the assumptions that promote extractive thinking and sets out to tell another story; one aimed at helping Californians leave the state at the close of the 21st century healthier, more resilient, and more ecologically whole than it was at the century’s start. Deriving inspiration from Traditional Ecological Knowledge, the lessons of deep time, and the blueprints of renowned naturalists including Aldo Leopold, Gary Snyder, and Robin Wall Kimmerer, Kaufmann sketches the contours of an emergent conservation ethic for the 22nd century. Rejecting the inherited “man versus nature” model, he proposes creative frameworks for realizing equity and mutuality between humans and the wider living world. Kaufmann’s approach is deeply Socratic, inviting readers to consider provocative questions: What if wildfire were revered rather than reviled? What if humans respected the creative capacity of other species? What if watersheds have volition and rivers were accorded legal rights? At the heart of California Inside Out is a quest to find the new premises—or long-forgotten verities—that may reveal enough intrinsic value in nonhuman entities to inspire people to retrieve their responsibility as stewards of the systems upon which all life depends. For the notion that wilderness exists separate from human development is ahistorical, Kaufmann reminds us. “The structural makeup of habitat spaces is largely the product of a consistent, multimillennia-long project of human stewardship,” he observes, invoking Indigenous traditions and technologies that have shaped the American West for thousands of years. Everything from faunal biogeography to soil fecundity has been shaped by human hands, human history, and increasingly, human policy: “California’s landscape is an ecological artifact of human activity.” With California Inside Out, Kaufmann challenges readers to consider what kind of landscape will emerge from continuing along with a now centuries-long protocol of human activity that is driven primarily by extraction and capital utility—and appeals to the reader to ensure that another story, a better story, prevails. "Obi Kaufmann’s books are like bibles to me. They explain California’s natural beauty better than anything I’ve read before.” —DAVE EGGERS “A full immersion into the astonishingly varied natural worlds. Gorgeous.” —CBS SAN FRANCISCO "Obi leaves no leaf unturned in his quest to capture the wonder and fragility.” —SUNSET "Kaufmann’s gaze easily ranges from the micro to the macro. As a reader you are invited to join him on a journey of discovery—not as a passenger but as an active partner.” —SAN FRANCISCO CHRONICLE “An original contribution to the genre … Immersive.” —LOS ANGELES REVIEW OF BOOKS Obi Kaufmann is an artist, conservationist, and the bestselling and award-winning author of The California Field Atlas series. Kaufmann is a former board member of the California Wilderness Coalition and winner of the 2019 Mark Dubois River Protection Award. Notable recent illustration projects include a 2022 residency with the National Wildlife Federation as the illustrator for the Wallis Annenberg Wildlife Crossing and a 2025 writing and painting residency for the National Gallery of Art in Yosemite. In 2026 he will participate in an authors' residency in Stockholm with the Swedish Institute. His most recent book is California Inside Out: Mapping an Ecology of Mind (2026). When he is not backpacking, the painter-poet can be found at home in the East Bay, posting trail paintings @coyotethunder on Instagram. Victoria Schlesinger is editor-in-chief of Bay Nature . Schlesinger has worked as a raft guide in Colorado, a backpacking counselor in the Trinity Alps, and spent the better part of her 20s researching and writing a book about ecology in Central America. Her journalism career began at California Wild magazine and the Point Reyes Light newspaper, and she has since earned two master’s degrees from Columbia University Graduate School of Journalism. Her articles have appeared in Harper’s Magazine , Mother Jones , Audubon and The New York Times , among many other outlets, and she’s been on staff with Discover , PBS Frontline, Plenty , and California Lawyer . She lives in Berkeley with her husband and daughter. events.title: Versus
events.location: Balboa Theatre, 3630 Balboa St, San Francisco, CA 94121
events.description: A relentless one-of-a-kind sensory assault chock-full of hyper-kinetic fight scenes, gangster shootouts, sword-slashing violence and gory zombie horror, Versus was a key title amongst the barrage of innovative horror and action movies that appeared as if from nowhere from Japan at the turn of the millennium, leading to a new wave of appreciation for Asian extreme cinema. A mysterious face-off in a wooded clearing between two escaped convicts and a carload of sharply dressed yakuza holding a beautiful woman captive ends in hails of bullets and showers of blood. The location for this violent encounter is the mythic Forest of Resurrection, the site of the 444th portal of the 666 hidden gates that link this earthly domain to the netherworld - and it didn't get this name for nothing. As one of the surviving prisoners escapes with the girl into the darkness of the forest, disgruntled gangsters soon become the least of their worries as an earlier battle between a lone warrior against hordes of zombie samurai is carried over from a millennium ago into the present day... Toshiro Mifune stars as Isaburo Sasahara, an aging swordsman living a quiet life until his clan lord orders that his son marry the lord's mistress, who has recently displeased the ruler. Reluctantly, father and son take in the woman, and, to the family’s surprise, the young couple fall in love. But the lord soon reverses his decision and demands the mistress’s return. Against all expectations, Isaburo and his son refuse, risking the destruction of their entire family. Director Masaki Kobayashi's Samurai Rebellion is the gripping story of a peaceful man who finally decides to take a stand against injustice. events.title: DAMIEN ESCOBAR
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: One of the most influential and impactful violinists in modern history · Hailed as one of the most influential and impactful violinists in modern history, two-time Emmy award-winning artist Damien Escobar has spent nearly two decades cementing his legacy as the “King of Strings”. He’s inspired listeners, broken barriers, and created a blueprint for other contemporary violinists who aspire to top the charts and make their way onto main stages around the world. And his work is just getting started. The Jamaica, Queens native, who is known for his charisma, sincere humility, and undeniable talent, has always believed the key to his success is rooted in his humble beginnings. It is the main source that keeps him connected to his fans and cultivates his unending love for performing. And if you’ve heard his story, you know that Escobar’s journey after Juilliard (from which he graduated at the age of 12) wasn’t easy! But his passion and vision took him from playing for straphangers on NYC subways to serenading everyone from Oprah to the Obamas while achieving several lifetime goals in between— including an NAACP award nomination, topping the 100 Billboard charts, and selling 1M+ records. In 2023, Escobar sold out venues across the nation with his “Victory Lap” tour — an inspiring experience intended to empower audiences to celebrate their lives and all they’ve overcome. Escobar has a lot to celebrate on his musical journey, with his song “Taboo” earning the #1 song in the country and topping the Billboard charts, as well as the release of his highly anticipated album, Gemini. Escobar is letting it be known that his reign as the King of Strings will not cease. He’s on a mission to prove there’s astonishing power in instrumental music, and he intends to motivate listeners and make an impact on mainstream music like never before. With the release of his studio album, “Gemini”, Escobar is showing no signs of slowing down.

This Italian-French-German co-production stars British actor Rupert Everett ( My Best Friend’s Wedding) as Franceso Dellamorte, a graveyard keeper tasked with putting the dead that rise each night. Despite his gristly job, Dellamorte is a romantic at heart. But is he free to find love, or is fate bound to something far darker? And what does the Angel of Death have to do with all of it? Inspired by Tziano Sclavi’s novel Dellamorte Dellamore and his comic character Dylan Dog (who was visually based on Everett), this film is equal parts scary, comedic, and sexy, with surprising surreal and philosophical developments as the plot develops. A must see film, straight from the cold expanse of Hell to ring in Halloween! events.title: Marina Crouse
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Joe Henderson Lab
events.description:
A jazz vocalist with “an awe-inspiring voice” (The Mercury News), Marina Crouse is known for her latest album Canto de mi Corazón and for her sold-out Hotplate tributes to Eydie Gormé and Ernestine Anderson. A powerful and versatile Bay Area artist, Crouse blends jazz, blues, soul, Latin music, and classic bolero traditions into performances marked by emotional honesty and deep cultural connection. Raised in California and deeply influenced by her Chicana heritage, she first gained recognition for her expressive interpretations and remarkable vocal control, shaped in part by early classical training. Her 2018 debut album, Never Too Soon, introduced audiences to a singer equally at home with blues, R&B, and jazz-inflected storytelling.

With Canto de mi Corazón, Crouse turned toward the Spanish-language music that filled her childhood home, paying heartfelt tribute to Eydie Gormé and Los Panchos through lush, intimate renditions of beloved boleros. The album earned praise for its warmth, authenticity, and elegant vocal phrasing, solidifying her place as one of the Bay Area’s most compelling interpreters of Latin jazz and traditional song.

Beyond the recording studio, Crouse has collaborated with leading regional musicians and become celebrated for honoring jazz and blues legends while bringing her own soulful perspective to every performance.

Personnel: Marina Crouse (vocals); Others TBA

events.title: Lila Downs
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
With “a stunning voice, a confident multicultural vision grounded in her Mixtec Indian roots” (LA Times), Lila Downs is one of Latin America’s most influential voices - an artist with a singular sound, magnetic stage presence, and recognized with multiple GRAMMY and Latin GRAMMY Awards, including the recipient of the 2026 Latin GRAMMY Lifetime Achievement Award. With her new album Cambias mi Mundo (You Change My World), she returns to the Miner stage for four nights after her hugely successful run of Día de los Muertos performances at the Paramount. The album marks a return to her essence: deeply committed to global causes, passionate, intimate and celebratory.

She made her major label debut with 1999’s jazz-informed La Sandunga, and her contributions to the 2002 Frida Kahlo biopic Frida elevated her status to that of a major international star. Downs has become recognized worldwide as a global ambassador for Mexico’s folkloric traditions and champion for the preservation of native Mexican culture, recording songs in indigenous Mayan, Nahuatl, Trique, and Purépecha languages.

Rooted in Oaxaca and shaped between Mexico and the United States, she weaves Mexican tradition with jazz, cumbia, folk, and contemporary rhythms. Her music is both celebration and conscience; she turns each concert into a gathering—intimate, fearless, and deeply human.

Personnel: Lila Downs (vocals); Josh Deutsch (trumpet, keyboards); George Saenz (trombone, accordion); Rafael Gomez (guitars); Luis Guzman (bass, synthesizer); Sinuhe Padilla (jarana, bajo, zapateado); Lautaro Burgos (drums); Nakeiltha Cambpell (percussion)

events.title: Dominican University Faculty Lecture Series - From Snake Oil to Social Media
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: From Snake Oil to Social Media: Deciphering Medical Truths in the Wellness Age Our desire for health, longevity, and bodily control makes us susceptible to the promise of quick cures. Today’s wellness landscape prioritizes algorithmic advice, viral detoxes, and AI diagnoses. Relying on unverified remedies is far from new. To understand how we navigate medical "truth,” we can look across history, psychology, and modern healthcare systems to see how information spreads, why it takes root, and who stands to profit. Join Dominican University faculty members Vivian Delchamps Wolf, Sophie Whynacht, and Michael Skolnik for a panel exploring the boundaries of medicine, wellness, and trust. Drawing connections from 19th-century medicines to modern influencer culture and politicized care, the panelists will examine why mythical cures persist, how digital culture shapes our relationship with our bodies, and how patients can build critical information literacy in an age of digital noise. The 90-minute session will feature short presentations from each panelist followed by an open audience Q&A. This conversation brings together interdisciplinary faculty from Dominican University: Vivian Delchamps Wolf (PhD, UCLA English, 2022) is an Assistant Professor of English at Dominican University of California (DUC). Her research and teaching focus upon 19th-century American literature and feminist disability studies. Peer-reviewed articles have been published or are forthcoming in the J19: The Journal of 19th-Century Americanists, Disability Studies Quarterly, the Emily Dickinson Journal, and Literature and Medicine. Her monograph, Resisting Diagnosis: Women’s Disability Literature of the 19th-Century U.S., argues that women writers use literature to challenge patriarchal medicine and racialized pathologization and to imagine expansive forms of care. Wolf serves or has recently served professional organizations including the Modern Language Association, C19: The Society of Nineteenth-Century Americanists, and the Health Humanities Consortium through conference organizing, committee work, and disability advocacy. Sophie Whynacht, Ph.D. is an Assistant Professor of Psychology at Dominican University of California, where she leads the Body Image and Stigma (BIAS) Research Lab. She is also a Licensed Psychologist and the founder of Embodied Psychotherapy and Counseling, a private practice specializing in the clinical treatment of eating disorders, body image concerns, and related mental health challenges. Her academic work centers on the psychological and sociocultural factors that drive body image issues, weight stigma, and disordered eating. Dr. Whynacht’s writing on body image is featured on Psychology Today. Michael Skolnik , Academic Director of the Healthcare Executive MBA program, who brings deep expertise in healthcare leadership, institutional strategy, and the systemic challenges patients face when navigating medicine, technology, and misinformation. Vivian Delchamps Wolf, Sophie Whynacht, Ph.D., Michael Skolnik - photos courtesy of the organizers

events.title: Builders Night
events.location: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco + 540 Cafe
events.description:
Builders Night is a weekly space where people show up with a project, work side by side, and leave with more momentum than they could have generated alone. It exists because building can be lonely, and the hardest part is often simply showing up consistently.
The tone is focused and warm. Mostly quiet during deep work, with moments of spontaneous connection when someone gets unstuck or discovers something worth sharing. This is not a networking event or a lecture. The work itself is the center of the night.
Flow
6:30–6:45 PM: Arrival and settling in
6:45–6:55 PM: Opening circle: name, what you're working on, one intention for the night
6:55–8:30 PM: Deep work sprint: quiet, side-by-side building
8:30–9:00 PM: Share-back: what you built, learned, or got stuck on. Make an ask, offer what you know, and support each other.
Who This Is For
People working on software, hardware, businesses, creative projects, writing, design, research, art, anything you're trying to make real. Come if you want accountability, momentum, and the energy of working alongside others. First-timers and regulars both welcome.
What to Bring
Laptop, notebook, sketchbook, instrument, whatever tools your project requires. Come with something to work on, or come ready to figure out what that is.
Norms
Respect the deep work sprint by keeping conversation low during focused time. Share-back is how we learn from each other: share what you built, ask for what you need, and offer what you can. Everyone participates.
Rally (rallysf.com) is an AI builder community in SF.

events.location: City Lights, 261 Columbus Ave, San Francisco
events.description: FREE Part of Words Around the World Sponsored by Center for the Art of Translation Co-presented with City Lights and New York Review of Books First published in 1922, and rich in startling neologisms and other forms of verbal play, Trilce is a blazingly vivid revelation of what poetry can be, at once a love poem, a poem of erotic urgency and frustration, a poem of family life, of political fury, a lament for the dead, a work of intense privacy and an address to the world. In this new edition of Trilce from NYRB—the recipient of the prestigious Premio Valle Inclán for the best translation from Spanish into English—the translators Helen Dimos and William Rowe accompany each poem with a gloss. Their incisive commentary on these legendarily challenging poems opens them up to new understanding while inviting readers to find their own pathways to and through them.

Or Watch on YouTube Live/Link Available Soon

About The Names of the New World
The highly anticipated second novel from the award-winning author Kawai Strong Washburn: an extraordinary saga of resilience and ambition in the face of a chaotic world.

A ferocious superstorm strikes Minneapolis, obliterating swaths of the city in minutes. In its wake, three people forge an unlikely bond that will shape their lives for the next twenty-five years: Naomi, a lawyer and an amateur MMA fighter, is a Pacific Islander transplanted to the Midwest for her less-than-satisfying career; Amaré, an investment banker, has grand designs for all the money he’s about to make; and Raheem, a diesel mechanic, is nearly paralyzed by the storm and struggles to save his business.

When Naomi recognizes that energy companies are responsible for the climate-induced superstorm—and the many more to come, potentially dooming her island homeland—she initiates a bitter legal battle, one that culminates in her appointment to a powerful political office in DC with the potential to prevent future tragedies. Yet her rise risks a burgeoning romance with Amaré, whose own ambitions test Naomi’s ethical limits, while Raheem’s fate as a small business owner depends on the couple’s growing power.

Following his much-loved debut, Kawai Strong Washburn turns his gift of mythic sight to the oceans and landscapes we so often overlook in the name of progress. Ranging from the American Midwest to the nation’s halls of power to islands across the Pacific, The Names of the New World is a startling, energetic, and optimistic vision of how we’ll live in this era of overwhelming change.

About Kawai Strong Washburn
Kawai Strong Washburn was born and raised on the Hāmākua coast of the Big Island of Hawai‘i. Today, he lives with his wife and daughters in Minneapolis. Sharks in the Time of Saviors, his first novel, was a New York Times Notable Book and winner of the PEN/Hemingway Award.

events.location: Mrs. Dalloway's, 2904 College Ave, Berkeley, CA 94705
events.description: Join us at Mrs. Dalloway's Bookstore on Monday, October 19 at 7:00 PM when Marina Richie comes to the store to present her new book Feathered Forest: Aloft with Birds in Ancient Trees . Marina will sign copies of her book after the presentation. A narrative of perception change, memoir, and kinship, Feathered Forest is a soaring ode to birds and wild trees. “Luminous. You can feel the deep, cool shadow of the great Western forest and the flicker of bird color flashing across it. The kind of book that inspires contemplation but also action.” —Bill McKibben, author of Here Comes the Sun Beginning with an ascent of a 200-foot-tall Douglas-fir with a bird biologist, author Marina Richie leads us from her home in Central Oregon into the ancient forests of Cascadia, a bioregion which rivals the Amazonian rainforest in significance for climate and biodiversity. Birds are guides to intricate and imperiled communities thriving at every level, from understory to midstory to overstory. They steer us to cool havens within multilayered, centuries-old groves that are critical refugia in a time of climate crisis. Their songs and flights show us what we must protect for the future of threatened birds, forests, and humankind.

events.title: Bonnie Garmus with Kate Schatz - Peck & Peck
events.location: Calvary Presbyterian 2515 Fillmore St San Francisco, CA 94115
events.description: We are honored to welcome Bonnie Garmus to Calvary Presbyterian for an evening celebrating the release of Peck & Peck. The author of the global sensation Lessons in Chemistry returns with an irresistible, delightful, and tender literary novel set in the publishing world of 1980s New York City about a young man whose life turns upside down when he is hired by the most prestigious, secretive, and dysfunctional poetry journal in the world: the renowned Peck & Peck . Bonnie will be joined in conversation by Kate Schatz, a feminist author, educator, and public speaker. Presented in partnership with Calvary Presbyterian San Francisco A MOST ANTICIPATED BOOK FOR COUNTRY LIVING AND BOOKPAGE Find originality. Reward creativity. Burn the rest. It’s 1982, New York City. Crime is on the rise, muggings are in the streets, and Batter Gray, recent college graduate with a skill that no one wants—an “ear” for poetry—is worried about his future. While all of his friends have real jobs, he’s folding T-shirts at the Gap. As for love? No. Not unless you count Sallie Mae, the student loan tyrant. He hears from Sallie all the time. But when Batter gets a dream job at Peck & Peck , the most prestigious poetry quarterly in the world, his life moves into the literary fast lane. Soon Batter is knee-deep in the secret war between the two Editors in Chief, the famous Peck brothers—twins and enemies—as well as being privy to the private affairs of their thirty-nine editors, whose professed mission is the same: Find originality. Reward creativity. Burn the rest. And by burn, they mean incinerate. Because at Peck & Peck , “good” isn’t good enough, “interesting” doesn’t cut it, plagiarists aren’t tolerated, and parolees run the mailroom. Still want to submit your poem? Go with God. Welcome to another dazzling and unforgettable novel from Bonnie Garmus. If you loved Lessons in Chemistry , you will love Peck & Peck. “Tender-hearted… [Garmus] packs the novel with the antic humor and colorful characterizations that drew readers to her debut. There’s much to cherish in this charming tale.” — Publishers Weekly “[People are] hungry for another Bonnie Garmus hit. Thankfully Peck & Peck is here to feed those gaping mouths... With the trappings of the literary world, and the heart of a bildungsroman, Peck & Peck vows to fill the void in all our hearts with a needed dash of wit and poignancy." — Literary Hub, Most Anticipated Books of 2026, Part Two “Garmus applies her unique comic sensibility to the story of Batter Gray… charming… with some really lovely things to say about poetry.” — Kirkus "I'm absolutely over the moon about Bonnie Garmus' new novel. It is EXACTLY what I needed to read right now. Charming, uplifting, soulful, and original, this is the perfect successor to Lessons in Chemistry . If you loved Elizabeth Zott, you will adore Batter Gray. Book clubs will adore this novel. I loved it." —Kristin Hannah, #1 New York Times bestselling author of The Nightingale and The Women Bonnie Garmus is a coffee-dependent American novelist. Her debut novel, Lessons in Chemistry , was a Good Morning America Book Club Pick, a Goodreads Choice Best Book of the Year, spent nearly two years on the New York Times bestseller list and was named by Times readers as one of the top 100 books of the 21st century. Translated into over forty languages, Lessons in Chemistry was honored with sixteen international literary awards and made into an Apple TV limited series. Peck & Peck is her second novel. KATE SCHATZ is a feminist author, educator, and public speaker. She's the New York Times- bestselling author of the "Rad Women" book series; the novel Where the Girls Were; the 33 ⅓ book Rid of Me: A Story ; and Do the Work: An Anti-Racist Activity Book , co-written with W. Kamau Bell. She lives in the Bay Area with her wife, three children, and pets. In all she does, Kate is committed to sharing radical histories that shine light on the marginalized people who've truly made America (and the world) great: the people of color, the immigrants, the queers, the punks, the weirdos, the artists, the workers, and the women.
