events.title: Going to the Moon?
events.location: Clio’s Books, 353 Grand Avenue, Oakland, CA 94610, Oakland, CA
events.description: What Earthlings should expect. · The Moon inspires myth, song, poems, and journeys. Mysterious and elegant, it lights the night, generates tides, and affects Earth’s climate. Since human beginnings, the Moon has been our common heritage owned by no one, shared by all peoples; a revered object, not a destination. And yet, in the present, global forces race and compete to claim lunar resources. What plans are underway? Do the peoples of our planet have a say? Can poetry, or any art, make a difference? What will it be like to look up at an inhabited Moon? When she found out that a poem would be sent to the Moon in a time capsule, former Santa Clara County Poet Laureate Sally Ashton realized her resistance to the forces of lunar exploitation is in very real conflict with her excitement at being part of a lunar landing. Her book, Going to the Moon , explores this paradox and the fraught relationship of humans with conquest and the non-human world. Join her conversation with Dr. Persis Karim, faculty emerita at San Francisco State University, as they ponder the Moon, consider the progress of the lunar goldrush, and explore our role in the revived race to space at this transformational moment in human history—the colonization of the Moon. Sally Ashton is a poet, writer, teacher, and editor-in-chief of DMQ Review , an online journal featuring poetry and art. Publishing in three genres, she is the author of five books of poems including Listening to Mars (Cornerstone Press, 2024). San José State University faculty emerita, she continues to teach workshops locally and online. Her poem “4.6 Billion Years” is archived on the Moon with the Lunar Codex. Her new book of nonfiction, Going to the Moon , (Duke University Press, 2026) explores her personal experience and the global race to space. www.sallyashton.com Persis Karim , Ph.D., is poet, essayist, editor, and retired San Francisco State University professor of Comparative and World Literature. She is the editor of three anthologies of Iranian diaspora writing and her poetry has appeared in a number of national and local publications. Co-director of the documentary, “The Dawn Is Too Far: Stories of Iranian-American Life,” she is also an avid birdwatcher, moonchaser, and gardener.

events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Grammy Award winner and three-time Tony Award nominee Shoshana Bean can currently be seen starring in The Lost Boys musical on Broadway. Prior to that, she starred in Alicia Keys' hit Broadway musical, Hell's Kitchen . Her portrayal of ‘Jersey’ earned her a Grammy Award, her second Tony Award nomination, a Drama League Award nomination, and a Drama Desk nomination. Her performance in the Public Theater’s Hell’s Kitchen Off-Broadway production earned her a Lucille Lortel Award nomination. In 2022, she received Tony and Grammy nominations as well as an Outer Critics Circle Award Nomination and a Drama League Award Nomination for her role as Susan Young opposite Billy Crystal in Broadway’s Mr. Saturday Night . She previously starred on Broadway as the first replacement for Elphaba in Wicked and as Jenna in Waitress . Her six independent studio albums and EPs have landed her on top of the iTunes and Billboard charts, including the peak position of #1 on the Billboard Jazz Chart. She has sold out concerts around the globe and lent her voice to countless films and television shows, including The Boys , Sing, Sing 2, Enchanted , Jersey Boys , Glee, and Galavant . Shoshana made her Broadway debut in the original cast of Hairspray, appeared Off-Broadway in the 2000 revival of Godspell, and appeared in Songs for a New World at City Center Encores. Regionally, she appeared in Sarah Silverman’s The Bedwetter , won an IRNE Award for her performance as Fanny Brice in Funny Girl , and earned a Jeff Award nomination for her portrayal of CeeCee Bloom in the pre-Broadway musical production of Beaches . She has appeared in Bloodline, Bill and Ted Face the Music , Great Performances: 50 Years of Broadway’s Best, and recently filmed a solo concert special for PBS.

events.title: Julian Lage Quartet
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Davies Symphony Hall
events.description:
Feat. John Medeski, Jorge Roeder, & Kenny Wollesen

“One of jazz’s breezier virtuosos, possessed of an unflappable technical facility and a seemingly boundless curiosity” (The New York Times), guitarist and former SFJAZZ Resident Artistic Director Julian Lage returns with original music from his newest Blue Note album Scenes from Above with his superlative quartet including organ star John Medeski, bassist Jorge Roeder and drummer Kenny Wollesen.

Transcending his prodigious beginnings — which include being the subject of the Oscar-nominated documentary film Jules at Eight, a GRAMMY Awards performance at 13, and faculty status at the Stanford Jazz Workshop at 15 – Santa Rosa-born guitarist Julian Lage has emerged as a stunningly accomplished creative force and savvy bandleader. Making his recording debut in duet with bluegrass luminary David Grisman, Lage demonstrated deep maturity and intellectual acuity from the start, impressing jazz vibraphone innovator and discerning talent scout Gary Burton, who recruited the then 16-year-old for his quartet in 2004. Lage’s trajectory has been linear since then, embracing jazz, pop, country, bluegrass, and acoustic folk with equal élan.

His fifth Blue Note release, 2026’s Scenes from Above, marks the debut of this new quartet and a set of original compositions specifically written with this formidable set of all-stars in mind.

Personnel: Julian Lage (guitar); John Medeski (organ); Jorge Roeder (bass); Kenny Wollesen (drums)

events.title: Erin French with Tanya Holland - The Lost Kitchen Volume 3
events.location: Calvary Presbyterian 2515 Fillmore St San Francisco, CA 94115
events.description: We are honored to welcome Erin French to Calvary Presbyterian for an afternoon celebrating the release of The Lost Kitchen Volume 3: Seize the Supper. The stunning third volume in The Lost Kitchen cookbook series from Erin French, award-winning restaurant founder and New York Times -bestselling author of Finding Freedom, The Lost Kitchen, and Big Heart Little Stove Erin will be joined in conversation by Tanya Holland, the author of Tanya Holland's California Soul: Recipes from a Culinary Journey West [A Cookbook]. Presented in partnership with Calvary Presbyterian San Francisco Erin French brings you perfectly crafted meals for dining outside the box and living in the moment in her latest cookbook, Seize the Supper . From her beloved home and restaurant, the Lost Kitchen in Freedom, Maine, come hearty main dishes balanced with crisp, bright salads and sweet and spiced desserts. Her well-rounded meals are made with true comfort and seasonal nourishment that are perfect for carrying you from shorter days and late-afternoon feasts to snowy winter nights sitting by the fire to picnics that welcome the blooming of spring. In simple yet rewarding steps, French shares delicious recipes that will foster connection and inspiration around the table. From flavorful salads and sides such as Soft Polenta with Honey & Ricotta, Roasted Asparagus with Tarragon Vinaigrette, and Pear, Walnut & Blue Cheese Waldorf to rich mains including Provençal Roasted Chicken, Fried Halibut, and Buttermilk Leg of Lamb with Fennel & Orange to irresistible desserts like Baked Vanilla Spice Puddings with Cherry Compote and Rosemary Maple Ice Cream, French’s recipes are filled with warmth, heart, and meaningful tips for embracing the joy of now. Erin French , a born-and-raised Mainer, is the owner and chef of the Lost Kitchen, a fifty-seat restaurant in Freedom, Maine, listed among Time ’s World’s Greatest Places to visit and Bloomberg ’s " 12 Restaurants Worth Traveling Across the World to Experience.” With two New York Times bestsellers to her name, Finding Freedom and Big Heart Little Stove , Erin is featured in three seasons of the Magnolia Network series The Lost Kitchen and Getting Lost with Erin French, where she travels the country searching for new experiences and culinary inspiration, streaming on HBO Max. Erin knows the importance of simple pleasures found in gathering for thoughtfully prepared meals. Her love of Maine and sharing its delicious heritage with dinner guests has garnered several James Beard nominations and the attention of The New York Times , Martha Stewart Living, The Wall Street Journal, The Boston Globe, and Food & Wine, as well as NPR’s All Things Considered, CBS News Sunday Morning, and Today. After more than a decade in business, the Lost Kitchen has become so much more than a restaurant, now boasting a farmer’s market, overnight cabins, a retail shop, and a café called the Little Lost Kitchen. Tanya Holland is an award-winning chef, restaurateur, cookbook author, educator, media personality, wine professional, and U.S. State Department Culinary Diplomat. A French-trained chef with more than four decades of experience, she is best known as the founder and executive chef of Oakland’s Brown Sugar Kitchen, where she earned national recognition for modern African American cuisine and thoughtful, inclusive hospitality. Holland is the author of Brown Sugar Kitchen and Tanya Holland’s California Soul and has appeared on Food Network’s Melting Pot, Bravo’s Top Chef, and other programs. Her work has been featured in The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, Bon Appétit, Gourmet, House Beautiful, and O, The Oprah Magazine. She serves on the James Beard Foundation Board of Trustees and, in 2026, joined the University of Virginia as a Senior Lecturer. Across food, wine, teaching, media, and diplomacy, Holland creates memorable experiences that bring people together around the table. events.title: Somatic Breathwork Journey: Emotional Release, Clarity & Nervous System Reset
events.location: 550 Laguna St, San Francisco + Full Studio
events.description:
Come breathe, release, & reset...
Somatic Breathwork is an embodiment experience designed to take you out of your thinking mind and into the deep intelligence of your body — where true healing, clarity, and release happen. It allows your body to express and discharge stored emotions, stress, and old narratives that may be weighing you down.
Somatic Breathwork uses circular connected breathing together with rhythmic music to produce a cathartic emotional release. This release may be in the form of moving, shaking, yelling, crying, laughing, or simply deep stillness.
It gives your body the opportunity to express emotions or actions that may otherwise be unacceptable in modern social settings, allowing your nervous system to process traumas and restore balance.
Using the breath, you’ll engage your body’s innate ability to heal — sweeping out any defenses, blockages, restrictions, or pains that hold you back from showing up as your truest self.
Many participants experience profound emotional release, newfound clarity, and a grounded sense of calm even after a single session.
This experience is designed to:
Move you out of your mind and into your body's electrical network
Release stuck energy, emotions, or trauma responses
Reset your nervous system into grounded calm and clarity
Break old patterns and reconnect you to your authentic self
Increase compassion, presence, and emotional resilience
Support cathartic release in a safe, guided container
Participants often report:
Deep emotional release
More calm, peace, and clarity
Release of anger, grief, frustration, or stagnant energy
Increased presence, awareness, and intuition
Breakthrough insights about their life, patterns, and purpose
Feeling more open, soft, and connected to themselves and others
What to expect:
✨ Opening Check-In & Introduction
✨ 60-Minute Guided Somatic Breathwork Journey
✨ Integration & Optional Group Sharing
Whether you're seeking release, clarity, a reset, or simply a moment to reconnect with yourself — this session is for you.
Please bring a journal and water bottle, and wear comfortable clothes.
NOTE: Please be on time for this session — doors will close promptly and there will be NO LATE ENTRIES!
About Anna Bolender:
Anna Bolender is a certified Somatic Embodiment & Intuitive Life Coach, Somatic Breathwork and Quantum Wellness Practitioner, Reiki Master, and lifelong student of holistic health and well-being.
Through her coaching programs and workshops, Anna guides others to return home to themselves — releasing what keeps them stuck, reconnecting with their body and inner wisdom, and creating real, lasting transformation from the inside out.
Blending somatics, energy healing, quantum wellness, and mindset work, she helps clients break free from self-sabotaging patterns, repattern their nervous system, and cultivate simple daily rituals that support a fulfilling, grounded, and aligned life.
Anna’s mission is to empower others to feel connected, alive, and radiant — no matter what life brings.
Instagram: @annaalexbee
Podcast: RADIANT YOU (available on all podcast platforms)
Website: www.annabolender.com

events.title: Katie Sanders: Ortiz’s War
events.location: The Commonwealth Club of California, San Francisco
events.description: Peter Ortiz’s path to becoming the most battle-decorated member of America’s first spy agency—and one of the most decorated Marines of World War II—was unlike any other. Born in New York and raised in both California and France, he was a merchant seaman, dude ranch manager, race car driver, lion tamer, circus performer, and Hollywood stuntman and actor. As a teenager, Ortiz ran away from boarding school to join the French Foreign Legion. He fought in North Africa against Saharan tribesmen, and on the front lines against the Germans in 1940, where he was badly wounded and captured.

events.description: Join this month's All Things Romance Book Club at Books Inc. Mountain View. This month we're reading Grim Tidings: A Novel by B.K. Borison! About the book: From #1 New York Times bestselling author B.K. Borison comes a new whimsical, haunting romance. When a runaway grim reaper tries to save a life, she clashes with a skeptical Guardian, forcing them to form an unlikely partnership beyond the grave. Darcy Moore is tired of death. Which would be fine and good ... if she wasn’t a Grim Reaper. Determined to outrun her designation as the villain, Darcy decides she won’t be dragging her next assignment to the underworld. She’ll be saving him instead. Unfortunately for Darcy, there’s a complication in her plan. Guardian Angel Gabriel Aetos doesn’t tolerate threats to his little corner of the world, and a Grim Reaper showing up at his bar is as deadly as it gets. But when he realizes Darcy is not as she seems, Gabriel must decide if he can trust his growing feelings or hold on to his long-standing grudge. But magic doesn’t come without consequences. And the Department of Hauntings & Spirits will eventually come calling for their missing Reaper. A spooky yet simmering enemies-to-lovers tale to keep you warm this fall.

events.title: THE BIG PICTURE PRESENTS: Halloween & Halloween III: Season of the Witch
events.location: Balboa Theatre, 3630 Balboa St, San Francisco, CA 94121
events.description: A special Halloween double feature hosted by Sean Fennessey, Amanda Dobbins and friends of The Big Picture podcast. The evening will begin with an introduction before Halloween (1978) followed by an extended post-film conversation and brief intermission before Halloween III: Season of the Witch (1982). Halloween (1978) On a cold Halloween night in 1963, six-year-old Michael Myers brutally murdered his 17-year-old sister, Judith. He was sentenced and locked away for 15 years. But on October 30, 1978, while being transferred for a court date, a 21-year-old Michael Myers steals a car and escapes Smith’s Grove. He returns to his quiet hometown of Haddonfield, Illinois, where he looks for his next victims. Halloween III: Season of the Witch (1982) When a terrified toy salesman is mysteriously attacked and brought to the hospital, babbling and clutching the year's most popular Halloween costume, an eerie pumpkin mask, doctor Daniel Challis is thrust into a terrifying Halloween nightmare. Working with the salesman's daughter, Ellie, Daniel traces the mask to the Silver Shamrock Novelties company and its founder, Conal Cochran. Ellie and Daniel uncover Cochran's shocking Halloween plan and must stop him before trick-or-treaters across the country never come home in this terrifying thriller. Doors at 5 PM/Show at 6 PM Tuesday, October 20 Doors at 5 PM/Show at 6 PM

events.title: Alexander Maksik with Anthony Marra - Passengers
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: A taut, emotionally gripping, and surprisingly funny novel about a father and daughter stranded in an airport at the end of the world, Passengers is a story of loving across gaps—between parent and child, between things said and unsaid—and what happens when the outside world finally mirrors the chaos within. ​This is Maksik’s most timely and accomplished novel yet! Ivan is a solitary man in his seventies, set in his ways and haunted by the failures of his past. His smart and cynical daughter, Nina, is in the twilight of her twenties and has long kept a distance from her sentimental father. But when Ivan proposes a trip to Europe in hopes that it will bring them closer together, Nina reluctantly agrees. They meet at LAX, where their departure is delayed. And delayed again. And again. As the hours drag on, their sharp, caustic and wide-ranging conversation reveals a lifetime of misunderstandings, unhealed wounds, and stubborn love. Soon more flights are canceled, security tightens, airport staff grow evasive, and it becomes clear to Ivan and Nina that something is wrong. They begin to suspect that they’re being held prisoner—sequestered from the world without explanation. At last, the surreal starts to overtake the mundane, and their need to escape—and to protect each other—turns increasingly urgent. What begins as a piercing portrait of a father and daughter becomes a novel of eerie suspense, as Nina and Ivan navigate not only their fractured bond but also a world teetering on the brink of collapse. A story of loving across gaps—between parent and child, between things said and unsaid—and about what happens when the outside world finally mirrors the chaos within, Passengers is Maksik’s most timely and accomplished novel yet. “A beautiful, unsettling novel about the depths of love, the burden of nostalgia and the maddening impossibility of translating feeling into language.”—Imbolo Mbue, author of Behold the Dreamers “A novel of surpassing beauty and among the most moving portraits of parenthood I’ve ever read. It also happens to be exceptionally funny, propulsive and wise—an example of the alchemy that occurs when a writer finds the work he was born to pursue. Passengers is Alexander Maksik’s masterpiece.”—Anthony Marra, author of Mercury Pictures Presents "Maksik's best to date. Passengers is really about how we're all trying to get somewhere different, somewhere better--to a place where we can be closer to those we love, during this one precious life we have. I could not put it down."—Adam Ross “This is the stuff we live for—a spinning dream of a book, pure heart-in-your-throat magic. I can’t say this enough: read it, today, now.”—Paul Yoon, author of The Hive and the Honey , winner of The Story Prize “ Passengers is a tour de force that reveals just how deeply two ordinary people can love one another…This superb novel takes on the very hardest stuff of life and never looks away.”—Ben Fountain, author of Billy Lynn’s Long Halftime Walk “Maksik’s latest, Passengers, is propulsive and fierce and uncompromising in its humanity. And funny too, in often unexpected ways. Also, my kind of book in that it doesn’t waste a single word. It's kept me intensely good company these past few weeks. Seems to me: A necessary book for these batshit times.”—Peter Orner Alexander Maksik is the author of You Deserve Nothing , a New York Times and IndieBound bestseller; A Marker to Measure Drift , which was a New York Times Notable Book, as well as a finalist for the William Saroyan Prize and Le Prix du Meilleur Livre Étranger, and the basis of the 2023 motion picture Drift ; Shelter in Place , named one of the best books of the year by the Guardian and the San Francisco Chronicle; and The Long Corner , a New York Times Book Review Editor’s Choice, and named one of the best books of the year by The Australian . Maksik is the recipient of a Guggenheim Fellowship, a Pushcart Prize and The Sewanee Review’s Andrew Lytle Prize. His books have been translated into a dozen languages. Anthony Marra is the author of the New York Times bestselling novels A Constellation of Vital Phenomena and Mercury Pictures Presents , as well as the story collection The Tsar of Love and Techno. Alexander Maksik - photo courtesy of the author; Anthony Marra - photo credit Paul Duda Event details: This event will be hosted by Book Passage at our Corte Madera store. Free Admission / Open Seating Following the presentation, there will be a signing line or a meet-and-greet. For any questions regarding our events, please contact us at books@bookpassage.com .

events.title: Erin French Book Signing • The Lost Kitchen Volume 3: Seize the Supper
events.location: Omnivore Books on Food, 3885a Cesar Chavez St, San Francisco, CA 94131
events.description: Erin French , a born-and-raised Mainer, is the owner and chef of the Lost Kitchen, a fifty-seat restaurant in Freedom, Maine, listed among Time’s World’s Greatest Places to visit and Bloomberg’s "12 Restaurants Worth Traveling Across the World to Experience.” With two New York Times bestsellers to her name, Finding Freedom and Big Heart Little Stove, Erin is featured in three seasons of the Magnolia Network series The Lost Kitchen and Getting Lost with Erin French, where she travels the country searching for new experiences and culinary inspiration, streaming on HBO Max. Erin knows the importance of simple pleasures found in gathering for thoughtfully prepared meals. Her love of Maine and sharing its delicious heritage with dinner guests has garnered several James Beard nominations and the attention of The New York Times, Martha Stewart Living, The Wall Street Journal, The Boston Globe, and Food & Wine, as well as NPR’s All Things Considered, CBS News Sunday Morning, and Today. After more than a decade in business, the Lost Kitchen has become so much more than a restaurant, now boasting a farmer’s market, overnight cabins, a retail shop, and a café called the Little Lost Kitchen. The Lost Kitchen Volume 3: Seize the Supper- The stunning third volume in The Lost Kitchen cookbook series from Erin French, award-winning restaurant founder and New York Times bestselling author of Finding Freedom, The Lost Kitchen, and Big Heart Little Stove. Erin French brings you perfectly crafted meals for dining outside the box and living in the moment in her latest cookbook, Seize the Supper . From her beloved home and restaurant, the Lost Kitchen in Freedom, Maine, come hearty main dishes balanced with crisp, bright salads and sweet and spiced desserts. Her well-rounded meals are made with true comfort and seasonal nourishment that are perfect for carrying you from shorter days and late-afternoon feasts to snowy winter nights sitting by the fire to picnics that welcome the blooming of spring. In simple yet rewarding steps, French shares delicious recipes that will foster connection and inspiration around the table. From flavorful salads and sides such as Soft Polenta with Honey & Ricotta, Roasted Asparagus with Tarragon Vinaigrette, and Pear, Walnut & Blue Cheese Waldorf to rich mains including Provençal Roasted Chicken, Fried Halibut, and Buttermilk Leg of Lamb with Fennel & Orange to irresistible desserts like Baked Vanilla Spice Puddings with Cherry Compote and Rosemary Maple Ice Cream, French’s recipes are filled with warmth, heart, and meaningful tips for embracing the joy of now.

events.title: FOREIGN INTRIGUE BOOK CLUB: A Corpse in the Koryo
events.location: Books Inc. Laurel Village, 3515 California St, San Francisco, CA 94118
events.description: Do you like to travel? Experience a country through the eyes of a local? Try the food of another country? Join the Foreign Intrigue Book Club at Books Inc. Laurel Village! Meets on the third Tuesday of the month. This month we're reading A Corpse in the Koryo by James Church. Sit on a quiet hillside at dawn among the wildflowers; take a picture of a car coming up a deserted highway from the south. Simple orders for Inspector O, until he realizes they have led him far, far off his department's turf and into a maelstrom of betrayal and death. North Korea's leaders are desperate to hunt down and eliminate anyone who knows too much about a series of decade's-old kidnappings and murders---and Inspector O discovers too late he has been sent into the chaos. This is a world where nothing works as it should, where the crimes of the past haunt the present, and where even the shadows are real. Author James Church weaves a story with beautifully spare prose and layered descriptions of a country and a people he knows by heart after decades as an intelligence officer. ". . . an outstanding crime novel. . . . a not-to-be-missed reading experience. " --- Library Journal (starred) "Inspector O is completely believable and sympathetic . . . The writing is superb, too . . . richly layered and visually evocative." --- Booklist (starred) ". . . an impressive debut that calls to mind such mystery thrillers as Martin Cruz Smith's Gorky Park . . . ." --- Publishers Weekly (starred)

events.title: KISS & TELL LITERARY SALON
events.location: Books Inc. Alameda, 1344 Park St, Alameda, CA 94501
events.description: Meet featured authors Lexi Sharabianlou and C.C. Dador, this month's featured authors of the Kiss & Tell Literary Salon, celebrating their new books, The Blue Moon Café & 24-Hour Occult Emporium, and Merry Ex-Mas! Hosted by Rebecca Hunter and Addie Woolridge and members of Bay Area Romance Writers Association. Please join us. About the The Blue Moon Café & 24-Hour Occult Emporium: A magical witness protection program, a town in need of saving, and a sorceress-in-training . . . oh, and the human woman she's not supposed to fall for. The Blue Moon Café has a little bit of everything (except, you know, decent coffee). In the tiny town of Pine Hollow, barista and fledging sorceress Talula Smith runs The Blue Moon Café & 24-Hour Occult Emporium, aka the worst coffee shop in town. The café's horrible reputation hides its true purpose: providing new identities and safe passage to at-risk magical beings while keeping humans far, far away. That is, except for town local Dahlia. Dahlia's devastating dimples, addiction to Talula's cocoa recipe, and keen observation skills keeps the smitten barista scrambling to ensure that her magical abilities (or, lack thereof) stay a secret. But when big game hunters start preying on magical beings, her powerful sorceress mother is called away to track them down, leaving Talula and her barely-there magic in charge of The Blue Moon. With the impending Samhain festival to organize, magical refugees to help, half of the town turning against her, and her ever-growing feelings for Dahlia, Talula's magical destiny feels further away than ever. But as the hunters set their sights closer to home, it'll be up to Talula to master her craft, trust her heart, and bring her magical and human communities together . . . before she loses everything she loves. "You're in for a treat! The Blue Moon Café & 24-Hour Occult Emporium is deliciously delightful and absolutely adorable! I loved it!" -Sarah Beth Durst, New York Times bestselling author of The Spellshop Lexie Sharabianlou earned her Master’s in creative writing from the University of Edinburgh. She has sold cupcakes, taught high school English Lit, and written audio tours for zoos. By day, she’s a copywriter for a makeup company (yes, she gets to name the makeup). By night, she writes stories about magic, food, and falling in love. She lives in the San Francisco Bay Area. Tell your dog she says hi. She is the author of The Blue Moon Café & 24-Hour Occult Emporium and The Blue Moon Diner & Drive-In Movie Theater. About Merry Ex-Mas : Fall in love. Again. And again. This irresistible holiday time loop rom-com is perfect for fans of In a Holidaze and The Holiday Swap . Which man from her past will make the perfect Christmas present? All Marygrace Silva wants for Christmas is a date to impress her big, boisterous family. Instead, a disastrous setup and an awkward run-in with her ex-best friend Robbie leave her wishing for a holiday miracle. Then a slip on the ice lands her in a time loop—reliving Christmas Eve with a different ex each time. There’s Flynn the finance bro, Dale the rising music star, Jamie the fitness influencer. Glamorous? Sure. Perfect? Not so much. Between caroling and cookie baking, Marygrace is checking exes off her list—but somehow, Robbie keeps showing up too. Maybe the love she’s been searching for has been there all along ... With a sprinkling of sugar and just the right amount of spice, this romance about family, friendship, finding your voice, and the promise of “what-if” is a holiday treat you won’t want to miss. “An enjoyable time-loop holiday rom-com about choosing one’s own path and finding one’s voice.” — Library Journal C.C. Dador writes heartwarming romances filled with big laughs, cozy vibes, and sexy moments you’ll want to snuggle up with again and again. Like her work in event planning, C.C. is all about swoon-worthy details and making sure her readers are having their best day. C.C. is a first generation Filipino American and currently lives in the D.C. metro area. When she isn't writing, C.C. can be found enjoying seasonal drinks and hunting for the perfect gifts for friends and family.

events.title: Sonny Buttar's The Daughters of Rosebud, with Vanessa Hua
events.location: Bookshop West Portal 80 West Portal Ave San Francisco, CA 94127
events.description: Join us to celebrate Sonny Buttar's stunning debut novel, The Daughters of Rosebud . This multigenerational family saga will leave you at once heartbroken and hopeful. Sonny will be joined in conversation by Vanessa Hua , bestselling author of Coyoteland. This event is FREE to attend. Seating is first-come, first-served. (RSVPs are optional, but encouraged for our planning purposes.) You don't need to have read the book beforehand to enjoy the event, but we do recommend reserving your copy ahead of time. About the Book: In a heart-wrenching debut, author Sonny Buttar delivers a multigenerational family saga at once haunting and hopeful. Teacher Salma Chaudhry lives a quiet life, avoiding all attachments. But after a call from her estranged father, the protective shell she lives within starts to crack and the trauma she's buried for eighteen years emerges. Salma and her older sister Asma were inseparable growing up in small-town Rosebud. While Asma was bold and fearless, Salma tried to keep the peace in their fractured family. But amid their mother's decline and their parents' rigid expectations, Asma makes a choice that tears the family apart. The fallout changes everything--and forces Salma to choose between her sister and her parents. Salma has spent years trying to forget. But as she recollects her past and considers reconciliation with her father, a young student opens a surprising connection to Asma's past. In finally facing her history, Salma finds the bravery to love and hope again. The Daughters of Rosebud is a powerful exploration of sisterhood, family loyalty, and the courage it takes to heal. About the Author: Sonny Buttar was born in Pakistan and raised in England and the American Midwest. Her first novel, The Daughters of Rosebud, will be released in October 2026. About the Conversation Partner: Vanessa Hua is the nationally bestselling author of Coyoteland, A River of Stars and Forbidden City , and the story collection Deceit and Other Possibilities , a New York Times Editors’ Pick. A National Endowment for the Arts Literature Fellow, she has also received a Rona Jaffe Foundation Writers’ Award, the Asian/Pacific American Award for Literature, a California Arts Council Fellowship, and a Steinbeck Fellowship in Creative Writing, as well as honors from the de Groot Foundation, the Society of Professional Journalists, and the Asian American Journalists Association. She was a finalist for the California Book Award, the Northern California Book Award, and the New American Voices Award. Previously, she was an award-winning columnist for the San Francisco Chronicle . She teaches at the Warren Wilson MFA Program, Sewanee Writers Conference, and elsewhere. This fall, she is an Ann-Getty Endowed Visiting Artist-Scholar at the University of San Francisco. Her debut narrative nonfiction, Uprooted, is forthcoming.

events.title: Alain Damasio: Horde of the Counterwind
events.location: Telegraph Hill Books, 1501 Grant Ave, San Francisco
events.description: FREE, $10–$15 suggested donation Part of Words Around the World Sponsored by Center for the Art of Translation Co-presented with Villa Albertine In 2004, Alain Damasio’s Horde of the Counterwind: An Epic Voyage to the Upper Reaches gained acclaim as France’s genre-defining sci-fi odyssey of the 21st century, inspiring the celebrated video game Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 and igniting the imaginations of millions around the world. Now, this seminal work appears in English translation for the very first time, offering even more readers the opportunity to experience a masterpiece of epic scope and visionary world-building in which twenty-three adventurers climb endlessly against the wind that plagues their desolate homeland. Their only purpose: identifying the mysterious source where eight centuries of past climbers have tried and failed. Join Damasio and Horde’s English translator, Alexander Dickow, for a conversation moderated by award-winning writer and translator Edward Gauvin. Doors at 6:30pm.

events.title: Pitchapalooza
events.location: Gilman Brewing, 912 Gilman St, Berkeley
events.description: Pay what you can ($15 suggested) for guaranteed seat; FREE to walk-ups (space depending) Pitchapalooza is American Idol for books (only kinder and gentler). Twenty writers, selected at random, will pitch their book for one minute only! Judges (including The Book Doctors, Arielle Eckstut and David Henry Sterry) will help you improve your pitch, not tell you how bad it is. Judges critique everything from idea to style to marketplace potential, and authors gain concrete advice as well as a greater understanding of the publishing industry. Whether potential authors pitch themselves, or simply listen to the critiques, Pitchapalooza is educational and entertaining for one and all. At evening’s end, the judges will pick a winner. Like the dozens of Pitchapalooza winners who have gone from talented amateurs to professionally published authors, this lucky participant will receive an introduction to an agent or publisher. Doors at 6:30pm.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong

events.description: The Cornley Polytechnic Drama Society is back, and this time they’re taking on Peter Pan . It’s their most ambitious production yet, complete with flying rigs, sword fights, and a very real crocodile problem. What could possibly go wrong? As technical mishaps pile up and tempers flare, the cast battles to keep the show on track while everything around them spectacularly falls apart. Lines are forgotten, scenery refuses to cooperate, and rivalries spill onto the stage in real time. From the creators of The Play That Goes Wrong , this riotous comedy delivers nonstop mayhem, perfectly timed chaos, and the kind of theatrical disaster you have to see to believe.

events.title: Grace Krilanovich in conversation with Kate Folk
events.location: Tally Ho! Books, 3941 Piedmont Ave, Oakland, CA 94611
events.description: 20 years after her cult classic The Orange Eats Creeps, Grace Krilanovich ("singular, mistress of a pitiless psychedelic noir lurking in our american woods just beyond the back window.” —Steve Erickson) returns with new novel Acid Green Velvet, in which two young vagabonds in 19th century California navigate class struggle, fringe societies, American identity, and the threat of a menacing man. Also scary dogs. She'll be here in conversation with Kate Folk (“[Folk] writes witty, cinematic fiction that merges familiar scenarios with uncanny menace [and] capably captures the lunacy of the moment we’re living through.”—San Francisco Chronicle) whose latest novel, Sky Daddy, is already a cult classic and an indie bookstore favorite as well!

events.title: Witches of the Wheel — Lindsay Merbaum
events.location: Fabulosa Books, 489 Castro St, San Francisco, CA 94114
events.description: In her metaphysical mystery Witches of the Wheel , Lindsay Merbaum weaves a spellbinding tale of mythology, bartending, and queer belonging. Gold grows up knowing only a few things about herself: something lets her see ghosts and read her neighbors' secrets, and her mother seems to hate her. But when she strikes out on her own, she stumbles into a job at The Wheel, a literally-underground lesbian bar where a coven gathers every Thursday and each entrance requires a painful sacrifice. It feels like the first place she's belonged. But the bar, its patrons, and its history are more complicated, and more dangerous, than Gold ever realized. As she entangles herself in her new community, she learns more about herself than she wanted to know--and attracts an ancient goddess's deadly attention.

events.title: Memoirs: Writing Against Silence or Erasure
events.location: Mrs. Dalloway's, 2904 College Ave, Berkeley CA 94705
events.description: FREE, $10–$15 suggested donation Co-presented with Memoir Nation These four memoirists are, in different ways, writing into spaces where their experience has been minimized, misread, or actively suppressed. Judy Juanita's California Fever Dream spans sixty years of writing focused on Black activism and feminism. In I Love You So Many, journalist Terria Smith shares lessons learned from a career sharing stories about the richness of Native people’s lives. Elena Dudum's They Told Me Back Home Would Be Beautiful is a call to action against institutional silencing and censorship. Finally, Caroline Paul has spent her career writing women into adventure narratives that historically excluded them, most recently in Why Fly. Brooke Warner and Grant Faulkner, co-founders of the Memoir Nation podcast and online community, will guide a compelling discussion on the power of this truth-telling form. Doors at 6:30pm.

events.title: Brian Evenson: Phantom Limb
events.location: City Lights, 261 Columbus Ave, San Francisco
events.description: FREE, $10-15 suggested donation Co-presented with City Lights Master of literary horror Brian Evenson returns with a long-awaited follow-up to his 2016 novel, Last Days. After destroying the headquarters of an underground amputation cult, a burned and battered Kline finds himself in a holding cell. When he enlists the help of an ex-cop to commute his prison sentence, Kline inadvertently tangles with a schism of the very cult he sought to destroy. Can Kline investigate the sect’s ritualistic murder spree without getting lured into their ranks? Frigid and precise, Phantom Limb interrogates our notions of wholeness, fate, and the lengths we are willing to go to connect with a higher power. In conversation with Colin Winnette.

events.title: Celebrating 50 Years of Publishers Group West
events.location: Clio’s, 353 Grand Ave, Oakland
events.description: FREE, $10–15 suggested donation Sponsored by Publishers Group West From a shoestring investment of $500 in 1976, Berkeley-based Publishers Group West grew, by the turn of the century, into the US’s largest distributor of independent presses. Since then, it’s maintained its focus on resilience, innovation, and a passion for independent publishing—not to mention the value of throwing a really great party. We’ll toast to a half-century of PGW, which continues to distribute books for 150 publisher clients, including some beloved local presses. How does PGW’s history reflect the larger story of Bay Area publishing? And how can lessons learned over the past fifty years inform its future? Join PGW founder Charlie Winton, executive VP Sean Shoemaker, VP of field sales Elise Cannon, and Litquake co-founder Jack Boulware for a walk down memory lane—and stick around to buy a beverage or two from Clio’s on-site bar. Doors at 6:30pm.

events.title: Smith Dobson Quartet
events.location: The Dawn Club, San Francisco
events.description: Drummer/Vibraphonist/Saxophonist Smith Dobson V has been performing in the Bay Area for nearly twenty years. Originally from Santa Cruz, Ca., Dobson is a member of an important Jazz family. His father, the late Smith Dobson IV, was a world renown Pianist and director of the Jazz series at the Garden City in San Jose for over twenty years, where he accompanied artists’ like Art Pepper, Stan Getz, Bobby Hutcherson, Harold Land, Chet Baker, Red Norvo, Tal Farlow, and Lee Konitz, to name a few. Also in the family, Grandfather Smith III is a Jazz Accordionist, Grandmother Norma, Mother Gail, and Sister Sasha are all Jazz Vocalists. The family often performed as a group at the Garden City, and other venues, as well as many local schools and workshops. As a child, Smith V had the opportunity to study with legendary Jazz Drummer Albert “Tootie” Heath, who said of his pupil, “He has the talent, determination and persistence as a musician, combined with the dedication necessary to succeed… improvisational skills totally advanced, excellent sensitivity, both solo and as an accompanist… my most talented student!” Smith has had the honor of working with some of the great Jazz artists, locally and internationally, such as Bobby Hutcherson, Red Rodney, John Handy, Sheila Jordan, Red Holloway, Pete and Conte Condoli, Phillip Harper, Hal Stein, Noel Jewekes, Ben Goldberg, Graham Connahs’ Sour Note Seven, Darren Johnstone, Will Bernard, and Kenny Brooks.

events.title: Nafissa Thompson-Spires: The Four Wives and Five Deaths of Richard Milford
events.location: Museum of the African Diaspora, 685 Mission St, San Francisco
events.description: FREE, $10-$15 suggested donation Co-presented with Museum of the African Diaspora From the author of the multi-award-winning, National Book Award–longlisted, “vivid, fast, funny, way-smart, and verbally inventive” (George Saunders) story collection Heads of the Colored People, comes a sly, spry, literary debut novel. We find ourselves in 1920s Oklahoma, just far enough out of Tulsa, just long enough after the Race Massacre of 1921. For as long as anyone can remember, the Milfords have led plentiful lives on the backs of the townspeople of Newville. On the ominous brink of the Great Depression and at the height of Prohibition, Richard Milford is an infamous moonshiner and womanizer who, it seems, finally crossed the wrong person at the wrong time. He’s dead and buried with only his women to mourn him, but a question remains: Who killed him, and why? Top suspects are his four “wives,” but as their stories burst to light, the very idea of a true story comes apart before our eyes. In conversation with Margaret Wilkerson Sexton. Doors at 5:30pm.

events.title: Nara Aziza Smith - Homemade
events.location: Book Passage Ferry Building 1 Ferry Building San Francisco, CA 94111
events.description: Join us as we welcome Nara Aziza Smith (@naraaziza), the best-dressed culinary creator in digital media, who is bringing her signature style to 80 delicious, homemade family-friendly recipes in her debut cookbook HOMEMADE. You may think you know Nara Smith—the glamorous outfits, the soothing ASMR voice, the beautiful family, the seemingly effortless approach to making food from scratch—but behind it all is a working mom with a relatable goal: preparing nourishing whole foods for herself and her family. Tickets include a copy of the book, the chance to get your copy personally signed, and a photo with Nara. A NOTE FROM NARA “This cookbook means the world to me. It holds the way I live and cook at home. It’s about slowing down, making things with your hands, and finding whimsy in the everyday. I’ve put together the recipes that I cherish so much and are things I either grew up eating or now serve to the people I love most. They’re simple, from scratch, and meant to be made and shared often.” —Nara Aziza Smith ABOUT THE BOOK You may think you know Nara Smith—the glamorous outfits, the soothing ASMR voice, the beautiful family, the seemingly effortless approach to making food from scratch—but behind it all is a working mom with a relatable goal: preparing nourishing whole foods for herself and her family. Nara grew up in Germany inspired by her grandmother’s cooking and the intention behind it. While working as a model, she soon met and married supermodel Lucky Blue Smith and started a family. When she was diagnosed with an autoimmune disease and eczema, she found that she could manage her symptoms by cutting out most processed foods. She turned her scratch-cooking expertise in a new curated direction while sharing her cooking online with compelling and elevated content. In her eagerly awaited and beautifully photographed first cookbook, Nara shares recipes from simple to complex, such as: Cinnamon Toast Squares , a quick breakfast beloved by Nara’s toddlers and better than anything you can find in stores Baked Fall Vegetable Salad with Miso-Sherry Dressing , a gorgeous salad that fuels Nara for long workdays Soy-Glazed Flank Steak with Plum Herb Salad , a beautiful, nourishing meal made from whole ingredients Lucky’s Oat Chocolate Chip Cookies , Nara’s husband’s recipe for the best American classic In HOMEMADE , Nara brings ease and elegance to the creation of homemade food—inspiring readers to elevate their own reality, in the kitchen and beyond in their daily life. Nara Aziza Smith is a globally recognized lifestyle creator, entrepreneur, and model. With a South African mother and a German father, she grew up in Frankfurt, first learning to cook by watching her father and grandmother in the kitchen. While working as a model, she met her husband, supermodel Lucky Blue Smith, and gradually began her growing curiosity for cooking from scratch and the intention behind it. Nara now resides in Connecticut with Lucky and their four children. She continues to build her authentic brand and grow her multi-million follower digital and culinary empire. events.title: Jad Youssef Author Talk • Lebnani: A journey through family, food & the flavour of Lebanon
events.location: Omnivore Books on Food, 3885a Cesar Chavez St, San Francisco, CA 94131
events.description: Jad Youssef is chef patron of the award-winning Lebnani in Reigate, Surrey which Jay Rayner highly praised in The Observer: ‘one taste of its gloriously zingy Lebanese flavours and you know you’re in the right place.’ Jad was born in Beirut during the Lebanese Civil War, the youngest of six siblings. He learnt to cook in his mother Khadija’s kitchen and in his father’s pastry shop before training at the Ecole Hoteliere in Beirut. After early work in local hotels and restaurants, he moved to Oslo in 2000 as Head Chef at Jeppe Restaurant, later relocating to London to lead the kitchen at Fakhreldine in Piccadilly and serve as Executive Chef at the Levant Group. In 2009, Youssef founded Yalla Yalla in Soho, one of London’s first Lebanese street food restaurants, expanding to Fitzrovia and Shoreditch in the following years. The restaurant received wide critical attention and achieved a cult following. His signature dish, Sawda Djej (chicken livers with pomegranate molasses), developed an equally devoted following and was named one of Time Out London's "100 Best Dishes." After time in Hong Kong, Youssef and his wife Aga returned to the UK to open Lebnani in Reigate, Surrey, in 2020. The restaurant was named Best Restaurant in Surrey by Muddy Stilettos in 2024, awarded an AA Rosette, and was the recipient of the Be Inclusive Hospitality Middle Eastern Food Award in 2025. Jad has also appeared at Meatopia, Taste of London, and Taste of Hong Kong, served as a judge on Celebrity MasterChef UK, appeared on BBC's MasterChef, and worked with Miele among many others. His work has been featured in The Times, The Observer, Financial Times, The Guardian, and numerous other publications. Lebnani - In Lebnani , celebrated chef Jad Youssef invites readers to experience the warmth, generosity and soul of Lebanese cooking through recipes passed down through generations of his family. In his debut book, Jad returns to the dishes and memories that shaped his life in Beirut and beyond, celebrating Lebanese food as it is truly lived and eaten. Featuring 84 authentic recipes from his family’s kitchen in Lebanon and his award-winning restaurant Lebnani in Surrey, the book reveals secret spice blends, time-honoured techniques and beloved family dishes that bring people together around the table. Chapters echo the rhythm of daily life - Lebanese Mornings, Mezza at Home, Tabkha (everyday meals), Mashawi (grills), Sandwiche (street wraps), Helweyet (sweets) and Namlieh (the pantry) - reflecting the meals and moments that shape Lebanese identity. Family stories are woven throughout, tracing how food sustained Lebanese families through conflict, change and celebration. From gathering wild za’atar to mornings spent collecting trays of freshly baked mana’eesh, Jad’s memories root Lebanese cuisine in gratitude, connection and resilience. With evocative imagery and heartfelt storytelling, Lebnani offers a rich portrait of a culture where food, memory and family life are deeply intertwined.

events.title: Artificial Intimacy: Sherry Turkle and A.I.
events.location: YBCA Screening Room, 701 Mission St, San Francisco
events.description: Co-presented with Yerba Buena Center for the Arts Sherry Turkle has spent decades studying how digital technologies isolate us from one another. Now, in her latest book, Artificial Intimacy: Who We Become When We Talk To Machines, the psychologist who pioneered our understanding of human-computer relationships explores the seductive and beguiling nature of chatbots presented as “perfect” companions. How does their popularity point to existing wells of deep loneliness in our current culture, and how does increasing reliance on a one-sided digital ear affect users’ ability to maintain offscreen relationships with other humans? In conversation with New Yorker cartoonist Amy Kurzweil, whose graphic novel Artificial: A Love Story suggests an alternate path in which A.I. isn’t used as a human connection substitute, but rather a tool to support and deepen the real-world relationships we already have. The conversation is part of Free Wednesdays at YBCA, which offers extended gallery hours, hands-on afternoon art-making, and special evening programs—all for free. Doors at 6:00pm.

events.title: Surreal or real? A conversation between two writers on their styles and what inspires them.
events.location: Medicine for Nightmares, 3036 24th St, San Francisco, CA 94110
events.description: A conversation between fiction writers Donna Miscolta and Marianne Villanueva about where stories come from, what scares them and what makes them laugh when they’re creating characters and situations. Marianne Villanueva, author of four books of dystopian, surreal, and fantasy fiction, will pose questions to Donna Miscolta about her new realist novel Ofelia and Norma . Miscolta, author of four books of fiction, will ask Villanueva about her latest story collection Residents of the Deep . Donna Miscolta’s latest of four books of fiction is Ofelia and Norma . Her stories, essays, and book reviews have appeared in dozens of journals and anthologies. A recording of her work is part of the Library of Congress PALABRA Archive, a showcase for Latin American and Latino writers. She recently moved to Spain and blogs monthly at donnamiscolta.com . Marianne Villanueva is the author of the story collections Ginseng and Other Tales from Manila , Mayor of the Roses , The Lost Language , and Residents of the Deep . A recipient of fellowships from Stanford University and the California Arts Council, she is writing her first novel, set in 16th-century Spain and the Philippines. In Ofelia and Norma , large-bodied twin sisters struggle for a sense of self. When Ofelia sheds pounds from long, solo walks, Norma senses their twinness slipping away. She slips away to an out-of-town college, leaving Ofelia for the first time, and each sister confronts alone life as a large person in an anti-large-person world. Ofelia, having previously lost weight without trying, now makes a deliberate effort to do so, resulting in a disaster that shakes her to her senses. Meanwhile, Norma escapes into her solitude by swimming laps in the college pool where she suffers an experience that sends her into emotional retreat. They move into careers, still estranged until a tender moment leads to the sharing of their secrets and revenge for what one of them has suffered. In Residents of the Deep , Marianne Villanueva explores human resilience in moments of extremity through a series of gripping stories. In “Ice,” two men confront their future in a barren, post-apocalyptic world where survival itself becomes the only meaning: “The point is, there is no point. You just keep going.” In Dumaguete, a young boy is forced to protect his mother, a role that threatens to unravel him. The title story follows a ship captain who discovers a submerged city and is thrust into a moral reckoning that challenges his understanding of responsibility. Clear-eyed and unflinching, these stories reveal the raw tenacity and unyielding spirit of humanity, even in the face of profound vulnerability and hardship.

events.title: Assimilation

events.description: A Word for Word and Z Space production · Stories by E.L. Doctorow & Tatyana Tolstaya Presented by Word for Word and Z Space Directed by Rotimi Agbabiaka In “Assimilation” by E. L. Doctorow, Ramon is offered a promotion and cash which could pay for grad school – if he agrees to enter a green-card marriage with his boss’s niece. When he agrees, he gets more than he bargained for. “Smoke and Shadows” by Tatyana Tolstaya centers on a Russian professor living in the U.S., navigating her professional life, her intimate relationships, and the mysteries of culture. Told with Tolstaya’s sharp, restrained wit, the story zeros in on the experience of living in a new culture, and the confusions and imbalance that can cause. What does it mean to assimilate? These two writers offer two very different perspectives.

events.title: Haunted Oakland
events.location: Clio’s Books, 353 Grand Avenue, Oakland, CA 94610, Oakland, CA
events.description: An evening of storytelling with Dead Reckoning · There is an Oakland where the apparition of a woman appears in the mist at Joaquin Miller Park after dark, where the doorbell at the two-story Clarke Mansion at 16th and Castro begins clanging incessantly just after midnight, and where the Camron-Stanford House, one of the last Victorian homes that once lined Lake Merritt, has urged more than one living visitor to "get out." These are just a few of the stories that blur the line between the living and the dead that have lingered in Oakland for generations, passed between those who have witnessed things they still can't explain. Join us for an evening of storytelling with Beth Winegarner and Courtney Minick, hosts of Dead Reckoning : the podcast where death isn't the end of the story. The hosts of the San Francisco-based podcast will share local ghost stories, explore the legends surrounding some of Oakland's most notable residents, and uncover the histories that linger long after death. As the veil grows thin, come prepared to share your own story if you've experienced a haunting in the East Bay. You never know who, or what, might be listening. Courtney Minick is a storyteller with a career spanning technology, law, politics, and creative media based in San Francisco. She is the creator of Here Lies a Story a multi-platform storytelling project that explores history, folklore, and the way the buried past continues to shape our present including the Lost Cemeteries of San Francisco series . Beth Winegarner is a journalist and writer who’s contributed to the New York Times, the New Yorker, The Guardian, and many others. She is the author of several books, most recently San Francisco’s Forgotten Cemeteries: A Buried History and Swim Poems , and she is the co-host of the Dead Reckoning podcast.

events.title: Cookbook Night! Get the inside scoop from Nik Sharma and a Cookbook Editor
events.location: Bookshop West Portal 80 West Portal Ave San Francisco, CA 94127
events.description: Bookshop West Portal is delighted to welcome Nik Sharma , America's Test Kitchen Editor-in-Residence and author of Veg-Table and The Flavor Equation , to celebrate his new cookbook, The Fundamentals of Flavor . Joining Nik in conversation will be Sarah Billingsly , the Publishing Director of Food & Lifestyle at Chronicle Books ! Join us to get the inside scoop about what goes into making a cookbook, from the vision to the recipes to the design and publishing. This is a very special opportunity to get a peek behind the curtain of the publishing industry and to meet two marvelously creative food enthusiasts! We are so excited to be working alongside Chronicle Cooks! They bring together home cooking enthusiasts and cookbook lovers in one flavorful community. Discover behind-the-scenes author content, be the first to explore upcoming titles, and enjoy curated recipes and samples that spark creativity in the kitchen through the Chronicle Cooks Substack . This event is FREE ! Though we encourage RSVPing for our planning purposes. Seating is first-come, first-served. About the Cookbook Acclaimed cookbook author, America's Test Kitchen Editor in Residence, and molecular biologist Nik Sharma brings his deep scientific knowledge, delicious recipes, and stunning photography to home cooks with Fundamentals of Flavor . These 100 recipes deepen your understanding of how fire, earth, air, and water improve your kitchen techniques and the flavor of your meals. Building on the science-forward thinking and accessibility, Nik Sharma's latest cookbook brings fascinating technical know-how to exciting everyday recipes. In these pages, Sharma explores the four powerful elements of nature and their profound influence on how we cook, delving into such topics and dishes as: Fire: How caramelization deepens the flavor of Caramelized Shallot and Feta-Labneh Dip Earth: How salt's minerality brings crispness to Salt-Baked New Potatoes with Gochujang Vinaigrette Air: Why drying out cookie dough results in perfect Extra Rich Chocolate-Cinnamon Crinkle Cookies Water: Why sous vide is the best way to cook a hearty, tender loaf of Icelandic Rye Bread And much more. With more than 150 evocative photographs and 20+ infographics that simplify scientific principles for visual learners, this is a beautiful, foundation-building reference book for home cooks who approach their meals with a hunger for knowledge and big flavor. Accessible Recipes: This book packs big flavor while remaining highly cookable. From the basics like how to make your own Hot Honey, Homemade Set Yogurt, and Cultured Butter to mastering more complex dishes such as Eggplant, Burrata, and Mozzarella Pitadinas; Steak with Porcini-Thyme Sauce; and Cinnamon Churro Ice Cream with Dulce de Leche, these recipes help you achieve spectacular, complex flavors. Science for the Home Cook: As a former molecular biologist, Sharma wants you to eat delicious food while understanding how you made it happen--so you can make it again! This volume is packed with information on how roasting, baking, boiling, stir-frying, and other cooking techniques help you put delicious meals on the table, plus handy tips for better understanding how to get the most from your kitchen equipment, such as testing your oven temperature to make sure it's accurate. About the Author: Nik Sharma is an accomplished chef and cookbook author. Veg-Table won the 2024 Golden Poppy Award and was named a Best Cookbook of the Year by NPR, The Los Angeles Times , Epicurious , Vice , Food Network , Good Housekeeping , and more. His previous books, The Flavor Equation and Season , were also named to multiple Best Cookbook lists, including The New York Times , Eater , Food & Wine , Forbes , Saveur , Bon Appetit , Food52, The San Francisco Chronicle , The Los Angeles Times , The Boston Globe , The Chicago Tribune , CNN Travel, and many others.

events.title: Seth Fleisher's "THE FARTHER SHORE"
events.location: Mrs. Dalloway's, 2904 College Ave, Berkeley, CA 94705
events.description: Local author Fleisher presents his gripping historical novel based on the life of little-known naturalist Eugene Marais. Join us at Mrs. Dalloway's Bookstore on Wednesday, October 21 at 7:00 PM when Berkeley author Seth Fleisher comes to the store to launch his new novel The Farther Shore. Seth will be joined by Mindela Ruby for the conversation and will sign copies of his book after the presentation. The Farther Shore is a sweeping novel about fathers and sons, memory and race, and the dangerous fictions that shape us—inspired by the true story of Eugene Marais, one of history's most extraordinary and forgotten minds. Southern Africa, 1890s. Eugene Marais is a brilliant naturalist and iconoclastic journalist whose evolving theories about memory, addiction, and the hive mind are decades ahead of their time. But when tragedy strikes, he abandons his newborn son and disappears into a remote South African forest—leaving behind his child and his conscience, and embarking on research that will haunt both their lives. Thirty years later, his son Charles—now a professor of ancient Buddhist history at Harvard—discovers that his father's work has been weaponized. University faculty are mining Eugene's research to bolster theories of racial hierarchy, and their ambitions are growing darker by the day. Accompanied by a mysterious Jewish graduate student whose fate is becoming entangled with his own, Charles will make an epic journey across continents to heal his fractured past and stop a sinister plot quietly taking root at the world's most prestigious institution. Set across two interlocking timelines—from the British concentration camps of the Boer War to the rising shadow of the Third Reich and WWII— The Farther Shore is a heart-breaking, exhilarating novel about memory, love, and identity, and about the vast distances we’ll travel to find our way home. SETH FLEISHER is an American author whose work has appeared in the Bellevue Literary Review, Pearl, the Journal of Anthropological Research, and elsewhere. Based in Berkeley, California, he has worked with the World Bank Group and other NGOs in South Africa, India, and more than 40 other countries, and co-founded Walk the Walk USA, a U.S.-based democracy initiative to counter the rising tide of authoritarianism. A former Fulbright scholar in Sri Lanka, Seth did Ph.D. work at Harvard in Buddhist social history, a fellowship at Harvard's Center for the Study of World Religions, and a B.A. in literature at Swarthmore, where he and his wife first met in a Chaucer seminar. The Farther Shore is his first novel. MINDELA RUBY is an author, editor and educator. Her novel, Mosh It Up , is about Bay Area garage punk rock. Her prose and poetry appear in T he Dribble Drabble Review, Terrain.org, Santa Monica Review, WomenArts Quarterly, Coachella Review, Rivet: and other outlets plus the anthology Unmasked with a foreword by Gloria Steinem. Her works have been Pushcart and Best Of the Net nominated, including her poetry series Africa Safari Journal (in haiku) (with footnotes). She holds a Ph.D. from UC Berkeley. Her new memoir is currently on submission.

events.title: Vigdis Hjorth: Repetition
events.location: Telegraph Hill Books, 1501 Grant Ave, San Francisco
events.description: FREE, $10-$15 suggested donation Sponsored by Norway House and Center for the Art of Translation Part of Words Around the World From International Booker Prize– and National Book Award–nominated author Vigdis Hjorth comes her latest novel finally translated into English, Repetition. As winter approaches in Norway and the daylight dwindles, a chance encounter prompts a novelist to reexamine her past. The seismic events following her sixteenth birthday return with haunting vividness, exposing a story both utterly familiar and desperately strange. It was the year she first got drunk, the year she first had sex with a boy. She was watched like a hawk by an anxious mother and a silent, distant father. It was a year of typical teenage fixation and typical teenage frivolity, and of all the usual parental fretting. Until something else took hold, and her family made an unspoken decision and a terrible sacrifice. Only now, decades later, can these events come close to being comprehended. In conversation with Daniela Blei.

events.title: Adam Grant - Vibe (City Arts & Lectures)
events.location: Sydney Goldstein Theater 275 Hayes St San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description: In this new work, Adam Grant illuminates the surprising science behind building strong connections. Adam will be joined in conversation with Mark Rober, the creator of the STEM subscription box company CrunchLabs. A vibe—a special connection between people that creates a spark—is an engine of happiness and success. Yet building meaningful ties is one of the most pressing problems of our time. As social media forces face-to-face interaction behind digital screens, communication gets outsourced to AI, and the world becomes more polarized than ever, our loneliness crisis shows no signs of slowing. To reveal how we can forge faster, stronger, and longer bonds, Grant offers groundbreaking studies, expert insights, and myth-busting stories. Filled with the eye-opening takeaways that have brought millions of readers to his books, Vibe teaches us that similarity is not necessary for solidarity, chemistry doesn’t always happen quickly, and closeness doesn’t always take time. Along the way, Grant introduces us to a crew of astronauts who learned to trust people they don’t like, a comedy troupe that swears by taking time apart as a key to staying together, a band that grew closer by learning to fight more, and a journalist who designed a gathering that led to seventy-eight marriages. He also opens up about his personal struggles to find his place as a shy introvert and the lessons that propelled his transformation into an enthusiastic convener. Through these examples and more, Grant uncovers the keys to creating deeper relationships and tighter communities. Vibe will change how you approach your interactions. No matter how good you are at connecting, you can always get better—and help others get better too. As an organizational psychologist, Adam Grant is a leading expert on how we can find motivation and meaning, and live more generous and creative lives. He is the author of Think Again, Give and Take, Originals, Option B, and Power Move s and host of the podcast WorkLife. events.title: RISING - Dara Kosberg's HOMECOMING
events.location: San Francisco
events.description: (Please do not bring infants to the show) “there’s a mystical and ever-moving line that solo shows sometimes cross into the realm of other worldliness and soul changing. I have seen probably thousands of solo shows and very few cross that line… Homecoming did, almost as soon as the show began.” – NoHo Arts District Dara gets the call that her mom is dying while studying abroad in Australia, and their already complicated mother-daughter relationship suddenly becomes a lot more complicated. On a winding path full of humor, absurdity, and connection, Dara faces the impossible question: How to make amends with a dead mom? What she discovers is deeply personal, universal, and surprisingly hopeful. Just because someone is gone, it doesn’t mean you can’t heal your relationship with them. Homecoming , nominated for Comedic Theatre at the 2026 Hollywood Fringe Festival, is a dark comedy about grief and identity. Moth StorySLAM winner Dara Kosberg shares her journey of losing a parent and finding herself. So please, laugh, cry, or just sit there silently questioning your own life choices. Directed by David Ford, Artist-in-Residence at The Marsh, with original direction by Iris Bahr (NYC debut) and David Crabb (LA debut). Dara Kosberg is a storyteller, comedian, writer, and actor. This year she debuted her solo storytelling show “Homecoming” to multiple sold-out audiences in NYC, LA, Chicago and Atlanta, including a sold-out run at the 2026 Hollywood Fringe Festival, where it was nominated for Comedic Theatre and selected for the StageCrafts’ Freeway Circuit. She’s a Moth StorySlam winner and has performed at San Francisco’s Punch Line Comedy Club and Brooklyn’s Union Hall. As part of the Reimagine End of Life arts festival in SF and NYC, she’s produced and performed in comedy shows about grief and loss that demonstrate the healing power of humor. She’s a Founding Team Member of both Reimagine and The Dinner Party, two innovative organizations working in the grief space. events.title: CLAY AIKEN
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Multi-platinum Idol alum known for his big voice · America first fell in love with Clay Aiken's extraordinary voice and undeniable charisma on the second season of American Idol . His journey on the show became a cultural phenomenon, drawing nearly 40 million viewers to the finale—one of the highest-rated live television broadcasts of the 21st century—and launching one of the most successful recording careers to emerge from the series. Aiken's first single, “This Is The Night,” made history as the first track by a brand-new artist to enter the Billboard Hot 100 at No. 1, selling nearly 400,000 copies in its opening week. The follow-up, “Invisible,” became a defining early-2000s pop hit, climbing to No. 37 on the Hot 100 and earning RIAA Gold certification. His debut album, Measure of a Man , then entered the Billboard 200 at No. 1 and went multi-platinum, cementing him as one of pop music's biggest new artists. Among his early highlights was the chart-topping holiday album Merry Christmas with Love , which still holds the record for the largest debut week ever for a holiday album in the SoundScan era. During the first seven years of his recording career, Aiken sold more than six million albums worldwide while becoming a fixture on television and one of the most successful touring artists to emerge from the early 2000s pop era. His rich tenor voice, emotional delivery, and ability to effortlessly move between contemporary pop, adult contemporary, inspirational music, and timeless standards have earned him a loyal, multi-generational audience. Aiken’s career has extended well beyond the recording studio, including a Broadway run in Monty Python’s Spamalot and a reunion with Ruben Studdard in 2018 for Ruben & Clay’s First Annual Christmas Carol Family Fun Pageant Spectacular Reunion Show , which The New York Times hailed as “a Christmas miracle.” The pair reunited once again in 2023 for a tour celebrating the 20th anniversary of their landmark American Idol season before competing together on Fox’s The Masked Singer in 2024 as The Beets. Beyond his music, Aiken has long been an advocate for children with disabilities. Drawing on his pre-fame experience as a special education teacher, he co-founded the National Inclusion Project in 2003, which has since helped thousands of kids with disabilities take part in camps, after-school programs, and community activities in more than 40 states. He also spent a decade as a UNICEF ambassador, traveling to Afghanistan, Somalia, Indonesia, Mexico, Uganda, and Kenya to advocate for children's protection and education. In 2026, Aiken began an exciting new musical chapter with the release of his first new music in eighteen years. His single "Rewind," written by Colton Avery and Grammy Award-winning producer and songwriter Dave Audé and produced by Audé, marked both a return to recording and a fresh creative direction. The release coincided with Aiken's homecoming to the American Idol stage, where he debuted the song during the season finale. As he reintroduces himself to longtime fans and new listeners alike, Aiken is once again focused on what has always defined his career: exceptional songs, unforgettable performances, and one of the most recognizable voices in popular music. "Rewind" is the first offering from a new full-length studio album, due at the end of 2026, his first in nearly two decades.

events.title: TOMMY DAVIDSON - PRE SHOW MEET & GREET (SHOW TICKET NOT INCLUDED)
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: SHOW TICKET NOT INCLUDED · PRE-SHOW MEET & GREET TICKETS ONLY - (FOR SHOW TICKETS CLICK HERE) Tommy Davidson’s exceptional range – from stand-up comedy and acting to versatile music accomplishments – has earned him a reputation as an extraordinary performer who delivers no matter the arena. Best known as one of the stars of the hit television show In Living Color, Davidson’s visibility has allowed him to become a household name known for his innovative talent across all platforms. His forthcoming series, Varnell (BET), in which he partners with Martin Lawrence, is one of the most eagerly anticipated of 2026 and premieres on Paramount+ on September 1 with a late August impressive rollout campaign. Davidson started his career as a standup comedian in Washington D.C., earning an ardent following. Spotted by major concert promoters, he was first booked as the opening act for Patti LaBelle, Kenny G, and Luther Vandross. It wasn’t long before he came to Hollywood and was headlining the biggest rooms and met Robert Townsend. This led to his movie debut, Partners in Crime, the conduit to Keenan Ivory Wayans, who offered Tommy the opportunity to audition. Soon, history was made with ILC. Davidson starred in Disney’s beloved animated series The Proud Family (2001-05) and is now the main star in its current animated series, “The Proud Family: Louder and Prouder” (Disney +) now in its fourth season. Other notable guest starring credits include comedy series Poppa’s House opposite Damon Wayans and The Neighborhood (both CBS), VH1’s hit A Black Lady Sketch Show; the Nick Cannon-directed Miracles Across 125th Street, Netflix’s Sarah Cooper: Everything’s Fine and many more. The multihyphenate is perhaps best known for starring in the groundbreaking sketch comedy series In Living Color and becoming a standout with his impressions of Sammy Davis Jr., Michael Jackson and other entertainment icons. His performance on the series resulted in three Showtime specials: On Strength of New York, Illin’ in Philly, and Takin’ it to DC. Davidson also hosted and starred in the network’s Chocolate Sundaes Comedy Show, as well as three seasons of ABC’s Vacation Creation. Davidson voiced the series regular role of Cream Corn in the Adult Swim action-comedy spoof Black Dynamite and has also made multiple guest appearances on hit shows like CBS’ Poppa’s House opposite Damon Wayans last year and just filmed BET’s award-winning Ms. Pat Show, consistently garnering Emmy nominations. He continues to co-headline with Katt Williams, Mark Curry and others, selling out large areas across the country. Davidson’s feature credits include Spike Lee’s Bamboozled, Morgan Creek’s Juwanna Mann, Ace Ventura II: When Nature Calls opposite Jim Carrey, and Strictly Business opposite Halle Berry among others. He also recently starred in the feature documentaries I Am Comic opposite Tim Allen and Lewis Black and Dying Laughing alongside Jamie Foxx, Kevin Hart, Amy Schumer and Sarah Silverman. His critically lauded music collaboration with one of the greatest bands in history, Earth Wind & Fire, for his fourth single, Stronger, last spring was a huge hit and catapulted him to the top of the Jazz charts. Previous collabs include Sweet Reunion with multi-Grammy winner Dave Koz and a host of others. He just won Best Jazz Single 2026 from the Hollywood Independent Music Awards for Come Take My Hand. Kensington Books published Davidson’s bestselling memoir Living in Color: What’s Funny about Me (2020), recounting his personal triumphs and incredible journey, which earned countless critical lauds.
