events.description: After her baby brother is abducted by a murder of crows, headstrong teenager Prue McKeel (Peyton Elizabeth Lee) launches a desperate rescue mission into the Impassable Wilderness—an enchanted forest hidden just beyond Portland, Oregon. Joined by her hapless but loyal classmate Curtis Mehlberg (Jacob Tremblay), Prue navigates a world of talking animals, bandits, and powerful figures driven by grief and ambition. As the pair is drawn into a conflict threatening the balance of the forest itself, Prue must discover the strength and belief she never knew she possessed. If she hopes to save her brother and protect Wildwood’s fragile future, she will have to risk everything. From Oscar®-nominated and BAFTA®-winning LAIKA, Wildwood is a sweeping adventure about love, sacrifice, and the magic that reveals itself when we dare to look beyond the familiar. events.title: All About San Francisco’s Stairways: No Walking Required! w/ Mary Burk & Alexandra Kenin
events.location: Bird & Beckett Books & Records, 653 Chenery Street, San Francisco
events.description: Take a comfy seat and celebrate the grand finale of SF Stairway Month hearing authors Mary Burk (Stairway Walks in San Francisco) and Alexandra Kenin (Urban Trails series, San Francisco, East Bay, Peninsula and South Bay). And sharpen your wits: We will have special SF stairway trivia game designed by moderator Liz Novoa (aka Instagram’s staircase queen). Mary and Alex will delight you with stories of SF’s known and hidden stairways, tell you about the best views, and share the whereabouts of secret gardens and more. Mary enjoyed a longstanding partnership with Adah Bakalinsky, co-authoring these now renowned stairway books until Adah’s passing at over 100 years old. Alex is the embodiment of energy. In addition to highlights from her book(s), she will share her detailed map of everything that you have wanted to know about SF’s roughly1000 stairways. This event is organized by Glen Park Beautiful (www.gpbeautiful.org). It is the 3rd annual SF Stairway Month, which was inspired by the creation of Glen Park’s Burnside Tiled Steps. The event is also featured in this inaugural year of Walktober, a month-long celebration of guided walks in San Francisco hosted by the Crosstown Trail.

events.title: Matthew Aldrich's "THE NATURAL ORDER" Book Launch And Signing
events.location: Mrs. Dalloway's, 2904 College Ave, Berkeley, CA 94705
events.description: The acclaimed screenwriter shares his provocative, propulsive debut about a billionaire tech visionary who creates a method to stop aging. Join us at Mrs. Dalloway's Bookstore on Tuesday, October 27 at 7:00 PM when local author and renowned screenwriter Matthew Aldrich comes to the store to launch his debut thriller The Natural Order . Matthew will be joined by Jason Headley for the conversation and will sign copies of his book after the presentation. Paul Whitmore, the world’s wealthiest man, begins each day on his secluded Marin, California, estate with a guided meditation, an hour of exercise, and a proprietary nutritional shake. These are the first three steps in a strict, monastic protocol known as the Method—a protocol which arrests the aging process. Paul is 122 years old, yet he appears no older than fifty; he has unlocked the secret to eternal life and is ready to bring his breakthrough to market. The world is poised to enter a post-aging future. But not everyone wants Paul to succeed, and his enemies are prepared to use violence to keep the Method from launching. Alone in his private Xanadu, Paul is well-insulated from the steady stream of death threats. But when a new threat emerges that targets Paul’s estranged son, Max, he is forced to take action. Max is eighty-five years old, living in a nursing home, and has not spoken to his father since he was a child. As far as he’s concerned, Paul Whitmore can rot in hell. Paul brings Max to his compound to protect him, but the real test soon becomes clear: can he care for his son? Is it ever too late to be a father? Is it ever too late to be a son? Unfortunately, the answers to these questions require time—and time is suddenly in short supply. The men who have threatened his son are coming for them both, and the gates surrounding his compound are less secure than he realizes. A page-turner with unusual depth and substance, The Natural Order grapples with issues of technology, mortality, and the true value of time. MATTHEW ALDRICH , a renowned writer for film and television, is best known for cowriting Disney Pixar’s Coco , which won two Academy Awards, including Best Animated Feature. His screenplay also won top prize at the International Animated Film Association Awards and was nominated for the Humanitas Prize. The Natural Order is his first novel. JASON HEADLEY co-wrote Pixar’s Onward and Lightyear and wrote and directed the SXSW Special Jury Prize-winning feature A Bad Idea Gone Wrong . His short films—including the viral videos It's Not About the Nail and F*ck That: An Honest Meditation —have been featured at Banksy's Dismaland, NBC's TODAY Show, SundanceTV, the TED Conference, Vimeo Staff Picks, and more. Jason is a Cinereach Fellow as well as a former IFP/Gotham Labs Fellow and member of SFFILM FilmHouse. He’s also been commissioned by Heineken, Sony, and Chrysler to write, direct, and produce original films

Adding a few of Abba’s live traits, such as great solos, musical numbers, and a complete live band with back-up singers, ensures an extra dimension unheard of in most similar productions. Dance, sing along, and enjoy the hits such as Dancing Queen, Chiquitita, Waterloo, Mamma Mia, The Winner Takes it All, Fernando, SOS, Take a Chance, Money Money Money, Knowing Me Knowing You, Super Trouper, Gimme Gimme Gimme, Voulez-Vous, and many more. With over 400 million records sold, ABBA is Sweden’s biggest export ever! When the Musical “Mamma Mia” hit the American Stages in 2000, it became an instant classic, and the ABBA tribute was born. ABBA is the greatest pop group of all time, only compared to Elvis and The Beatles. ABBA started in 1971 and ended as a group in 1982. Their music continues to be passed on from generation to generation and is loved by the whole world. Direct from Sweden, The Music of ABBA will deliver the closest ABBA experience you’ll ever get with some of Sweden’s most experienced and talented singers and musicians playing 100% live. The audience will be on their feet the entire show!!

events.title: Shannon Lee & Fonda Lee with Andrea Stewart - Mark of the Warrior
events.location: Book Passage Ferry Building 1 Ferry Building San Francisco, CA 94111
events.description: Join us for an upcoming event celebrating Mark of the Warrior —the explosive sequel to the instant New York Times bestseller Breath of the Dragon —featuring Shannon Lee and Fonda Lee in conversation with Andrea Stewart. Author Shannon Lee is the CEO of the Bruce Lee Family Companies and chairperson of the Bruce Lee Foundation. Fonda Lee is the award-winning, New York Times -bestselling author of a dozen fantasy and science fiction books. They will be joined by Andrea Stewart, the acclaimed author of The Bone Shard Daughter . Two brothers. Two nations. One destiny. Exiled as a traitor after the Guardian’s Tournament, Li Jun has vowed to retrieve the stolen Scroll of Heaven and to honor his father’s dying request: find his mother and twin brother, Sai. Fleeing into the East in search of their friend Ren, Jun and his longtime rival Yin Yue have no choice but to trust the two breathmarked women who saved their lives but who answer to the mysterious and draconian Council of Virtue that tore Jun’s family apart and banished him and his father a decade ago. Recovering the Scrolls of Heaven or Earth in order to stop the brewing war that threatens to devastate East and West alike isn’t Jun’s only seemingly insurmountable challenge. The twin he was separated from in childhood is now the High Keeper who resides in the Sun Pagoda, protecting the precious Scroll of Earth from all potential enemies…including Jun. The fate of the entire land hinges on an inevitable reckoning between brothers that will test their skills, their loyalties, and everything they thought they knew about themselves and the nature of destiny. Praise for Breath of the Dragon (Breathmarked, Volume 1) The instant NEW YORK TIMES and USA TODAY bestseller! "Packed with beautifully detailed fight scenes... Breath of the Dragon moves forward at a relentless, addictive pace, serving up dizzying plot twists one after another." - The Washington Post "The unpredictable plot twists and innovative magic system, which incorporates religious elements, are intriguing and, along with Jun’s realistic emotional development and reactions, create a gripping narrative...A complex, hard-hitting, epic martial arts journey." - Kirkus (starred review) "An intense tale full of action, with political intrigue galore...that absolutely does justice to its Bruce Lee inspiration." - Booklist (starred review) "Jun’s inability to stay still and his struggles with self-control will make him an instantly relatable character to teen boys, while the fast-paced ­nature of the tournament will keep any reader’s ­attention locked on the page...even the side characters have a compelling presence that heightens the stakes...[a] straight shot of pure ­shonen manga energy." - School Library Journal (starred review) "The authors extol Bruce Lee’s principles while continually raising the stakes and surprising readers with thoughtful twists in this relentlessly paced and exquisitely choreographed martial arts fantasy series opener." - Publishers Weekly As the steward of her father’s legacy, Shannon Lee serves as the CEO of the Bruce Lee Family Companies and the chairperson of the Bruce Lee Foundation. Her mission is to provide access to her father’s philosophy and life through education and entertainment. She is the author of Be Water, My Friend: The Teachings of Bruce Lee . An in-demand speaker, she has spoken at TED, TEDx, and CreativeMornings, among others. Shannon is the cocreator and host of the Bruce Lee Podcast, which has more than four million downloads, and the Executive Producer of Max’s Warrior series based on a treatment written by Bruce Lee. Fonda Lee is the award-winning, New York Times- bestselling author of a dozen fantasy and science fiction books, including the science fiction novel The Last Contract of Isako , and the modern epic fantasy Green Bone Saga, which has been translated into fifteen languages and named one of Time magazine’s 100 Best Fantasy Books of All Time. She is also the author of the novella Untethered Sky and several young adult novels. Fonda is a winner of the World Fantasy Award and the Locus Award, as well as a six-time winner of the Aurora Award and a finalist for the Nebula Award and the Hugo Award. A former corporate strategist and black belt martial artist, she hails from Canada and the Pacific Northwest and currently resides in New England. Learn more about her work at fondalee.com . Andrea Stewart is the Sunday Times bestselling author of The Drowning Empire trilogy and The Hollow Covenant trilogy, and works as a writing coach at The Novelry. The Bone Shard Daughter was her debut and was a finalist for numerous awards, including the Goodreads Choice Award and the British Fantasy Award. When her (admittedly ambitious) dreams of becoming a dragon slayer didn't pan out, she instead turned to writing books. She now lives in sunny California, and in addition to writing, can be found herding cats, looking at birds, and falling down research rabbit holes. Shannon Lee & Fonda Lee - photos courtesy of the publicist; Andrea Stewart - photo courtesy of the publicist Event details: This event will be hosted by Book Passage at our Ferry Building store. Free Admission / Open Seating There will be a signing line or meet and greet following the presentation.

events.title: Rebekah Moyer Author Event • Simple Kitchen Magic: Whole-Food Recipes and Remedies for a Holistic Life
events.location: Omnivore Books on Food, 3885a Cesar Chavez St, San Francisco, CA 94131
events.description: Rebekah “Ebby” Moyer- is a content creator, artist, and third-generation nutrition fanatic. She grew up in Cornwall, England, reading Brambly Hedge, picking wild elderflowers, and taking tinctures from the local herbalist. Her world-traveling foodie family inspired her love of flavor and cooking, and her kombucha-brewing mom sparked her interest in food’s healing “magic.” For the past 10 years, she has pursued her curiosity about holistic nutrition through independent study and all the teaching she can access, and she shares that journey on her social media channels. Through sharing, she hopes to encourage others in their health journeys and show that anyone can learn if they know where to look. She makes simple, nourishing meals using accessible, whole-food ingredients and home remedies for common ailments, and seeks to find the magic in every day while raising two rambunctious boys with her husband, Kandreas. Simple Kitchen Magic - Build a holistic, health-minded kitchen with over 100 nourishing recipes for healthy meals and natural remedies, from Rebekah "Ebby" Moyer On her popular social media channels, Rebekah Moyer makes simple, nourishing meals with accessible, whole-food ingredients. Not only are her recipes delicious, but they are also incredibly nutrient dense—in a single video, she’ll make kefir for gut-healthy probiotics, quick-pickled carrots as a fiber source for estrogen detox, kabocha squash for thyroid-friendly vitamin A, and more. Simple Kitchen Magic is Rebekah’s delicious recipes and warm, comforting nutritional advice in book form. The simple, whole-food recipes—like Curried Turkey Meatball Soup, Harissa Roasted Eggplant, and Black Bean Brownies—highlight functional ingredients to help you embrace food as medicine for a healthy lifestyle. Simple Kitchen Magic will leave you feeling like health is attainable, nutrition is simple, and cooking from scratch is doable. With whimsical, illustrated spreads on topics like adrenal health and menstrual cycle syncing, recipes for healing tinctures and basic kitchen remedies, this is the essential first book for any wannabe homesteader, ancestral eater, or cottagecore dreamer.

“This excavation of family, violence and shame is woven through with beautiful imagistic detail, and—unexpectedly—shades of hope. We loved the rich, textural detail of the story.”—The Booker Prize 2026 judges

“John of John is another mesmeric, transportive, vividly sensory and astonishingly textured novel from one of our greatest writers.”—Bernardine Evaristo

“Like Marilynne Robinson’s Gilead, Douglas Stuart explores the visible and invisible chains of love forged between a parent and child — as each grapples with his respective faith and complex humanity. Stuart’s characters yearn and yield tenderly as they struggle with fate and free will. The inimitable world of John of John is passionate, liberating, and gorgeous.“—Min Jin Lee

“Douglas Stuart’s John of John has the emotional range and sense of sympathy of his earlier books, but this book is special, it has an urgency, an immediacy, a brilliant sense of place, the drama of fierce emotion repressed, concealed and volcanically exposed.”—Colm Tóibín

About John of John
LONGLISTED FOR THE BOOKER PRIZE • AN OPRAH'S BOOK CLUB PICK • AN INSTANT NEW YORK TIMES BESTSELLER

From the Booker Prize-winning and New York Times bestselling author of Shuggie Bain and Young Mungo comes a vivid, moving novel following a young man returning to his Hebridean island home, a portrait of a father’s expectations and a son’s desires

Out of money and with little to show for his art school education, John-Calum Macleod takes the ferry back home to the Isle of Harris in the Outer Hebrides to find that little has changed except for him. He returns to the windswept croft and the two pillars of his childhood: his father John, a sheep farmer, tweed weaver, and lay preacher in the local Presbyterian church, and his maternal grandmother Ella, a profanity-loving Glaswegian whose steady warmth helped Cal weather the sudden departure of his mother.

Cal privately wonders if any lonely men might be found on the barren hillsides of home, while John is dismayed by his son’s long hair, strange clothes, and seeming unwillingness to be Saved. But Cal isn't the only one in the croft house who is keeping secrets. As lambing season turns to shearing season, the threads holding together the community together become increasingly frayed, and nothing will remain as it was before.

John of John is a singular novel about duty, passion, and the transformative power of the truth. It is a magnificent literary work that cements Douglas Stuart's reputation as one of our greatest novelists working today.

About Douglas Stuart
Douglas Stuart is a Scottish-American author. His New York Times bestselling debut novel Shuggie Bain won prizes including the 2020 Booker Prize and the Sue Kaufman Prize from the American Academy of Arts and Letters, was a finalist for the National Book Award and the PEN/Hemingway Award, and was named one of the "25 Best Books of the 21st Century" by the Sunday Times (UK). His second novel, Young Mungo, was a national bestseller, longlisted for the Andrew Carnegie Medal and a finalist for the British Book Award, and one of the most highly acclaimed books of the year. His stories are published in The New Yorker and his essays have featured on Literary Hub. He lives in New York City.

About Matthew Clark Davison
Matthew Clark Davison is co-author (with bestselling writer Alice LaPlante), of The Lab: Experiments in Writing Across Genre (W.W. Norton ’25) and author of the novel Doubting Thomas (Amble Press ’21), which was hailed as one of “46 Must-Read Books by Queer Authors” in Esquire Magazine. He is creator and teacher of The Lab :: Writing Classes with MCD, a non-academic school started in 2007. Matthew is a member of The Writers Grotto and has served on the board of Foglifter Journal and Press. Matthew is Emeritus Faculty in Creative Writing at San Francisco State University, where he also earned a BA and MFA.

events.title: Frish Brandt with Tony Bravo - Unfinished Business
events.location: Book Passage Ferry Building 1 Ferry Building San Francisco, CA 94111
events.description: An inspiring and eminently useful guide to the art of letter writing, including prompts and exercises to help deepen our most important connections and heal old wounds, by a beloved “letter midwife.” Unfinished Business: Writing the 5 Essential Letters of Your Life by Frish Brandt is the guide we’ve all been waiting for on letter writing, the next personal step after reading books centered on the art of letters. Frish will be joined in conversation by the Chronicle’s arts and culture columnist, Tony Bravo. Given this zeitgeist-like moment around letters, UNFINISHED BUSINESS fills a gap in the available literature. Frish is a letter writing midwife who teaches essential letter writing at Stanford University’s School of Medicine, and with UNFINISHED BUSINESS, she presents the work of her life: how to write five essential letters (Thank you, I’m sorry, I miss you, I love you, and Goodbye) that provide her clients, students, and readers with a path forward to never let the most essential messages of our life remain unsaid. We all have unfinished business: thank-you notes we meant to write, goodbyes we never spoke, apologies we never managed to give. Here to help us put those words on paper, letter midwife Frish Brandt provides singular guidance on how to write the five fundamental missives that make up the meaning of our lives: Thank you, I’m sorry, I miss you, I love you, and Goodbye. With real-world examples from her experience of teaching at Stanford Medical School, Harvard Divinity School, and in workshops and individual sessions around the country, she weaves practical writing prompts with gentle reflections on grief, connection, forgiveness, and closure, offering the tools—and the courage—to help us write what we have long held inside. At once a permission slip, a guidebook, and a lyrical ode to the power of the written word, Unfinished Business is a book to read, to write alongside, and to return to again and again. “Unfinished Business is a pragmatic, empathetic, urgent call to stop avoiding the hardest conversations and start enjoying the world beyond hurt and regret. A true service to readers.”—Kelly Corrigan, New York Times bestselling author of Tell Me More and The Middle Place “This is an antidote to despair and a practice of peace, a book of intimacy and radical reflection. Frish Brandt is a magical presence in the world.”—Terry Tempest Williams, author of The Glorians and When Women Were Birds “Frish Brandt has tapped into a secret vein of gold lurking in every human heart. Even the best-designed and well-lived life has some unfinished business. Kindly, compassionately, and with unexpected ease, Brandt reveals how to find and finish your essential letter. Completing your letter is life-changing—and it awaits you in these pages. Don’t miss it.”—Dave Evans, New York Times bestselling author of Designing Your Life, Cofounder of Stanford Life Design Lab “Unfinished Business offers a way to come safely closer to the unfathomable, bringing light to emptiness and love to fear. Brandt’s work is an extraordinary tool to help heal, connect, and transform your relationships. Her work is altogether a gorgeous phenomenon, and I’ve seen it work wonders time and again.”—Dr. B.J Miller, Director of the Center for Living and Dying, author of A Beginners Guide to the End “Frish Brandt evokes relief, wonder, and immense gratitude in all who encounter her letter writing practice. Unfinished Business is a book for every one of us.”—Nancy Horan, New York Times bestselling author of Loving Frank and The House of Lincoln Frish Brandt teaches essential letter writing at Stanford University’s School of Medicine and to individuals and institutions around the country, including museums, universities, hospitals, and caregiving associations. She worked in the arts for more than four decades before becoming a full-time Letter Midwife. She lives and writes in San Francisco. Tony Bravo is the Chronicle’s arts and culture columnist. He joined the Chronicle in 2015 as a reporter for the Style section: His beats include visual art, LGBTQ issues and the culture of clothes. Bravo is also an adjunct instructor at the City College of San Francisco Fashion Department, where he teaches journalism. With photographer Stephen Lam Bravo is the recipient of the 2026 Excellence in Online Journalism Award from the NLGJA Association of LGBTQ+ Journalists. events.title: Somatic Healing Workshop: Get Out of Your Head & Into Your Body
events.location: 550 Laguna St, San Francisco + Full Studio
events.description:
A somatic healing experience to help you quiet the mental noise, reconnect with yourself, and return to the wisdom of your body.
Do you find yourself constantly overthinking, analyzing, worrying, planning, or second-guessing yourself?
Maybe you know what you should do, but still feel stuck. Maybe you struggle to trust yourself, feel disconnected from your emotions, or find yourself living in your head instead of fully experiencing your life.
You're not alone. Many of us have been taught to rely almost exclusively on our minds while ignoring the wisdom of our bodies. But when we're constantly thinking, analyzing, and trying to figure everything out, we often become disconnected from the very thing that can guide us most: ourselves.
In this immersive somatic workshop, you'll learn how to shift out of overthinking and back into your body through simple yet powerful practices that support nervous system regulation, self-awareness, emotional processing, and deeper connection.
You'll learn:
Why overthinking is often a sign of nervous system dysregulation
How stress and survival patterns keep us stuck in our heads
The connection between the body, emotions, and intuition
Why healing and transformation require more than mindset alone
How to create more presence, clarity, and connection in your daily life

Through guided somatic practices, you'll experience grounding exercises, breathwork, body awareness practices, gentle movement, embodiment exercises, and nervous system regulation techniques designed to help you reconnect with yourself and the present moment.
You'll leave with:
A greater sense of calm, clarity, and inner connection
Practical tools to navigate overwhelm and overthinking
A deeper understanding of your body's signals and needs
More trust in yourself, your intuition, and your inner wisdom
Simple ways to deepen your sense of presence and connection in your daily life
This workshop isn't about fixing yourself or becoming someone new. It's about remembering how to listen to the wisdom that's already within you.
If you're ready to spend less time in your head and more time feeling grounded, present, and fully alive, this experience is for you.
Please bring a journal and water bottle, and wear comfortable clothes.
NOTE: Please be on time for this session — doors will close promptly and there will be NO LATE ENTRIES!
About Anna Bolender:
Anna Bolender is a certified Somatic Embodiment & Intuitive Life Coach, Somatic Breathwork and Quantum Wellness Practitioner, Reiki Master, and lifelong student of holistic health and well-being.

Blending somatics, energy healing, quantum wellness, and mindset work, she helps clients break free from self-sabotaging patterns, repattern their nervous system, and cultivate simple daily rituals that support a fulfilling, grounded, and aligned life.

events.title: What Should Stay Human When Agents Join the Team?
events.location: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco + 540 Cafe
events.description:
Your team works with AI agents now, and nobody has agreed what the agents get to decide. So everyone draws their own line. One person lets the agent send the client email. Another rewrites everything it touches. Someone hides how much they use it. None of it gets said out loud, and slowly the team stops trusting the work, and each other.
This workshop is where a team draws the line together: which calls stay human, which go to the agents, and which the agent drafts and a human decides. What you leave with is a one-page agreement your team wrote, and a monthly practice to keep it current as the work changes.
WHO IT'S FOR: Founders and team leads bringing AI agents into a team, and anyone on a team that already works with them. Heads of HR / People & Culture who want a way to do this across teams.
LEAVE WITH: A one-page team agreement: what stays human, what goes to the agents, what needs a human check. A 45-minute monthly version you can run with your own team.

events.description: This collection brings together powerful voices from around the world to inspire ordinary citizens to keep working for change in an age of despair. “A magnificent anthology celebrates hope, guts, and the power of taking action.” — Oprah Magazine In a world where each day can bring new reasons for outrage or despair, Paul Loeb answers with stories of hope, inspiration, and raw courage from heroes of world-changing political movements. In this comprehensively updated edition, Loeb helps us keep acting for change whatever the odds. The Impossible Will Take a Little While shows what it's like to go up against Goliath and win—on battlefields from the 2024 South Korean coup, Putin’s prisons, South African apartheid, American slavery, and defeatism about climate change. Authors include Nelson Mandela, Alexei Navalny, Bill McKibben, Diane Ackerman, Jesmyn Ward, Howard Zinn, Heather Cox Richardson, Alice Walker, Sherman Alexie, Vaclav Havel, Paul Hawken, Rutger Bregman, Bill Moyers, Audre Lorde, Mary Pipher, Tony Kushner, Maya Angelou, Pablo Neruda, Terry Tempest Williams, Desmond Tutu, and fifty-two other powerful voices. Without minimizing the obstacles, their stories inspire hope to keep on pushing for what we believe. “An indispensable anthology of hope and inspiration. Put away your Prozac, and pick up The Impossible Will Take a Little While .”— Arianna Huffington “A magnificent anthology celebrates hope, guts, and the power of taking action… Loeb has compiled for us the words of 49 of the most gifted and heroic men and women of our time, 49 testimonials to stamina and compassion in the face of seemingly insurmountable odds, 49 reasons to keep hope alive in this time of frustration and fear.”— Oprah Magazine “Loeb has been doing wonderfully patient work, exploring the American conscience from the inside. I regard him as something of a national treasure.”— Susan Sontag “An anthology of some of the most powerful voices of our time.” — Boston Globe “For anyone worn down, The Impossible Will Take a Little While is a bracing double cappuccino.”— Barbara Ehrenreich Paul Rogat Loeb is the author of Soul of a Citizen . He has written for The New York Times , The Washington Post , USA Today , AARP Bulletin , Redbook , The Chronicle of Higher Education , The Nation , Huffington Post , and Raw Story , and has appeared on NBC, ABC, CNN, PBS, Fox News, NPR, and the BBC. events.title: David Maisel and the Apocalyptic Sublime
events.location: Clio's Books, 353 Grand Avenue, Oakland, CA 94610, Oakland, CA
events.description: View from the Precipice: A Retrospective Monograph · For over forty years, David Maisel has made work that spans photography, painting, and video, situating himself above the surface—of the Earth, of the canvas—in such a way that his unmistakable sensibility transcends any given medium. His aerial photographs and video installations address the aesthetics and environmental impact of landscapes radically transformed by mineral extraction, natural resource reclamation, desertification, and military weapons testing. Seen through Maisel’s lens, these sites become abstractions that pulse with other-worldly colors and geometries — endangered landscapes imbued with a disquieting allure. Across each series, Maisel uses beauty “as a tool, a device for helping us focus our attention.” His large-scaled, immersive abstract paintings respond to catastrophic climate change events such as wildfire and flood. In each of these mediums, Maisel’s images are spatially ambiguous and destabilizing, and describe a world wholly remade by human activity. View from the Precipice , a new monograph published by Radius Books, is the most comprehensive survey of Maisel’s career to date and is the first to place his paintings and lens-based works in direct dialogue. The volume begins with a chronological primer offering both technical insight and anecdotal background information, provided by Maisel, for projects spanning four decades of his practice. Essays by art historian Alexander Nemerov and writer Geoff Manaugh and a conversation between Maisel and novelist Samantha Harvey weave through the visual chapters that comprise the second half of the book. Together, the images and texts offer an expansive account of one of the most distinctive artistic practices of the past several decades. This evening’s event will bring Maisel, Nemerov, and Clio’s founder Timothy Don together in conversation around the themes of Maisel’s practice and the development of his new survey monograph. DAVID MAISEL is a visual artist. He is the recipient of Fellowships from the Guggenheim Foundation, the Getty Research Institute, and the National Endowment for the Arts, and has been an Artist in Residence at the Headlands Center for the Arts, among other awards and honors. His work is in the permanent collections of more than fifty museums internationally and has been the subject of eight monographs, the latest being a survey on his career, View from the Precipice , published by Radius Books in fall 2026. Maisel’s photographs were featured this year at the National Gallery of Art in Beneath the Surface: Mining and American Photography . His series Spiraling , on severe drought conditions at the Great Salt Lake, is being developed as a solo traveling museum exhibition by the Barry Lopez Foundation for Art and Environment. ALEXANDER NEMEROV is the author of Fierce Poise: Helen Frankenthaler and 1950s New York (Penguin), praised by Vogue as one of its best books of 2021 and a finalist for the National Book Critics Circle Award in Biography that year. Nemerov’s most recent book, The Forest: A Fable of America in the 1830s , has been called by the novelist Annie Proulx “one of the richest books ever to come my way…Deeply beautiful, achingly painful, and astonishingly tender.” Nemerov is featured in Nathaniel Kahn’s HBO documentary about the art world, The Price of Everything (2018). At Stanford University, Nemerov is the Carl and Marilynn Thoma Provostial Professor in the Arts and Humanities and served as chair of the Department of Art and Art History from 2015 to 2021.

events.title: 9th Ave: Daisy Fried with Katie Peterson
events.location: Books on the Park on 9th Avenue, 1231 9th Ave., San Francisco, CA 94122
events.description:
Join us on Thursday, October 29 at 7pm when we celebrate the release of Daisy Fried's collection, My Destination, with Katie Peterson at 9th Ave!

Free to Attend, Please RSVP
Or Watch on YouTube Live/Link Available Soon

Praise for My Destination
"In My Destination, Daisy Fried writes with unsparing clarity from within grief, desire, motherhood, illness, and public anger. These poems attend closely to bodies, objects, and moments where private life collides with moral and civic force. Restless, comic, and exacting, Fried's music refuses consolation while insisting on attention—choosing, again and again, not to turn away."—Rowan Ricardo Phillips

"When I am reading a poem by Daisy Fried, I often forget that I am reading a poem, and believe myself instead to be experiencing an event. This may be a result of Fried's effortless command of those aspects of storytelling, like character and action, that we falsely reserve for novelists. But I prefer to think that My Destination succeeds for reasons of poetry—the poet's unapologetic curiosity about experience, and her remorseless hunger for the right words to know her moment. 'I begin to take an interest in life,' she writes at a moment few would dare (this is not the only audacious moment here, far from it). This book quite simply embeds itself in human life, and intriguing new ground is broken, in poems of widowhood, motherhood and more. Fried's conditions are epic, her voice is human, and her ability to describe the human comedy astonishing. With the tenacity of Athena and the craftiness of Penelope, she makes her way. I admire this book tremendously."—Katie Peterson

About Daisy Fried
Daisy Fried is the author of five books of poetry: My Destination, The Year the City Emptied, Women's Poetry: Poems and Advice, My Brother is Getting Arrested Again, and She Didn't Mean to Do It. A poetry critic and a member of the faculty of the Warren Wilson College MFA Program for Writers, she lives in San Francisco.

About Katie Peterson
Katie Peterson is the author of Fog and Smoke, published by FSG in early 2024. Poems from the collection have appeared in the Atlantic, the New Republic, the New York Review of Books, and the Yale Review, among other publications. Her previous book, Life in a Field (2021) is a collaboration with the photographer Young Suh. She is the author of other books of poetry: This One Tree (New Issues, 2006), Permission (New Issues, 2013), The Accounts (University of Chicago, 2013), and A Piece of Good News (Farrar, Straus & Giroux, 2019), a finalist for the Northern California Book Award in 2020. She is the editor of the New Selected Poems of Robert Lowell (Farrar, Straus & Giroux, 2017). She is Professor of English at the University of California at Davis, where she is Professor of English and a Chancellor’s Fellow.

Isaiah will be guiding the conversation, so you only really need to bring yourself (and maybe the book). Our next read is Meet Me in the Garden by Nina LaCour. New Orleans, 1944. Odette has always been one of the Honore sisters, glamorous and admired in their Creole community. But while Odette’s older sisters are content to be wives and mothers, Odette has always wanted something else. It is only with her beloved cousin, Delphine, that Odette can tell her secret: she is in love with a woman, and she longs to be an artist. Delphine has a secret lover, too, a white man. In the hidden garden they’ve discovered, Odette and Delphine can dream of futures full of passion and freedom. But five years later, Odette's life is nothing like what she'd planned. She's a widowed mother, living in Los Angeles, and she and Delphine, who is passing as white, have spiraled away from each other. When Delphine reaches a breaking point, Odette must make a shattering choice to try to hold her family together. Profound and expansive, a story of love and longing, art and motherhood, friendship and desire, Meet Me in the Garden is a decades-spanning tour de force, inspired by the author’s family and tracing the history of the Great Migration. events.description:

From there, Every Saturday Night pulls audiences back into the 1950s, the vibrant “Harlem of the West,” when the Fillmore pulsed with jazz, community, and possibility.

Following two Black boys—one in each era—the musical explores home, belonging, and resilience, revealing how the Fillmore’s past and present are connected by displacement, gentrification, and the enduring fight to stay rooted in the community.

Inspired by true events, this boisterous and heartfelt new work commissioned and presented by San Francisco Bay Area Theatre Company (SFBATCO) celebrates a historic neighborhood while asking urgent questions about who gets to remain in the city today.

events.title: David Sánchez’s Carib presents Tambó
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
For his night in our series devoted to solo projects by SFJAZZ Collective members, tenor saxophonist and composer David Sánchez brings his Carib ensemble to the stage, presenting the West Coast premiere of his new work, Tambó.

Formed to record his 2019 album of the same name, Carib represents a deeply personal journey for Sánchez, and the GRAMMY-nominated debut recording was a trailblazing use of modern jazz to explore the kinship between the West African drum rhythms of Yuba, Calinda, and Sika and traditional music in Haiti, Carriacou, and his native Puerto Rico.

Dedicated to the memory of Sánchez’s mentor, the late Nuyorican piano legend Eddie Palmieri, Tambó (drum) was inspired by a recent trip to Haiti and Puerto Rico and the chants and rhythms drawn from the *bomba* tradition he heard in Loíza and San Basilio de Palenque in Colombia.

Since his early exposure with Dizzy Gillespie’s United Nations Orchestra, Sánchez has become one of the most celebrated instrumentalists in jazz, recording ten albums as a leader and winning a Latin GRAMMY Award for his 2004 orchestral session, Coral. Over a career full of highlights, he’s performed with a roster of greats including Charlie Haden, Eddie Palmieri, Roy Haynes, Tom Harrell, Roy Hargrove, and Pat Metheny, among others.

In addition to Palmieri, Tambó is, in Sánchez’s words, “dedicated to the ancestors who live through us and inspire us with their spiritual strength.”

Personnel: David Sánchez (tenor saxophone); Others TBA

events.title: Michael Connelly - The Hollow
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera & Online 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: Retired LAPD detective Harry Bosch delves into the darkest chapter of his past in this electric thriller from #1 New York Times bestselling author Michael Connelly. When Harry Bosch was eleven years old, his mother was murdered and he became a ward of the state, housed in MacLaren Children’s Center, a notorious facility where abuse was rampant. Decades after its closure, a massive class action lawsuit has resulted in a multibillion-dollar settlement for former residents. But when Bosch’s half-brother, defense attorney Mickey Haller, brings him word that Harry is entitled to $400,000, Bosch says he doesn’t want the money. He wants justice. News of the settlement awakens his memories of a place he had hoped never to revisit, and a boy named Chops, a fellow inmate who wound up dead. Chops’s body was found in a hidden space under a staircase that the staff used to discipline their charges. The kids knew it only as “the hollow.” But Chops’s death was covered up and never solved. Now Bosch knows he must reopen the investigation and learn the truth, even if the killer is long dead. As Bosch digs into the files, he picks up the trail of a predator who not only survived, but went on to a life of vicious crime. Forced to face a history that both scarred him and launched him on his mission as a cop, Bosch must bring down a sadistic criminal and finally put to rest the demons of his past. Praise for The Waiting: A Ballard and Bosch Novel (A Renée Ballard and Harry Bosch Novel #6) “The Waiting is a milestone of sorts for Bosch…He is a complicated, maddening, impulsive, brilliant, beautifully drawn character. Connelly’s books are gripping, with a momentum that starts on the first page and builds steadily to the last. And he describes Los Angeles as well as any writer ever has.”— Los Angeles Times "Despite having to navigate the byzantine politics of the city’s justice system, including meddling higher ups and an intransigent prosecutor, Ballard and her team ultimately win the day. The multiple plot lines are suspenseful and unfold at a torrid pace, and as usual in a Connelly novel, the prose is tight and the characters are compelling and well-drawn. The Waiting is the habitually best-selling author at the top of his game.”— Bruce DeSilva, Associated Press "Michael Connelly is a powerhouse, an unstoppable force in crime fiction. The Waiting is proof he is at the top of his game."— Mick Herron, #1 bestselling author of Slow Horses Michael Connelly is the author of forty-two previous novels, among them New York Times bestsellers Ironwood , The Proving Ground , and The Waiting . His books, which include the Harry Bosch series, the Lincoln Lawyer series, the Renée Ballard series, and the Catalina novels, have sold more than ninety-two million copies worldwide. events.description:
Join us on Friday, October 30 at 6:30pm when we welcome Kirk Lombard for the release of his book, The Shadow Stream, at Sports Basement Presidio!

Refreshments and live music followed by an author talk and book signing

Free to attend, Please RSVP

Praise for The Shadow Stream
"Kirk Lombard’s The Shadow Stream is a book of great originality, a book like no other, propelled by brilliant storytelling and original thinking (and fish!) that will engage readers of all ages—a perfect family book."⸺Mark Kurlansky, author of Cod and Salt and World Without Fish

"The Shadow Stream is a book that will change your mind: brilliantly told, it is an odyssey and an oddity, a tale that defies expectations and redefines the notion of hero." ⸺Annie Barrows, bestselling co-author of The Guernsey Literary and Potato Peel Pie Society and author of the Ivy & Bean series

About The Shadow Stream
A throwback to family reads of yore, this epic follows a troubled boy and a host of hilariously vexed animals who must save a river before it’s dammed, so they can save themselves.

Gabriel (“G” for short) is wasting away in the Abiddon County Juvenile Center when he’s introduced to the Shongunk River by his dying uncle. The river valley—trash-heaped but chock-full of mysteries and fish—wins G over. But, as G has learned, good things can’t last. The Shongunk is scheduled to be dammed by a local developer. In a matter of days, it will cease flowing, and all of the talkative creatures who live there in the river valley will be as homeless as G.

Just as G decides it’s no time to accept his fate, so too do the animals. To inspire an uprising, a young trout is nominated to make a fateful journey up the river; a raccoon swears a violent oath against humans; and a newly sober buck leads his skittish flock out of harm’s way. Together with G, they show that good can triumph and that there is power in all of us, even the smallest minnow.

About Kirk Lombard
Kirk Lombard is an author, angler, sustainable fishmonger, and tuba player who once worked inside the juvenile rehabilitation system. His first book, the award-winning Sea Forager's Guide to the Northern California Coast, was described as "poetry" for fish by NPR. He lives in the Bay Area with his family, raising his children on herring and sea shanties.

events.description:
Be transported to San Francisco’s Fillmore District—beginning in the present day, where the echoes of a once-thriving Black neighborhood still shape the streets. From there, Every Saturday Night pulls audiences back into the 1950s, the vibrant “Harlem of the West,” when the Fillmore pulsed with jazz, community, and possibility.

Following two Black boys—one in each era—the musical explores home, belonging, and resilience, revealing how the Fillmore’s past and present are connected by displacement, gentrification, and the enduring fight to stay rooted in the community.

events.title: RICK BRAUN
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Master of the trumpet and flugelhorn · Over three decades, 20+ albums, and more than 20 #1 Billboard hits into one of contemporary jazz's most inspiring careers, Rick Braun remains a master of the trumpet and flugelhorn. The Allentown, Pennsylvania-born Braun began playing music in elementary school, ultimately winding up at the prestigious Eastman School of Music. There, he hooked up with like-minded musicians to form the jazz-fusion combo Auracle. Braun's first big break came when he composed "Here With Me," a Top 20 hit for REO Speedwagon. He soon became a highly regarded pop sideman, touring and recording with the likes of Rod Stewart, War, Sade, Tina Turner, Natalie Cole, Glenn Frey, Tom Petty, and Crowded House. The trumpeter became a Smooth Jazz fixture with his 1993 debut, Intimate Secrets, and broke through with 1995's Beat Street. His records have consistently ranked in the Top 10 of Billboard's Contemporary Jazz Chart, with Kisses in the Rain reigning at #1 for 11 weeks. The recipient of numerous awards, he shared a Best Collaboration honor with Boney James for their hit Shake It Up, and his duo project RnR with Richard Elliot also hit #1. He's recorded three albums with the all-star trio BWB alongside Grammy winners Kirk Whalum and Norman Brown. A much-in-demand producer, he has delivered #1 radio hits with artists including David Benoit, Marc Antoine, Peter White, and the late Jeff Golub. His most recent release, Rick Braun Plays Chuck Mangione, is his first-ever tribute album, honoring one of his musical heroes. Braun says with a grin, "I am one of the luckiest guys in the world. I mean, when you really think about it, I make my living blowing into plumbing."

events.title: El David Aguilar
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Joe Henderson Lab
events.description:
Singer-songwriter El David Aguilar has become one of the most inventive and emotionally resonant voices in contemporary Latin music, blending folk, bolero, jazz, and rock into songs marked by poetic lyricism and fearless experimentation. Born in Culiacán, Sinaloa, Mexico, Aguilar began writing songs as a teenager and quickly distinguished himself through his literary approach to songwriting and his richly expressive voice. Over the past decade, he has built a devoted international following while earning acclaim for albums that merge traditional Mexican influences with sophisticated modern arrangements.

Aguilar has collaborated with celebrated artists including Natalia Lafourcade, Jorge Drexler, and Mon Laferte, establishing himself as a central figure in the new generation of Latin American troubadours. His work has received multiple nominations from the Latin GRAMMY Awards, including five 2018 nominations for his 2017 album Siguiente Segundo including Album of the Year and Song of the Year for Embrujo.

Aguilar’s latest album, Compita del Destino, showcases the artist at his most adventurous and intimate. Filled with vivid storytelling, intricate harmonies, and warm acoustic textures, the record explores fate, friendship, love, and personal transformation. The album confirms Aguilar’s reputation as a songwriter capable of turning deeply personal experiences into music of universal emotional power.

Personnel: El David Aguilar; Others TBA

events.title: John Scofield’s Electrospective
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
Featuring Oteil Burbridge, Larry Goldings, Adam Dietch

For this exclusive week, guitar giant John Scofield revisits his hugely influential electric jazz songbook from his iconic career with an all-star quartet including organist Larry Goldings, bassist Oteil Burbridge, and drummer Adam Dietch.

Though Scofield is recognized as one of jazz’s most creative guitarists of the past half century, the three-time GRAMMY Award winner has often branched off from the straight-ahead path to get his funk on. After five decades of prolific touring and recording, he’s looking back at many of his now classic fusion groove compositions with Electrospective. Sco being Sco, he’s not interested in replicating past triumphs. Rather, he plans to reimagine fan favorites from the bands with which he created 1987’s Blue Matter, 1997’s A GoGo, and 2002’s Überjam, as well as new material in the same vein.

He’s bringing the same ensemble aesthetic to Electrospective, relying on interpretative input from long-time collaborators and new friends. Multidimensional keyboardist Larry Goldings and Überjam drummer Adam Deitch, who won a GRAMMY for his work with Lettuce, have toured and recorded extensively with Sco. Bass star Oteil Burbridge, revered for his work with Dead & Company, Tedeschi Trucks Band, and the Allman Brothers, brings a fresh set of frets to Scofield’s deepest grooves.

Personnel: John Scofield (guitar); Larry Goldings (organ); Oteil Burbridge bass; Adam Dietch (drums)

events.title: Dr. Jekyll & Mr. Hyde
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
with Dorothy Papadakos, organ

The sacred space of Grace Cathedral will transform into a grand movie palace for a special Halloween week screening of John S. Robertson’s 1920 adaptation of the Robert Louis Stevenson novella of a doctor wrestling with split identities, starring John Barrymore and featuring a live score performed on Grace’s famous pipe organ by renowned organist and composer Dorothy Papadakos.

A member of the GRAMMY-winning Paul Winter Consort and former Cathedral Organist of New York’s Cathedral of St. John the Divine, Papadakos has accompanied the greatest silent films in venues around the world.

A smash success upon its release and a star-making vehicle for Barrymore, the film was easily the most successful silent version of Stevenson’s 1886 novella, earning universal praise for Barrymore’s bravura turn in the dual roles of London physician Henry Jekyll and his evil alter ego, as well as its terrifying makeup effects.

This performance will take full advantage of Grace’s 7,500 pipe Aeolian-Skinner organ, a historic instrument installed in 1934 that has been played by many of the world’s great organists and earned a place in jazz history as well, being employed for the premiere of Duke Ellington’s Concert of Sacred Music in 1963 and pianist Vince Guaraldi’s 1965 Jazz Mass.

Personnel: Dorothy Papadakos (pipe organ)

events.title: How We See: Description in Memoir with Connie Josefs: 4 Meetings
events.location: Online via Zoom
events.description: 4 Saturdays: Oct 31 - Nov 21, 2026 “How we see the world reveals who we are.” —Ocean Vuong Memoir is an imagining of the past, a re-creation of sights, sounds and experience. Description is one of our most powerful tools. It sets the scene and engages the reader through sensory detail. When we write, the details of scene also reveal the one who is looking. The way the narrator sees, hears and feels lets us know who they are. More than a series of events, memoir offers insight into the heart of the storyteller. This generative workshop will explore how description illuminates the character of the narrator and offers access to their inner world. Format includes readings, discussion, writing exercises and supportive feedback. Topics include: Embodied writing The role of description in writing scene Understanding the narrator as character How description conveys a narrator’s innermost thoughts and feelings Class size is limited to 20 participants. * Note that for all classes held on Zoom, registration closes the day before the class begins. Same-day registrations are not available, so please plan ahead. (Classes will be recorded and replay will be available for a limited time.) Meet Your Instructor Connie Josefs is a writer, teacher and memoir coach. She leads workshops in memoir and memoir-based fiction and has taught at the University of New Mexico, Southwest Writers, The Taos Writers Conference and Santa Monica College, where she was founding editor of the literary journal, “E-33: Writings from Emeritus.” She holds an MFA in fiction from Antioch University LA and has worked as a writer and story analyst for film and television. More at www.conniejosefs.com . What students are saying about Connie: "The class went above and beyond my expectations! Connie is gifted in approach, connection, and content." – Erin P. "Connie was clear and specific, answered questions thoughtfully and had us do writing exercises in each segment. She is an excellent teacher. I feel so much better equipped to work on my memoir now." – Ruth M. "Connie always does a fabulous job of teaching her subject. I learned a great deal...She is the best." - Susan F. "The instructor is deeply knowledgeable and wove many helpful concepts and exercises together to great effect." – Athena K.

events.title: John Scofield’s Electrospective
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
Featuring Oteil Burbridge, Larry Goldings, Adam Dietch

For this exclusive week, guitar giant John Scofield revisits his hugely influential electric jazz songbook from his iconic career with an all-star quartet including organist Larry Goldings, bassist Oteil Burbridge, and drummer Adam Dietch.

Though Scofield is recognized as one of jazz’s most creative guitarists of the past half century, the three-time GRAMMY Award winner has often branched off from the straight-ahead path to get his funk on. After five decades of prolific touring and recording, he’s looking back at many of his now classic fusion groove compositions with Electrospective. Sco being Sco, he’s not interested in replicating past triumphs. Rather, he plans to reimagine fan favorites from the bands with which he created 1987’s Blue Matter, 1997’s A GoGo, and 2002’s Überjam, as well as new material in the same vein.

He’s bringing the same ensemble aesthetic to Electrospective, relying on interpretative input from long-time collaborators and new friends. Multidimensional keyboardist Larry Goldings and Überjam drummer Adam Deitch, who won a GRAMMY for his work with Lettuce, have toured and recorded extensively with Sco. Bass star Oteil Burbridge, revered for his work with Dead & Company, Tedeschi Trucks Band, and the Allman Brothers, brings a fresh set of frets to Scofield’s deepest grooves.

Personnel: John Scofield (guitar); Larry Goldings (organ); Oteil Burbridge bass; Adam Dietch (drums)

events.title: Jacob Weisberg - Profiles in Cowardice
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera & Online 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: “Valuable and dauntless.” — The New York Times “We badly need [this] book.” —Tina Brown A devastating reckoning with the people and institutions whose failure to stand up to Trump’s brazen grab for authoritarian power has been particularly shocking and consequential It may be scant solace, but history will be particularly harsh to a subset of Trump enablers with a few key things in common: They have money and power. They represent intuitions that are central in determining whether America remains a free, functioning democracy or not. And they absolutely know better. History starts now. In Profiles in Cowardice , Jacob Weisberg has written one of the first defining books of the Trump Era—how this pitch-black political moment happened, why so few resisted, and what it reveals about the character of American leadership. Jeff Bezos, Amazon, and Big Tech. Stephen Schwarzman, Blackstone, and Wall Street. Brad Karp, Paul, Weiss, and Big Law. Mitch McConnell and the United States Senate. Eight individuals in all, together forming an entwined network of power in America, and a new way to understand how authoritarianism can take root in an open society—not by overthrowing institutions, but by bending and bullying them into submission. The book is a masterful study of the ways people create rationalizations to justify basic human instincts such as greed, vanity and fear—above all fear. Fear is the great enemy of democracy, and the book illuminates how it operates, how it disguises itself, and how it spreads. The book is timeless: its profiles are case studies, but they are also mirrors. They ask readers to examine their own instincts, their own silences, their own thresholds for action. This is not a morality tale with easy villains. It is an attempt to describe the moral mechanics of democratic failure. By studying that failure up close, we may better understand what courage truly requires—and why it is so rarely summoned when it matters most. “A cutting compendium of collusion.” — Publishers Weekly “A highly readable study of the politics and price of capitulation.” —Kirkus Reviews “In this perilous moment in American history, much political courage is required; understanding where it went is essential to bringing it back. In Profiles in Cowardice, the extraordinary Jacob Weisberg examines how, when, and why so many Americans and American institutions capitulated to monstrous abuses of the office of the American presidency. The appeasement of Donald Trump is a sordid story. It is also, in Weisberg’s hands, a gripping one.” —Jill Lepore Jacob Weisberg is the author of books including Ronald Reagan (2016) , The Bush Tragedy (2008), and In an Uncertain World (2003), co-written with former Treasury Secretary Robert E. Rubin. A native of Chicago, he is the former longtime editor of Slate and the co-founder of the podcast company Pushkin Industries. He serves as Chair of The Committee to Protect Journalists and is a regular contributor to the New York Review of Books. events.description:
Hi Everyone,
We’re continuing our Purpose Alignment Circle series with a community gathering: Life After the Leap.
You took the leap. You left the job. You took the sabbatical. You made the big change. And now you’re back - and what often goes unspoken is how disorienting this phase can feel.
Coming back isn’t a finish line. It’s its own transition. And most of us are navigating it without a map.
This evening is for career changers, sabbatical-takers, and anyone who has ever wondered: “Okay, I did the brave thing… now what?”
Hosted and facilitated by Bernadette Lagman join us to come together to share real stories, reflect honestly, and find our footing, together.
Come as you are. Bring your questions. And an open mind. You're not alone in this.

Intentional Flow:
Welcome (10 min)
Introduction to the space, intention, and vision
Check-In (10 min)
Name, pronouns, where you're from
Sitting Meditation (10 min)
Guided / silent grounding practice
Big Group Discussion (40 min)
Open reflections and deep listening
What feels most alive or unclear in your current path?
Small Breakout Groups (30 min)
What feels most alive or unclear in your current path?
Accountability Pairing (10 min)
Pair up and share one action step
Align on follow-up/accountability
Closing (10 min)
Final reflections + gratitude What support do you still need?

events.title: Julianna Glasse with Tara Schuster - This Is What Happens When Women Read
events.location: Book Passage Ferry Building 1 Ferry Building San Francisco, CA 94111
events.description: An empowering story of self-actualization by a former Christian pop star whose life was transformed by reading. “In telling her story, Julianna Glasse blazes a trail for every woman who has ever felt oppressed by religion and the patriarchy and muted by other people’s rules and judgment. This is a page-turning, sexy, and eye-popping memoir of liberation. I couldn’t put it down.”—Chelsea Handler, author of the #1 New York Times -bestseller Life Will Be the Death of Me Julianna will be joined in conversation by Tara Schuster. In 2017, Julianna Glasse performed at President Trump's first National Prayer Breakfast. At the time, she was a Christian pop star married to a star MLB player. They were a glamorous, high-profile Evangelical power couple. She led prayer sessions for players' wives. She wrote handbooks for Christian women. And she hid books like contraband. When her husband discovered books she'd hidden in her lingerie drawer—Plato, Dickinson, Rumi, de Beauvoir—he threw them on the floor and shouted, "This is what happens when women read!" His condemnation became her wake-up call. Now, in THIS IS WHAT HAPPENS WHEN WOMEN READ (Spiegel & Grau; October 13, 2026), Julianna tells the unforgettable, unvarnished, deeply moving story of her escape from the cave—her personal path to freedom and the power of books to change lives. When Julianna began reading Plato’s Republic, something in her shifted. She started asking questions, hiding books around the house, and reading late at night. What followed: a very public, contested divorce. Horrific public shaming. Self-hatred, depression, suicidal impulses. But also: befriending the gay couple next door (one a pastor who opened her to a new understanding of Christianity), sexual liberation, an Oxford business degree, and the creation of a nonprofit, also called “This Is What Happens When Women Read,” which provides scholarships, curriculum, and community to women breaking free from fundamentalist religions around the globe. In an America where book bans are being imposed, when the cultural moment is obsessed with shows like The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives and endless tradwife discourse, and when American women are questioning who gets to decide their futures, the timing of this book is ideal. Julianna believes & "the political future of this country lies in the votes of the women I'm writing for"—women trapped in patriarchal religious systems. Julianna refused to accept her cage—and has built a ladder for others to climb out. This isn’t just a memoir, it’s a manifesto. I invite you to read this remarkable book and join her mission: to help women become "autonomous, curious, fully realized human beings." “Powerful debut memoir . . . Patient and curious rather than rageful or high-minded, Glasse’s account is a love letter to art, literature, and finding beauty in the world on one’s own terms. It makes for empowering reading.” —Publishers Weekly “This book is a searing bibliography of self-expression, one book at a time. It’s breathlessly propulsive, with courage mounting on every page. In an era of rising illiteracy, I found myself as a reader alternately lamenting what non-readers miss and cheering for what Julianna found. This book is what happens when women read: they transform into who they were always meant to be. Julianna uses her radiant light to liberate, and I’m so grateful that she persevered in her journey of revolutionary reading.” —Tia Levings, author of The New York Times bestseller A Well-Trained Wife and I Belong to Me “Women's reading is often dismissed as a hobby or a trivial distraction. But as Glasse's fierce own story and fierce analysis shows, a woman reading can be the most radical act.” —Soraya Chemaly, author of Rage Becomes Her Julianna Glasse is the founder and CEO of This Is What Happens When Women Read, a global movement advancing women's intellectual autonomy through education, scholarship, and community. An alumna of the University of Oxford and a member of the Saïd Business School Dean's Circle, Glasse leads a growing global scholarship initiative in partnership with Oxford that provides women access to one of the world's leading graduate business programs. She has spoken at global forums including the United Nations, the Skoll World Forum, and the Clinton Global Initiative on women's leadership and the role of intellectual agency in social transformation. She currently resides in New York City.For more information, go to https: // www.thisiswhathappenswhenwomenread.org . events.title: Artist Reception: Sarelyn Wager - Candid Expressions
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tama Vista Blvd Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: We are pleased to introduce Sarelyn Wager, a passionate Marin County-based artist. This exhibition is a dramatic and poetic expression of her subjects’ lives and experiences. It is a poignant window into the world of the elderly. Each piece reflects her love for humanity, it will resonate with all who have the opportunity to experience it. It is a testament to the power of artistic perseverance and the timeless nature of human expression. Sarelyn's art will be in the Gallery November through January, and visitors are welcome to come and enjoy her work. More About This Event: This event will be hosted in person at Book Passage's Corte Madera Store. About Sarelyn Wager Sarelyn is a 98-year-old Marin County-based artist who has been painting since childhood. Educated at Chouinard Art Institute and UCLA, her work has been exhibited in various locations and private salons over the years. Sarelyn's art embodies her interior life and her curiosity about people, capturing their goodness through her vibrant use of color and form. Sarelyn has been painting for over 80 years. Her passion and creativity capture the essence of the human experience through her masterful use of color and texture. "I live and dream in color," says Sarelyn. "My paintings speak for themselves. I'm a feisty, opinionated nonagenarian with a quirky world view, and my art is my most potent natural expression." Sarelyn's journey as an artist has been shaped by the challenges faced by women in the art world throughout her lifetime. Despite these barriers, she chose to follow her heart and dedicate herself to her craft, painting tirelessly for decades. Her work stands strong alongside accomplished artists, showcasing a remarkable abstract composition within figurative paintings. events.title: David Gottfried - Regen360
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: What if Earth came with a user manual? Regen360 argues that humanity’s crisis is not a lack of care, but a broken operating system—and introduces the Earth Code, a practical framework for aligning human systems to work in harmony with the planet. When incentives, governance, and institutional structures prioritize short-term gain, even well-intentioned efforts can accelerate harm. Sustainability stalls because systems are designed to reward immediate profit over long-term regeneration. Regen360 reframes regeneration as an operating discipline rather than an aspiration, showing how economics, leadership, technology, and daily decisions can be realigned with the self-regulatory patterns of Earth. As AI accelerates decision-making and shortens time horizons, the consequences of systemic misalignment intensify. Regen360 explores how human and institutional behavior responds under pressure—and how emerging technologies can either reinforce short-term priorities or support long-term stewardship. Bridging inner purpose with outer systems, David Gottfried, founder of the global green building movement, demonstrates how values, identity, and responsibility shape outcomes at every scale. The framework for a regenerative future is here—but the question remains: will it be embraced? "David Gottfried doesn't moralize; he analyzes. He gives us code — fifteen Earth Code equations, nestled in a framework called HOPE. At this bleak moment in our planet's history, hope is just what we need." — Denis Hayes, founder of Earth Day; President Emeritus, Bullitt Foundation " Regen360 is his most honest book yet — part memoir, part systems manifesto, part father's reckoning with what his daughter's generation is inheriting. He's not selling optimism. He's offering an operating system. That distinction matters, and so does this book." — Chip Conley, New York Times bestselling author and founder of MEA " Regen360 is what happens when someone who helped build the green building movement steps back and interrogates his own life's work with total honesty. It's essential reading for the journey forward." — Joel Makower, Chairman and Co-founder, Trellis Group David Gottfried is widely recognized as a father of the global green building movement. He founded both the U.S. Green Building Council and the World Green Building Council, which now spans 85 countries. His pioneering work catalyzed a global movement resulting in billions of square feet of certified projects across more than 186 countries, over a trillion dollars of economic activity, and hundreds of thousands of accredited professionals. Gottfried serves as Founder and CEO of Regen360 Inc., providing strategic advisory in decarbonization, sustainability, and regeneration for leading global green building companies. His personal mission is accelerating HOPE. Previously, Gottfried was Chief Commercial Officer of Blue Planet Systems, a carbon sequestration start-up. He spent two decades as CEO of Regenerative Ventures and its RegenNetwork, and held senior leadership roles in real estate development, including Senior Vice President at Thomas Properties Group. His new book, Regen360: An Operating System for a Regenerative Earth (Morgan James Publishing, October 2026), asks a question: what if everything we've built isn't enough — and the problem isn't technological or economic, but the operating logic underneath everything? The book proposes an Earth Code of 15 governing codes for a regenerative civilization and a framework called HOPE — Health on Planet Earth. His earlier book, Explosion Green, was an Indie Book Awards winner with a cover testimonial from President Bill Clinton. He is the author of four books and hosts the Regen360 podcast with 80 episodes. Gottfried holds a degree in Engineering and Resource Management from Stanford University, where he has lectured for three decades. His honors include the WorldGBC Global Green Building Entrepreneurship Award, USGBC Leadership Award, induction into the Green Industry Hall of Fame, and the 2025 NetZero/Metropolis Magazine Trailblazer Award. The USGBC Northern California Super Hero Award is now given annually in his name. He serves on the Advisory Boards of USGBC California, the Smart Surfaces Coalition, My Superhuman Race (India) and Verdant Building Products. Gottfried is a devoted father, painter, martial artist, fly fisherman, and cyclist — a five-time finisher of the Death Ride. He lives in the East Bay of Northern California with his Labradoodle, Juneau. events.title: Roopa in Flux
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Joe Henderson Lab
events.description:
Roopa Mahadevan and her ensemble Roopa in Flux have emerged as one of the most adventurous voices in contemporary global music, blending Carnatic classical traditions with jazz, soul, free improvisation, and experimental sound. A second-generation Indian American artist raised in the Bay Area, Mahadevan trained rigorously in South Indian classical vocal music before expanding her artistic language through collaborations across jazz, dance, theater, and interdisciplinary performance. Her work is rooted equally in virtuosity and fearless innovation, creating music that feels both deeply ancestral and unmistakably modern.

Mahadevan’s accomplishments span prestigious stages including SFJAZZ, Jazz at Lincoln Center, Carnegie Hall, the Kennedy Center, and the Metropolitan Museum of Art. She was a featured soloist on Christopher Tin’s GRAMMY-winning album Calling All Dawns and has collaborated with artists including Wynton Marsalis, Sunny Jain, George Brooks, and Karsh Kale.

Roopa in Flux’s latest work continues to push boundaries through emotionally charged improvisation, intricate rhythmic interplay, and contemporary storytelling centered on migration, identity, and joy. In 2023, the ensemble opened for Red Baraat at SFJAZZ’s Festival of Colors concert, delivering a dynamic performance that introduced new audiences to Mahadevan’s electrifying cross-cultural vision.

Personnel: Roopa Mahadevan (vocals); Rohan Krishnamurthy (mridangam, drums); Others TBA

events.title: John Scofield’s Electrospective
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
Featuring Oteil Burbridge, Larry Goldings, Adam Dietch

For this exclusive week, guitar giant John Scofield revisits his hugely influential electric jazz songbook from his iconic career with an all-star quartet including organist Larry Goldings, bassist Oteil Burbridge, and drummer Adam Dietch.

Though Scofield is recognized as one of jazz’s most creative guitarists of the past half century, the three-time GRAMMY Award winner has often branched off from the straight-ahead path to get his funk on. After five decades of prolific touring and recording, he’s looking back at many of his now classic fusion groove compositions with Electrospective. Sco being Sco, he’s not interested in replicating past triumphs. Rather, he plans to reimagine fan favorites from the bands with which he created 1987’s Blue Matter, 1997’s A GoGo, and 2002’s Überjam, as well as new material in the same vein.

He’s bringing the same ensemble aesthetic to Electrospective, relying on interpretative input from long-time collaborators and new friends. Multidimensional keyboardist Larry Goldings and Überjam drummer Adam Deitch, who won a GRAMMY for his work with Lettuce, have toured and recorded extensively with Sco. Bass star Oteil Burbridge, revered for his work with Dead & Company, Tedeschi Trucks Band, and the Allman Brothers, brings a fresh set of frets to Scofield’s deepest grooves.

Personnel: John Scofield (guitar); Larry Goldings (organ); Oteil Burbridge bass; Adam Dietch (drums)
