Doctorow, Ramon is offered a promotion and cash which could pay for grad school – if he agrees to enter a green-card marriage with his boss’s niece. When he agrees, he gets more than he bargained for. “Smoke and Shadows” by Tatyana Tolstaya centers on a Russian professor living in the U.S., navigating her professional life, her intimate relationships, and the mysteries of culture. events.title: Ben Wolfe Quartet
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Joe Henderson Lab
events.description:
An artist whose music has been described as “Mingus and Miles Davis meet Bartok and Bernard Herrmann” (The New York Times), bassist and composer Ben Wolfe performs music from his most recent album, Any Time After Now, with an all-star quartet of master instrumentalists.

A former member of the Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra and a veteran of work with Wynton Marsalis, Diana Krall, Harry Connick Jr., Branford Marsalis, Michael Bublé, and Benny Green, Wolfe is a highly regarded bandleader and composer whose work bridges a mastery of modern jazz. The bassist is a two-time recipient of Chamber Music America’s New Works: Creation and Presentation Program Grant through the Doris Duke Foundation and has released a dozen albums including Any Time After Now, his 2026 release for his own Resident Arts Records.

Featuring an all-star lineup including vibraphonist Joel Ross, pianist Sullivan Fortner, saxophonist Chris Lewis, and drummer Aaron Kimmel, the album is a masterfully constructed program of original music that further demonstrates Wolfe’s compositional acuity and sumptuous sense of swing. In his liner notes, the eminent drumming great Jeff “Tain” Watts relates, “These great artists have come together and made a beautiful thing.”

Personnel: Ben Wolfe (bass); Joel Ross (vibraphone); Nicole Glover (tenor saxophone); Aaron Kimmel (drums)

events.title: Joshua Redman Quartet
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
“One of the 21st century’s finest jazz improvisers” (The Guardian), saxophonist and composer Joshua Redman brings back his current quartet with pianist Paul Cornish, bassist Philip Norris, and drummer Nazir Ebo, performing material from his 2025 Blue Note album Words Fall Short — his second for the label and first with this remarkable ensemble of young masters-in-the-making.

Assembled after the first leg of his tour for his 2023 release Where Are We, Redman knew this new band was going to make waves. “My approach to band leading is unchanged,” Redman says.“ Play with the best musicians I can find, virtuosos who have mastered all the different jazz vocabularies, but who are also great listeners and collaborators—who know how to express their individual brilliance through group improvisation and collective interaction.”

After 20 studio albums as a leader, co-leading the all-star groups James Farm and Yaya3, co-founding and performing with our own SFJAZZ Collective, and serving as a sideman to the likes of McCoy Tyner, Chick Corea, and Elvin Jones, the Berkeley-born Redman has built an incomparable career as an innovator and restless seeker.

With Words Fall Short, Redman embraces the idea of imperfection and language’s inadequacy to capture and express the depth of human feeling, saying, “Perfection is unattainable. But it’s that struggle, that fallibility, that makes us so marvelously and exquisitely human.”

Personnel: Joshua Redman (tenor saxophone); Paul Cornish (piano); Philip Norris (bass); Nazir Ebo (drums)

In his liner notes, the eminent drumming great Jeff “Tain” Watts relates, “These great artists have come together and made a beautiful thing.”

events.title: You Aren't Alone Creative Relief Mini-Retreat
events.location: 550 Laguna St, San Francisco + Full Studio
events.description:
Join the You Aren't Alone Project for a one day Creative Relief Retreat designed for people of all backgrounds to engage in creative expression exercises and discussions as a tool for mental health, self-care, support and solace in a safe and collaborative environment.
Spend the afternoon with us exploring how creativity and mental health intersect to support your overall wellbeing. We'll start with a meditation and movement exercise, then hear from guest artists and mental health and wellness practitioners, and wrap up with a creative mental health workshop for tangible tools you can take with you and use in your daily life.
You do not have to be a practicing artist to attend. We just ask that you come with a creative mindset and an openness to the healing power of art and connection.
The You Aren’t Alone Project is a nonprofit organization dedicated to facilitating & changing conversations around mental health so that no one ever has to feel alone.
We offer community programming, events, and resources that bring people together over shared creative journeys to foster holistic connections and we aim to do it all at a very low to no cost.
By tapping into the power of art and storytelling, we create safe, supportive, and inclusive spaces that encourage positive mental health & wellbeing.
From the founder: While healing is a continuous journey and I am far from done, I have spent the last 10 years building spaces and collecting the tools that I wish I had when I was younger. Through that process, I obtained my Masters in Mental Health Counseling and have used that training to grow YAAP. The project started in Louisiana and I am excited to bring our programs to San Francisco and beyond. I hope you'll join for the first in what we hope to be regularly scheduled gatherings.

events.title: Write Your Heart Out with Britta Stromeyer
events.location: Book Passage, Corte Madera Store 51 Tamal Vista Blvd Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: "There is no greater agony than bearing an untold story inside you." – Maya Angelou Ever feel like your life has a million stories waiting to be told, but you aren't sure where to start? Join us for this soulful, 90-minute workshop designed to help you pause, reflect, and put pen to paper. Whether you want to craft "mini-stories" from your favorite memories or simply use journaling to make sense of the beautiful chaos of daily life, this workshop is your safe space to explore. What to Expect Guided Prompts: We’ll move past "dear diary" with creative triggers that spark vivid memories and deep insights. The Art of the Mini-Story: Learn how to capture a life lesson or a fleeting moment in just a few paragraphs. Clarity & Connection: Use writing as a tool to de-clutter your mind and find the "why" behind your experiences. Low Pressure, High Expression: No "writer" credentials required—just you, a notebook, and an open heart. Whether you’re looking for a new creative outlet or a way to process your journey, come discover how powerful your own narrative can be. Leave with a clearer mind, a fuller heart, and at least one story that’s uniquely yours. Meet Your Instructor Britta Stromeyer is a member of the National Book Critics Circle. Her writing appears in The Common, World Literature Today, Tupelo Quarterly, Beyond Words Magazine, Necessary Fiction, On the Seawall, Flash Fiction Magazine, Bending Genres Journal, Marin Independent Journal, and other publications. Britta was a finalist for the Bellingham Review Tobias Wolff Award for Fiction 2021. She is a frequent reader for the CLMP’s Firecracker Awards. A former editor for Tuxedo Literature & Arts & FastForward Magazine, Britta holds an MFA from Dominican University, CA, an M.A. from American University, and a Certificate in Novel Writing from Stanford University. Read more at brittastromeyer.com . What students are saying about Britta: "Britta was thoughtful and full of wisdom. This class was inspiring and thought provoking. I left inspired and full of possibility!" - Rebecca R. "As the first writing class I ever took, Britta’s workshop was an excellent way to kickstart my writing efforts. The rapidly paced and diverse prompt-writing exercises were challenging, thought-provoking and fun at the same time." - Laurie W

events.title: Stacey Gordon - The Pearl Farmers
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: This layered multigenerational novel follows three sisters upholding their family’s Tennessee pearl farm legacy. Rich with emotional depth and anchored by the pearl’s symbolism of beauty born from irritation, this story of resilience will captivate fans of Ann Patchett, Celeste Ng, and Claire Lombardo. Three estranged sisters—Helen, Anna, and Penn Lockshire—are bound by the shimmering but fragile legacy of their family’s freshwater pearl farm in rural Tennessee. When the business that once made them famous faces collapse, the sisters are pulled back into each other’s lives and forced to reckon with old betrayals, unspoken resentments, and the complicated truth of their inheritance. Soon, what began as a fight for survival becomes a reckoning with the myths that shaped them and the secrets buried in the family’s past. From the discovery of a rare pearl in 1981 to the struggles of a failing farm in 2008, the Lockshire sisters must navigate love, loss, ambition, and forgiveness to decide whether their heritage is a blessing to preserve—or a burden to escape. Rich with emotional depth and anchored by the pearl’s enduring symbolism—a thing of beauty born from irritation—this sweeping story of family, identity, and resilience will captivate readers of Celeste Ng and Claire Lombardo. “Gordon expertly handles her ambitious narrative and sprawling cast . . . A textured tale of renewed kinship and self-discovery.” —Kirkus Reviews “Heart-warming story of sisterhood, purpose, and family legacy.” —BookLife Reviews “ The Pearl Farmers was such a satisfying read . . . It’s an uplifting tale that resonates in these times.” —Ann Bancroft, author of Almost Family “I fell in love with Penny, Helen, and Anna, and was pulling for these three sisters to find a way back to each other. The Pearl Farmers is Yellowstone meets Little Women —but with way better jewelry!” —Emma Tourtelot, author of No One You Know Stacey Gordon grew up in the Appalachian foothills of southern Ohio and began her career as a trade journalist covering the cultured pearl and jewelry industries, visiting farms across Asia and companies around the world. For the past twenty-five years she’s worked in marketing and user experience design for the Silicon Valley tech industry. This is her debut novel. She lives with her family in Alameda, California. events.title: Kirk Lombard - The Shadow Stream
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: A throwback to family-reads-of-yore, this epic follows a troubled boy and a host of hilariously vexed animals who must save a river before it’s dammed, so they can save themselves. Perfect for ages 10+ and all adults! School Library Journal: Review of the Day “Kirk Lombard’s The Shadow Stream is a book of great originality, a book like no other, propelled by brilliant storytelling and original thinking (and fish!) that will engage readers of all ages — a perfect family book.” — Mark Kurlansky, author of Cod and Salt and World Without Fish Gabriel (“G” for short) is wasting away in the Abiddon County Juvenile Center when he’s introduced to the Shongunk River by his dying uncle. The river valley — trash-heaped but chock-full of mysteries and fish — wins G over. But, as G has learned, good things can’t last. The Shongunk is scheduled to be dammed by a local developer. In a matter of days, it will cease flowing, and all of the talkative creatures who live in the river valley will be as homeless as G. Just as G decides it’s no time to accept his fate, so too do the animals. To inspire an uprising, a young trout is nominated to make a fateful journey up the river; a raccoon swears a violent oath against humans; and a newly sober buck leads his skittish flock out of harm’s way. Together with G, they show there is power in all of us, even the smallest minnow. Kirk Lombard is an author, angler, sustainable fishmonger and tuba player who worked inside the juvenile rehabilitation system. His first book, the award-winning Sea Forager’s Guide to the Northern California Coast , was described as “poetry” for fish, by NPR. He lives in the Bay Area with his family, raising his children on herring and sea shanties. events.description: Join us for First Saturday Story time. Featuring Tala Rooh reading and signing copies of her new book: The Emotion Owl. Age Range: 4-8 (Note: Storytime age range is roughly 5-8 due to emotional awareness themes, though a mature 4-year-old should follow along as well.) Emmie is a kind and gentle Great Horned Owl. She finds her emotions can run quite foul. A wise mentor shows her a colorful way to turn those emotions into powers any day. But when a big storm hits in the night, can she use her powers to make things right? Author Bio: Tala Rooh’s debut children’s book draws on her distinctive background in design and workforce development, blending creativity with a deep understanding of people. She spent many years collaborating with a team of life coaches specializing in emotional awareness and mindfulness techniques. These experiences offered her a powerful new lens to view emotions, not as problems to fix, but as valuable internal tools to use. This insight, combined with her favorite mantra “Use your tools!” became the guiding light behind this story. Tala created this book to help young children connect more deeply with their big emotions. Through thoughtful storytelling and vibrant visuals, she invites readers to explore life’s ups and downs together, making the journey a little less bumpy and a lot more colorful. She is truly grateful for her loving family, who have been her biggest cheerleaders, trusted editors, and constant source of inspiration!

events.title: Joyful Raven's TACTICAL FRIVOLITY
events.location: Berkeley
events.description: (Please do not bring infants to the show) Born into a radical theater company, Joyful Raven was tasked from the tender age of 5 with the daunting mission to save the world from impending doom… using theater. Forced into animal-print unitards and political positions long before she was a consenting adult, she never had a fighting chance at anything resembling a normal life. You think your parents were embarrassing? Did you have to sing about salmon sex on stage, in a unitard, at 12 years old… WITH your parents? I didn’t think so. In an attempt to heal her hippie trauma, she runs away from home to seek solace in the arms of a spiritual teacher… and accidentally finds herself in the yoga-to-fascism pipeline. Can she save herself? Can she save the world… using theater?! Blending standup, drag, storytelling, & clown, Raven takes audiences on a dystopian and hilarious romp through the looking glass. ACTOR : Joyful Raven is an award-winning actor, director, and “story midwife” known for her powerful and thought-provoking solo shows, where she tackles thorny social issues with humor, heart, and nuance. Born into an iconic political theater family, she has been devising original work for over 20 years. Her first solo comedy, Tales of a Sexual Tomboy , was dubbed “…one of the funniest shows now on display on Bay Area stages” by the SF Chronicle, won Best of the Fringe at the 2016 San Francisco International Fringe Festival, and enjoyed an Off-Broadway run in 2017. Her latest solo show, Breed or Bust , was nominated for Best Comedy at the 2022 Hollywood Fringe Festival, critically acclaimed at the 2023 Edinburgh Fringe, where it won an Offie (OffWestEnd Award), and went on to have an extended run at The Marsh, where it received a Critics’ Pick in the SF Chronicle. She co-founded the award-winning theater company Rococo Risqué and co-authored four plays for the Prize of Hope-winning company Human Nature. As an actor, she has appeared in numerous stage and film projects, including Odyssey Works, the film The Pursuit of Happyness alongside Will Smith, and Spring Awakening, directed by Stafford Arima. Joyful holds an MFA in Dramatic Art from the University of California, Davis, and teaches solo performance and storytelling at Berkeley Rep School of Theatre, The Marsh, and her own studio in Berkeley. Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/joyfulraven/ Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/joyful.raven DIRECTOR : Jael Weisman , a founding member of the Dell’Arte Players Co. and a multi-Obie-winning director, is a trailblazer in actor-based theater, directing acclaimed productions like “Whiteman Meets Bigfoot,” “Performance Anxiety,” and “Mad Love.” With Dell’Arte, his works have toured extensively in South America and Europe, earning him numerous Dramalogue Awards for Directing. Noteworthy projects include “The Dragon Lady’s Revenge,” which traveled to New York and was awarded an Obie, the American premiere of “Red Noses” at the San Diego Repertory Co., “Uncle Gunjiro’s Girlfriend” at the Adelaide Festival, and “Mermaid Meat” for the Berkeley Symphony Orchestra. He has collaborated with luminaries like Carlo Mazzone-Clementi and Joe Chaikin and worked with renowned Bay Area performance artists including Jeff Raz and Brenda Wong Aoki. In his early career, he worked with The San Francisco Mime Troupe, directing among other things “The Dragon Lady’s Revenge,” which was awarded an Obie. Weisman holds a BA from Reed College and an MFA from Carnegie Tech Lighting Design : Kiara Valderrama Show Photos : Cynthia Smalley It is with great love and a deep bow of gratitude that I roast by inimitable parents, Jane Lapiner and David Simpson and their theater company Human Nature. events.title: Chris Trinidad’s Chroma Tonic
events.location: Bird & Beckett Books & Records, 653 Chenery Street, San Francisco
events.description: Naima Shalhoub, voice/keyboards; Scott Oshiro, flute/quantum electronics; Alex Heigl, guitar/effects; Chris Trinidad, bass/guitar/synth/bass; Cy Thompson, drums/percussion Chris Trinidad’s latest project Chroma Tonic weaves together musicians from wildly divergent backgrounds in order to concoct unique sounds and intriguing groove music. Drawing inspiration from ambient music pioneers Brian Eno and Robert Fripp, the early avant-garde space psychedelia of Pink Floyd, the progressive electronic rock of Tu-Ner, the adventurous electric hybrid experimentations of early seventies Miles Davis, Chris Trinidad’s Chroma Tonic blends these explorations with the influences of the members of the group. Naima Shalhoub provides vocal and synthesizer textures, Alex Heigl plays ambient and looped guitars, Cy Thompson brings an array of Afro-Caribbean percussive elements, Scott Oshiro performs on flute and programs the quantum (!!) electronic improvised live interactions, while Chris Trinidad holds down the foundation on bass guitar and synth bass. $25 cover charge; byob Students $10 For a reservation, call the bookshop at 415-586-3733

events.title: Lynne Kaufman's THE SECRET MUSEUM
events.location: San Francisco
events.description: Opening Reception Sunday, November 8 (Please do not bring infants to the show) Francesca, a contemporary American filmmaker, is shooting a documentary on a newly excavated fresco in Pompeii said to provide startling evidence about sex and the sacred. She has obtained exclusive rights to film the fresco through the good graces of Paolo, the museum’s director and her former college sweetheart. Through three time periods and the lives of three couples, THE SECRET MUSEUM explores the mysteries of eros. Lynne Kaufman ( Playwright ) is the author of 20 full-length plays that have been produced in San Francisco, Los Angeles, Washington D.C., and Louisville at such theatres as Magic Theatre, Actors Theatre of Louisville, TheatreWorks Silicon Valley, and many more –with Shameless Hussy being her most recent work which premiered at The Marsh San Francisco spring 2025. Four of Kaufman’s plays, Extreme Acts, Acid Test, Two Minds , Who Killed Sylvia Plath , and Poetic Justice, have premiered on stage at The Marsh, while two others, Exposing Margaret Mead and The Smartest Woman in America, have appeared on The Marsh’s digital platform MarshStream. Who Killed Sylvia Plath went on to win Best Play in The Marsh’s 2020 MarshStream International Solo Festival. Kaufman’s plays have won many awards including the Glickman Award for Best New Play ( The Couch ), the Kennedy Center’s Fund for New American Plays Award ( Speaking in Tongues ), and the Neil Simon Festival New Play Award ( William Blake in Hollywood ). Kaufman has published four novels, and her short stories have appeared in Cosmopolitan , Redbook , and McCall’s . She was also the recipient of the Otis Guernsey Outstanding New Voice in American Theatre Award from the William Inge Theatre Festival. Warren David Keith ( Director ) is delighted to be reunited with Playwright Lynne Kaufman. His work with her began in 2012 with the Marsh Berkeley premier of Acid Test: The Many Incarnations of Ram Dass , a solo piece in which he played the title role. The play was extended twice in Berkeley then transferred for one performance to a massive tent on Maui, Hawaii where it was seen and enjoyed by Ram Dass and about 300 devoted followers. Subsequently, Acid Test opened at the Marsh San Francisco in 2013 where it also had several runs. Keith has acted in theaters throughout the Bay Area, most recently in 1984 at the Aurora Theatre Company and as the Porter in the California Shakespeare Theater’s production of Macbeth . His film credits include Nomadland , The Last Black Man in San Francisco , Haiku Tunnel , Love and Taxes , Raising Arizona , Fargo , A Serious Man , and The Big Lebowski . As a director he mounted more than 15 productions for American Conservatory Theater’s Young Conservatory Program. He reunited with Ms. Kaufman to direct Who Killed Sylvia Plath and The Smartest Woman in America about the final days of Susan Sontag, both at the Marsh San Francisco. Arwen Anderson ( Performer ) returns to The Marsh, where she previously collaborated with Lynne Kaufman on a staged reading of her musical Map of Your Mind and performed in Kaufman’s Extreme Acts . Selected regional credits include Testmatch, Men On Boats, Heisenberg , Let There Be Love , A Christmas Carol , and Tales of the City (workshop) at American Conservatory Theater; King Lear , Romeo and Juliet , and The Verona Project at California Shakespeare Theater; August: Osage County , Anne Boleyn , Circle Mirror Transformation , Bellwether , and A Streetcar Named Desire at Marin Theatre ; An Accident , Mrs. Whitney , Expedition 6 , The Rules of Charity , and Mauritius at Magic Theatre; A White Girl’s Guide to International Terrorism, The Fit, and 77% at San Francisco Playhouse; Miss Julie at Stanford Repertory Theater; Lobby Hero and The Shape of Things at Aurora Theatre Company; You Know When the Men Are Gone and 4 Adverbs with Word for Word; and roles with American Stage Festival, San Jose Repertory Theatre, Marin Shakespeare Company, Brava Theater, Encore Theatre Company, and Central Works Theater Company. Her film work includes Hog Island , Ashley 22 , and Dark Retreat . Johnny Moreno ( Performer ) returns to The Marsh, where he previously performed in Lynne Kaufman’s Extreme Acts . He has also appeared at theaters throughout the Bay Area including American Conservatory Theater, Berkeley Repertory Theatre, San Francisco Playhouse, San Jose Stage Company, Marin Shakespeare Company, Center Repertory Company, Marin Theatre , Crowded Fire Theater, and Pacific Repertory Theatre. He has played award winning roles, such as Macheath in San Francisco Playhouse’s production of The Threepenny Opera (Theatre Bay Area Award for Best Actor in a Musical) , and Henry Higgins in San Francisco Playhouse’s production of My Fair Lady (San Francisco Bay Area Theatre Critics Circle Award for Best Actor in a Musical). He has appeared in numerous film and television productions, such as “Betas,” Callback (winner of the Chicago Indie Fest for Best Film), Upside Out (with Olympia Dukakis), Paradise Club, and I’m Still Here (with Joaquin Phoenix). Lyndsy Kail ( Performer ) Marsh Debut. Regional credits include The White Chip at Marin Theatre. California Shakespeare Theater, Center Repertory Theatre, B Street Theatre, Capital Stage, San Francisco Shakespeare Festival, San Jose Stage. FILM/TELEVISION: Trauma, All About Evil, The Optimist . Other: voice and performance capture for Star Wars: Tales from the Galaxy’s Edge, Star Tours, Fortnite, Monster High , many 2K games including BioShock Infinite, NBA2K, and the latest Mafia game. Training: BA in Classics at UC Berkeley and The Groundlings in LA. Joseph O’Malley ( Performer, AEA ) makes his Marsh debut, having performed at the Kennedy Center, La Jolla Playhouse, Berkeley Rep, Marin Theatre, Cal Shakes, Aurora Theatre, Marin Shakespeare and Center Rep. He is thrilled to reunite with director Warren David Keith for The Secret Museum . Up next: The Gift of Nothing and The Crucible at Marin Theatre, as well as Ang Lee’s film Gold Mountain . events.title: Assimilation
events.location: Z Below
events.description: A Word for Word and Z Space production · Stories by E.L. Doctorow & Tatyana Tolstaya Presented by Word for Word and Z Space Directed by Rotimi Agbabiaka In “Assimilation” by E. L. Doctorow, Ramon is offered a promotion and cash which could pay for grad school – if he agrees to enter a green-card marriage with his boss’s niece. When he agrees, he gets more than he bargained for. “Smoke and Shadows” by Tatyana Tolstaya centers on a Russian professor living in the U.S., navigating her professional life, her intimate relationships, and the mysteries of culture. Told with Tolstaya’s sharp, restrained wit, the story zeros in on the experience of living in a new culture, and the confusions and imbalance that can cause. What does it mean to assimilate? These two writers offer two very different perspectives.

events.description: The Cornley Polytechnic Drama Society is back, and this time they’re taking on Peter Pan . It’s their most ambitious production yet, complete with flying rigs, sword fights, and a very real crocodile problem. What could possibly go wrong? As technical mishaps pile up and tempers flare, the cast battles to keep the show on track while everything around them spectacularly falls apart. Lines are forgotten, scenery refuses to cooperate, and rivalries spill onto the stage in real time. From the creators of The Play That Goes Wrong , this riotous comedy delivers nonstop mayhem, perfectly timed chaos, and the kind of theatrical disaster you have to see to believe.

events.description: SFDanceworks returns to Z Space for its 9th season with a boldly curated program spanning modern-dance lineage and today's most distinct contemporary voices, ramping up toward the company's 10th anniversary. Highlights include a Merce Cunningham solo performed by San Francisco Ballet Principal Joseph Walsh, two world premieres including; a new group work for five dancers by Jermaine Maurice Spivey, and a piece for three performers by longtime collaborator Brett Conway. Yue Yin also returns with A Measurable Existence , newly cast with Lani Yamanaka and Sarah Chou. Together, the four evenings offer a program shaped by lineage, risk, and intimacy — a showcase of SFDanceworks' role as an incubator for contemporary dance heading into its milestone tenth season.

events.title: Brandon Woody’s Upendo / Gabrielle Cavassa
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
This concert, part of Terence Blanchard’s UpSwing series, shines a light on a pair of rising greats — trumpeter Brandon Woody and vocalist Gabrielle Cavassa — both rising artists with stunning debuts on Blue Note Records.

Starting his musical journey at seven, Brandon Woody is the most exciting young trumpeter of his generation. Already a veteran of work with Marc Cary, Solange, Robert Glasper, and Danilo Pérez, the Baltimore native will bring the stimulating compositions from his 2025 Blue Note debut, For The Love Of It All, with his hard-hitting band Upendo featuring keyboardist Troy Long, bassist Michael Saunders, and drummer Quincy Phillips. Woody made a major impression with Upendo during his appearance at the 42nd San Francisco Jazz Festival, and his Miner Auditorium debut will be a night to remember.

Vocalist and songwriter Gabrielle Cavassa, co-winner of the 2021 International Sarah Vaughan Jazz Vocal Competition, is best known to SFJAZZ audiences for her stunning performances with Joshua Redman’s quartet. She fell in love with jazz while attending San Francisco State and it was the city’s jazz scene that she credits for her “real education.” Since relocating to New Orleans in 2017, she’s thrived as a performer, bandleader, and composer, earning critical raves for her eponymous 2020 debut album. Her Blue Note debut, Diavola, features Redman, Jeff Parker, Larry Grenadier, Paul Cornish, and Brian Blade.

Personnel: Brandon Woody's Upendo; Brandon Woody (trumpet); Troy Long (keyboards); Michael Saunders (bass); Quincy Phillips (drums); Gabrielle Cavassa; Gabrielle Cavassa (vocals); Others TBA

events.title: Tierney Sutton & Tamir Hendelman Duo
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Joe Henderson Lab
events.description:
“One of the most lauded jazz vocalists of her generation” (The New York Times), Tierney Sutton is joined in duo by piano great Tamir Hendelman, exploring the trove of American Songbook classics from her latest album SPRING. Over a career spanning more than three decades, Tierney Sutton has earned international acclaim for her luminous tone, emotional depth, and fearless interpretive artistry. A nine-time GRAMMY nominee, Sutton first rose to prominence through her celebrated work with the Tierney Sutton Band, becoming known for inventive reimaginings of jazz standards and tributes to artists including Joni Mitchell and Frank Sinatra. Her recordings have consistently topped jazz charts while showcasing a rare balance of sophistication and intimacy.

Israeli-born pianist Tamir Hendelman is equally revered for his lyrical touch, harmonic brilliance, and dynamic versatility. After moving to Los Angeles as a teenager, Hendelman became a central figure in West Coast jazz, performing with the Clayton-Hamilton Jazz Orchestra, Barbra Streisand, Natalie Cole, and countless leading artists. His elegant playing and sensitive accompaniment have made him one of the most sought-after pianists in contemporary jazz.

Together, Sutton and Hendelman share a profound musical chemistry built on nuance, trust, and spontaneity. Their new duo album, SPRING, offers fresh interpretations of beloved standards, transforming familiar melodies into intimate conversations filled with warmth, wit, and timeless beauty.

Personnel: Tierney Sutton (vocals); Tamir Hendelman (piano)

events.title: The Commons Public Hours ☕
events.location: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco + Full Space
events.description:
🎉 Public Hours at the Commons 🎉
Every Sunday, the Commons opens to the public — no membership required. Come co-work, connect, create, or just explore the space at your own pace. ✨
🕘 When: Every Sunday, 9 AM – 10 PM
📍 Where: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco (corner of Hayes & Laguna, basement level)
RSVP and we'll email you your entry code ahead of time — so you can let yourself straight in when you arrive.
──────────────────────────────
🧭 A self-guided day
Public Hours are self-guided — come in, settle in, and make the space your own. Weekends are usually unstaffed, so there's no check-in desk or guided tour. Our members are glad to answer questions about the space; for anything else — including guided tours, which we don't offer as drop-ins — email hello@thesfcommons.com ahead of time.
──────────────────────────────
🔭 Getting in
Your entry code comes by email. Once you RSVP, we'll send you a personal QR code — that's your key for the day. Keep it handy on your phone (and check spam if you don't see it).
Find us. We're at 540 Laguna St, on the corner of Hayes & Laguna. Head down the stairs beside Earthbody to the basement level — that's the Commons.
Scan your QR code at the reader to unlock the door. Hold your phone just below the Kisi reader by the door and it'll let you in.
Your access stays active all day, 9 AM – 10 PM, so you can come and go freely.
Can't find your code on the day? No problem — scan the QR posted on the door to check in and get a fresh one on the spot.
We're shoes-off 🧦 — please clean up after yourself, including dirty dishes and mugs, and use only the front entrance. Trouble getting in? Email hello@thesfcommons.com.




The Commons is a modern-day town square for communal meaning-making, personal discovery, and self-expression in the heart of San Francisco. Apply to become a member here__.

events.title: Robin Rosenbluth, Rosanne Annoni & Georgine Hodgkinson - She Writes Press Event
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: Mothers and Daughters: Writing Formative Relationships in Memoir What does it mean to reckon with the past and find yourself on the other side? In this panel, three She Writes Press memoirists, Robin Rosenbluth, Georgine Hodgkinson, and Rosanne Annoni, explore the profound and complicated ways their mothers shaped them, and the unexpected journeys that led each of them home to herself. From a young white woman navigating the semi-nomadic communities of 1970s Kenya while carrying the wounds of the U.S. foster care system, to a spiritual seeker tracing the long arc between a childhood vision of Christ and a solitary winter at Gampo Abbey, to a college professor who upended her carefully controlled life for the wilds of Puerto Rico's cryptocurrency scene, these are stories of displacement, desire, and hard-won transformation. Moderated by She Writes Press publisher Brooke Warner, this panel is an invitation to explore those moments that break us open and the unlikely places where healing takes root. Each of these memoirs reminds us that growing up isn't something that happens only in childhood, and that our mothers, for better or worse, are the first maps any of us is given to navigate ourselves and our lives. Robin Rosenbluth is a former foster teen who advocates for finding permanent homes for older foster youth. She has worked in the nonprofit sector in New York as a fundraiser, an adjunct professor at Columbia University and New York University. She has studied memoir and the craft of writing with many renowned authors and writes a Substack, My Jagged Journey as a Debut Writer . Robin and her wife have raised two children who now have families of their own. She lives in Brooklyn, New York. Rosanne Annoni was a successful psychotherapist for thirty-five years in the Bay Area before becoming an ordained teacher of the Diamond Approach in 2000. She has taught students and mentored teachers in the United States, the UK, and the EU. In 2024, she was awarded an Emerging Writer Fellowship from Aspen Words. She is married, has one son, and lives with her husband and dog on Cape Cod. Georgine Hodgkinson is a professor of communication studies at Cosumnes River College in Sacramento, where she also served as program coordinator for Re-Emerging Scholars, a program for formerly incarcerated students. Her published scholarship includes book chapters, journal articles, and essays exploring politics, gender, and spirituality. In 2025, she was a People’s Choice Winner for the Amy MacRae International Memoir Award. A certified yoga instructor who loves to run and play pickleball, Georgine splits her time between Dorado, Puerto Rico, and Folsom, California, with her husband, Mark. Brooke Warner is publisher of She Writes Press, a memoir coach, and author of Write On, Sisters!, Green-light Your Book, What's Your Book?, and three books on memoir. She’s a TEDx speaker, weekly podcaster (of “Write-minded” with co-host Grant Faulkner of NaNoWriMo), and publishes a weekly newsletter, Writerly Things, on Substack at brookewarner.substack.com . Robin Rosenbluth, Rosanne Annoni, Georgine Hodgkinson, Brooke Warner - photos courtesy of the authors Event details: This event will be hosted by Book Passage at our Corte Madera store. Free Admission / Open Seating Following the presentation, there will be a signing line or a meet-and-greet. For any questions regarding our events, please contact us at books@bookpassage.com .

events.title: Kevin Waite - The Boundless Biddy Mason
events.location: Book Passage Ferry Building 1 Ferry Building San Francisco, CA 94111
events.description: Prize-winning historian Kevin Waite uncovers an extraordinary story of survival in this first book-length biography of Biddy Mason. The narrative follows Mason's journey from the cotton South to metropolitan California, detailing how she crossed the continent, broke free from slavery, and built Black Los Angeles. Through the lens of the Civil War, Reconstruction, and the dawn of Jim Crow, Waite reveals Mason's profound impact on California's history. Los Angeles’s leading Black property owner entered the city as a piece of property herself. Born enslaved in 1818, Biddy Mason was forcibly transported 3,000 miles to California before winning her freedom in a landmark 1856 court case. By the time of her death, she had become one of the wealthiest African Americans in the West – an entrepreneur, philanthropist, and founding mother of Black Los Angeles. The Boundless Biddy Mason: An Odyssey from Slavery to Freedom Across the American West, Kevin Waite’s masterful biography of Mason – the first full-length study of her extraordinary life – places Mason at the center of a larger American story: the expansion of slavery into the West, the legal battles that tested freedom’s meaning, and the rise of a vibrant Black Los Angeles community she helped build. Waite documents Mason’s early years in Mississippi and follows her forced journey across the continent, as one of roughly 1,500 enslaved African Americans who were trafficked from the slave states to the frontier. Her enslaver, Robert Smith, a convert to Mormonism, marched Mason and her children from Mississippi to Utah and ultimately to California. Despite the state’s constitutional ban on slavery, Smith became the largest slaveholder in California, with fourteen people under his control. But it wasn’t until Smith attempted to relocate his human chattel to Texas that the law intervened. A pitched legal battle in Los Angeles resulted in freedom for Mason, her three daughters, and ten other women and children. From that moment forward, Mason reshaped her destiny – and the destiny of her city. She built a respected practice as a nurse and midwife, invested shrewdly in downtown real estate, cultivated influential alliances, and helped found Southern California’s first Black church. Her canny ability to disarm her denigrators with kindness and competence earned Mason a reputation as a leader. Award-winning historian Kevin Waite ably connects Mason’s life to the nation’s great upheavals: the westward expansion of slavery, the Civil War and Reconstruction, and the dawn of Jim Crow. In doing so, he restores Mason to her rightful place in American history, detailing her role as a survivor of forced migration, a litigant in a landmark freedom suit, and an architect of Black Los Angeles. Mason’s legacy in Los Angeles endures to this day, not only as founding member of the First African Methodist Episcopal Church but also in the public works she inspired. “In this astute work of historical recovery, Kevin Waite has provided us with a definitive, modern biography of the remarkable Biddy Mason…a tremendous achievement and a cautionary tale for our own fraught times.” ―Manisha Sinha, author of The Rise and Fall of the Second American Republic: Reconstruction, 1860–1920 “Combining meticulous scholarship with taut, propulsive prose, Kevin Waite tells the story of how the quietly extraordinary Biddy Mason helped break slavery's hold on Southern California. Absorbing and revelatory, this is history at its best.” —Nathaniel Philbrick, National Book Award–winning author of In the Heart of the Sea and The Rush “Kevin Waite has written the book we’ve needed for a long time. Biddy Mason was a most extraordinary woman. With great care and exhaustive research, Kevin Waite has written her biography as part of the stories of enslavement and emancipation as well as faith and community at the western edge of the United States.” —Kelly Lytle Hernández, author of Bad Mexicans Kevin Waite is Anne Stark Watson and Chester Watson Distinguished Professor of History at the University of Texas at Dallas. His first book, West of Slavery , won the 2022 Wiley-Silver Prize and was shortlisted for three other awards, including the Lincoln Prize. His writing appears in The Atlantic , the Los Angeles Times , The Washington Post , Slate , National Geographic , and The New Republic . Kevin moonlights in the TV and film industry, most recently as the writer and producer of a six-episode docuseries on the American Revolution for National Geographic and Disney+. Emerging from the powerful Los Angeles music tradition, he’s known for his deeply expressive sound, high‑energy performances, and his belief in music as a force for healing, elevation, and cultural memory.

This performance highlights music from Lawrence’s new recording Turn the Music Up , a vibrant chapter in his catalog that celebrates joy, ancestral memory, and creative freedom. Over his extraordinary career, Lawrence has performed with giants such as McCoy Tyner, Miles Davis, Freddie Hubbard, Woody Shaw, Elvin Jones, Buster Williams, and Pharoah Sanders. His sound channels the spirit of John Coltrane while remaining unmistakably his own—expansive, soulful, and spiritually charged. With The Azar Lawrence Experience, he brings this legacy forward through a powerful ensemble rooted in master musicianship, improvisational fire, and deep spiritual intention.

The Azar Lawrence Experience is more than a concert — it is a transmission of sound, spirit, history, and uplift.

events.title: Lynne Kaufman's THE SECRET MUSEUM
events.location: San Francisco
events.description: Opening Reception Sunday, November 8 (Please do not bring infants to the show) Francesca, a contemporary American filmmaker, is shooting a documentary on a newly excavated fresco in Pompeii said to provide startling evidence about sex and the sacred. She has obtained exclusive rights to film the fresco through the good graces of Paolo, the museum’s director and her former college sweetheart. Through three time periods and the lives of three couples, THE SECRET MUSEUM explores the mysteries of eros. Lynne Kaufman ( Playwright ) is the author of 20 full-length plays that have been produced in San Francisco, Los Angeles, Washington D.C., and Louisville at such theatres as Magic Theatre, Actors Theatre of Louisville, TheatreWorks Silicon Valley, and many more –with Shameless Hussy being her most recent work which premiered at The Marsh San Francisco spring 2025. Four of Kaufman’s plays, Extreme Acts, Acid Test, Two Minds , Who Killed Sylvia Plath , and Poetic Justice, have premiered on stage at The Marsh, while two others, Exposing Margaret Mead and The Smartest Woman in America, have appeared on The Marsh’s digital platform MarshStream. Who Killed Sylvia Plath went on to win Best Play in The Marsh’s 2020 MarshStream International Solo Festival. Kaufman’s plays have won many awards including the Glickman Award for Best New Play ( The Couch ), the Kennedy Center’s Fund for New American Plays Award ( Speaking in Tongues ), and the Neil Simon Festival New Play Award ( William Blake in Hollywood ). Kaufman has published four novels, and her short stories have appeared in Cosmopolitan , Redbook , and McCall’s . She was also the recipient of the Otis Guernsey Outstanding New Voice in American Theatre Award from the William Inge Theatre Festival. Warren David Keith ( Director ) is delighted to be reunited with Playwright Lynne Kaufman. His work with her began in 2012 with the Marsh Berkeley premier of Acid Test: The Many Incarnations of Ram Dass , a solo piece in which he played the title role. The play was extended twice in Berkeley then transferred for one performance to a massive tent on Maui, Hawaii where it was seen and enjoyed by Ram Dass and about 300 devoted followers. Subsequently, Acid Test opened at the Marsh San Francisco in 2013 where it also had several runs. Keith has acted in theaters throughout the Bay Area, most recently in 1984 at the Aurora Theatre Company and as the Porter in the California Shakespeare Theater’s production of Macbeth . His film credits include Nomadland , The Last Black Man in San Francisco , Haiku Tunnel , Love and Taxes , Raising Arizona , Fargo , A Serious Man , and The Big Lebowski . As a director he mounted more than 15 productions for American Conservatory Theater’s Young Conservatory Program. He reunited with Ms. Kaufman to direct Who Killed Sylvia Plath and The Smartest Woman in America about the final days of Susan Sontag, both at the Marsh San Francisco. Arwen Anderson ( Performer ) returns to The Marsh, where she previously collaborated with Lynne Kaufman on a staged reading of her musical Map of Your Mind and performed in Kaufman’s Extreme Acts . Selected regional credits include Testmatch, Men On Boats, Heisenberg , Let There Be Love , A Christmas Carol , and Tales of the City (workshop) at American Conservatory Theater; King Lear , Romeo and Juliet , and The Verona Project at California Shakespeare Theater; August: Osage County , Anne Boleyn , Circle Mirror Transformation , Bellwether , and A Streetcar Named Desire at Marin Theatre ; An Accident , Mrs. Whitney , Expedition 6 , The Rules of Charity , and Mauritius at Magic Theatre; A White Girl’s Guide to International Terrorism, The Fit, and 77% at San Francisco Playhouse; Miss Julie at Stanford Repertory Theater; Lobby Hero and The Shape of Things at Aurora Theatre Company; You Know When the Men Are Gone and 4 Adverbs with Word for Word; and roles with American Stage Festival, San Jose Repertory Theatre, Marin Shakespeare Company, Brava Theater, Encore Theatre Company, and Central Works Theater Company. Her film work includes Hog Island , Ashley 22 , and Dark Retreat . Johnny Moreno ( Performer ) returns to The Marsh, where he previously performed in Lynne Kaufman’s Extreme Acts . He has also appeared at theaters throughout the Bay Area including American Conservatory Theater, Berkeley Repertory Theatre, San Francisco Playhouse, San Jose Stage Company, Marin Shakespeare Company, Center Repertory Company, Marin Theatre , Crowded Fire Theater, and Pacific Repertory Theatre. He has played award winning roles, such as Macheath in San Francisco Playhouse’s production of The Threepenny Opera (Theatre Bay Area Award for Best Actor in a Musical) , and Henry Higgins in San Francisco Playhouse’s production of My Fair Lady (San Francisco Bay Area Theatre Critics Circle Award for Best Actor in a Musical). He has appeared in numerous film and television productions, such as “Betas,” Callback (winner of the Chicago Indie Fest for Best Film), Upside Out (with Olympia Dukakis), Paradise Club, and I’m Still Here (with Joaquin Phoenix). Lyndsy Kail ( Performer ) Marsh Debut. Regional credits include The White Chip at Marin Theatre. California Shakespeare Theater, Center Repertory Theatre, B Street Theatre, Capital Stage, San Francisco Shakespeare Festival, San Jose Stage. FILM/TELEVISION: Trauma, All About Evil, The Optimist . Other: voice and performance capture for Star Wars: Tales from the Galaxy’s Edge, Star Tours, Fortnite, Monster High , many 2K games including BioShock Infinite, NBA2K, and the latest Mafia game. Training: BA in Classics at UC Berkeley and The Groundlings in LA. Joseph O’Malley ( Performer, AEA ) makes his Marsh debut, having performed at the Kennedy Center, La Jolla Playhouse, Berkeley Rep, Marin Theatre, Cal Shakes, Aurora Theatre, Marin Shakespeare and Center Rep. He is thrilled to reunite with director Warren David Keith for The Secret Museum . Up next: The Gift of Nothing and The Crucible at Marin Theatre, as well as Ang Lee’s film Gold Mountain . events.title: Tierney Sutton & Tamir Hendelman Duo
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Joe Henderson Lab
events.description:
“One of the most lauded jazz vocalists of her generation” (The New York Times), Tierney Sutton is joined in duo by piano great Tamir Hendelman, exploring the trove of American Songbook classics from her latest album SPRING. Over a career spanning more than three decades, Tierney Sutton has earned international acclaim for her luminous tone, emotional depth, and fearless interpretive artistry. A nine-time GRAMMY nominee, Sutton first rose to prominence through her celebrated work with the Tierney Sutton Band, becoming known for inventive reimaginings of jazz standards and tributes to artists including Joni Mitchell and Frank Sinatra. Her recordings have consistently topped jazz charts while showcasing a rare balance of sophistication and intimacy.

Israeli-born pianist Tamir Hendelman is equally revered for his lyrical touch, harmonic brilliance, and dynamic versatility. After moving to Los Angeles as a teenager, Hendelman became a central figure in West Coast jazz, performing with the Clayton-Hamilton Jazz Orchestra, Barbra Streisand, Natalie Cole, and countless leading artists. His elegant playing and sensitive accompaniment have made him one of the most sought-after pianists in contemporary jazz.

Together, Sutton and Hendelman share a profound musical chemistry built on nuance, trust, and spontaneity. Their new duo album, SPRING, offers fresh interpretations of beloved standards, transforming familiar melodies into intimate conversations filled with warmth, wit, and timeless beauty.

Personnel: Tierney Sutton (vocals); Tamir Hendelman (piano)

events.title: Maria Geyman Author Talk • With Tea: Culture, Accoutrements, and Rituals
events.location: Omnivore Books on Food, 3885a Cesar Chavez St, San Francisco, CA 94131
events.description: Maria Geyman is a board-certified naturopathic doctor and writer on culture, food, and beauty. With Tea is her first book. Her work has been featured in NYT, Goop, Vogue. She lives in Brooklyn, NY with her husband and two kids- Mona and Simon. Lauren Haynes is an herbalist, writer and the founder of Wooden Spoon Herbs. Her work centers around connection with the natural world through medicinal plants, and has been featured in Bon Appetit, The New York Times, Vogue and New York Magazine. She lives in Napa, California with her partner. Tea is the most consumed drink in the world after water, and a new generation is creating fresh ways of thinking about and drinking tea. Thoughtful, detailed, and visually stunning, this elevated, category-defining book explores tea’s health benefits and creates a framework for the new wave of recipes and tea rituals. Divided into three richly illustrated sections, each adorned with delicate watercolors and photography by a Vogue staff photographer, Part One explores tea culture, the importance of teas and herbs throughout history, and how tea culture can be found and enjoyed anywhere. Part Two brings tea into daily life with brewing techniques, recipes, accoutrements, rituals, and hosting tips. Part Three focuses on wellness and incorporating specific teas and herbs into health and beauty routines. Tea culture sits at the intersection of food, wellness, fashion, and beauty—and With Tea connects them seamlessly. Whether a seasoned connoisseur or a curious beginner, this is the ultimate celebration of tea, making it the perfect gift for tea lovers everywhere.

events.title: Song Circle with Amateur Music Network
events.location: Berkeley
events.description: October Theme: “Broadway and Show Tunes” There’s nothing that brings people together better than singing our favorite songs. It recalls summer nights around the campfire: someone strumming the guitar and all singing a mix of folk music, familiar songs we heard on the radio, and occasional new songs that someone shares. Nobody has to worry about whether you know the songs or can sing like a pro. This is our chance to share the joy of singing simply for the fun of it. Cary Sheldon is a singer, songwriter, and beloved Berkeley voice teacher with 30 years worth of grateful students. She has been playing and teaching in the Bay Area for the last 40 years. Her love for R & B music led her to be part of Zazu Pitts Memorial Orchestra in the 1980’s. Other affiliations include The Henry Kaiser Band, The Henriettas (a recreation of DeZurick sisters, a popular country music duo from the 1940’s), who appeared on Prairie Home Companion, and most recently her band DanceChant, a joyful community-inspired R&B band that encourages audience participation. She continues to be inspired by her love of singing in community. “Singing together with others is one of the greatest joys in my life.” Now in her 60’s, she returns to influences from her early life. Her grade school music teachers included John Langstaff, creator of the Christmas Revels, and the repertoire was based on the American folk tradition, including old English ballads, spirituals, freedom songs, and the popular folk and protest songs of the 1960’s. She hopes to inspire others to explore the depth of this material and rediscover the joy of community singing. Soprano Candace Johnson has led AMN’s Juneteenth Choral Celebration since its inception in 2020. The AMN community knows her through her commitment to the power of the Negro Spirituals tradition, but Candace has a deep connection to theater and to the music of the Broadway stage. A voice instructor at UC Berkeley for 17 years, in 2022 Candace also became the director of the University Gospel Choir. A lyric coloratura soprano, she crosses musical boundaries performing classical, jazz, musical theater, pop and gospel. She has sung on many stages, including Carnegie Hall and The Manhattan Center. Also a playwright and actress, Candace premiered her first one-woman show, Vox in a Box , in UC Berkeley’s Hertz Hall in 2018, which led to her becoming a resident solo artist at The Marsh theater (Berkeley/San Francisco). Candace has written and performed 5 full-length one-woman musicals. Her most recent show, Scat-ter Brain: The Music of ADHD , was commissioned by The Marsh in 2024 for its inaugural IFOYE festival of new works by women-identifying playwrights. Following an extended run, Scat-ter Brain was nominated by Broadway World SF for Best Solo Show of 2025. Please read our Health, Safety and COVID-19 Information Our commitment to our patrons

events.title: Alex George Author Talk • In the Mood to Bake: Extraordinary Treats from Lily P Crumbs
events.location: Omnivore Books on Food, 3885a Cesar Chavez St, San Francisco, CA 94131
events.description: Alex George is a self-taught baker, recipe developer, and food blogger whose TikTok channel, Lily P Crumbs, features her viral baking videos. She has been featured on Good Morning America and The Jennifer Hudson Show and collaborated with brands like Bob’s Red Mill and Domino Sugar. She lives in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. Becky Duffett is an award-winning food writer living and eating in San Francisco. Her work has appeared in Food & Wine, Bon Appétit, The New York Times, the San Francisco Chronicle, and the San Francisco Standard. She served as the deputy editor at Eater SF, reporting breaking news during the pandemic, while running the largest dining website in the Bay Area. She’s also a former cookbook editor and classically trained cook, graduating from the professional program at San Francisco Cooking School. She was a commis at Petit Crenn, and currently bakes at Kantine. In the Mood to Bake: Extraordinary Treats from Lily P Crumbs - Alex George, a.k.a. Lily P Crumbs, brings her joyful, over-the-top baking style straight to your kitchen. Known for her viral quest to test every chocolate chip cookie recipe she could find, George draws inspiration from the beloved snacks of the 1990s and early 2000s treats like Philadelphia Cheesecake Snack Bars, Confetti Snacking Cake, Salted Malted Blondies, and Baklava Monkey Bread . Her “more is more” approach invites home bakers to embrace bold flavors, playful textures, and the uninhibited joy of childhood sweets. In this debut collection, she guides readers through cookies, bars, breakfast bakes, cake-adjacent creations, and imaginative ice cream treats, all infused with her signature humor and warmth. Whether you’re whipping up Carrot Cake Scones or building Key Lime Pie Ice Cream Sandwiches , you'll rediscover the simple delight of dessert. With vibrant photography and endlessly creative sweets, In the Mood to Bake is a fresh, fun upgrade to the home-baking canon.

events.title: SCOTT LAMBRIDIS: ST. ULPHIA'S DEAD
events.location: Books Inc. Pruneyard, 1875 S Bascom Ave, Campbell, CA 95008
events.description: Join us at Books Inc. Campbell to celebrate author Scott Lambridis on the debut of his first novel, St. Ulphia’s Dead ! About the Book Disgraced medical researcher Mirs and his skeptical new supervisor Jo arrive on the remote island of St. Ulphia to investigate an outbreak of mass psychosis. The villagers claim they’re being possessed— one by one— by a cannibalistic demon known as the Wendigo. While unraveling the villagers’ strange tales, Mirs and Jo are drawn into a tangle of local politics, mysterious disappearances, and impossible contradictions. When the missing begin to reappear, the boundaries between fact and folklore become dangerously thin. As tensions rise and trust fractures, Mirs and Jo must confront the possibility that the madness around them may not be entirely imagined— or may not be the villagers’ alone. A psychological mystery laced with absurd humor, St. Ulphia’ s Dead explores how trauma warps truth, how isolation breeds belief, and how the most terrifying demons are the ones we conjure for ourselves. About the Author Born and raised in New York, Scott earned a degree in neurobiology from the University of Virginia. He’s toured the Midwest with a progressive rock band, founded an indie press and performance series, earned an MFA from San Francisco State University, tended a 40-acre olive farm, and read a book from every country of the world. He wrote St. Ulphia’s Dead during his daughter’s naps during a year in France, and finally settled with his wife and child in Bellingham, Washington, “the city of subdued excitement.”

events.location: City Lights, 261 Columbus Ave, San Francisco
events.description: FREE, $10–15 suggested donation Co-presented with City Lights Bookstore Jennifer Croft may be best known as one of our foremost literary translators, bringing such acclaimed international authors as Olga Tokarczuk and Urszula Honek to English-speaking audiences. She’s also gained acclaim for her own writing, including her novel The Extinction of Irina Rey and her hybrid coming-of-age memoir Homesick, called “stunning and surprising” by the New York Times. Now Croft follows up with a second memoir, detailing her lifelong wanderlust and her habit of both collecting and sending postcards along the way. Notes on Postcards utilizes an innovative format to delve into universal topics: love, loss, parenthood, communication, and connection. We’re thrilled to host the memoir’s official pub-day launch at City Lights, featuring Croft in conversation with Britta Stromeyer. Doors at 6:30pm.

events.title: RISING - Erin-Kate Whitcomb's Five Doors
events.location: Berkeley
events.description: (Please do not bring infants to the show) Delve into the fascinating world of five American women in different states across the country who are among the 80% of voters who rarely, if ever, engage in online rants or raves. We know that their votes count just as much. Experience their compelling stories, as they reveal intimate details of their lives and the experiences that shape their political beliefs. This captivating performance offers a rare glimpse into the moderate heart of America, often overshadowed by the radical fringes. Be prepared to laugh, reflect and question, as our writer and talented performer Erin-Kate Whitcomb impeccably brings these diverse characters to life. This riveting show offers a refreshing perspective on the political landscape, promising an evening of entertainment, humor and thought-provoking dialogue. Erin-Kate Whitcomb (AEA/AGVA/SAG-AFTRA) : Erin-Kate has been acting professionally for 30 years and has won Bay Area Critics Circle, Dean Goodman Choice and other awards for acting and playwriting. As a playwright, she was commissioned by Theatre Rhinoceros to write and perform her play “Route 80: Cars, Cows and Caffeine”, which won critical acclaim for her as a writer and multi-character actor. She has performed with 42 nd Street Moon, Berkeley Rep, TheatreWorks, Theatre Rhinoceros, Oasis SF and other Bay Area theatres. Erin-Kate performed in the US/Canadian tour with Dame Edna in “Dame Edna: My First, Last Tour” as Dame Edna’s disappointing daughter Valmai, and in the star-studded San Francisco revival of “Ruthless: The Musical”. Erin-Kate has supplied her voice for hundreds of radio and industrial jobs, and has appeared in TV and film for the past 35 years. Erin-Kate is a proud member and former Board Member of Northern California’s SAG-AFTRA, where she continues to serve both as an advisor, and on various committees. She is also a member of AEA (Actors Equity Association) and AGVA (American Guild of Variety Artists). EK is a fourth generation San Franciscan, and raised her sons, the fifth generation, in San Francisco with her wife, Michele. Francine Torres (Director) is a recent transplant from New York, where she served as Head of Acting at New Studio on Broadway. She holds an M.F.A. in Acting from UC San Diego/La Jolla Playhouse Professional Training Program, and a B.A. in Theatre from San Francisco State University. Presently, she serves on faculty at Foothill College. Francine began her career under the tutelage of Luis Valdez, founder of the iconic El Teatro Campesino. Steeped in the Teatro lifestyle of performing and touring, she began work with El Teatro de la Esperanza, and played the protagonist, Ana, in the inaugural production of Real Women Have Curves . Since then, she has been committed to educating, performing, and directing theatre exploring the Chicanx experience. She has mentored and taught underrepresented students of color at historically classical theatres such as the American Conservatory Theatre, the American Repertory Theatre, and the La Jolla Playhouse. Her work also includes nearly twenty years at the American Conservatory Theatre, teaching acting, improvisation, and clown work and transitions seamlessly between street and classical theatre. As a professional actor, she has created many indelible characters during her time at El Teatro Campesino and the American Repertory Theatre, has performed in repertory houses including Berkeley Rep, ACT, Dallas Theatre Center, La Jolla Playhouse, Theatresports, Killing My Lobster, and has toured the country and overseas. Francine’s most passionate interest is the intersection of diversity in theatre – gender, sexuality, color, neurodiversity and physical differences, and her experiences are published in the anthology Gravity Pulls You In . She plays the titular role in BITTEN (Bad Dog Productions), currently winning independent film festival awards across the country. events.title: Marcus Thompson, II - Game Changers
events.location: Book Passage Ferry Building 1 Ferry Building San Francisco, CA 94111
events.description: Acclaimed sports journalist Marcus Thompson II presents Game Changers , a fast-paced, stat-filled tribute to the unique players who changed basketball forever and spark endless GOAT debates among fans. Joining the fierce debates every obsessive fan loves to have, acclaimed sports journalist Marcus Thompson II presents a series of bold cases for who he thinks are the unique players who changed basketball forever. Michael Jordan. Dirk Nowitzki. Candace Parker. Steph Curry. These players from the modern era are among a handful of basketball's elite who have earned the rare title of Game Changer. Their contributions go beyond statistics and accolades, beyond wins and records. What they and others like them have achieved is nothing short of revolutionary when it comes to the trajectory of the game. In this utterly unique basketball history, Marcus Thompson II highlights a rare selection of players from the NBA and WNBA, building a thoroughly convincing case for each athlete that points to their irrefutable and lasting impact. Fast-paced with plenty of inarguable stats and well-reasoned takes sure to create endless debate among fans, Game Changers is a glowing tribute celebrating the players we love to crown as GOATS. Marcus Thompson II is a lead columnist at The Athletic. With more than twenty years’ experience, he has developed a respected voice in the industry through his storytelling, ability to connect with athletes, and unique perspective. He is the author of the national bestseller Golden: The Miraculous Rise of Steph Curry , KD: Kevin Durant’s Relentless Pursuit to Be the Greatest , and Dynasties: The 10 G.O.A.T. Teams That Changed the NBA Forever. He lives with his wife, Dawn, and daughter, Sharon, in Oakland, California. events.title: Santiago Lastra Author Talk • Mexican Soul: A New Style of Cooking
events.location: Omnivore Books on Food, 3885a Cesar Chavez St, San Francisco, CA 94131
events.description: Santiago Lastra- Born in Mexico City and raised in Cuernavaca, Santiago Lastra has worked in Michelin-starred establishments around the globe, including the legendary Mugaritz in San Sebastián, Spain and noma in Copenhagen. In October 2020, he opened the doors of KOL in Marylebone, immediately capturing the attention and acclaim of the world’s media. Within three years, KOL secured its first Michelin star, a place on The World’s 50 Best and La Liste, and is regarded as the best Mexican restaurant outside of Mexico. Santiago was also awarded Best Chef at the GQ Food and Drink Awards, and Three Knives by The Best Chef Awards. In 2024, Santiago opened Fonda, a family-style restaurant serving vibrant interpretations of the food found in Mexican markets and homes. Santiago’s ethos is to develop food that celebrates his homeland’s rich cultural tastes, aromas and textures with meticulously sourced seasonal local produce. Mexican Soul is his first book. Mexican Soul - D id you know you can make the best guacamole you’ve ever tasted without using avocado? Or that tortillas and tamales can be made with potato? Through years of research, exploration and cooking in restaurants around the globe, chef Santiago Lastra has discovered a secret: you can make incredible Mexican food without having to hunt down specific ingredients or buy traditional produce that has lost its freshness by the time it lands in your kitchen. Mexican flavor can be unlocked anywhere in the world, with almost any ingredient, and this book is the key to finding it. By breaking down the basics of Mexican flavour profiles then exploring how you can find a wide variety of these elements in your home kitchen, Santiago shows a new way of understanding one of the richest cuisines on the planet so that anything from a Salsa Macha and Tomato and Cherry Aguachile to Tinga Tostadas and Chocolate Tamales with Chocolate and Mezcal Cream can be on the table in minutes, regardless of what you have to hand. Get ready to discover Mexican Soul: A New Style of Cooking .

events.title: Andy Richter - Elf Unwrapped
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: Step into the magical world of ELF with this captivating oral history, written by beloved comedian and actor Andy Richter, who watched the on-set shenanigans unfold before his very eyes, and featuring a foreword by Will Ferrell!! Ever since Elf hit theaters, audiences around the world have fallen in love with the story of Buddy, the charming (and oversized) "elf" with a heart of gold. But what most people don’t know is that when the screenplay first hit Hollywood, no studio was willing to touch it. How, then, did such a risky gamble turn into one of the most beloved Christmas classics of all time? In this laugh-out-loud oral history, comedian and co-star Andy Richter goes on a mission to find out by reconnecting with the very people who brought this festive vision to life. Through exclusive interviews, hilarious anecdotes, and heartfelt reflections with key players like Will Ferrell, Zooey Deschanel, director Jon Favreau, and many others, Andy ultimately unwraps the story of how a quirky holiday film about a human raised by elves became such an enduring cultural phenomenon. Packed with never-before-seen photos, behind-the-scenes secrets, a foreword by Buddy himself (aka Will Ferrell), and a sprinkle of festive fun, this book is the perfect gift for anyone who believes in the magic of Christmas—and knows that the best way to spread holiday cheer is by singing loud for all to hear. Andy Richter is a comedian, actor, writer, and host. He's best known for his many years as Conan O’Brien’s collaborator and sidekick. He has appeared in numerous television shows and films, some of them quite good. He is also the host of the Three Questions podcast and The Andy Richter Call-In Show , and enjoyed a longer-than-expected run on Dancing with the Stars . He's based in Los Angeles. Aaron Karo (not appearing) is a comedian, screenwriter, author, and podcaster. His books include Ruminations on College Life , Ruminations on Twentysomething Life , I’m Having More Fun Than You , Lexapros and Cons , Galgorithm , and the #1 New York Times bestseller The Hidden Power of F*cking Up . He has developed television series for many studios and networks, and starred in his own one-hour Comedy Central stand-up special. He is based in Los Angeles. Along the way he studied classical music, jazz, played in basements and coliseums and absorbed the Bay Area Multi Kulti , the funk of New Orleans, and the New York Downtown edge. His 2007 CD “Party Hats” as well as his 1997 collaborative project T.J. Kirk “If Four Was One” were both nominated for Grammys. “Pond Life”, released 2022 on Dreck to Disk records is his11th album as a leader.

events.title: HERLIN RILEY
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: One of today’s premier jazz drummers · "The Groove Master", Herlin Riley is widely considered one of the best drummers in any genre of music performing today. The longtime drummer for the legendary Ahmad Jamal and the Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra now leads two groups, his quintet and the New Orleans Groove Masters featuring himself, Jason Marsalis, and Shannon Powell. Herlin’s most recent album, Perpetual Optimism, reunites the quintet of rising stars that Riley assembled for his Mack Avenue Records debut, New Direction. Since the release of that acclaimed album, all four of Riley’s bandmates – trumpeter Bruce Harris, saxophonist Godwin Louis, pianist Emmet Cohen, and bassist Russell Hall – have been making major waves across the modern jazz scene, attesting to the master drummer’s Art Blakey-like ear for talent and sage musical guidance. Herlin Riley's source of strength comes from his faith in God, his wife of four decades, and his family of five children and 10 grandchildren; his lifelong home in New Orleans, the creative community that surrounds it, and his positive approach to life and music. His roots in the church are also vital, shining through in the congregational claps that help establish the celebratory spirit that is showcased in the album opener “Rush Hour.” He also relies on his musical family, including his long-established ties with Wynton Marsalis and the Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra. Riley’s connection to the Marsalis dynasty traces back a generation earlier, to family patriarch and fellow lifelong New Orleanian Ellis Marsalis. It was while performing with Ellis at the annual New Orleans Jazz and Heritage Festival in a trio with bassist Reginald Veal that Riley first caught the ear of Wynton, who invited both members of his father’s rhythm section to join him, launching a vital relationship that’s now lasted more than three decades. Riley pays homage to his mentor on the closing track of Perpetual Optimism, the funky arrangement of Ellis Marsalis’ composition “Twelve’s It.” In the quintet’s lively rendition, the tune is not just a cover but a tribute, as Riley intones a short ode to passing the torch that refers to the elder Marsalis as “a great musician who taught a whole lot of fellows.” Another Crescent City icon, the late singer, pianist, songwriter, and producer Allen Toussaint, was the motivator behind Riley’s other vocal turn on the album, a gritty take on Willie Dixon’s blues classic “Wang Dang Doodle.” Toussaint stopped in to hear Riley play at a New Orleans club and heard the drummer’s 5/4 arrangement of the familiar standard. “He was really impressed,” Riley recalls. “He said, ‘Wow, man, I’ve heard ‘Wang Dang Doodle’ a thousand times, but I’ve never heard it performed in 5 before. You should record that.’ A few months later, he passed away, so I recorded the tune to pay homage to the wishes of the great Allen Toussaint.” Though he conveys vivid emotion in his voice, Riley stops short of calling himself a singer. His willingness to step to the mic comes from advice he was given by New Orleans vocal great Germaine Bazzle. “She’s a very elegant and regal lady, but when she’s performing, she scats, rolls her shoulders, dances, and really engages in the music with honesty and passion,” says Riley. When he asked her how she reconciled those two extremes, Bazzle told him, “’ You have to allow yourself to become emotionally naked when you’re on the bandstand.’ When she said that, a light bulb went off in my head. I’m not a singer, but I just do what I do, and I have the audacity to be uninhibited.” The same can be said for Riley’s work behind the kit, where he leads his stellar band with infectious enthusiasm and bristling swing. His “Be There When I Get There” captures the anticipation and excitement of rushing to an eagerly awaited appointment, whether a romantic rendezvous, a gathering of friends, or a night of music. The brisk “Borders Without Lines” comes from the pen of Riley’s Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra bandmate Victor Goines, while the classic “You Don’t Know What Love Is” becomes a sultry simmer, highlighted by Harris’ mournful, muted trumpet. The title track is the rare Riley original composed in a major key, and its sunny disposition perfectly communicates his unflagging hopefulness. The lovely “Touched,” featuring Louis’ achingly lyrical alto, recalls a tender moment with the drummer’s mother before she passed away. “I was in her room in her last days, and she rubbed my head. I’m a grown man, but I felt like an innocent child. There’s a special love wrapped in the touch of a mother of every living creature. That special euphoria only comes from her.” The bittersweet “Wings and Roots” looks to the next generation, referring to Riley’s philosophy of raising children: “You have to root them in good values and fundamental characteristics, but once they get to be a certain age, you have to give them the wings to be free, to go out and be themselves.” Finally, “Stella By Starlight” is another nod to the American Songbook, taken at a graceful midtempo pace with Cohen’s deft touch over Riley’s sensitive brushwork. In the end, Riley hopes that the music of Perpetual Optimism helps spread the upbeat manifesto that he’s chosen to live by. “I always look forward, no matter what happens in life. If you’re grieving or faced with an emotional challenge, keep in mind: If you’re still breathing, there’s a chance that you can overcome and thrive. Commit yourself to PERPETUAL OPTIMISM!”

events.title: Somatic Healing 101: The Missing Link to Lasting Change
events.location: 550 Laguna St, San Francisco + Full Studio
events.description:
A somatic workshop to understand your nervous system, reconnect with your body, and learn practical tools for real transformation...
Have you ever known exactly what you "should" do, but still found yourself stuck in the same patterns?
Maybe you've read the books, listened to the podcasts, journaled, reflected, and tried to think your way into change. Yet anxiety, overwhelm, self-sabotage, emotional reactivity, procrastination, or feeling disconnected from yourself keep showing up.
That's because lasting transformation doesn't happen through the mind alone. It happens through the body.
In this immersive workshop, you'll learn the foundations of somatic healing and nervous system regulation, and why working with your body is often the missing piece when it comes to creating meaningful, sustainable change.
We'll explore how stress, emotions, beliefs, and protective patterns are stored in the body, and why healing becomes more effective when we include the nervous system in the process.
You'll learn:
What somatics actually is (and why it's becoming more popular)
Why mindset work alone isn't enough to create real, lasting change
How your nervous system influences your emotions, behaviors, and daily experiences
Simple somatic tools you can use to feel more grounded, present, and connected
How to work with your body instead of constantly trying to push through or override it
This workshop isn't just educational — you'll also experience somatics firsthand through guided practices, including breathwork, body awareness, grounding exercises, mindful movement, and embodiment practices designed to help you reconnect with yourself and your body's wisdom.
You'll leave with:
A clear understanding of what somatic healing is and how it works
Practical tools you can immediately integrate into daily life to finally feel more calm and present
Greater awareness of your nervous system and stress responses
Simple ways to deepen your connection to your body, emotions, and intuition
A new approach to personal growth that feels supportive, sustainable, and effective

Whether you're completely new to somatics or looking to deepen your understanding of holistic healing, this workshop will give you a strong foundation and simple practices you can return to anytime!
Please bring a journal and water bottle, and wear comfortable clothes.
NOTE: Please be on time for this session — doors will close promptly and there will be NO LATE ENTRIES!
About Anna Bolender:
Anna Bolender is a certified Somatic Embodiment & Intuitive Life Coach, Somatic Breathwork and Quantum Wellness Practitioner, Reiki Master, and lifelong student of holistic health and well-being.
Through her coaching programs and workshops, Anna guides others to return home to themselves — releasing what keeps them stuck, reconnecting with their body and inner wisdom, and creating real, lasting transformation from the inside out.
Blending somatics, energy healing, quantum wellness, and mindset work, she helps clients break free from self-sabotaging patterns, repattern their nervous system, and cultivate simple daily rituals that support a fulfilling, grounded, and aligned life.
Anna’s mission is to empower others to feel connected, alive, and radiant — no matter what life brings.
Instagram: @annaalexbee
Podcast: RADIANT YOU (available on all podcast platforms)
Website: www.annabolender.com
