events.title: Illah Nourbakhsh - Crunch Time
events.location: Book Passage Ferry Building 1 Ferry Building San Francisco, CA 94111
events.description: As workers and as parents, we all care deeply about how we must prepare ourselves and our children for fulfilling careers at a time when the changing nature of labor is opaque. In this interactive book talk, co-author Illah Nourbakhsh will share brief remarks regarding our voyage in researching and writing a book about careers, AI and the future of education. We will be joined by two special pioneers who will make brief remarks from the audience: Alan Eustace and Professor Michael Genesereth. Alan Eustace served as senior vice president at Google and has witnessed the digital and AI technology revolutions firsthand. Michael Genesereth is faculty at Stanford University and charted the course of artificial intelligence research as one of its founding scholars. Both Alan and Michael care deeply about the next generation, and the ways in which careers will evolve as AI changes the shape of work. We look forward to a dynamic conversation with the audience. Featuring curated essays from leaders in tech and education, Crunch Time empowers parents, educators, students, and professionals to get informed and access their agency in the AI age. The AI revolution is underway, and none of us are fully prepared. In Crunch Time , education and AI experts Illah Nourbakhsh and Michael Druckman confront one of the central questions of our time: How will artificial intelligence reshape careers, education, and opportunity, and what should we do about it now? Rather than predicting a single future, Crunch Time presents AI as a dynamic, uncertain force that demands informed participation. Originally conceived for educators and parents, the book expands its lens to include students, alumni, mid-career professionals, employers, policymakers, and anyone navigating work and learning in the age of AI. Crunch Time weaves together perspectives from AI inventors, business leaders, educators, technologists, and community leaders, featuring more than forty contributors including AI experts Daniela Rus, Hoda Heidari, Michael Genesereth, Sanjay Sarma, university presidents Nancy Cantor, Lisa Ryerson, Laura Walker, Juan Salgado; business leaders David Siegel, Steve Malony, Dan Draper; visionaries Dame Diane Coyle, William Haseltine, Paul LeBlanc; and leading K to 12 educators. Readers will encounter competing viewpoints, practical guidance, and concrete steps for action. Crunch Time is an invitation to understand, to prepare, and to actively shape a more equitable and human-centered AI future. This timely and empowering book is essential reading for students, parents, educators and leaders who wish to shape an AI future that expands opportunity and strengthens our shared humanity. — Farnam Jahanian, President, Carnegie Mellon University For a book about artificial intelligence, this is brimming with human intelligence. You'll find thoughtful, nuanced, and provocative strategies for growing up and thriving in the age of AI. This book challenges us to redesign the connection between education and employment with intention and courage. This is a powerful call to ensure the AI age expands opportunity and strengthens pathways to meaningful work for all. — Lisa Marsh Ryerson, President, Southern New Hampshire University Our youth are growing up in the middle of a massive transition into the age of AI. Smart guides are critical to navigating this rough terrain, and this book is one of those guides. It elevates the power of human intellect and creativity, providing much-needed guidance on how to harness new technologies for the good of society and humanity. — Lisa Guernsey, Senior Director of Birth-12th Grade Policy, New America Illah R. Nourbakhsh is Kavcic-Moura Professor of Robotics at Carnegie Mellon University, inaugural Executive Director of the Center for Shared Prosperity, and co-director of the Community Robotics, Education and Technology Empowerment Lab. He was the Inaugural K&L Gates Professor of Ethics and Computational Technologies. He obtained his PhD in Computer Science from Stanford University. In 2009 the National Academy of Sciences named him a Kavli Fellow. In 2013 he was inducted into the June Harless West Virginia Hall of Fame. He was previously Robotics Group Lead for NASA/Ames. In 2019 he was named a Hastings Fellow. He has co-authored textbooks and popular literature, including Turn Left , AI and Humanity , Robot Futures , and Parenting for Technology Futures . He has authored articles for The New Yorker and Foreign Affairs, in addition to academic journals and book chapters. He is a trustee of the Claude Worthington Benedum Foundation, Winchester Thurston School and the Southwestern Pennsylvania Environmental Health Project. Michael Druckman (not appearing) is the Executive Chairman and architect of Schools That Can, a national not-for-profit network of urban K to12 schools since 2006 that prepares historically marginalized youth for post-secondary success. He currently is a Fellow of the Leadership and Society Initiative at the University of Chicago. Michael established the “Senator Robert F. Kennedy Education Awards” in partnership with Robert and Ethel Kennedy Human Rights in 2014 to recognize K to 12 school leaders, teachers and students for moral courage and the “Schools That Can Leaders That Can Awards” in 2017 to recognize leaders giving back to our society’s well-being in service of our youth. Both recognitions remain active. Michael chaired the Trey Whitfield School board in East New York, Brooklyn for many years, served on the Portal Learning board in Los Angeles, acted as an advisor to many K-12 schools over the last twenty years and was recognized as Founding Chairman Emeritus of the NYU Center for Global Affairs where he served as Co-Chairman for fourteen years. Illah R. Nourbakhsh - photo courtesy of the publicist Event details: This event will be hosted by Book Passage at our Ferry Building store. events.title: Kate Doerge with Myra Sack - Reimagining Grief
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: An inspiring guide that reimagines the stages of grief into five healing actions, Reimagining Grief offers light and a new way forward in the midst of darkness. This is the book Kate wishes she'd had, and she wrote it for you. Kate will be joined in conversation by Myra Sacks, the author of award-winning memoir, " Fifty-Seven Fridays: Losing Our Daughter Finding Our Way ," and founder of E-Motion, Inc. There is no way to spin grief. It's hard. It's messy. It's destabilizing. And every single one of us has to go through it. Author and grief coach Kate Doerge knows this too well. Over six years, she lost her father to heart failure and her mother in a car accident five days before Christmas. She also faced the hardest challenge for any parent, losing her sixteen-year-old daughter, Penny, to complications from a rare genetic condition. After Penny's death, Kate knew she had a choice, she could lose herself to a grief so powerful she might not come back from it—or she could find another way through. Reimagining Grief is the result of that search. Drawing from her own experience, the latest research, and conversations with others who have faced devastating loss, Kate offers five actions that can help ground you when you feel out of control, lift you when you're depleted, and help you process the pain of loss. In this book, you'll learn: Why There Isn’t One Right Way to Grieve — and How to Find Your Own Path An Approach to Saying Goodbye That Honors Both You and Your Loved One The 5 Actions Through Grief — and How to Use Them to Heal What Post-Traumatic Growth Really Looks Like How to Find Joy Again Turning Pain into Purpose These actions won’t make grief vanish or disappear; everyone has to go through the difficult path that you are put on after losing someone you loved deeply. However, Reimagining Grief offers some light and healing in the midst of darkness and a different way forward. This is the book Kate wishes she'd had. She wrote it for you. Kate Doerge is a USA TODAY bestselling author, motivational speaker, certified grief coach, and founder of Penny’s Flight Foundation. Through heartfelt storytelling, research-backed insights, and practical strategies, Kate inspires audiences to navigate change, embrace resilience, and lead lives filled with greater purpose and connection. Myra Sack is the author of award-winning memoir, " Fifty-Seven Fridays: Losing Our Daughter Finding Our Way ," and founder of E-Motion, Inc. a nonprofit organization created to support community, movement and ritual to enhance coping and resilience. Myra's life changed when her older daughter, Havi, died in January 2021. Blending Myra's lived experience and knowledge as a certified Compassionate Bereavement Care provider with her lifelong identity as an athlete and career in social impact, E-Motion evolved out of a new way of living with the most difficult reality. Myra holds an MBA in Social Impact from Boston University, and graduated with a B.A. cum laude from Dartmouth College, where she captained the women's soccer team and earned All-America honors. Myra serves on the Board of the Courageous Parents Network. events.title: And If I Die Before I Wake: George M. Johnson with Maggie Tokuda-Hall
events.location: Marcus Books, 3900 Martin Luther King Jr Way, Oakland, CA 94609
events.description: FREE, $10–15 suggested donation Co-presented with Marcus Books Journalist and activist George M. Johnson’s All Boys Aren’t Blue, their bestselling, critically acclaimed YA “memoir-manifesto” about growing up Black and queer, has been, since its 2020 publication, a source of solace and support for young people. It’s also consistently been at or near the top of the ALA and PEN America’s lists of the most challenged and banned books. Undeterred, Johnson continues to practice their fearless form of truth-telling, this time in their first memoir for adults, And If I Die Before I Wake. Here Johnson relates a traumatic 15 years in their life—navigating an HIV diagnosis, alcoholism, loss, and those disheartening and frightening book bans—while relying more than ever on the love of friends, family, and community and finding, against the odds, their most authentic self. events.description: The Cornley Polytechnic Drama Society is back, and this time they’re taking on Peter Pan . It’s their most ambitious production yet, complete with flying rigs, sword fights, and a very real crocodile problem. What could possibly go wrong? As technical mishaps pile up and tempers flare, the cast battles to keep the show on track while everything around them spectacularly falls apart. Lines are forgotten, scenery refuses to cooperate, and rivalries spill onto the stage in real time. From the creators of The Play That Goes Wrong , this riotous comedy delivers nonstop mayhem, perfectly timed chaos, and the kind of theatrical disaster you have to see to believe.

events.title: Matt O'Hara's "THE FLYING DEATH"
events.location: Mrs. Dalloway's, 2904 College Ave, Berkeley, CA 94705
events.description: Matt shares his dramatic tale of gentlemen-explorers of the 1930s racing to find and harvest a poisonous Amazon vine. Join us at Mrs. Dalloway's Bookstore on Thursday, November 12 at 7:00 PM when Matt O'Hara comes to the store to present his new book The Flying Death: Poison, Plunder, and the Quest for a Miracle Medicine in the Amazon . Matt will be joined by Rebecca Herman for the conversation and will sign copies of his book after the presentation. In the fall of 1938, a young, frail American explorer set off down a river in the western Amazon in search of curare, a poison he thought might save his life. Richard Gill had learned that local tribes used curare-laced blow darts to kill animals, but it was also potentially a cure for many ailments, including his own. He also thought he could make a fortune by connecting the knowledge of two worlds. Obsessed with curare, he raced to make deals with Indigenous poison masters in the Amazon and pharmaceutical companies back home, even as his Russian-born rival Boris Krukoff sought to do the same. In The Flying Death , the historian Matt O'Hara asks who and what we are willing to sacrifice in the name of discovery and profit. O'Hara brings to life Gill's epic quest, a stranger-than-fiction true story that moves from unexplored territory in the Amazon to rogue medical trials and cutthroat corporate boardrooms in the United States. Navigating treacherous terrain and politics, Gill and Krukoff successfully created a veritable curare–industrial complex, as the plant became a key element in shock therapy, transformed surgery in the United States and across the globe, and eventually led to a Nobel Prize. The Flying Death offers a thrilling ride across Indigenous knowledge, scientific exploration, and exploitation, unearthing a story of discovery that poses searching questions about the price of progress, who pays it, and who gets credit. MATT O'HARA is a professor of history at the University of California, Santa Cruz. He is the award-winning author of many journal articles and two books, The History of the Future in Colonial Mexico and A Flock Divided: Race, Religion, and Politics in Mexico, 1749–1857. REBECCA HERMAN is Associate Professor of History at UC Berkeley, where she teaches about environmental politics, US-Latin American relations, and modern Latin America. She is the author of Cooperating with the Colossus: A Social and Political History of US Military Bases in World War II Latin America and is currently at work on a book about anti-extractivism in Antarctica. Her first novel, The Outposters , will be published next summer by Cardinal.

events.title: JACKIEM JOYNER
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Contemporary saxophonist, author, and music producer Jackiem Joyner is set to release his 7th album, Touch, worldwide this fall, 2019. After more than 12 years as a recording artist, Jackiem continues to stand out with electrifying live performances and brilliant music productions. As a performer, he has toured over 30 countries and performed with the likes of the late George Duke, Marcus Miller, Keiko Matsui, Donnie McClurkin, Angela Bofill, Najee, Kirk Whalum, Peter White, and many, many more. Joyner’s radio success is widely known within the industry. Joyner has two number-one hit songs, five top 10 Billboard singles, and a number-one debut album under his belt. In addition, he published the highly acclaimed science fiction novel Zarya , which received high praise and a five-star rating on Amazon. “This album is about romance,” Joyner explains of Touch . “I wanted to give everyone something hip, smooth, and sexy at the same time.” The record has an urban feel, laced with the hottest downtempo vibes. The album shares similar textures to the music of artists Tank and Trey Songz. Joyner’s soprano sax leads the charge through most of the album. “My approach to performing on this record was to be melodic and dynamic with my horn”. Peter White joins Jackiem on the first single, “Last Dance”. The combination of soprano sax and nylon guitar pulls you in with its romantic and catchy melody. Najee serves up the flute on a dreamy urban song called “Fairytales”. The unique mix of flute and soprano sax on this vibey tune forms one of Joyner’s best performances and productions. The song was written together with Tim Bailey, aka Twizzboy. Born to a Vietnam War veteran father and a dedicated mother in Norfolk, VA, growing up wasn’t easy for Jackiem. He set his sights high from a young age; he always dreamed of being a performing artist, as unlikely as it was, given his humble upbringing. Even as a child, he loved the attention he received from his family when he danced to Michael Jackson songs. Now, Jackiem is proud to stand front and center on the main stage most weekends around the country. A quick glance at Joyner’s track record makes it clear that he continues to beat the odds in a tough and competitive music industry. “I love what I do, and I have passion”, Jackiem says. “I don’t care how hard things get, it’ll never stop me from doing what I love: playing the sax, writing music and stories, and performing live.” His love of writing novels came as a surprise to many of his fans. “I’m very excited to release my second novel soon after my album release,” Joyner says. “Writing stories is now a big part of my creative journey.” The first single from Joyner’s last album, Main Street Beat (2017), was named for his daughter, Trinity. Joyner’s adoration for his little girl is clearly expressed through the live, pop-influenced song, driven by Steve Oliver’s guitar. The song was an instant hit. Reaching no. 2 on the Billboard. We’re all dying to see if she follows in dad’s footsteps with her own stage career someday! With the creation of his company, JOYNER MEDIA COMPANY L.L.C., Joyner hopes to inspire other creators to follow their dreams and realize their true potential in art and multimedia. When Jackiem is not touring the world, he spends time giving lectures to students across the country. He also enjoys talking to band classes, helping them with practice, and offering insight on how to pursue a career in the performing arts. Currently, Joyner is on a US tour in support of his new album, Touch . He will be touring Los Angeles, CA – Washington, DC – Hampton, VA – Melbourne, FL – Detroit, MI – Chicago, IL – Charleston, SC – Houston, TX – Rehoboth Beach, DE – Mazlatan, Mexico – Syracuse, NY – Tampa, FL – Atlanta, GA, and many more cities.

events.title: LIVE MUSIC: School Fair, goldenstar, Poor Image (Presented by THROWIN' BO'S)
events.location: 4-Star Theater, 2200 Clement St, San Francisco, CA 94121
events.description: Throwin’ Bo’s presents: School Fair School Fair (Findlay Buchanan, Semisi Ma’ia’i, Hamish Morgan, De Stevens and Rose Pickernell) make music embedded in the human experience. It’s a product of the band’s native New Zealand, a place that remains intimate and remote, where emotion is magnified over both distance and familiarity. The five band members began the project renting out a factory-sized, sub-zero degree Celsius room normally operated by construction workers in the industrial area of Ōtepoti, Dunedin, New Zealand in 2021, recording music on the 4-track tape recorder that would become debut Gorse on a Hill . The album remained the only trace of the band online for a few years, an artifact for those who know where to look. School Fair’s music has this sense of self-discovery when you find it, a sound that feels both recognizable and like the vacant expanse of a country whirring by on a train. Still with little to no self-promotion, the appearance of sophomore effort Bird the Kid online in early 2025 was a new portal to their world of melodic and intricate indie music that retains a kind of atmospheric beauty. Unexpected Violence (Mutual, 2026) is the first record made between geographical places, with the band now split in between London and New Zealand. You can hear this fragmented approach in the patchwork quality and inherent connective tissue of the album. Recorded initially in a studio in East London, it was the first time the band brought in an outside engineer (Syd Kemp?), as opposed to the band’s prior live recordings, where the tendency was to “feed back off each other in quite a messy abstract and complicated way that works for us but isn’t typically structured.” The band then took these recordings and evolved them back home in Dunedin, with the addition of vocals on some tracks by Pickernell adding to the cohesive energy and collective, dialed-in synergy of the quintet. School Fair is built upon the many eclectic mediums from which the band members individually create: time spent repairing old machines, making short films, metalworking and jewelry-making, writing and engineering. All these counterparts bring a kind of industrial electricity to the music where each part feels necessary and agile, as well as perfectly in conjunction. It’s these points beneath the surface where the songs really bloom. The moody transference of guitar lick to guttural vocal and back again, where melody conjoins with surprising inflection and sharp-hued ambiance, littered with both poetic spoken-word and a self-referentiality of clues and repetition that rewards close listening yet remains accessible and immediate. Transportive lyrics shine with the lore and mythology of a world that is both deeply specific and transcendent in its curiosity toward the surrounding environment. Unexpected Violence is filled with resounding descriptors: from “cat runs blind in the smoke / birds slap their wings away / trees thrash and crash / each lonely in their chosen way” (the meandering “Angelika”) or the consequently spellbinding phrasing of “come out to your dead animal river gushing hard / come out to your heart split open and lit up with stars” of “In Boredom You Shoot Your Gun”. It’s a starkly poetic snapshot into the band’s own universe and a showcase in the thoroughfare of language, where the specificity of one person’s memory counteracts with a landscape that blurs and unravels with the passage of time. Unexpected Violence a record that could only be made in a place like New Zealand, yet its vantage point expands far beyond to the vast unwieldiness of human sentiment. “There’s a sense of remoteness to the record, both emotionally but also in the sense of place, broken farms, cast iron beaches, blank midday fires, lost friends.” Or as the band recites in the austere glimmer of “Spirally Staircase Memory”: “memories are just stories that can’t be found.” But School Fair reaches some sort of access point, a way for them to live on. The name Unexpected Violence was born out of Buchanan and Ma’ia’i coming across the genre title in a bookstore in Berlin, and is a fitting discernment of the heartbreak that often comes with the realities of existence. In album highlight “Gussied Up,” the band intones: “I never never never ever / wanna hear you / see you, feel you or touch you.” It’s a harsh statement that feels swept up in the parallel admission that these are relationships you may never fully escape; they have left their mark. We still pass the places they inhabit, and feel the uncanny emptiness even after moving on. It’s fitting that the record ends on a similar contradiction. Just discernable above spirals of drummed up, ambient noise: “I miss you now you’re gone.” For all things can be true at once. Bandcamp | IG goldenstar Montreal’s goldenstar operate within a distinctly fraught strain of the North American musical canon, dancing in (and emerging from) the shadow of beloved forebears like Duster, Sonic Youth, and Sparklehorse. Their self-released 2025 debut EP alongside a sophomore release on OST have established the band as an essential voice on the contemporary slowcore-noise rock continuum. Bandcamp | IG Poor Image Poor Image is a 7 piece emo/americana tinged slowcore band based in the Bay Area. The project came to fruition when members Reid Devereaux, Nick Ferguson, Keenan Lewis, Declan Lewis, Patrick Madden, Tammer Bagdasarian and Nick Ross, who spent their formative years between Silicon Valley, San Francisco, and San Jose participating in the broader bay area music scene, decided to join forces. Poor Image’s recent debut self titled album out on American Death Records is about coming of age strife and trying to “make it” in the age of supersaturation. As written by Nina Protocol, Poor Image’s debut album “...refers back to a micro-glory age of low-stakes indie music in a way that could only come from a band a few generations removed from the source material. It finds a perfect balance between slowcore and Americana; it incorporates a variety of roots-leaning instrumental flourishes when it needs to; it rocks when it needs to”. Featured on Perfectly Imperfect as ones to watch, Poor Image has recently come off national tours opening for Horse Vision & Dutch Interior and are currently recording their second album. events.title: Stanley Clarke and Ron Carter
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
Listeners can expect to hear a lot of the “right notes” as two of the true legends of low-end meet for these momentous evenings of duets over four nights. Between them, 2022 NEA Jazz Master Stanley Clarke and 1998 NEA Jazz Master Ron Carter have defined and redefined the bass’s role in modern jazz, from the hard bop innovations of the early 1960s to the jazz-fusion revolution of the 1970s and 1980s.

The four-time GRAMMY winning Clarke achieved worldwide fame as a pioneer of jazz fusion with Chick Corea and Return to Forever, and his subsequent career as a bandleader. The Philadelphia native has recorded 24 albums as a leader, leading a procession of masterful bands, and collaborating with George Duke, McCoy Tyner, Dexter Gordon, Freddie Hubbard, Al Di Meola, Paul McCartney, Keith Richards, Stewart Copeland, and dozens more.

Ron Carter is, quite simply, the face of jazz bass. A towering figure, he was already a creative force on the roiling early ‘60s scene when he joined Miles Davis in 1962, the first piece of what became the trumpeter’s second great quintet.

With more than 2,300 albums to his credit, including over 60 as a leader, "The Maestro” holds the Guinness World Record as jazz’s most recorded bassist.

Clarke and Carter collaborated in a trio with guitarist Russell Malone as part of the recent PBS documentary on Carter’s life, Ron Carter: Finding the Right Notes.

Personnel: Stanley Clarke (electric and acoustic bass); Ron Carter (acoustic bass)

events.title: Henry J. Evans - Bombs, Bacon, and Bankruptcy
events.location: Book Passage Ferry Building 1 Ferry Building San Francisco, CA 94111
events.description: Crisis leadership can be the toughest type of leadership—and the most crucial to master. Whether the stakes are literally life-and-death or just feel that way, this is the essential guide to keeping your team at their best when things are at their worst. Successfully navigating a crisis doesn’t require an innate talent for high-pressure situations. It requires understanding why we act the way we do when business as usual is disrupted—and how to stay calm, think clearly, and execute on the right priorities. Henry J. Evans has spent decades studying, practicing, and coaching other leaders through crises. He’s seen firsthand that whether a crisis is as deadly as roadside bombs during counterterrorism operations, as frustrating as bacon shortages during a pandemic, or as stressful as a family business on the edge of bankruptcy, the strategic, interpersonal, and emotional challenges are the same. Drawing on psychology, brain science, vivid true stories, and proven tools and tactics, Evans shows readers how to: Juggle the demands of today’s crisis without dropping the ball on tomorrow’s priorities. Decide when to trust data and AI and when to trust their gut instincts. Hold people accountable without destroying their sense of Emotional Safety.® Take care of the team’s needs without sacrificing the leader’s well-being. This is an invaluable guide for entrepreneurs, corporate leaders, and anyone trying to guide a team through tough times. It includes practical tools for honing your resilience, reaction times, listening and communication skills, threat assessment, emotional regulation, and more. Henry J. Evans is the founder and CEO of Dynamic Results, a strategy and culture transformation firm. While building a global leadership firm, Evans concurrently spent more than 20 years in counterterrorism and national security under four U.S. presidential administrations, holding a Top Secret security clearance. He has logged more than 16,000 hours of executive coaching and 6,000 hours of strategic planning facilitation with leaders across more than 80 countries. A sought-after keynote speaker and international MBA instructor, Evans is the bestselling author of Winning with Accountability and co-author of Step Up . He lives in San Francisco. Henry J. Evans - photo courtesy of the publicist Event details: This event will be hosted by Book Passage at our Ferry Building store. events.title: Devon Halliday with Daniel Gumbiner - To Stay, To Stay, To Stay
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: “ To Stay, To Stay, To Stay is about the great contradiction of love, that it brings both great bafflement and great clarity, and somehow, ultimately, isn’t a contradiction. So much hard-earned daily wisdom here. I needed this book. You probably do too.”—Peter Orner, author of The Gossip Columnist’s Daughter Devon will be joined in conversation by Daniel Gumbiner, the author of Fire in the Canyon. An ensemble cast collides and crosses paths in their small corner of the Midwest where no one is a stranger: the baker, the realtor, the poet, the gardener, the frustrated artist. In Devon Halliday’s transcendent debut novel, secrets turn contagious, impulses transform into resolutions, and no one is certain whether they will remain in the confines of their Appalachian college town or step out into the unknown. Surrounded by hills, buried in green, Eden is a forgotten town full of ordinary lives. But over the course of a humid summer week, seven of these ordinary lives reach their boiling point, as the existential questions of each begin to urgently entwine. Underneath the threat of marital infidelity, financial ruin, and life-changing illness is always the same question: To stay, or to go? If you choose to stay, is it ever a permanent choice? Can you be sure you’ll choose it again tomorrow? A mosaic portrait of love and its close substitutes, the novel suggests, fearfully, that even our best decisions might be fragile, arbitrary, and impermanent. “This brims with insights into the human condition.”— Publishers Weekly “A heartfelt debut … Halliday offers varied, honest looks at the intimate struggles that accompany life’s unexpected turning points.”— Booklist “Devon Halliday has such a mastery of language and storytelling artistry that it’s hard to believe To Stay, To Stay, To Stay is her debut. This novel, a wry and incisive exploration of how people behave (and misbehave) at the critical inflection points in their lives, is a marvel.”—Marisa Silver, author of At Last “In this enchanting tale of small-town love, artisanal bread, and sketchy real estate, Devon Halliday explores the webs that connect us and the mysterious forces that break those webs apart. Everything and everyone in this wonderful novel is rendered with precision, wit, and uncompromising humanity.”—David Haynes, author of Martha’s Daughter “With rare emotional precision and a fierce, glowing heart, Devon Halliday investigates the stories people tell themselves about love and the combustible, constant anxieties that sustain those stories. This marvelous debut novel wisely asks an urgent, contemporary question: What’s braver? Blowing up your life? Or simply living it, however it unfolds?”—Dean Bakopoulos, author of Summerlong “What a delightful debut novel by Devon Halliday—its pages full of sun and shadow, love and gravity. To Stay, To Stay, To Stay handles its cast of characters with deftness and grace, showing us the many facets of people in a small town as they connect and disconnect from one another.”—Alix Ohlin, author of Dual Citizens “A preternaturally wise and wickedly ambitious debut. Halliday’s small town and big cast of characters cast a spell under which I would happily have stayed, stayed, stayed. Alas, the ending is perfection, too.”—Anna Solomon, author of The Book of V Devon Halliday is a Pushcart Prize winner and a Rona Jaffe Foundation Graduate Fellow. Her writing appears in Ploughshares , One Story , the Los Angeles Review of Books , and Lit Hub , among other journals. Her debut novel To Stay, To Stay, To Stay has been longlisted for the Center for Fiction First Novel Prize. Daniel Gumbiner’s first novel, The Boatbuilder (2018), was a nominee for the National Book Award and a finalist for the California Book Award. His second book, Fire in the Canyon (2023), was a finalist for the California Book Award and a New Yorker Best Book of the Year. He is the Editor of The Believer and lives in San Francisco. As a high schooler, he worked as a barista at the Book Passage Cafe in Corte Madera. events.title: Joyful Raven's TACTICAL FRIVOLITY
events.location: Berkeley
events.description: (Please do not bring infants to the show) Born into a radical theater company, Joyful Raven was tasked from the tender age of 5 with the daunting mission to save the world from impending doom… using theater. Forced into animal-print unitards and political positions long before she was a consenting adult, she never had a fighting chance at anything resembling a normal life. You think your parents were embarrassing? Did you have to sing about salmon sex on stage, in a unitard, at 12 years old… WITH your parents? I didn’t think so. In an attempt to heal her hippie trauma, she runs away from home to seek solace in the arms of a spiritual teacher… and accidentally finds herself in the yoga-to-fascism pipeline. Can she save herself? Can she save the world… using theater?! Blending standup, drag, storytelling, & clown, Raven takes audiences on a dystopian and hilarious romp through the looking glass. ACTOR : Joyful Raven is an award-winning actor, director, and “story midwife” known for her powerful and thought-provoking solo shows, where she tackles thorny social issues with humor, heart, and nuance. Born into an iconic political theater family, she has been devising original work for over 20 years. Her first solo comedy, Tales of a Sexual Tomboy , was dubbed “…one of the funniest shows now on display on Bay Area stages” by the SF Chronicle, won Best of the Fringe at the 2016 San Francisco International Fringe Festival, and enjoyed an Off-Broadway run in 2017. Her latest solo show, Breed or Bust , was nominated for Best Comedy at the 2022 Hollywood Fringe Festival, critically acclaimed at the 2023 Edinburgh Fringe, where it won an Offie (OffWestEnd Award), and went on to have an extended run at The Marsh, where it received a Critics’ Pick in the SF Chronicle. She co-founded the award-winning theater company Rococo Risqué and co-authored four plays for the Prize of Hope-winning company Human Nature. As an actor, she has appeared in numerous stage and film projects, including Odyssey Works, the film The Pursuit of Happyness alongside Will Smith, and Spring Awakening, directed by Stafford Arima. Joyful holds an MFA in Dramatic Art from the University of California, Davis, and teaches solo performance and storytelling at Berkeley Rep School of Theatre, The Marsh, and her own studio in Berkeley. He has collaborated with luminaries like Carlo Mazzone-Clementi and Joe Chaikin and worked with renowned Bay Area performance artists including Jeff Raz and Brenda Wong Aoki. In his early career, he worked with The San Francisco Mime Troupe, directing among other things “The Dragon Lady’s Revenge,” which was awarded an Obie. events.title: KRS-ONE
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Rapper, social activist, and hip-hop pioneer from the Bronx, known as "The Teacha" · Appearing on the rap scene in 1986 as Boogie Down Productions, releasing his first hit single “South Bronx” with his late DJ Scott La Rock, KRS “the one” made it clear that Hip Hop was going to have to take itself a lot more seriously than simply being a music genre. KRS, an acronym for “Knowledge Reigning Supreme”, has been called the “conscience of Hip Hop” (Rolling Stone), “the greatest live emcee ever” (The Source), the “spokesperson for Hip Hop” (Wall Street Journal), “master teacher” (Zulu Nation) and the “son of Hip Hop” (Kool DJ Herc). With 20 published albums to his credit and his numerous appearances with other artists, KRS-One is believed to have written the most rhymes in Hip Hop’s history. In the 1990s, as “hip-hop” grew more and more commercialized and corporate, it was KRS-One that openly rejected such cultural exploitation and materialism, grounding Hip Hop in its original principles of peace, love, unity, and safely having fun. Teaching everything from self-creation to stopping violence; from vegetarianism to transcendental meditation, from the establishment of Hip Hop Appreciation Week (every third week in May), to establishing Hip Hop as an international culture at the United Nations (2001), KRS-One has single-handedly held the history and original arts of Hip Hop together now for over two decades. In addition to lecturing at over 500 universities in the United States and publishing three ground-breaking books; “The Science of Rap” (1995), “Ruminations” (2003), and the Gospel of Hip Hop” (2009), KRS-One has also established the Stop The Violence Movement (1989), influenced the creation of the “West-Coast All-Stars’ anti-gang anthem “We’re All In The Same Gang” (1990), warned the Hip Hop community against giving up their humanity for technological advancement (H. E. A. L.—Human Education Against Lies-1991), and has established the Temple of Hip Hop for the spiritual exploration of Hip Hop’s culture (1996). It was KRS-One who first argued that “rap is something we do; Hip Hop is something we live” and introduced the “I am Hip Hop” philosophy in 1994, which Black Entertainment Television uses as the title of their Hip Hop Lifetime Achievement Award today. Without question, KRS-One has been the loudest voice for the actual preservation and expansion of original Hip Hop worldwide. When he is not touring or lecturing, on his so-called “down-time”, KRS-One continues to share his unique knowledge of Hip Hop to younger audiences eager to hear the ‘teacha’ speak. Operating as a kind of “pop-up” school, KRS-One’s Temple of Hip Hop has appeared in various cities in the USA and also in the UK and Europe, offering the more serious student of Hip Hop an effective way to live and understand the culture of Hip Hop more deeply.

events.title: Janet Thornburg's COGNITIVE DIVINE
events.location: San Francisco
events.description: (Please do not bring infants to the show) You think it’s hard to herd cats? Try getting seven sub-personalities to agree on anything! Wild Child, Rosie, and Mauve love living in San Francisco, but Raisin and Hannah want to go back to Colorado. When Cora soothes Raisin with cinnamon rolls, Hannah complains that sugar is bad for us. Hannah and Wild Child lock horns over Wild Child’s party behavior. Rosie wants to go shopping for clothes and skin-care products, but Mauve wants to spend the money on writers’ conferences and research for her novel. The conflicts never end, and the arguments create quite a din. All seven of Janet’s sub-personalities are delighted to have this opportunity to give their opinions of Janet’s life choices! Janet Thornburg (writer/performer) is a soloist whose solo show Cognitive Divine won the Best Full-Length Comedy award in the In Front of Your Eyes Festival 2026 at the Marsh. She has written and performed eight solo shows in San Francisco at venues including The Marsh, StageWerx Theatre, Theatre Rhinoceros, Theatre of Yugen, Venue Nine, Next Stage Theatre,Young Performers’ Theatre, and the Solo Mio Festival. Her multi-character play Dinner Roles was presented at the San Francisco Repertory Theatre, and her play Antony and Cleopatra Meet Godzilla enjoyed two runs at the Intersection Theatre. She holds an MFA in playwriting from San Francisco State University and an MFA in fiction from Warren Wilson College. Her fiction has been widely published in literary journals, and Rhubarb Pie , a collection of her short stories, was published by Thunderegg Press. For further information about her performances and publications, visit www.janetthornburg.com. Instagram: @jthornburg111 Sound design : Robert Perez Light and sound design : Raye Goh Special thanks to Steve Thornburg and Kuniko Shibata Thornburg for support from start to finish. events.title: John Proctor Is the Villain
events.location: A.C.T., 415 Geary St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description:
In a one-stoplight town in Georgia, in a high school AP English class, five young women begin questioning the stories and the heroes they’ve been taught to believe in, against a soundtrack of pop music and fury. As their class dissects a canonical work of literature, the parallels between the play and their own lives become uncomfortably real, and they begin to re-examine who we deem heroic, who we call a villain, and who gets burned in the process.

In a bold artistic collaboration, three of the nation’s leading regional theaters join forces to bring Kimberly Belflower’s explosive coming-of-age story to the West Coast. Centering young voices, this Broadway sensation and new cult classic ignites the kind of conversation that lingers long after the final bell.

events.title: Holly Bowling
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Joe Henderson Lab
events.description:
ABOUT THIS SHOW
Whether behind the piano on a windswept mountainous cliff, at a hallowed venue such as Carnegie Hall, or playing shoulder-to-shoulder with some of the most legendary musicians in history, solo pianist Holly Bowling subverts convention with virtuosic playing, emotional immersion, and a thirst for invention. Known for her ingenious reimagining of the Grateful Dead songbook, she makes a highly anticipated return to the JHL stage for a three-night run.

After a childhood dedicated to the instrument, she studied piano performance at SF State University. After catching a 2013 Phish show, she transcribed and arranged the entire 37-minute improvisational masterpiece “Tweezer” into a nuanced and intricate piano opus.

She became a phenomenon among Grateful Dead fans as well as Rolling Stone, Billboard, and Relix for ingeniously reimagining the Dead’s most beloved staples on her 2016 album Better Left Unsung and 2020 follow-up Seeking All That’s Still Unsung — the latter of which bowed in the Top 25 of the Billboard Top Classical Albums Chart.

Bowling went on to share the stage with everyone from The Dead’s Weir and Lesh to Haynes, John Scofield, Jim James, Branford Marsalis, Don Was, Robert Randolph, Greensky Bluegrass, and more.

Her newest release is Lacuna, a duo album with guitarist Tom Hamilton.

Personnel: Holly Bowling (piano)

events.title: Stanley Clarke and Ron Carter
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
Listeners can expect to hear a lot of the “right notes” as two of the true legends of low-end meet for these momentous evenings of duets over four nights. Between them, 2022 NEA Jazz Master Stanley Clarke and 1998 NEA Jazz Master Ron Carter have defined and redefined the bass’s role in modern jazz, from the hard bop innovations of the early 1960s to the jazz-fusion revolution of the 1970s and 1980s.

The four-time GRAMMY winning Clarke achieved worldwide fame as a pioneer of jazz fusion with Chick Corea and Return to Forever, and his subsequent career as a bandleader. The Philadelphia native has recorded 24 albums as a leader, leading a procession of masterful bands, and collaborating with George Duke, McCoy Tyner, Dexter Gordon, Freddie Hubbard, Al Di Meola, Paul McCartney, Keith Richards, Stewart Copeland, and dozens more.

Ron Carter is, quite simply, the face of jazz bass. A towering figure, he was already a creative force on the roiling early ‘60s scene when he joined Miles Davis in 1962, the first piece of what became the trumpeter’s second great quintet.

With more than 2,300 albums to his credit, including over 60 as a leader, "The Maestro” holds the Guinness World Record as jazz’s most recorded bassist.

Clarke and Carter collaborated in a trio with guitarist Russell Malone as part of the recent PBS documentary on Carter’s life, Ron Carter: Finding the Right Notes.

Personnel: Stanley Clarke (electric and acoustic bass); Ron Carter (acoustic bass)

events.title: The Wisdom of the Odyssey with Phil Cousineau
events.location: Book Passage, Corte Madera Store 51 Tamal Vista Blvd Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: “As you set out for Ithaka, / hope your road is a long one, /full of adventure, full of discovery.” —Constantine Cavafy, “Ithaka” Spurred by the summer release of Christopher Nolan’s blockbuster film version of The Odyssey , Homer has never been “hotter,” and The Odyssey has never been more relevant. How can a 3,000-year-old story still matter so much to people around the globe, and at the same time be culturally combustible? Where is the wisdom in this endlessly protean tale? Join us to explore the soulful thread of themes in Phil Cousineau's new book, The Wisdom of the Odyssey . The class will explore: the meaning of home the role of mentors and muses in our lives the loss of soul at war, the need to heal from trauma the redemptive power of love The daylong class and journey into ancient Greece will include film clips, mythic images, vibrant discussions, and a Greek-inspired lunch included in the cost of the class. Recommended reading: The Wisdom of the Odyssey by Phil Cousineau Richard Lattimore’s glorious translation of Homer’s epic , or the translation of your choice Recommended viewing: Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey Meet Your Instructor Phil Cousineau is a freelance writer, filmmaker, independent scholar, and writing consultant, who has led mythological tours to Greece for over thirty years. He has published over forty books, including the international best-seller The Hero’s Journey: Joseph Campbell on His Life and Work, The Art of Pilgrimage, Once and Future Myths, The Blue Museum, The Lost Notebooks of Sisyphus, Who Stole the Arms of the Venus de Milo? and most recently The Wisdom of the Odyssey. Cousineau also has over forty film and television credits, and has been a commentator on “Myth in the Movies” for myriad movie studios, including Warner Brothers, Pixar, Lucas Films, Twentieth-Century Fox, and the Smithsonian and Discovery Channels. What students are saying about Phil: "Loved it! Phil is fun, informative and entertaining. He clearly loved his topic and that is infectious. And the food was excellent!" Lesley H. "(I enjoyed) Phil's depth and breadth of knowledge, compassion and patience. (His) interest and HIGH and DEEP scholarship level kept (my) attention and curiosity...FABULOUS job with the food!" Grace R. "We loved Phil, his personality, his delivery, his vast knowledge, and his immense excitement about the topic...There was a vibrant discussion. Phil's use of classical paintings of the Odyssey was lovely. Phil's points were resonant, profound, sometimes funny - always entertaining. " Ben L. "Phil Cousineau is a unique mind with vast experience and enthusiasms. (The class was) above and beyond with food, scale and quality of presentation and engagement." John C.

events.title: Devendra Banhart - Four Nose Jobs a Day
events.location: Book Passage Ferry Building 1 Ferry Building San Francisco, CA 94111
events.description: Join us at the Ferry Building for a meet-and-greet celebration of Venezuelan-American singer-songwriter and visual artist Devendra Banhart. Like his music and visual art, Banhart’s poetry converges at the intersection of humor and sorrow. In his second collection, Four Nose Jobs A Day , he explores the heart and soul through a lens that is both slyly absurdist and deeply compassionate. "Banhart approaches somber themes with whimsy... his work expounds on a crucial tenet of queerness: liberation in lightness and in unabashed optimism. Funny and enduringly weird. " — PITCHFORK Like Devendra Banhart’s music and visual art, his poetry appears at the convergence of humor and sorrow, tragedy and joy. With Four Nose Jobs A Day , Banhart’s second collection, the poet explores matters of the heart and soul through an absurdist lens both sly and compassionate. As the opening lines of the collection alert us, Banhart loves “a Love Poem/One that reads/Like Blackberries/On a wooden cup”. With iconoclastic verve, Banhart builds small, often silly paths of poetic language that lead to meaningful conclusions: “Poetry is when/the dead end/Starts to go somewhere” Like professional musicians constantly on tour, Banhart reminds us that we, the readers, have countless places to visit both in the world around us, and inside ourselves—whether these places resonate and register is up to us, not the places. The poems of Four Nose Jobs A Day break the surface of reality, small bubbles of insight. Sometimes there is laughter in the face of absurdity; consolation for grief or despair; and sometimes there is simply gratitude. “What an Honor,” the poet reminds us, “To have emotions/Any of them.” **** Devendra Banhart is a Venezuelan-American singer-songwriter and visual artist. His drawings have been exhibited, among others, at the San Francisco Museum of Modern Art, the Centre for Fine Arts in Brussels, and Los Angeles’ Museum of Contemporary Art. He has released over ten albums and has performed at venues such as Carnegie Hall, Bonnaroo, and Coachella. This is one of many books he has published. He lives in Los Angeles. events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: Please join us for a reading by LeeAnn Pickrell from her new book, Tsunami . This event is organized by the Left Coast Writers and hosted by Book Passage. This story explores the tsunami through a lens of separation, reunion, and the psychic shifts of such an experience. It is a moving account of coming home, letting go of outdated faith, and discovering the connections forged through the stories we tell. On the morning of December 26, 2004, an undersea earthquake struck off the coast of Sumatra in the Indian Ocean. The resulting tsunami killed an estimated 230,000 people across fourteen countries, from Indonesia to Sri Lanka to Thailand to the Maldives to India and all the way to East Africa. Everyone who was there and survived has a story of where they were when the tsunami hit. But there are too many stories that will never be told. This is one woman's story of her experience of that day and its aftermath.LeeAnn Pickrell was in Rai Leh, Thailand, just off the beach drinking coffee that morning when the ocean went away. Everyone ran to the top of the beach to see a wall of white approaching the shore, at first slowly and then picking up speed as boats overturned and they realized the wave wasn't going to stop. It's the story of the tsunami in a particular place, of not understanding what was happening, of separation and reunion. It's also a story of coming home, of not being hurt physically but the psychic shifts of such an experience. It's about letting go of old ideas of faith that no longer make sense and opening to the connections we have to each other through the stories we tell. LeeAnn Pickrell is the author of Tsunami (Unsolicited Press, 2026). Her debut collection, Gathering the Pieces of Days , was published in 2025 by Unsolicited Press. She is also the author of the chapbook Punctuated , published by Bottlecap Press in 2024. She lives in the East Bay with her partner and two fabulous cats. events.description:
In a one-stoplight town in Georgia, in a high school AP English class, five young women begin questioning the stories and the heroes they’ve been taught to believe in, against a soundtrack of pop music and fury. As their class dissects a canonical work of literature, the parallels between the play and their own lives become uncomfortably real, and they begin to re-examine who we deem heroic, who we call a villain, and who gets burned in the process.

events.title: Seth Fleisher with Anna Norberg- The Farther Shore
events.location: Book Passage Ferry Building 1 Ferry Building San Francisco, CA 94111
events.description: The Father Shore is a sweeping novel about fathers and sons, memory and race, and the dangerous fictions that shape us--inspired by the true story of Eugene Marais, one of history's most extraordinary and forgotten minds. Southern Africa, 1890s. Eugene Marais is a brilliant naturalist and iconoclastic journalist whose evolving theories about memory, addiction, and the hive mind are decades ahead of their time. But when tragedy strikes, he abandons his newborn son and disappears into a remote South African forest--leaving behind his child and his conscience, and embarking on research that will haunt both their lives. Thirty years later, his son Charles--now a professor of ancient Buddhist history at Harvard--discovers that his father's work has been weaponized. University faculty are mining Eugene's research to bolster theories of racial hierarchy, and their ambitions are growing darker by the day. Accompanied by a mysterious Jewish graduate student whose fate is becoming entangled with his own, Charles will make an epic journey across continents to heal his fractured past and stop a sinister plot quietly taking root at the world's most prestigious institution. Set across two interlocking timelines--from the British concentration camps of the Boer War to the rising shadow of the Third Reich and WWII-- The Farther Shore is a heart-breaking, exhilarating novel about memory, love, and identity, and about the vast distances we'll travel to find our way home. "An astonishing reimagining of the life of Eugene Marais, The Farther Shore is as intellectually daring as it is lushly immersive. Seth Fleisher renders history with a decadent richness—each page steeped in atmosphere, obsession, and unease—while excavating the dangerous fictions of race and the seductive machinery of rising fascism. What emerges is not just a portrait of a man, but a mirror held up to our own moment: a world still grappling with identity as both inheritance and invention." —Jamie Ford, NYT bestselling author of Hotel on the Corner of Bitter and Sweet "In a rich and visceral style akin to Abraham Verghese’s Cutting for Stone , this novel asks profound questions about memory and instinct in a cross-continental tale of father and son that is deeply moving and unforgettable. Set mostly in South Africa in the early decades of the 1900s—with that new nation recently ravaged by British concentration camps and twisting toward the ugliest of human beliefs— The Farther Shore tells of Eugene Marais, a real-life doctor and lawyer whose passion was furthering Darwin’s work, and his son, Charles, whom Eugene abandoned after his beloved wife died in childbirth. Charles teaches ancient Buddhist texts at Harvard in the 1930s, when the university is embracing Nazi fascism and researching a mode of social control based on the misuse of Eugene’s studies. On discovering this, Charles must abandon his hard-won independence and journey back to South Africa to meet a father intent on escaping from pain, while he himself finally opens to love." —Janet Benton, author of Lilli De Jong “In this achingly relevant debut novel, Seth Fleisher achieves great magic, embodying continents and centuries. Recalling aspects of The English Patient and A Gentleman in Moscow , this rich exploration introduces a cast of fascinating, complex mortals whose voices are accurate not just to history but to the longings of their flawed hearts.” —EDIE MEIDAV, author of Dogs of Cuba and Crawl Space Seth Fleisher is an American author whose work has appeared in the Bellevue Literary Review , Pearl , the Journal of Anthropological Research , and elsewhere. Based in Berkeley, California, he has worked with the World Bank Group and other NGOs in South Africa, India, and more than 40 other countries, and co-founded a U.S.-based democracy initiative to counter the rising tide of authoritarianism. A former Fulbright scholar in Sri Lanka, Seth did Ph.D. work at Harvard in Buddhist social history, a fellowship at Harvard's Center for the Study of World Religions, and a B.A. in literature at Swarthmore, where he and his wife first met in a Chaucer seminar. The Farther Shore is his first novel. Anna Nordberg is an author and journalist whose essays have appeared in Slate magazine, The Washington Post , The New York Times , and the San Francisco Chronicle . Her debut novel, When She Was Ours, came out this summer. Anna grew up in New York City and now lives in San Francisco with her family. events.title: Alejandra Siroka - Language Alchemy
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: Language Alchemy: Cultivating Peace and Authenticity in Our Relationships - Workshop & Book Signing Free event · Book signing and refreshments provided What is easy for you to express, and what is hard? In this workshop celebrating the launch of Language Alchemy: The Essential Communication Tool Kit for a Life of Peace, Authenticity, and Meaning , transformative communication expert Alejandra Siroka invites to explore how what you find easy or hard to communicate shapes your relationships, your family, and the world we all live in. The language we speak is something we learned, which means we can learn to communicate differently — moving what now feels impossible to say into the realm of the possible. This is not another workshop that offers contrived communication formulas. Language Alchemy® helps you discover your authentic expression for the benefit of all, so that the way you speak and relate becomes a model for the present and the future. In this workshop you will: • Discover how what you find easy or hard to communicate shapes your life and relationships • Hear an excerpt from the book on maturing our language to match our own growth and development • Leave with a new way of understanding communication as a practice of building meaningful relationships About the book We inherited a language of survival, fear, and competition. For centuries we have been taught to win arguments, defend positions, and prove our worth. That language once helped us survive — now it leads us to divisiveness, superficiality, and a global epidemic of loneliness. Language Alchemy offers a groundbreaking, embodied system for turning the Language of Survival™ into a Language of Interconnectedness™, integrating linguistics, Nonviolent Communication, neuroscience, the behavioral insights of Neuro Linguistic Programming, and ancient Eastern wisdom. Through vivid personal stories, reflective exercises, and eight Language Alchemy Principles, it guides readers to unlearn divisive communication, reconnect to body, emotions, and values as guides for authentic expression, and use language as a vehicle for personal healing and collective evolution. This is the book our conversations — and our world — have been waiting for. Refreshments will be provided. Books will be available for purchase and signing.

events.title: Joyful Raven's TACTICAL FRIVOLITY
events.location: Berkeley
events.description: (Please do not bring infants to the show) Born into a radical theater company, Joyful Raven was tasked from the tender age of 5 with the daunting mission to save the world from impending doom… using theater. Forced into animal-print unitards and political positions long before she was a consenting adult, she never had a fighting chance at anything resembling a normal life. You think your parents were embarrassing? Did you have to sing about salmon sex on stage, in a unitard, at 12 years old… WITH your parents? I didn’t think so. In an attempt to heal her hippie trauma, she runs away from home to seek solace in the arms of a spiritual teacher… and accidentally finds herself in the yoga-to-fascism pipeline. Can she save herself? Can she save the world… using theater?! Blending standup, drag, storytelling, & clown, Raven takes audiences on a dystopian and hilarious romp through the looking glass. ACTOR : Joyful Raven is an award-winning actor, director, and “story midwife” known for her powerful and thought-provoking solo shows, where she tackles thorny social issues with humor, heart, and nuance. Born into an iconic political theater family, she has been devising original work for over 20 years. Her first solo comedy, Tales of a Sexual Tomboy , was dubbed “…one of the funniest shows now on display on Bay Area stages” by the SF Chronicle, won Best of the Fringe at the 2016 San Francisco International Fringe Festival, and enjoyed an Off-Broadway run in 2017. Her latest solo show, Breed or Bust , was nominated for Best Comedy at the 2022 Hollywood Fringe Festival, critically acclaimed at the 2023 Edinburgh Fringe, where it won an Offie (OffWestEnd Award), and went on to have an extended run at The Marsh, where it received a Critics’ Pick in the SF Chronicle. She co-founded the award-winning theater company Rococo Risqué and co-authored four plays for the Prize of Hope-winning company Human Nature. As an actor, she has appeared in numerous stage and film projects, including Odyssey Works, the film The Pursuit of Happyness alongside Will Smith, and Spring Awakening, directed by Stafford Arima. Joyful holds an MFA in Dramatic Art from the University of California, Davis, and teaches solo performance and storytelling at Berkeley Rep School of Theatre, The Marsh, and her own studio in Berkeley. Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/joyfulraven/ Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/joyful.raven DIRECTOR : Jael Weisman , a founding member of the Dell’Arte Players Co. and a multi-Obie-winning director, is a trailblazer in actor-based theater, directing acclaimed productions like “Whiteman Meets Bigfoot,” “Performance Anxiety,” and “Mad Love.” With Dell’Arte, his works have toured extensively in South America and Europe, earning him numerous Dramalogue Awards for Directing. Noteworthy projects include “The Dragon Lady’s Revenge,” which traveled to New York and was awarded an Obie, the American premiere of “Red Noses” at the San Diego Repertory Co., “Uncle Gunjiro’s Girlfriend” at the Adelaide Festival, and “Mermaid Meat” for the Berkeley Symphony Orchestra. He has collaborated with luminaries like Carlo Mazzone-Clementi and Joe Chaikin and worked with renowned Bay Area performance artists including Jeff Raz and Brenda Wong Aoki. In his early career, he worked with The San Francisco Mime Troupe, directing among other things “The Dragon Lady’s Revenge,” which was awarded an Obie. Weisman holds a BA from Reed College and an MFA from Carnegie Tech Lighting Design : Kiara Valderrama Show Photos : Cynthia Smalley It is with great love and a deep bow of gratitude that I roast by inimitable parents, Jane Lapiner and David Simpson and their theater company Human Nature. events.description: THIS IS MEET & GREET TICKETS ONLY (For Show Tickets CLICK HERE) Since their dynamic arrival in 2007, DAY26 has stood as one of the premier male vocal groups of the 21st century, carrying the torch of R&B with timeless harmonies, heartfelt lyrics, and an undeniable stage presence. Discovered and brought together on MTV’s hit reality series Making the Band 4 under the guidance of Sean “Diddy” Combs, the five-member ensemble Brian, Willie, Robert, Mike, and Qwanell captured the attention of millions with their unmatched vocal blend and authentic brotherhood. ​ Their self-titled debut album DAY26 (2008) made history by debuting at No. 1 on the Billboard 200, powered by singles like “Got Me Going” and “Since You’ve Been Gone.” Their second album, Forever in a Day (2009), followed closely behind, debuting at No. 2 on the Billboard 200 with first-week sales of around 113,000 copies. These early successes confirmed DAY26’s ability to resonate deeply with R&B audiences and cross over into mainstream appeal. ​ Over the years, DAY26 has become known not just for chart achievements, but for their electrifying live performances and their ability to balance lush ballads with dance-driven anthems. Songs like “Made Love Lately” (from their 2012 project A New Day) have showcased their versatility, blending vulnerability with mature artistry. ​ In 2024, DAY26 reaffirmed their legacy with the release of Day Ones, an album that celebrates their journey while speaking directly to the fans who have supported them from the beginning. The project is both a love letter to R&B and a statement of the group’s evolution, featuring the soulful harmonies, emotional storytelling, and dynamic energy that first made them household names, now seasoned with years of artistry and growth. Day Ones embodies their mission to honor the roots of classic R&B while inspiring a new generation of listeners. Through their music, DAY26 has always represented unity, resilience, and the power of authentic artistry. With a catalog of memorable hits, a loyal fanbase known as the Day Ones, and a renewed creative spirit, the group continues to prove why they are one of R&B’s most enduring and beloved acts. Their story is far from over, and with Day Ones, DAY26 reminds the world that real harmony never fades.

events.title: In a Silent Way: Joel Harrison Quintet plays Miles Davis
events.location: Bird & Beckett Books & Records, 653 Chenery Street, San Francisco
events.description: Paul Hanson, reeds; Joel Harrison, guitar; Michael Manring, bass; Scott Amendola, drums Former Berkeley resident, guitarist Joel Harrison, returns to the Bay Area to journey into Miles Davis’ iconic 1970 record, “In a Silent Way.” The band consists of old allies, some of the Bay Area’s finest and most creative musicians—they will also perform some of Harrison’s original music. Harrison recently released a live record from the Big Ears Festival of this music. The band’s approach will be to “make it new.” Guitarist, composer, arranger, lyricist, writer, educator and vocalist Joel Harrison has “created a new blueprint for jazz” (New Orleans Times-Picayune). He has released 27 records, a body of work that connects multiple American traditions. While rooted in jazz, his music moves fluidly through classical, rock, country, and American roots music. The New York Times has described his work as “protean… brilliant.” Harrison is the founder and director of the Alternative Guitar Summit, an annual festival devoted to innovative and unconventional guitar music. The Summit has featured artists such as Fred Frith, Nels Cline, Bill Frisell, Julian Lage, Michael Gregory Jackson, Mary Halvorson and Pat Metheny, who has called it “one of the most interesting and distinguished forums for guitar on the planet.” Harrison is the author of Guitar Talk: Conversations with Visionary Players , Pity the Genius and Modern Jazz Standards for Guitar. https://joelharrison.com/ https://www.paulhansonmusic. com/ https://manthing.com/ https://scottamendola.com/ $25 cover charge; byob Students $10 For a reservation, call the bookshop at 415-586-3733

events.description:
In a one-stoplight town in Georgia, in a high school AP English class, five young women begin questioning the stories and the heroes they’ve been taught to believe in, against a soundtrack of pop music and fury. As their class dissects a canonical work of literature, the parallels between the play and their own lives become uncomfortably real, and they begin to re-examine who we deem heroic, who we call a villain, and who gets burned in the process.

In a bold artistic collaboration, three of the nation’s leading regional theaters join forces to bring Kimberly Belflower’s explosive coming-of-age story to the West Coast. Centering young voices, this Broadway sensation and new cult classic ignites the kind of conversation that lingers long after the final bell.

events.title: Lynne Kaufman's THE SECRET MUSEUM
events.location: San Francisco
events.description: Opening Reception Sunday, November 8 (Please do not bring infants to the show) Francesca, a contemporary American filmmaker, is shooting a documentary on a newly excavated fresco in Pompeii said to provide startling evidence about sex and the sacred. She has obtained exclusive rights to film the fresco through the good graces of Paolo, the museum’s director and her former college sweetheart. Through three time periods and the lives of three couples, THE SECRET MUSEUM explores the mysteries of eros. Lynne Kaufman ( Playwright ) is the author of 20 full-length plays that have been produced in San Francisco, Los Angeles, Washington D.C., and Louisville at such theatres as Magic Theatre, Actors Theatre of Louisville, TheatreWorks Silicon Valley, and many more –with Shameless Hussy being her most recent work which premiered at The Marsh San Francisco spring 2025. Four of Kaufman’s plays, Extreme Acts, Acid Test, Two Minds , Who Killed Sylvia Plath , and Poetic Justice, have premiered on stage at The Marsh, while two others, Exposing Margaret Mead and The Smartest Woman in America, have appeared on The Marsh’s digital platform MarshStream. Who Killed Sylvia Plath went on to win Best Play in The Marsh’s 2020 MarshStream International Solo Festival. Kaufman’s plays have won many awards including the Glickman Award for Best New Play ( The Couch ), the Kennedy Center’s Fund for New American Plays Award ( Speaking in Tongues ), and the Neil Simon Festival New Play Award ( William Blake in Hollywood ). Kaufman has published four novels, and her short stories have appeared in Cosmopolitan , Redbook , and McCall’s . She was also the recipient of the Otis Guernsey Outstanding New Voice in American Theatre Award from the William Inge Theatre Festival. Warren David Keith ( Director ) is delighted to be reunited with Playwright Lynne Kaufman. His work with her began in 2012 with the Marsh Berkeley premier of Acid Test: The Many Incarnations of Ram Dass , a solo piece in which he played the title role. The play was extended twice in Berkeley then transferred for one performance to a massive tent on Maui, Hawaii where it was seen and enjoyed by Ram Dass and about 300 devoted followers. Subsequently, Acid Test opened at the Marsh San Francisco in 2013 where it also had several runs. Keith has acted in theaters throughout the Bay Area, most recently in 1984 at the Aurora Theatre Company and as the Porter in the California Shakespeare Theater’s production of Macbeth . His film credits include Nomadland , The Last Black Man in San Francisco , Haiku Tunnel , Love and Taxes , Raising Arizona , Fargo , A Serious Man , and The Big Lebowski . As a director he mounted more than 15 productions for American Conservatory Theater’s Young Conservatory Program. He reunited with Ms. Kaufman to direct Who Killed Sylvia Plath and The Smartest Woman in America about the final days of Susan Sontag, both at the Marsh San Francisco. Arwen Anderson ( Performer ) returns to The Marsh, where she previously collaborated with Lynne Kaufman on a staged reading of her musical Map of Your Mind and performed in Kaufman’s Extreme Acts . Selected regional credits include Testmatch, Men On Boats, Heisenberg , Let There Be Love , A Christmas Carol , and Tales of the City (workshop) at American Conservatory Theater; King Lear , Romeo and Juliet , and The Verona Project at California Shakespeare Theater; August: Osage County , Anne Boleyn , Circle Mirror Transformation , Bellwether , and A Streetcar Named Desire at Marin Theatre ; An Accident , Mrs. Whitney , Expedition 6 , The Rules of Charity , and Mauritius at Magic Theatre; A White Girl’s Guide to International Terrorism, The Fit, and 77% at San Francisco Playhouse; Miss Julie at Stanford Repertory Theater; Lobby Hero and The Shape of Things at Aurora Theatre Company; You Know When the Men Are Gone and 4 Adverbs with Word for Word; and roles with American Stage Festival, San Jose Repertory Theatre, Marin Shakespeare Company, Brava Theater, Encore Theatre Company, and Central Works Theater Company. Her film work includes Hog Island , Ashley 22 , and Dark Retreat . Johnny Moreno ( Performer ) returns to The Marsh, where he previously performed in Lynne Kaufman’s Extreme Acts . He has also appeared at theaters throughout the Bay Area including American Conservatory Theater, Berkeley Repertory Theatre, San Francisco Playhouse, San Jose Stage Company, Marin Shakespeare Company, Center Repertory Company, Marin Theatre , Crowded Fire Theater, and Pacific Repertory Theatre. He has played award winning roles, such as Macheath in San Francisco Playhouse’s production of The Threepenny Opera (Theatre Bay Area Award for Best Actor in a Musical) , and Henry Higgins in San Francisco Playhouse’s production of My Fair Lady (San Francisco Bay Area Theatre Critics Circle Award for Best Actor in a Musical). He has appeared in numerous film and television productions, such as “Betas,” Callback (winner of the Chicago Indie Fest for Best Film), Upside Out (with Olympia Dukakis), Paradise Club, and I’m Still Here (with Joaquin Phoenix). Lyndsy Kail ( Performer ) Marsh Debut. Regional credits include The White Chip at Marin Theatre. California Shakespeare Theater, Center Repertory Theatre, B Street Theatre, Capital Stage, San Francisco Shakespeare Festival, San Jose Stage. FILM/TELEVISION: Trauma, All About Evil, The Optimist . Other: voice and performance capture for Star Wars: Tales from the Galaxy’s Edge, Star Tours, Fortnite, Monster High , many 2K games including BioShock Infinite, NBA2K, and the latest Mafia game. Training: BA in Classics at UC Berkeley and The Groundlings in LA. Joseph O’Malley ( Performer, AEA ) makes his Marsh debut, having performed at the Kennedy Center, La Jolla Playhouse, Berkeley Rep, Marin Theatre, Cal Shakes, Aurora Theatre, Marin Shakespeare and Center Rep. He is thrilled to reunite with director Warren David Keith for The Secret Museum . Up next: The Gift of Nothing and The Crucible at Marin Theatre, as well as Ang Lee’s film Gold Mountain . events.title: Holly Bowling
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Joe Henderson Lab
events.description:
ABOUT THIS SHOW
Whether behind the piano on a windswept mountainous cliff, at a hallowed venue such as Carnegie Hall, or playing shoulder-to-shoulder with some of the most legendary musicians in history, solo pianist Holly Bowling subverts convention with virtuosic playing, emotional immersion, and a thirst for invention. Known for her ingenious reimagining of the Grateful Dead songbook, she makes a highly anticipated return to the JHL stage for a three-night run.

After a childhood dedicated to the instrument, she studied piano performance at SF State University. After catching a 2013 Phish show, she transcribed and arranged the entire 37-minute improvisational masterpiece “Tweezer” into a nuanced and intricate piano opus.

She became a phenomenon among Grateful Dead fans as well as Rolling Stone, Billboard, and Relix for ingeniously reimagining the Dead’s most beloved staples on her 2016 album Better Left Unsung and 2020 follow-up Seeking All That’s Still Unsung — the latter of which bowed in the Top 25 of the Billboard Top Classical Albums Chart.

Bowling went on to share the stage with everyone from The Dead’s Weir and Lesh to Haynes, John Scofield, Jim James, Branford Marsalis, Don Was, Robert Randolph, Greensky Bluegrass, and more.

Her newest release is Lacuna, a duo album with guitarist Tom Hamilton.

Personnel: Holly Bowling (piano)

events.description: MEET & GREET TICKETS AVAILABLE (NOT INCLUDING SHOW TICKETS - CLICK HERE) EXCLUSIVE WORLD PREMIERE OF THE NEW DAY26 DOCUMENTARY AT EACH SHOW! Since their dynamic arrival in 2007, DAY26 has stood as one of the premier male vocal groups of the 21st century, carrying the torch of R&B with timeless harmonies, heartfelt lyrics, and an undeniable stage presence. Discovered and brought together on MTV’s hit reality series Making the Band 4 under the guidance of Sean “Diddy” Combs, the five-member ensemble Brian, Willie, Robert, Mike, and Qwanell captured the attention of millions with their unmatched vocal blend and authentic brotherhood. ​ Their self-titled debut album DAY26 (2008) made history by debuting at No. 1 on the Billboard 200, powered by singles like “Got Me Going” and “Since You’ve Been Gone.” Their second album, Forever in a Day (2009), followed closely behind, debuting at No. 2 on the Billboard 200 with first-week sales of around 113,000 copies. These early successes confirmed DAY26’s ability to resonate deeply with R&B audiences and cross over into mainstream appeal. ​ Over the years, DAY26 has become known not just for chart achievements, but for their electrifying live performances and their ability to balance lush ballads with dance-driven anthems. Songs like “Made Love Lately” (from their 2012 project A New Day) have showcased their versatility, blending vulnerability with mature artistry. ​ In 2024, DAY26 reaffirmed their legacy with the release of Day Ones, an album that celebrates their journey while speaking directly to the fans who have supported them from the beginning. The project is both a love letter to R&B and a statement of the group’s evolution, featuring the soulful harmonies, emotional storytelling, and dynamic energy that first made them household names, now seasoned with years of artistry and growth. Day Ones embodies their mission to honor the roots of classic R&B while inspiring a new generation of listeners. Through their music, DAY26 has always represented unity, resilience, and the power of authentic artistry. With a catalog of memorable hits, a loyal fanbase known as the Day Ones, and a renewed creative spirit, the group continues to prove why they are one of R&B’s most enduring and beloved acts. Their story is far from over, and with Day Ones, DAY26 reminds the world that real harmony never fades.

events.title: Stanley Clarke and Ron Carter
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
Listeners can expect to hear a lot of the “right notes” as two of the true legends of low-end meet for these momentous evenings of duets over four nights. Between them, 2022 NEA Jazz Master Stanley Clarke and 1998 NEA Jazz Master Ron Carter have defined and redefined the bass’s role in modern jazz, from the hard bop innovations of the early 1960s to the jazz-fusion revolution of the 1970s and 1980s.

The four-time GRAMMY winning Clarke achieved worldwide fame as a pioneer of jazz fusion with Chick Corea and Return to Forever, and his subsequent career as a bandleader. The Philadelphia native has recorded 24 albums as a leader, leading a procession of masterful bands, and collaborating with George Duke, McCoy Tyner, Dexter Gordon, Freddie Hubbard, Al Di Meola, Paul McCartney, Keith Richards, Stewart Copeland, and dozens more.

Ron Carter is, quite simply, the face of jazz bass. A towering figure, he was already a creative force on the roiling early ‘60s scene when he joined Miles Davis in 1962, the first piece of what became the trumpeter’s second great quintet.

With more than 2,300 albums to his credit, including over 60 as a leader, "The Maestro” holds the Guinness World Record as jazz’s most recorded bassist.

Clarke and Carter collaborated in a trio with guitarist Russell Malone as part of the recent PBS documentary on Carter’s life, Ron Carter: Finding the Right Notes.

Personnel: Stanley Clarke (electric and acoustic bass); Ron Carter (acoustic bass)

events.title: The Commons Public Hours ☕
