events.title: Brittany Davis
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Joe Henderson Lab
events.description:
A powerhouse performer blessed with a voice made of pure soul, Seattle-based singer, composer, and keyboardist Brittany Davis brings their deeply felt songs blending jazz, R&B, and hard-grooving funk.

Raised in Kansas City, Davis developed into a commanding vocalist, pianist, producer, and songwriter whose work is rooted in vulnerability, social consciousness, and deep musical intuition.

Her breakthrough debut album, Image Issues, earned widespread acclaim from NPR, KEXP, SPIN, and Good Morning America, establishing her as an artist capable of transforming personal struggle into cathartic, transcendent art.

Davis has collaborated closely with Stone Gossard through the project Painted Shield and released music on his Loosegroove Records label, while also working with acclaimed Seattle musicians including Evan Flory-Barnes and D'Vonne Lewis. Her music draws comparisons to Nina Simone, Roberta Flack, and Rahsaan Roland Kirk for its emotional intensity and spiritual depth.

Her latest album, Black Thunder, is a bold, largely improvised work of spiritual jazz recorded live over two days. Featuring hypnotic grooves, explosive improvisation, and deeply personal storytelling, the album showcases Davis at her most raw and visionary, confirming her status as a transformative force in modern music.

Personnel: Brittany Davis (keyboards, vocals); Others TBA

events.title: Django Festival Allstars
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
Pioneering Romani jazz guitarist Django Reinhardt lamented that he might be neglected by history, but today the ebulliently swinging “jazz manouche” sound he created with French violinist Stéphane Grappelli is more pervasive than ever. For this very special night, the leading purveyors of the style, the Django Festival Allstars, return to the Miner stage for a magical evening of hot jazz.

Featuring the guitar mastery of Samson Schmitt of the Schmitt clan, the first family of jazz manouche, the Django Festival All-Stars also includes accordionist and keyboardist Ludovic Beier, violinist Pierre Blanchard, and rhythm guitarist Francko Mehrstein — all of whom gained fame as part of the original band led by family patriarch Dorado Schmitt — joined by bassist Antonio Licusati. This assemblage of masters in the Roma jazz style are regular performers at the annual Django Reinhart Festival in Samois-sur-Seine, France and New York’s celebration at Birdland, which celebrates over a quarter century of music.

The group performs in support of their new Motéma Music release, Evolution, a hard-swinging collection of original compositions written and arranged by the members of the band. DownBeat magazine hailed the release as “(jazz manouche) for the 21st Century!”

Personnel: Samson Schmitt (guitar); Francko Mehrstein (guitar); Pierre Blanchard (violin); Ludovic Beier (accordion, keyboards); Antonio Licusati (bass)

events.title: GERALD ALBRIGHT
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Grammy-nominated saxophonist and multi-instrumentalist · Born and raised in Los Angeles, Albright was already an accomplished saxophonist by the time he enrolled at the University of Redlands, but he switched to bass after he saw Louis Johnson in concert. A few months after graduating from college, he joined jazz pianist/R&B singer Patrice Rushen, who was in the process of forming her own band. Later, when the bassist left in the middle of a tour, Albright replaced him and finished the tour on bass guitar. Playing both sax and bass, he became the consummate session and touring musician in the 80s, working with everyone from Anita Baker, Ray Parker, Jr., Atlantic Starr, The Temptations, and Maurice White to Les McCann, Teena Marie, the Winans, and Whitney Houston. He launched his solo career in the infancy of what became the smooth jazz format, with Just Between Us in 1987, and has been a core part of the genre with chart-topping albums, countless radio hits, and as a member of many all-star tours, including Guitars & Saxes and Groovin’ For Grover. In the late 90s, he fronted a big band and toured with pop star Phil Collins and did a dual recording with vocal great Will Downing called Pleasures of the Night . Between his last two Grammy-nominated solo albums, Pushing The Envelope (2010) and Slam Dunk (2014), he enjoyed hit collaborations with two huge hits – 24/7 with guitarist Norman Brown and Summer Horns by Dave Koz and Friends (including Mindi Abair and Richard Elliot), which were also Grammy-nominated for Best Pop Instrumental Albums. He toured with Brown and Summer Horns, and most recently has been on the road with South African gospel/jazz singer and guitarist Jonathan Butler. Albright’s other albums, whose titles perfectly reflect their flow, include Smooth (1994), Groovology (2002), Kickin’ It Up (2004), and Sax for Stax (2008). Because Albright’s musical muse has taken him to so many fascinating locales along the contemporary R&B/urban jazz spectrum, he’s joyfully defied easy categorizations. “Top to bottom,” Albright says, “Whether in concert, listening to my music over the radio or CD player, I always want my listeners to be taken on a musical journey with different textures, rhythms, chord progressions, and moods. I want people to know where I’ve been and where I’m going, and to let them hear that I’m in a really good place in my life.”

events.location: Ferry Building Foodwise Classroom San Francisco, CA 94111
events.description: Meet & Greet Book Signing Only • SF Ferry Plaza Market 11:00 AM PT Food Demo // 11:30 AM PT Book Signing Please join us for a special meet-and-greet signing event with Ann M. Evans & Georgeanne Brennan, following their Foodwise demo at the Ferry Plaza Farmers Market. Ann M. Evans & Georgeanne Brennan's beautiful new work, Market Memories Cookbook , celebrates 50 years of the Davis Farmers Market with 92 all-new seasonal recipes illustrated by the authors. Guest essays about the market’s origins, the battle for farmers market certification and the sense of optimism and change of the 1970s add yet another dimension to this celebratory book. Throughout the pages, heartfelt anecdotes from the farmers, vendors and shoppers illuminate the poignant role the market continues to play in our daily lives. The Davis Farmers Market was voted USA Today’s 10 Best Farmers Market (2015) and America’s Favorite Farmers Market (2009). For more information on awards and the market, go to www.davisfarmersmarket.org . “When the Davis Farmers Market opened, it was extraordinary, and it is astonishing that it is still here fifty years later. It stands as a testament to the simple, radical idea of connecting people directly with local organic farmers and ranchers. I am so impressed.” ALICE WATERS, Chez Panisse Restaurant and Edible Schoolyard Project, Berkeley For more than fifty years, Ann M. Evans , former mayor and Citizen of the Year of Davis, California, has helped to bring healthful eating to an ever-growing audience through both her work with government and non-profit organizations and her writing. Among her many accomplishments is the co-founding of three regional food-system mainstays: Davis Farm to School, one of the first farm-to-school programs in the country; the 51-year-old Davis Food Co-op; and the award-winning Davis Farmers Market. She was also at the table for the creation of the Certified Farmers Market regulations, representing the Department of Consumer Affairs. Ann is the author of several cookbooks and texts to improve school lunch, as well as a botanical artist drawing inspiration from her garden, the creeks and wildlands of Yolo County, and the market. Her food influences stem from a lifetime of international travel, childhood summers in Chapel Hill and Durham, North Carolina, summers in Provence, France, her northern England family heritage, and a lifetime amidst the agricultural landscape of Northern California. She lives in Davis with her husband, surrounded by a small edible garden where she keeps bees and chickens. At age eight, Georgeanne Brennan wrote her first cookbook. The recipes were written on lined foolscap paper stapled together with a bright yellow cover, titled My Recipes. Since then, she's written more than thirty cookbooks, won a Julia Child award for one and a James Beard award for another. She has lived in Provence, where she raised goats and made and sold cheese, taught high school in Arctic Alaska, and cooking classes across the nation. For six years, she hosted her own Culinary Vacation program, bringing people to share a week for shopping, cooking, and foraging in the interior Provence, where she has had a home for more than forty years. In the early 1980s, Georgeanne co-founded Le Marche' Seeds and was instrumental in importing European heirloom seeds and selling them to farmers across the United States, earning her place in the pantheon of the California Food Revolution. She lives in Winters with her husband, where she gardens, cooks, writes, and paints between welcoming her extended family, including eight grandchildren and their dogs. Ann M. Evans & Georgeanne Brennan - photos courtesy of the publicist Event details: This event is a non-seated Meet & Greet signing only. This event will be hosted by Foodwise with Book Passage at the Ferry Plaza Farmers Market (Foodwise Classroom tent) at the SF Ferry Building. events.title: Joyful Raven's TACTICAL FRIVOLITY
events.location: Berkeley
events.description: (Please do not bring infants to the show) Born into a radical theater company, Joyful Raven was tasked from the tender age of 5 with the daunting mission to save the world from impending doom… using theater. Forced into animal-print unitards and political positions long before she was a consenting adult, she never had a fighting chance at anything resembling a normal life. You think your parents were embarrassing? Did you have to sing about salmon sex on stage, in a unitard, at 12 years old… WITH your parents? I didn’t think so. In an attempt to heal her hippie trauma, she runs away from home to seek solace in the arms of a spiritual teacher… and accidentally finds herself in the yoga-to-fascism pipeline. Can she save herself? Can she save the world… using theater?! Blending standup, drag, storytelling, & clown, Raven takes audiences on a dystopian and hilarious romp through the looking glass. ACTOR : Joyful Raven is an award-winning actor, director, and “story midwife” known for her powerful and thought-provoking solo shows, where she tackles thorny social issues with humor, heart, and nuance. Born into an iconic political theater family, she has been devising original work for over 20 years. Her first solo comedy, Tales of a Sexual Tomboy , was dubbed “…one of the funniest shows now on display on Bay Area stages” by the SF Chronicle, won Best of the Fringe at the 2016 San Francisco International Fringe Festival, and enjoyed an Off-Broadway run in 2017. Her latest solo show, Breed or Bust , was nominated for Best Comedy at the 2022 Hollywood Fringe Festival, critically acclaimed at the 2023 Edinburgh Fringe, where it won an Offie (OffWestEnd Award), and went on to have an extended run at The Marsh, where it received a Critics’ Pick in the SF Chronicle. She co-founded the award-winning theater company Rococo Risqué and co-authored four plays for the Prize of Hope-winning company Human Nature. As an actor, she has appeared in numerous stage and film projects, including Odyssey Works, the film The Pursuit of Happyness alongside Will Smith, and Spring Awakening, directed by Stafford Arima. Joyful holds an MFA in Dramatic Art from the University of California, Davis, and teaches solo performance and storytelling at Berkeley Rep School of Theatre, The Marsh, and her own studio in Berkeley. Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/joyfulraven/ Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/joyful.raven DIRECTOR : Jael Weisman , a founding member of the Dell’Arte Players Co. and a multi-Obie-winning director, is a trailblazer in actor-based theater, directing acclaimed productions like “Whiteman Meets Bigfoot,” “Performance Anxiety,” and “Mad Love.” With Dell’Arte, his works have toured extensively in South America and Europe, earning him numerous Dramalogue Awards for Directing. Noteworthy projects include “The Dragon Lady’s Revenge,” which traveled to New York and was awarded an Obie, the American premiere of “Red Noses” at the San Diego Repertory Co., “Uncle Gunjiro’s Girlfriend” at the Adelaide Festival, and “Mermaid Meat” for the Berkeley Symphony Orchestra. He has collaborated with luminaries like Carlo Mazzone-Clementi and Joe Chaikin and worked with renowned Bay Area performance artists including Jeff Raz and Brenda Wong Aoki. In his early career, he worked with The San Francisco Mime Troupe, directing among other things “The Dragon Lady’s Revenge,” which was awarded an Obie. Weisman holds a BA from Reed College and an MFA from Carnegie Tech Lighting Design : Kiara Valderrama Show Photos : Cynthia Smalley It is with great love and a deep bow of gratitude that I roast by inimitable parents, Jane Lapiner and David Simpson and their theater company Human Nature. events.title: GERALD ALBRIGHT
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Grammy-nominated saxophonist and multi-instrumentalist · Born and raised in Los Angeles, Albright was already an accomplished saxophonist by the time he enrolled at the University of Redlands, but he switched to bass after he saw Louis Johnson in concert. A few months after graduating from college, he joined jazz pianist/R&B singer Patrice Rushen, who was in the process of forming her own band. Later, when the bassist left in the middle of a tour, Albright replaced him and finished the tour on bass guitar. Playing both sax and bass, he became the consummate session and touring musician in the 80s, working with everyone from Anita Baker, Ray Parker, Jr., Atlantic Starr, The Temptations, and Maurice White to Les McCann, Teena Marie, the Winans, and Whitney Houston. He launched his solo career in the infancy of what became the smooth jazz format, with Just Between Us in 1987, and has been a core part of the genre with chart-topping albums, countless radio hits, and as a member of many all-star tours, including Guitars & Saxes and Groovin’ For Grover. In the late 90s, he fronted a big band and toured with pop star Phil Collins and did a dual recording with vocal great Will Downing called Pleasures of the Night . Between his last two Grammy-nominated solo albums, Pushing The Envelope (2010) and Slam Dunk (2014), he enjoyed hit collaborations with two huge hits – 24/7 with guitarist Norman Brown and Summer Horns by Dave Koz and Friends (including Mindi Abair and Richard Elliot), which were also Grammy-nominated for Best Pop Instrumental Albums. He toured with Brown and Summer Horns, and most recently has been on the road with South African gospel/jazz singer and guitarist Jonathan Butler. Albright’s other albums, whose titles perfectly reflect their flow, include Smooth (1994), Groovology (2002), Kickin’ It Up (2004), and Sax for Stax (2008). Because Albright’s musical muse has taken him to so many fascinating locales along the contemporary R&B/urban jazz spectrum, he’s joyfully defied easy categorizations. “Top to bottom,” Albright says, “Whether in concert, listening to my music over the radio or CD player, I always want my listeners to be taken on a musical journey with different textures, rhythms, chord progressions, and moods. I want people to know where I’ve been and where I’m going, and to let them hear that I’m in a really good place in my life.”

Set to two of the most iconic works in the classical music canon, Copland’s Suite from Appalachian Spring and Debussy’s Prélude à l’après-midi d’un faune ( Afternoon of a Faun ) , the program offers the unparalleled experience of live symphonic music performed on stage alongside LINES’ extraordinary dancers, for an immersive dialogue between movement and sound. Join LINES Ballet and the SF Symphony as we celebrate movement and sound breathing together in real time. To learn more, visit our Fall Season webpage . events.title: Lynne Kaufman's THE SECRET MUSEUM
events.location: San Francisco
events.description: Opening Reception Sunday, November 8 (Please do not bring infants to the show) Francesca, a contemporary American filmmaker, is shooting a documentary on a newly excavated fresco in Pompeii said to provide startling evidence about sex and the sacred. She has obtained exclusive rights to film the fresco through the good graces of Paolo, the museum’s director and her former college sweetheart. Through three time periods and the lives of three couples, THE SECRET MUSEUM explores the mysteries of eros. Lynne Kaufman ( Playwright ) is the author of 20 full-length plays that have been produced in San Francisco, Los Angeles, Washington D.C., and Louisville at such theatres as Magic Theatre, Actors Theatre of Louisville, TheatreWorks Silicon Valley, and many more –with Shameless Hussy being her most recent work which premiered at The Marsh San Francisco spring 2025. Four of Kaufman’s plays, Extreme Acts, Acid Test, Two Minds , Who Killed Sylvia Plath , and Poetic Justice, have premiered on stage at The Marsh, while two others, Exposing Margaret Mead and The Smartest Woman in America, have appeared on The Marsh’s digital platform MarshStream. Who Killed Sylvia Plath went on to win Best Play in The Marsh’s 2020 MarshStream International Solo Festival. Kaufman’s plays have won many awards including the Glickman Award for Best New Play ( The Couch ), the Kennedy Center’s Fund for New American Plays Award ( Speaking in Tongues ), and the Neil Simon Festival New Play Award ( William Blake in Hollywood ). Kaufman has published four novels, and her short stories have appeared in Cosmopolitan , Redbook , and McCall’s . She was also the recipient of the Otis Guernsey Outstanding New Voice in American Theatre Award from the William Inge Theatre Festival. Warren David Keith ( Director ) is delighted to be reunited with Playwright Lynne Kaufman. His work with her began in 2012 with the Marsh Berkeley premier of Acid Test: The Many Incarnations of Ram Dass , a solo piece in which he played the title role. The play was extended twice in Berkeley then transferred for one performance to a massive tent on Maui, Hawaii where it was seen and enjoyed by Ram Dass and about 300 devoted followers. Subsequently, Acid Test opened at the Marsh San Francisco in 2013 where it also had several runs. Keith has acted in theaters throughout the Bay Area, most recently in 1984 at the Aurora Theatre Company and as the Porter in the California Shakespeare Theater’s production of Macbeth . His film credits include Nomadland , The Last Black Man in San Francisco , Haiku Tunnel , Love and Taxes , Raising Arizona , Fargo , A Serious Man , and The Big Lebowski . As a director he mounted more than 15 productions for American Conservatory Theater’s Young Conservatory Program. He reunited with Ms. Kaufman to direct Who Killed Sylvia Plath and The Smartest Woman in America about the final days of Susan Sontag, both at the Marsh San Francisco. Arwen Anderson ( Performer ) returns to The Marsh, where she previously collaborated with Lynne Kaufman on a staged reading of her musical Map of Your Mind and performed in Kaufman’s Extreme Acts . Selected regional credits include Testmatch, Men On Boats, Heisenberg , Let There Be Love , A Christmas Carol , and Tales of the City (workshop) at American Conservatory Theater; King Lear , Romeo and Juliet , and The Verona Project at California Shakespeare Theater; August: Osage County , Anne Boleyn , Circle Mirror Transformation , Bellwether , and A Streetcar Named Desire at Marin Theatre ; An Accident , Mrs. Whitney , Expedition 6 , The Rules of Charity , and Mauritius at Magic Theatre; A White Girl’s Guide to International Terrorism, The Fit, and 77% at San Francisco Playhouse; Miss Julie at Stanford Repertory Theater; Lobby Hero and The Shape of Things at Aurora Theatre Company; You Know When the Men Are Gone and 4 Adverbs with Word for Word; and roles with American Stage Festival, San Jose Repertory Theatre, Marin Shakespeare Company, Brava Theater, Encore Theatre Company, and Central Works Theater Company. Her film work includes Hog Island , Ashley 22 , and Dark Retreat . Johnny Moreno ( Performer ) returns to The Marsh, where he previously performed in Lynne Kaufman’s Extreme Acts . He has also appeared at theaters throughout the Bay Area including American Conservatory Theater, Berkeley Repertory Theatre, San Francisco Playhouse, San Jose Stage Company, Marin Shakespeare Company, Center Repertory Company, Marin Theatre , Crowded Fire Theater, and Pacific Repertory Theatre. He has played award winning roles, such as Macheath in San Francisco Playhouse’s production of The Threepenny Opera (Theatre Bay Area Award for Best Actor in a Musical) , and Henry Higgins in San Francisco Playhouse’s production of My Fair Lady (San Francisco Bay Area Theatre Critics Circle Award for Best Actor in a Musical). He has appeared in numerous film and television productions, such as “Betas,” Callback (winner of the Chicago Indie Fest for Best Film), Upside Out (with Olympia Dukakis), Paradise Club, and I’m Still Here (with Joaquin Phoenix). Lyndsy Kail ( Performer ) Marsh Debut. Regional credits include The White Chip at Marin Theatre. California Shakespeare Theater, Center Repertory Theatre, B Street Theatre, Capital Stage, San Francisco Shakespeare Festival, San Jose Stage. FILM/TELEVISION: Trauma, All About Evil, The Optimist . Other: voice and performance capture for Star Wars: Tales from the Galaxy’s Edge, Star Tours, Fortnite, Monster High , many 2K games including BioShock Infinite, NBA2K, and the latest Mafia game. Training: BA in Classics at UC Berkeley and The Groundlings in LA. Joseph O’Malley ( Performer, AEA ) makes his Marsh debut, having performed at the Kennedy Center, La Jolla Playhouse, Berkeley Rep, Marin Theatre, Cal Shakes, Aurora Theatre, Marin Shakespeare and Center Rep. He is thrilled to reunite with director Warren David Keith for The Secret Museum . Up next: The Gift of Nothing and The Crucible at Marin Theatre, as well as Ang Lee’s film Gold Mountain . events.title: John Proctor Is the Villain
events.location: A.C.T., 415 Geary St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description:
In a one-stoplight town in Georgia, in a high school AP English class, five young women begin questioning the stories and the heroes they’ve been taught to believe in, against a soundtrack of pop music and fury. As their class dissects a canonical work of literature, the parallels between the play and their own lives become uncomfortably real, and they begin to re-examine who we deem heroic, who we call a villain, and who gets burned in the process.

In a bold artistic collaboration, three of the nation’s leading regional theaters join forces to bring Kimberly Belflower’s explosive coming-of-age story to the West Coast. Centering young voices, this Broadway sensation and new cult classic ignites the kind of conversation that lingers long after the final bell.

events.title: Sarah Hanahan Quartet
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Joe Henderson Lab
events.description:
A short list of the most exciting young alto saxophonists to emerge in the last five years would have to include Sarah Hanahan. Her incendiary performances were already turning heads via far-flung touring with the Mingus Big Band, drummer Ulysses Owens Jr. and Generation Y, Sherrie Miracle and the Diva Orchestra, and drummer Joe Farnsworth. But the release of her 2024 debut album Among Giants catapulted her into a whole new realm, earning a rare five-star review from DownBeat. She brings the magic of that album to the Joe Henderson Lab with her powerful quintet.

More than holding her own with veteran masters Marc Cary (piano), Nat Reeves (bass) and Jeff “Tain” Watts (drums), Hanahan completed the journey from apprentice to leader, playing with the intensity, self-possession and audacious creativity of a major-league talent. She’d studied with Reeves at the Jackie McLean Institute of Jazz at the Hartt School of Music as an undergrad and with Cary at Juilliard, where she earned a Master’s in 2022. That same year Hanahan was tapped for the first-ever class of NPR Jazz Night in America’s Youngbloods and featured as one of five “up-and-coming jazz geniuses who are revolutionizing their genre” in their 20s. She’s been ascending steadily ever since.

Personnel: Sarah Hanahan (alto saxophone); Others TBA

events.title: Mireya Ramos & Flor de Toloache
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
This night features a solo set by the Latin GRAMMY-winning vocalist, composer, and producer Mireya Ramos featuring music from her self-titled debut album, and a performance by the revolutionary mariachi band she founded, Flor de Toloache.

An artist possessed of a musical wanderlust, Ramos embodies all her musical influences whether classical, mariachi, salsa, merengue or hip-hop, always creating a unique and refreshing sound. Her versatility, natural improvisational skills, and beautiful tone has made her one of the top Latin artists in New York City. She is currently promoting her debut solo album, the self-titled Mireya, which includes collaborations with Flor de Toloache, Gaby Moreno, Haydée Milanés, Camilo Lara, Adrian Quesada, Velcro, and the legendary Mike Garson.

The Latin GRAMMY Award–winning, all-female Flor De Toloache mixes tradition and innovation, breaking boundaries with its edgy, versatile, and fresh take on traditional Latin American music. Like the legendary love potion that the Toloache flower is used for in Mexico, the talented New York ensemble casts a spell over its audiences with soaring vocals and physical elegance. With a total of five studio albums to date, “Las Flores,” as their fans call them, recently released Motherflower, described by the artists as a fiercely feminist mosaic of genres inspired by mariachi.

Personnel: Mireya Ramos (vocals, violin, guitarrón); Shae Fiol (vocals, vihuela); Others TBA

events.title: The Commons Public Hours ☕
events.location: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco + Full Space
events.description:
🎉 Public Hours at the Commons 🎉
Every Sunday, the Commons opens to the public — no membership required. Come co-work, connect, create, or just explore the space at your own pace. ✨
🕘 When: Every Sunday, 9 AM – 10 PM
📍 Where: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco (corner of Hayes & Laguna, basement level)
RSVP and we'll email you your entry code ahead of time — so you can let yourself straight in when you arrive.
──────────────────────────────
🧭 A self-guided day
Public Hours are self-guided — come in, settle in, and make the space your own. Weekends are usually unstaffed, so there's no check-in desk or guided tour. Our members are glad to answer questions about the space; for anything else — including guided tours, which we don't offer as drop-ins — email hello@thesfcommons.com ahead of time.
──────────────────────────────
🔭 Getting in
Your entry code comes by email. Once you RSVP, we'll send you a personal QR code — that's your key for the day. Keep it handy on your phone (and check spam if you don't see it).
Find us. We're at 540 Laguna St, on the corner of Hayes & Laguna. Head down the stairs beside Earthbody to the basement level — that's the Commons.
Scan your QR code at the reader to unlock the door. Hold your phone just below the Kisi reader by the door and it'll let you in.
Your access stays active all day, 9 AM – 10 PM, so you can come and go freely.
Can't find your code on the day? No problem — scan the QR posted on the door to check in and get a fresh one on the spot.
We're shoes-off 🧦 — please clean up after yourself, including dirty dishes and mugs, and use only the front entrance. Trouble getting in? Email hello@thesfcommons.com.




The Commons is a modern-day town square for communal meaning-making, personal discovery, and self-expression in the heart of San Francisco. Apply to become a member here__.

events.title: CHESTER “CT” THOMPSON ORGAN QUARTET
events.location: Bach Dancing & Dynamite Society (Douglas Beach House), 311 Mirada Rd, Half Moon Bay, CA 94019
events.description:
Hearing the Chester “CT” Thompson Organ Quartet is an experience like no other. After 26 years with Carlos Santana and a decade with Tower of Power, CT brings a signature blend of deep‑pocket groove, soulful expression, and explosive energy to the stage. His unmistakable sound—anchored by his legendary left‑hand/left‑foot bass—moves effortlessly from smooth and lyrical to thunderous and driving. Saxophonist Howard Wiley adds a powerful tenor voice and relentless rhythmic feel, while guitarist Barry Finnerty—known for work with the Brecker Brothers, the Crusaders, Miles Davis, etc.—brings decades of jazz, blues, and rock mastery. Drummer Dante Roberson completes the quartet with the versatility and precision that have made him an in‑demand Bay Area musician. CT’s career spans iconic contributions to Tower of Power, Grammy‑winning collaborations with Santana, and performances with artists such as Wayne Shorter. Today, he returns to his jazz roots, leading a quartet united by a shared passion for improvisation and groove. Saxophonist Howard Wiley adds a powerful tenor voice and relentless rhythmic feel, while guitarist Barry Finnerty—known for work with the Brecker Brothers, the Crusaders, Miles Davis, etc.—brings decades of jazz, blues, and rock mastery. Drummer Dante Roberson completes the quartet with the versatility and precision that have made him an in‑demand Bay Area musician.

CT’s career spans iconic contributions to Tower of Power, Grammy‑winning collaborations with Santana, and performances with artists such as Wayne Shorter. Today, he returns to his jazz roots, leading a quartet united by a shared passion for improvisation and groove.

Chester "CT" Thompson – B3 Organ; Howard Wiley – Sax; Barry Finnerty – Guitar; Dante Roberson – Drums

events.title: Lynne Kaufman's THE SECRET MUSEUM
events.location: San Francisco
events.description: Opening Reception Sunday, November 8 (Please do not bring infants to the show) Francesca, a contemporary American filmmaker, is shooting a documentary on a newly excavated fresco in Pompeii said to provide startling evidence about sex and the sacred. She has obtained exclusive rights to film the fresco through the good graces of Paolo, the museum’s director and her former college sweetheart. Through three time periods and the lives of three couples, THE SECRET MUSEUM explores the mysteries of eros. Lynne Kaufman ( Playwright ) is the author of 20 full-length plays that have been produced in San Francisco, Los Angeles, Washington D.C., and Louisville at such theatres as Magic Theatre, Actors Theatre of Louisville, TheatreWorks Silicon Valley, and many more –with Shameless Hussy being her most recent work which premiered at The Marsh San Francisco spring 2025. Four of Kaufman’s plays, Extreme Acts, Acid Test, Two Minds , Who Killed Sylvia Plath , and Poetic Justice, have premiered on stage at The Marsh, while two others, Exposing Margaret Mead and The Smartest Woman in America, have appeared on The Marsh’s digital platform MarshStream. Who Killed Sylvia Plath went on to win Best Play in The Marsh’s 2020 MarshStream International Solo Festival. Kaufman’s plays have won many awards including the Glickman Award for Best New Play ( The Couch ), the Kennedy Center’s Fund for New American Plays Award ( Speaking in Tongues ), and the Neil Simon Festival New Play Award ( William Blake in Hollywood ). Kaufman has published four novels, and her short stories have appeared in Cosmopolitan , Redbook , and McCall’s . She was also the recipient of the Otis Guernsey Outstanding New Voice in American Theatre Award from the William Inge Theatre Festival. Warren David Keith ( Director ) is delighted to be reunited with Playwright Lynne Kaufman. His work with her began in 2012 with the Marsh Berkeley premier of Acid Test: The Many Incarnations of Ram Dass , a solo piece in which he played the title role. The play was extended twice in Berkeley then transferred for one performance to a massive tent on Maui, Hawaii where it was seen and enjoyed by Ram Dass and about 300 devoted followers. Subsequently, Acid Test opened at the Marsh San Francisco in 2013 where it also had several runs. Keith has acted in theaters throughout the Bay Area, most recently in 1984 at the Aurora Theatre Company and as the Porter in the California Shakespeare Theater’s production of Macbeth . His film credits include Nomadland , The Last Black Man in San Francisco , Haiku Tunnel , Love and Taxes , Raising Arizona , Fargo , A Serious Man , and The Big Lebowski . As a director he mounted more than 15 productions for American Conservatory Theater’s Young Conservatory Program. He reunited with Ms. Kaufman to direct Who Killed Sylvia Plath and The Smartest Woman in America about the final days of Susan Sontag, both at the Marsh San Francisco. Arwen Anderson ( Performer ) returns to The Marsh, where she previously collaborated with Lynne Kaufman on a staged reading of her musical Map of Your Mind and performed in Kaufman’s Extreme Acts . Selected regional credits include Testmatch, Men On Boats, Heisenberg , Let There Be Love , A Christmas Carol , and Tales of the City (workshop) at American Conservatory Theater; King Lear , Romeo and Juliet , and The Verona Project at California Shakespeare Theater; August: Osage County , Anne Boleyn , Circle Mirror Transformation , Bellwether , and A Streetcar Named Desire at Marin Theatre ; An Accident , Mrs. Whitney , Expedition 6 , The Rules of Charity , and Mauritius at Magic Theatre; A White Girl’s Guide to International Terrorism, The Fit, and 77% at San Francisco Playhouse; Miss Julie at Stanford Repertory Theater; Lobby Hero and The Shape of Things at Aurora Theatre Company; You Know When the Men Are Gone and 4 Adverbs with Word for Word; and roles with American Stage Festival, San Jose Repertory Theatre, Marin Shakespeare Company, Brava Theater, Encore Theatre Company, and Central Works Theater Company. Her film work includes Hog Island , Ashley 22 , and Dark Retreat . Johnny Moreno ( Performer ) returns to The Marsh, where he previously performed in Lynne Kaufman’s Extreme Acts . He has also appeared at theaters throughout the Bay Area including American Conservatory Theater, Berkeley Repertory Theatre, San Francisco Playhouse, San Jose Stage Company, Marin Shakespeare Company, Center Repertory Company, Marin Theatre , Crowded Fire Theater, and Pacific Repertory Theatre. He has played award winning roles, such as Macheath in San Francisco Playhouse’s production of The Threepenny Opera (Theatre Bay Area Award for Best Actor in a Musical) , and Henry Higgins in San Francisco Playhouse’s production of My Fair Lady (San Francisco Bay Area Theatre Critics Circle Award for Best Actor in a Musical). He has appeared in numerous film and television productions, such as “Betas,” Callback (winner of the Chicago Indie Fest for Best Film), Upside Out (with Olympia Dukakis), Paradise Club, and I’m Still Here (with Joaquin Phoenix). Lyndsy Kail ( Performer ) Marsh Debut. Regional credits include The White Chip at Marin Theatre. California Shakespeare Theater, Center Repertory Theatre, B Street Theatre, Capital Stage, San Francisco Shakespeare Festival, San Jose Stage. FILM/TELEVISION: Trauma, All About Evil, The Optimist . Other: voice and performance capture for Star Wars: Tales from the Galaxy’s Edge, Star Tours, Fortnite, Monster High , many 2K games including BioShock Infinite, NBA2K, and the latest Mafia game. Training: BA in Classics at UC Berkeley and The Groundlings in LA. Joseph O’Malley ( Performer, AEA ) makes his Marsh debut, having performed at the Kennedy Center, La Jolla Playhouse, Berkeley Rep, Marin Theatre, Cal Shakes, Aurora Theatre, Marin Shakespeare and Center Rep. He is thrilled to reunite with director Warren David Keith for The Secret Museum . Up next: The Gift of Nothing and The Crucible at Marin Theatre, as well as Ang Lee’s film Gold Mountain . events.title: Sarah Hanahan Quartet
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Joe Henderson Lab
events.description:
A short list of the most exciting young alto saxophonists to emerge in the last five years would have to include Sarah Hanahan. Her incendiary performances were already turning heads via far-flung touring with the Mingus Big Band, drummer Ulysses Owens Jr. and Generation Y, Sherrie Miracle and the Diva Orchestra, and drummer Joe Farnsworth. But the release of her 2024 debut album Among Giants catapulted her into a whole new realm, earning a rare five-star review from DownBeat. She brings the magic of that album to the Joe Henderson Lab with her powerful quintet.

More than holding her own with veteran masters Marc Cary (piano), Nat Reeves (bass) and Jeff “Tain” Watts (drums), Hanahan completed the journey from apprentice to leader, playing with the intensity, self-possession and audacious creativity of a major-league talent. She’d studied with Reeves at the Jackie McLean Institute of Jazz at the Hartt School of Music as an undergrad and with Cary at Juilliard, where she earned a Master’s in 2022. That same year Hanahan was tapped for the first-ever class of NPR Jazz Night in America’s Youngbloods and featured as one of five “up-and-coming jazz geniuses who are revolutionizing their genre” in their 20s. She’s been ascending steadily ever since.

Personnel: Sarah Hanahan (alto saxophone); Others TBA

events.title: Brian Blade & The Fellowship Band
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
GRAMMY-winning drummer and composer Brian Blade brings back The Fellowship Band to perform music from across their seven studio releases.
Easily one of the most versatile and soulful musicians in jazz, Blade grew up as the son of a Baptist pastor in Shreveport, Louisiana and was immersed in gospel music from his birth. He formed the Fellowship in 1997 with pianist and fellow Loyola student Jon Cowherd, releasing a series of increasingly accomplished sessions culminating in his 2023 session on his own Stoner Hill imprint, Kings Highway. Featuring Blade, Cowherd, saxophonists Melvin Butler and Myron Walden, and bassist Christopher Thomas, The Fellowship is recognized for a “sound that echoes grace and unity” (The New York Times).

As Blade was developing his own musical identity as a bandleader, he became an increasingly in-demand sideman and band member, cultivating long-term associations with Joshua Redman, Joni Mitchell, Kenny Garrett, Daniel Lanois, Bill Frisell, and Chick Corea, with whom he earned a GRAMMY. In 2000, Blade began his most visible and fruitful partnership as a member of jazz legend Wayne Shorter’s all-star quartet, touring the world and recording four albums with the saxophonist, including the GRAMMY-winning 2013 release, Without a Net.

The Fellowship band returns to SFJAZZ for their first performance since 2018.

Personnel: Brian Blade (drums); Melvin Butler (soprano & tenor saxophones); Myron Walden (alto saxophone, bass clarinet); Jon Cowherd (piano); Christopher Thomas (bass)

events.title: Builders Night
events.location: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco + 540 Cafe
events.description:
Builders Night is a weekly space where people show up with a project, work side by side, and leave with more momentum than they could have generated alone. It exists because building can be lonely, and the hardest part is often simply showing up consistently.
The tone is focused and warm. Mostly quiet during deep work, with moments of spontaneous connection when someone gets unstuck or discovers something worth sharing. This is not a networking event or a lecture. The work itself is the center of the night.
Flow
6:30–6:45 PM: Arrival and settling in
6:45–6:55 PM: Opening circle: name, what you're working on, one intention for the night
6:55–8:30 PM: Deep work sprint: quiet, side-by-side building
8:30–9:00 PM: Share-back: what you built, learned, or got stuck on. Make an ask, offer what you know, and support each other.
Who This Is For
People working on software, hardware, businesses, creative projects, writing, design, research, art, anything you're trying to make real. Come if you want accountability, momentum, and the energy of working alongside others. First-timers and regulars both welcome.
What to Bring
Laptop, notebook, sketchbook, instrument, whatever tools your project requires. Come with something to work on, or come ready to figure out what that is.
Norms
Respect the deep work sprint by keeping conversation low during focused time. Share-back is how we learn from each other: share what you built, ask for what you need, and offer what you can. Everyone participates.
Rally (rallysf.com) is an AI builder community in SF.

events.title: John Proctor Is the Villain
events.location: A.C.T., 415 Geary St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description:
In a one-stoplight town in Georgia, in a high school AP English class, five young women begin questioning the stories and the heroes they’ve been taught to believe in, against a soundtrack of pop music and fury. As their class dissects a canonical work of literature, the parallels between the play and their own lives become uncomfortably real, and they begin to re-examine who we deem heroic, who we call a villain, and who gets burned in the process.

In a bold artistic collaboration, three of the nation’s leading regional theaters join forces to bring Kimberly Belflower’s explosive coming-of-age story to the West Coast. Centering young voices, this Broadway sensation and new cult classic ignites the kind of conversation that lingers long after the final bell.

events.description: The Cornley Polytechnic Drama Society is back, and this time they’re taking on Peter Pan . It’s their most ambitious production yet, complete with flying rigs, sword fights, and a very real crocodile problem. What could possibly go wrong? As technical mishaps pile up and tempers flare, the cast battles to keep the show on track while everything around them spectacularly falls apart. Lines are forgotten, scenery refuses to cooperate, and rivalries spill onto the stage in real time. From the creators of The Play That Goes Wrong , this riotous comedy delivers nonstop mayhem, perfectly timed chaos, and the kind of theatrical disaster you have to see to believe.

events.title: KIMBERLY BEA with THE CURSE OF THE FEATHERS
events.location: Books Inc. Mountain View, 317 Castro St, Mountain View, CA 94041
events.description: Join local author and friend of the store Kimberly Bea at Books Inc. Mountain View for a celebration of her new book The Curse of Feathers! About the book: For fans of Katherine Arden and Kell Woods, an enchanting, feminist fantasy retelling of the Brothers Grimm tale “The Wild Swans”: a young woman’s handiwork and determination is tested to the limits to save her six brothers, cursed to become swans. “Know this; no word of yours shall ever break my spell.” As the only daughter in her noble family, Elisa von Ahlefeldt has always been the untamed outlier. Unlike her six brothers who follow the protocols and duty of the court, she is ellevilde —elf-wild—a child of nature. She spends her days in the woods where she has befriended Nuve, an ash-tree maid who teaches her the ways of forest magic. Elisa finds she has a gift for magic that matches the needlecraft talent she learned from her mother—whose tragic death has torn the family apart. Following the funeral, Elisa’s father reveals he has been spellbound by a Hexe into marriage and sends his young children into hiding. Years pass before stepmother Belinde locates them, transforms the boys into swans, and alters her husband’s perception of his daughter, casting her out of their lives. To break her brothers’ curse, Elisa is guided by Nuve to use her needlecraft to create magical garments from stinging nettles for each of them under a vow of silence. A silence she must keep while impersonating a missing noblewoman. A secret she must hold dear even as she is betrothed to a handsome stranger. A power she must wield to defy the evil Belinde and rescue her family before their bird nature steals their human lives away forever. For Elisa, despite the perils of the Hexen and her own fears, knows deep in her heart that: “Silence has its power, and not all that is wild can be tamed.” A coming-of-age fantasy adventure, Curse of Feathers , is a tale of inner strength at the crossroads of faith and mysticism, rich with historical details in this retelling of the classic Brothers Grimm fairy tale. Kimberly Bea is the author of mythology and fable-inspired fiction, including The Changeling Queen and The Curse of Feathers. A member of the Society for the Promotion of Speculative Fiction, her shorter work has been published in the anthologies Den of Thieves and Spring: Dreams and Nightmares and poetry in the anthology Nothing But Red . She is a social historian and lifelong feminist with undergraduate and graduate degrees in Ancient History with comparative fields in medieval history and the ancient Near East. A native of California, she lived in Minneapolis for 25 years before moving back to her home state. Visit her online at KimberlyBea.com .

events.title: IRISH CHRISTMAS IN AMERICA
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: A fascinating performance of music, song, dance, and stories of seasonal Irish traditions · The hugely popular Holiday show Irish Christmas in America returns in 2025, bringing a fascinating performance of music, song, dance, and stories of seasonal Irish traditions. Produced by Sligo fiddler Oisín Mac Diarmada, this year's show features an incredible line-up of talented artists including Cathy Jordan (vocals, bodhrán), Gráinne Hambly (Irish harp, concertina), Caoimhín Ó Fearghaíl (uilleann pipes, flute), Samantha Harvey (piano, dance), and Jack Warnock(guitar, vocals). Exceptional Irish music, song, and dance, combined with evocative photographic images, provide the perfect backdrop to a heartwarming celebration of the Christmas traditions of Ireland. Take a memorable glimpse into the enchanting spirit of Christmas, as the finest traditional artists from Ireland bring you on a fun-filled start to the holiday season of 2025. Show Origins: The holiday show was first conceived in 2005, with past tours featuring a stellar list of guest vocalists. Mac Diarmada enthuses about the program as a way to bring traditional and often unknown Irish customs to the States. “One of the most heartfelt themes of Irish Christmas is emigration,” says Mac Diarmada. “Music was a way that people stayed close to home.” A sparkling tradition among holiday events, Irish Christmas in America is a special show to see this season. For more information, visit irishchristmas.com.

events.title: Janet Thornburg's COGNITIVE DIVINE
events.location: San Francisco
events.description: (Please do not bring infants to the show) You think it’s hard to herd cats? Try getting seven sub-personalities to agree on anything! Wild Child, Rosie, and Mauve love living in San Francisco, but Raisin and Hannah want to go back to Colorado. When Cora soothes Raisin with cinnamon rolls, Hannah complains that sugar is bad for us. Hannah and Wild Child lock horns over Wild Child’s party behavior. Rosie wants to go shopping for clothes and skin-care products, but Mauve wants to spend the money on writers’ conferences and research for her novel. The conflicts never end, and the arguments create quite a din. All seven of Janet’s sub-personalities are delighted to have this opportunity to give their opinions of Janet’s life choices! Janet Thornburg (writer/performer) is a soloist whose solo show Cognitive Divine won the Best Full-Length Comedy award in the In Front of Your Eyes Festival 2026 at the Marsh. She has written and performed eight solo shows in San Francisco at venues including The Marsh, StageWerx Theatre, Theatre Rhinoceros, Theatre of Yugen, Venue Nine, Next Stage Theatre,Young Performers’ Theatre, and the Solo Mio Festival. Her multi-character play Dinner Roles was presented at the San Francisco Repertory Theatre, and her play Antony and Cleopatra Meet Godzilla enjoyed two runs at the Intersection Theatre. She holds an MFA in playwriting from San Francisco State University and an MFA in fiction from Warren Wilson College. Her fiction has been widely published in literary journals, and Rhubarb Pie , a collection of her short stories, was published by Thunderegg Press. For further information about her performances and publications, visit www.janetthornburg.com. Instagram: @jthornburg111 Sound design : Robert Perez Light and sound design : Raye Goh Special thanks to Steve Thornburg and Kuniko Shibata Thornburg for support from start to finish. Please read our Health, Safety and COVID-19 Information Our commitment to our patrons

events.title: LABA's NAME GAME
events.location: Berkeley
events.description: (Please do not bring infants to the show) What’s in a Jewish name? Two old friends seek to find out in NAME GAME . A playful and profound exploration of naming, identity, sexuality, and reinvention told through monologues, circus, and dance with a vaudeville flair. Come discover how veteran performers Sara Felder and Yehuda Hyman found their names—and themselves. ACTOR : Sara Felder is an Oakland-based theatre artist She has created and toured solo theatre shows that use humor and circus shtick to activate grass-roots discussion on significant topics. The popular June Bride was about a Jewish lesbian lesbian wedding, while her current show, Class Act, shatters the silence around money. ACTOR : Yehuda Hyman is a multi-disciplinary theater artist. His plays have been produced at McCarter Theatre, Mark Taper Forum, and many other venues. His essays have been published in Seeing Israeli and Jewish Dance; Dance in America, a Reader’s Anthology; Mahol Akshav/Dance Today; The Oxford Handbook of Jewishness in Dance. PRODUCER : Elissa Strauss is a writer, curator and cultural producer based in the Bay Area. She is the author of the book “When You Care” and an artistic director at LABA: A Laboratory for Jewish Culture. Please read our Health, Safety and COVID-19 Information Our commitment to our patrons

events.title: SHEILA E.
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Queen of Percussion · One of life’s constants for Sheila E. comes down to a simple phrase: follow the beat. And her impeccable inner rhythm is the pulse behind a trailblazing career that still knows no bounds. Family, faith and music were guiding forces for Sheila E. growing up in the Bay Area. In addition to percussionist dad Pete, the Oakland, CA native counts former Santana member/Azteca founder Coke Escovedo and The Dragons front man Mario Escovedo as uncles. Fellow Latin star Tito Puente was her godfather. In addition to being weaned on Latin jazz and Motown, Sheila E. was exposed to a diverse array of Bay Area acts. Those influences ranged from the rock of Jefferson Airplane and the Grateful Dead to the R&B/pop of the Pointer Sisters and the funk of Sly & the Family Stone. “I used to sit on the corner outside of the local community center with Twinkies and 7-Up listening to Sly and Larry Graham rehearse,” remembers Sheila E. “The sounds of the Bay Area molded me.” So it’s no surprise that after such a music-immersive childhood, the gifted, world-class drummer and percussionist began amassing an impressive string of credits playing not only with her dad but also with pioneering talents like George Duke, Herbie Hancock, Marvin Gaye, Diana Ross, Lionel Richie, Prince, Ringo Starr, Gloria Estefan, Beyoncé and Jennifer Lopez. Grammy Award-nominated singer/songwriter behind the seminal hits “The Glamorous Life” and “A Love Bizarre.” A fearless multi-instrumentalist, equally proficient on guitar and bass, actress, mentor and philanthropist. Following a Bay Area gig in the late ‘70s, Sheila E. met Prince backstage. Their Purple Rain recording sessions—including her vocals on the 1984 classic “Erotic City”—morphed into launching her solo career that same year. Debut album The Glamorous Life spun off the Grammy Award-nominated top 10 hit of the same name plus a second top 40 single “The Belle of St. Mark.” Between her ‘80s tenure as drummer, songwriter, and musical director for Prince’s backup band, Sheila E. released two more solo albums ( Romance 1600 and Shelia E.) and scored another classic hit with “A Love Bizarre.” Sheila E.’s fierce, dynamic verve onstage has made her a major concert draw since the ‘90s. Along the way, she has acted in the films “Krush Groove”, “The Adventures of Ford Fairlane”, “Chasing Papi” and launched various music projects (E-Train, C.O.E.D., E Family Band). She added to her arsenal of credits performing on the 2012 Academy Awards with pop hitmaker Pharrell Williams and composer Hans Zimmer. Sheila E. was also among the roster of stars chosen to perform at the 2013 Kennedy Center Honors, whose honorees included artists Herbie Hancock, Billy Joel, and Carlos Santana. Sheila E.'s producing, arranging, and performance talents have been showcased throughout the music and film industry with appearances on The Academy Awards, The Latin Grammy Awards, BET Awards, The American Music Awards, The Kennedy Center Honors, The Summer Olympics, WOW Awards, ALMA's, and The Image Awards, just to name a few. In 2010, Sheila was nominated for an Emmy Award for “Outstanding Music Direction” in recognition of her leadership as musical director for President Obama’s Performance at The White House: Fiesta Latina and again more recently in 2020 for “Let’s Go Crazy” Grammy Salute to Prince. Other projects include The E Family

events.title: Jason Marsalis Quartet
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
with Vanisha Gould

Vibraphonist Jason Marsalis knows a brilliant young musician when he hears one. Equally renowned as a drummer, the youngest brother in the illustrious New Orleans jazz clan has blazed a singular trail since co-founding the Caribbean jazz-steeped Los Hombres Calientes with Headhunters percussion legend Bill Summers. His sleek quartet plays with the dynamic control and precision of a chamber ensemble, and the band’s bluesy authority and improvisational firepower leave no doubt why Marsalis was named an NEA Jazz Master along with his father Ellis and his brothers Branford, Wynton, and Delfeayo.

Marsalis’s latest project features the startlingly accomplished vocalist Vanisha Gould. Raised in Simi Valley, she’s spent the past decade in New York City, where she’s earned widespread esteem as a bandleader, composer and performer. Inspired by greats like Ella Fitzgerald, Sarah Vaughan, Joni Mitchell, and Billie Holiday, Gould is an artist who thrives on bandstand give-and-take. Her third and latest album, 2024’s She’s Not Shiny, She’s Not Smooth, features her original songs and her commitment to unvarnished musical honesty. With no studio fixes or overdubs, it’s a celebration of the authenticity that makes Gould such a riveting performer. Partners in impromptu bandstand invention, the Marsalis Quartet is ideally equipped to meet Gould in the moment.

Personnel: Jason Marsalis (vibraphone); Vanisha Gould (vocals); Others TBA

events.title: Nicole Nelson - Family Language
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: In this striking debut, an ambitious academic faces difficult choices when confronted with overnight motherhood. Family Language explores the misogyny behind the question of whether women can "have it all" as Mona balances her career with new responsibilities. Dr. Mona Melamed is a happily married, purposefully childfree linguist at a top Southern California university. Her days are spent researching and stressing about finally, finally securing tenure. That is, until her brother-in-law and his wife die, leaving their six-year-old son orphaned. Everyone in Mona's orbit expects her to take the lead in caring for the child, including—to some extent—Mona herself. Motherhood is not something she wanted–it is still not something she wants. And yet, she finds herself negotiating a temporary leave to start looking after the boy. Along the way, as the gender expectations thrust upon Mona intensify, her tenure becomes threatened. Family Language confronts that age old question–Can women really have it all?--and uncovers the misogyny behind it. As Mona tries to balance her new responsibilities as a mother, she has to ask herself how hard is she willing to fight for the career she’s earned, and is it fair that she even has to? "In this post-Roe era, it’s a joy to meet a narrator who is unapologetically feminist! Mona’s story is about ordinary words that have extraordinary complexity and consequences. How does language narrow—or open up—the actual possibilities in our lives? Nicole Nelson writes with compassion and humor about gender, ambition, academia, and the politics of care.” —Leni Zumas, author of Red Clocks "Amidst tragic loss and injustice, Family Language affirms the power, the reparative work of showing up for one another. It asserts, language can heal, alchemize, and hold us. Nelson has created a salve, order among chaos. Tender, heart opening, and life affirming.” —A.M. Sosa, And I'll Take Out Your Eyes Nicole Nelson earned her MFA from Bennington Writing Seminars. Her work has appeared in The Masters Review Blog, Literary Mama, Fiction Writers Review, and elsewhere. For several years, she was a co-host of the podcast "Writers on Writing." She also holds a PhD in linguistics from Rutgers. Nicole Nelson - photo courtesy of the publicist Event details: This event will be hosted by Book Passage at our Corte Madera store. events.title: SHEILA E.
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Queen of Percussion · One of life’s constants for Sheila E. comes down to a simple phrase: follow the beat. And her impeccable inner rhythm is the pulse behind a trailblazing career that still knows no bounds. Family, faith and music were guiding forces for Sheila E. growing up in the Bay Area. In addition to percussionist dad Pete, the Oakland, CA native counts former Santana member/Azteca founder Coke Escovedo and The Dragons front man Mario Escovedo as uncles. Fellow Latin star Tito Puente was her godfather. In addition to being weaned on Latin jazz and Motown, Sheila E. was exposed to a diverse array of Bay Area acts. Those influences ranged from the rock of Jefferson Airplane and the Grateful Dead to the R&B/pop of the Pointer Sisters and the funk of Sly & the Family Stone. “I used to sit on the corner outside of the local community center with Twinkies and 7-Up listening to Sly and Larry Graham rehearse,” remembers Sheila E. “The sounds of the Bay Area molded me.” So it’s no surprise that after such a music-immersive childhood, the gifted, world-class drummer and percussionist began amassing an impressive string of credits playing not only with her dad but also with pioneering talents like George Duke, Herbie Hancock, Marvin Gaye, Diana Ross, Lionel Richie, Prince, Ringo Starr, Gloria Estefan, Beyoncé and Jennifer Lopez. Grammy Award-nominated singer/songwriter behind the seminal hits “The Glamorous Life” and “A Love Bizarre.” A fearless multi-instrumentalist, equally proficient on guitar and bass, actress, mentor and philanthropist. Following a Bay Area gig in the late ‘70s, Sheila E. met Prince backstage. Their Purple Rain recording sessions—including her vocals on the 1984 classic “Erotic City”—morphed into launching her solo career that same year. Debut album The Glamorous Life spun off the Grammy Award-nominated top 10 hit of the same name plus a second top 40 single “The Belle of St. Mark.” Between her ‘80s tenure as drummer, songwriter, and musical director for Prince’s backup band, Sheila E. released two more solo albums ( Romance 1600 and Shelia E.) and scored another classic hit with “A Love Bizarre.” Sheila E.’s fierce, dynamic verve onstage has made her a major concert draw since the ‘90s. Along the way, she has acted in the films “Krush Groove”, “The Adventures of Ford Fairlane”, “Chasing Papi” and launched various music projects (E-Train, C.O.E.D., E Family Band). She added to her arsenal of credits performing on the 2012 Academy Awards with pop hitmaker Pharrell Williams and composer Hans Zimmer. Sheila E. was also among the roster of stars chosen to perform at the 2013 Kennedy Center Honors, whose honorees included artists Herbie Hancock, Billy Joel, and Carlos Santana. Sheila E.'s producing, arranging, and performance talents have been showcased throughout the music and film industry with appearances on The Academy Awards, The Latin Grammy Awards, BET Awards, The American Music Awards, The Kennedy Center Honors, The Summer Olympics, WOW Awards, ALMA's, and The Image Awards, just to name a few. In 2010, Sheila was nominated for an Emmy Award for “Outstanding Music Direction” in recognition of her leadership as musical director for President Obama’s Performance at The White House: Fiesta Latina and again more recently in 2020 for “Let’s Go Crazy” Grammy Salute to Prince. Other projects include The E Family

events.description:
In a one-stoplight town in Georgia, in a high school AP English class, five young women begin questioning the stories and the heroes they’ve been taught to believe in, against a soundtrack of pop music and fury. events.title: Edmar Castaneda / Germán López
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
The latest installment of Terence Blanchard’s rising-talent series UpSwing showcases a exceptional example of the creative ferment emanating from what banjo maestro Béla Fleck calls “the odd instrument club.”

Over the past two decades Bogotá-born Edmar Castanneda has blazed a brilliant, improvisation-powered path on the Colombian harp, including the all-star BEATrio with Fleck and drummer Antonio Sánchez. Melding jazz with folkloric styles from Colombia and Venezuela, he’s collaborated with Cuban jazz heavyweights such as Pedrito Martinez, Gonzalo Rubalcaba and Paquito D’Rivera and a disparate cast of bandleaders such as Wynton Marsalis, John Scofield, and Hiromi. Elevating every musical setting with his extraordinary skillset, Castanneda is at his most expansive leading his own Family quartet.

Hailing from Spain’s Canary Islands, timple master Germán López has honed a virtuosic sound combining flamenco and West African rhythms with jazz’s harmonies and improvisatory ethos on an unlikely axe. Related to other “portable guitars” such as the Venezuelan cuatro, Brazilian cavaquinho, and Hawaiian ukulele, the timple is one of several traditional Canary Island instruments that has seized López’s musical imagination. In the hands of López it’s a vehicle for astounding musicianship. Focusing on his original tunes, he draws on his Canarios roots while taking the instrument far afield.

Personnel: Edmar Castaneda (harp); Birsa Chatterjee (tenor saxophone); Julian Miltenberger (drums); Andrea Tierra (vocals); Germán López (timple); Others TBA

events.title: Kazemde George Trio
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Joe Henderson Lab
events.description:
A Berkeley-raised saxophonist who is well on his way to international fame, Kazemde George steps back onto the Joe Henderson Lab stage with his phenomenal trio.

As a youth coming up in the Bay Area, George fell under the tutelage of area luminaries Khalil Shaheed, Charles McNeal, and Susan Muscarella, and combined his formal jazz training with his love of beat-making, inspired by the work of J Dilla and Flying Lotus.

After his move east for jazz studies at New England Conservatory and a joint program in Neurobiology at Harvard, George expanded his horizons beyond jazz and hip-hop to include work in the Afro-Cuban, Afro-Caribbean, and Afro-Brazilian traditions, and he has performed with a wide-ranging list of greats including Solange Knowles, David Murray, Jason Moran, and Ethan Iverson.

His 2021 debut album, I Insist, was released on trumpet great Dave Douglas’s Greenleaf Music label and features a vibrant collection of originals, backed by a superb young band including keyboardist Isaac Wilson, bassist Tyrone Allen II, and drummer Adam Arruda, along with vocalist Sami Stevens. In its review, DownBeat magazine enthused: “What is most successful about I Insist is an insistence of music as not simply technical proficiency, but as a spiritual plane to consider what is at stake in imagining and remembering who we are.”

George’s sophomore session, Ocean Passage, features his trio with bassist Allen and drummer Kayvon Gordon.

Personnel: Kazemde George (tenor saxophone); Tyrone Allen II (bass); Kayvon Gordon (drums)

events.title: Amy Oppenheimer's LOOKING FOR JUSTICE
events.location: San Francisco
events.description: (Please do not bring infants to the show) A hippie, activist, lesbian, feminist, lawyer, judge’s search for identity & justice. The at times humorous and at times deadly serious show begins when Amy moves to Berkeley in the early 1970’s during second wave feminism. Amy finds her identity as a lesbian feminist, goes to law school to fight for women’s rights, represents coal miners and battered women in Appalachia and returns to California to open a lesbian feminist law practice. She is representing women who had been sexually harassed – pre-Anita Hill – but keeps seeing all sides of things, becomes an administrative judge and starts a law firm to do mediation and impartial investigations of harassment and discrimination. She adopts two children – both biracial – and experiences racism up close and personal. In the meantime, she can’t stop revisiting her first experience with the criminal justice system in 1970 when she accompanied a friend to a rape trial. Her (white) friend had been raped by a (Black) boyfriend. The friend wanted him to get help, rather than serve a decade in prison. This restorative justice solution was not an option. Amy wonders about her role in the verdict and if real justice is possible in an unjust world. Content Advisories: The content of this production includes topics and events that may be triggering to some people including sexual violence/rape, sexual harassment, racism and familial violence. Artist Biography Amy Oppenheimer , a lesbian feminist lawyer and retired judge, has spent her 45-year legal career advocating for women and people of color and speaking truth to power. events.title: Swing Into The Holidays
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
with Caity Gyorgy & Christian Wiggs

For this family-friendly holiday matinee, vocalists Caity Gyorgy and Christian Wiggs take the audience on a trip down memory lane with a performance full of your favorite songs from holiday movies, traditional carols and more.

Caity Gyorgy is a dazzling force in contemporary jazz, celebrated for her virtuosic vocals, inventive songwriting, and irresistible swing. Hailing from Calgary, Canada, Gyorgy (pronounced “George”) has rapidly ascended the jazz world, earning three JUNO Awards for Vocal Jazz Album of the Year by age 24—a testament to her artistry and impact. Renowned for her mastery of bebop and swing, she brings a breezy, effortless quality to her singing, with improvisations that sparkle with wit and technical brilliance.

An emerging polymath in the music industry, Christian Wiggs is a vocalist, bandleader, lyricist, producer, and host of Jazz Tonight on PBS. Wiggs’ has built a remarkable career as an artist, leading and featured with ensembles at Birdland, Blue Note, Dizzy’s Club and SXSW. He has produced albums for pianist Emmet Cohen, Benny Benack, and Steven Feifke, and serves as the musical/band manager for global icon Jeff Goldblum and the Mildred Snitzer Orchestra.

Featuring hits like “Baby it’s Cold Outside” and “All I want for Christmas is You”, Swing Into The Holidays brings an afternoon of sing-alongs and fun during “the most wonderful time of the year” for the whole family!

Personnel: Jason Marsalis (vibraphone); Vanisha Gould (vocals); Others TBA

events.title: PAUL TAYLOR
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Smooth jazz alto and soprano saxophonist · Paul Taylor grew up in Denver, where he took up the saxophone at the age of seven. He played in school bands and in high school joined a Top 40 band called Mixed Company. Jazz keyboardist Keiko Matsui and her husband, producer Kazu Matsui, discovered him playing at the Catalina Island Jazz Festival and hired him to play in their band. He spent two years with them, and then Kazu Matsui produced his 1995 debut album, On the Horn, which reached the jazz charts and spawned a radio hit in “Til We Meet Again.” Pleasure Seeker, his second album, followed in 1997 and was equally successful. Taylor released his third album, Undercover, on Peak/N-Coded Music in February 2000. Also in 2000, he toured as a special guest artist with the Rippingtons. Subsequent albums Hypnotic (2001), Steppin’ Out (2003), Nightlife (2005), and Ladies’ Choice (2007), all issued by Peak Records, figured high in the contemporary jazz charts, with Ladies’ Choice going all the way to number one. Peak released Taylor’s eighth album, Burnin’, in 2009. Two years later, Taylor returned with the album Prime Time. In 2014, Taylor released Tenacity, which featured guest appearances from Jeff Lorber and Jonathan Fritzen. The album was produced by Dino Esposito, who was also at the controls for Taylor’s 2016 release Countdown, which cracked the Top Ten of the jazz album charts. The number thirteen is cloaked in mysticism, regarded by some cultures as unlucky and revered by others as a sacred good omen or the birth of a new beginning. Saxophonist Paul Taylor’s anticipated new recording and Shanachie debut, It’s A Brand New Day, is his thirteenth recording as a leader. The charming and down-to-earth saxman reveals, “This album in some ways signifies a new cycle for me, as this is my first new recording in three years. The title speaks to my desire to give my fans an optimistic outlook as we approach every brand new day.” The chart-topping saxophonist has enjoyed an enviable career with a string of Billboard #1 hits and collaborations with a genre-crossing list of musicians including Regina Belle, Maxi Priest, Peabo Bryson, and Keiko Matsui. The Rippingtons, Peter White, Euge Groove, Michael Lington, Jamie Jones and Marion Meadows. Taylor confesses, “I simply love creating and making my own music. I am the happiest when I am doing just this. It never gets old.” Danny Weiss, VP of Shanchie’s Jazz A&R, states, “I’ve been an admirer of Paul’s brilliant work dating back to his very first recordings. His superb tone and phrasing are second to none. Paul Taylor is a true icon whose status is well deserved.” “I am an optimist in every way. Each new year, I just keep trying to do my best, which means playing my horn, staying in shape, touring, and continuing to create,” shares Paul Taylor, who is an avid golfer. He scores an ace on It’s A Brand New Day, showcasing ten tracks of nine originals and one Billie Eilish cover, inspired by a character from one of her favorite movies, Spirited Away. Taylor’s saxophones conjure a mesmerizing recreation of Eilish’s ethereal vocals. He shares, “I heard this single over the speakers in a store and was like, ‘Wow, this is pretty cool.” When I heard it again, I knew I had to record my own version on soprano. When I got together with Dino, we put our own spin on it, and I think we paid a beautiful homage to the song. Who knows, maybe Billie will hear it and like it!” The feel-good track “Makin’ Moves” (another Esposito collaboration) features Paul’s fluid and melodic sax juxtaposed against the swinging and driving rhythm section. The hypnotic melody lingers long after the track fades away. The R&B-infused and sultry “Where I Want To Be” shines a spotlight on Paul Taylor’s gorgeous tone, which is amplified by layered effects. The rhythmic breakdown and soulful groove create the perfect place to be. The buoyant “Inner Circle” is a head-nodding jam while “What You Do For Me” is a funky dance groove with Paul Taylor’s sax out front set against a funky and gritty rhythm section. It’s A Brand New Day comes to a fitting finale with the sweet, reflective, and tender “Downtime.” Taylor reflects, “Music is like the wallpaper of our lives. There are songs from certain periods of our lives that stay with us. I hope my fans can grab onto some songs on the album that will stay with them and remind them of good times.

events.description: Susan Spungen is a cook, food stylist, recipe developer, and cookbook author. She was the Founding Food Editor at Martha Stewart Living Omnimedia from its inception until 2003, where she built one of the most influential visual food brands in publishing history. She served as Culinary Consultant and Food Stylist on the feature films Julie & Julia , It’s Complicated , and Eat, Pray, Love . She is the author of Recipes: A Collection for the Modern Cook , What’s a Hostess to Do? , and Strawberries (A Short Stack Edition) and co-author of the bestselling Martha Stewart’s Hors d’Oeuvres Handbook . Each year during the holiday season, she releases coveted cookie content through her Susanality newsletter, highlighting favorites and debuting new recipes. She lives in New York City and East Hampton, NY. Kristina Cho is an award-winning cookbook author, recipe developer, home cook, baker, food stylist, and food photographer. Her groundbreaking debut cookbook, Mooncakes and Milk Bread, won two James Beard awards and was described as an instant classic by The New York Times. Her latest cookbook, Chinese Enough, is a tribute to Chinese American home cooking, inspired by her family, growing up in the Midwest, and life in California. Cookie Queen: 80+ Irresistible, Doable, Giftable Recipes- Making cookies is both an art and a craft. With Cookie Queen , you have an exciting and invaluable resource whether for a single good cookie recipe or for embarking on a cookie box project, a holiday activity that in recent years has risen to the level of competitive sport. Want to bake but not sure which cookies would go well together? This book takes a modular approach, so whether you want to make three different cookies or thirteen, picking from the different sections will give your boxes and platters variety. No need to spend a lot of time planning to figure out what will taste good and look good together. This mix and match approach is baked into the concept. Try recipes such as: Tiger-Striped Sables Earl Grey Shortbread with Blood Orange Glaze Striped Black and Whites Chewy Ginger Crinkles Strawberry Iced Oatmeal Cookies Pecan Linzers There is no one more qualified to take you on this baking journey of joy than Susan Spungen. As food editor at Martha Stewart Living for twelve years from its founding in 1991, Susan is unmatched in her wealth of knowledge in the food world. Each year during the holiday season, Susan releases her coveted cookie content on her Susanality newsletter, highlighting her favorites as well as debuting new recipes. Cookies are connection. Whether making them together or sharing the delicious results with others, no other food has the power to bring people together and spread as much joy as cookies can.

events.title: Coming of Age in Macholand
events.location: Clio's Books, 353 Grand Avenue, Oakland, CA 94610, Oakland, CA
events.description: The hidden costs of becoming men. · In 2019, Sandeep Brar, a twenty-seven-year-old Punjabi man from an elite household, gunned down five members of his family before taking his own life after a date was set for his wedding. In his suicide note, he described feeling trapped by society’s expectations and condemned to a marriage - and a life - he had not chosen. His final act was horrific. But the question he left behind was harder to dismiss: What happens when patriarchy tells men they are powerful while giving them almost no freedom to decide who they will become? In Coming of Age in Macholand , anthropologist Harjant Gill explores how young men respond to a rigid patriarchy - submitting to it, rebelling against it, trying to escape it, and sometimes coming undone by it. Drawing on four years of research, conducted over a decade, Gill brings readers into the intimate worlds of Punjabi boys as they learn what it means to become men. In this deeply personal blend of memoir, ethnography, and social investigation, he makes a compelling case against a system that brutalizes women and queer people while also constricting the emotional, sexual, and intimate lives of the men it claims to serve. Gill will be in conversation with anthropologist David Vine to discuss what men must relinquish – and what they might reclaim – to become truly free. Harjant Gill is an anthropologist, filmmaker, and writer whose work explores masculinity, migration, sexuality, and the intimate effects of patriarchy in South Asia and its diasporas. He is the director of several award-winning documentaries which have been broadcast on the BBC, PBS, and Doordarshan (Indian National TV). Gill’s work has been supported by the Fulbright Program, the Whiting Foundation, the Wenner-Gren Foundation, the Point Foundation, the Institute for Citizens and Scholars, and the American Institute of Indian Studies. Born in Chandigarh (India) and raised in Northern California, he now lives in Washington, DC, and teaches anthropology at Towson University. Gill’s website is www.HarjantGill.com David Vine is the author of a trilogy of books about war and peace including The United States of War: A Global History of America’s Endless Conflicts, from Columbus to the Islamic State , which was a finalist for the LA Times Book Award in History. David has written about militarized masculinity in the US military and its role in the sexual violence epidemic in the armed forces, as well as how gender and masculinity shape US foreign policy and war making. David, a Clio's neighbor, was a professor of anthropology at American University in Washington, DC, for 18 years, before resigning with the rank of full professor in 2024.
