events.description:
Join us on Tuesday, December 1 when we welcome Jen Siraganian for the release of her debut poetry collection, Everything Has Been Moved, Even the Dead, at 9th Ave
Featuring Tongo Eisen-Martin, Nancy Miller Gomez, and Christin Rice
Presented in partnership with Litquake

Free to Attend, Please RSVP
Or Watch on YouTube Live/Link Available Soon

Proceeds from this event benefit Doctors Without Borders. Donate with your RSVP or directly at their website.

About Everything Has Been Moved, Even the Dead
In her debut collection, Everything Has Been Moved, Even the Dead, Jen Siraganian traces a self shaped by history, fragmentation, and memory as she weaves her family’s past in the Middle East with her identity as an Armenian-American woman and mother. Whether portraying a grandparent’s survival during the Armenian Genocide, a father’s childhood in 1940s Palestine, or a son’s birth when “death is a neighbor,” Siraganian’s poems interrogate concepts of home, origins, belonging, and displacement. Using a docupoetic lens, the poet braids narratives with archival photographs and artifacts to chart cycles of cultural and historic erasure while enacting an intertextual conversation with artists of the diaspora, and with art itself. Through poems that seed each other with recurring images of pomegranates, mushrooms, and fire, Everything Has Been Moved, Even the Dead pushes against annihilation with a voice that resists silence.

About Jen Siraganian
Jen Siraganian is an Armenian-American writer, educator, and former poet laureate of Los Gatos, California. Her poetry has appeared in AGNI, Best New Poets 2016 and 2025, The Cincinnati Review, Electric Literature, Poetry Daily, Prairie Schooner, The Rumpus, the anthology Heaven Looks Like Us: Palestinian Poetry, and elsewhere, and she is a winner of the New Ohio Review Poetry Prize and The Writing Salon’s Jane Underwood Poetry Prize, She served as managing director of Litquake: San Francisco’s Literary Festival, and she is a Lucas Artist Fellow at the Montalvo Arts Center in Saratoga, California. Everything Has Been Moved, Even the Dead is her first book.

events.title: Marie's Tree
events.location: Clio's Books, 353 Grand Avenue, Oakland, CA 94610, Oakland, CA
events.description: Implosions and Injustice in San Francisco · Marie Harrison (1948-2019), an environmental activist of San Francisco’s Bayview Hunters Point, spent her life fighting for basic services such as housing, energy, and employment that had become money makers for a few but a dream deferred for her community. What she endured, from the brown water that ran out of her taps at Geneva Towers, the blood that ran from her grandson’s nose while living next door to the PG&E smokestacks, and the fear of radiation poisoning from one of the country’s worst superfund cleanup sites, are environmental injustices that citizens of the United States suffer every day. Freelance journalist Tom Molanphy will be in conversation with Arieann Harrison , ennvironmental activist and Marie's daughter, about Marie's life, legacy, and the continued fight for environmental justice. Half of the book proceeds will go to the Marie Harrison Community Foundation . Tom Molanphy ’s journalism has appeared in 48 Hills, USA Today Travel.com, Earth Island Journal, and The San Francisco Chronicle , among other publications. His work as a 2022 USC Annenberg Center for Health Journalism Data Fellow led to a 2023 1st Place Award in Environmental Reporting from the California News Publishers Association. His essay “The Road Less: John Huston, Blue-Footed Boobies and Me” earned a 2017 Bay Area Travel Writers award, and his short story “Of Subareas and Public Bathrooms” was included in the California Prose Directory. His last book was a memoir, Loud Memories Of A Quiet Life . He is a member of the Society of Environmental Journalists and teaches journalism, composition, creative writing and art/design appreciation classes at the Academy of Art University in San Francisco. Arieann Harrison is the Founder and Executive Director of the Marie Harrison Community Foundation . Arieann Harrison is a resident of San Francisco District 10 and has lived and worked in the Bayview Community for 30+ years. Her work includes providing social services, employment opportunities, community resources, and engaging in environmental advocacy with local D10 residents, taking an all-inclusive, solutions-based approach to providing good information for the best outcome that will lead to preservation of life. #CanWeLive has become the rallying cry of a community that has gone long overlooked when it comes to social, environmental, and economic justice.

events.title: ISAIAH SHARKEY
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Confluence of modern soul, jazz, R&B, and Black American guitar tradition · Isaiah Sharkey stands at the confluence of modern soul, jazz, R&B, and Black American guitar tradition, carrying forward a lineage that links George Benson, Curtis Mayfield, Wes Montgomery, and Jimi Hendrix while forging a vocabulary entirely his own. A Grammy Award–winning guitarist, vocalist, composer, and producer, Sharkey has become one of the most respected musicians of his generation—celebrated for his sophisticated harmonic sensibility, unmistakable tone, and ability to shape-shift effortlessly between musical worlds. Born and raised on Chicago’s North Side in a deeply musical family, Sharkey was immersed from childhood in gospel, jazz, and classic R&B. His father, a working musician, recognized early his son’s extraordinary ear and feel, guiding him through professional-level repertoire before most children his age would form basic chords. By the time he was 14, Sharkey was touring nationally; by his late teens, he had already become a first-call session player in Chicago’s tight-knit recording community. Sharkey’s breakthrough into the international spotlight came through his long-standing creative relationship with D’Angelo. His guitar work on D’Angelo’s landmark album Black Messiah earned him a Grammy Award and positioned him among the most innovative guitarists shaping contemporary Black music. From that point forward, Sharkey’s trajectory accelerated: he became a go-to collaborator for a wide range of artists including John Mayer, H.E.R., Robert Glasper, Cory Henry, Lettuce, Chris Dave & The Drumhedz, Lalah Hathaway, Common, Paul Simon, Brian McKnight , Greg Phillinganes, among many others. As a solo artist, Sharkey has developed a distinctive, emotionally resonant sound that blends deep-pocket groove, virtuosic improvisation, and songwriter-driven storytelling. His current album, RED , introduced audiences to his modern fusion of soul, R&B, jazz, and guitar-based narrative. His follow-up projects—each expanding his sonic palette—solidify his standing as an artist capable of speaking fluently to instrumental purists and mainstream audiences alike. Sharkey is equally at home on global festival stages, intimate jazz clubs, and stadium tours. His work has spanned from serving as an MD for Raphael Saadiq's NBA All-Stars televised performance to late-night television appearances to the Grammys televised tribute to Quincy Jones and Blue Note residencies. Yet his most defining characteristic remains his musical integrity: a commitment to depth, craft, and authenticity. A multi-instrumentalist, arranger, and producer, Sharkey’s creative range continues to grow. His forthcoming releases explore new integrations of analog and electronic texture, guitar-forward harmonic architecture, and songwriting rooted in personal truth. Whether performing his own music or elevating the work of others, Sharkey brings the same signature qualities—precision, warmth, spirituality, and an unshakeable sense of groove. Today, Isaiah Sharkey is widely regarded as one of the most vital contemporary voices in the continuum of guitar excellence. His artistry honors his lineage while pushing the idiom forward, ensuring that his influence will resonate for decades to come.

events.title: The Bad Plus
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
Returning to the Miner stage for this date as part of their farewell tour, the groundbreaking, genre-smashing band featuring Reid Anderson, Dave King, Ben Monder, and Chris Speed says goodbye to the Bay Area with this performance.

A uniquely audacious group that has crossed into the mainstream to draw jazz fans and rock aficionados alike, they rose to fame over two decades ago by transforming pop and rock anthems like Black Sabbath’s “Iron Man,” Blondie’s “Heart of Glass” and Queen’s “We Are the Champions” into epic improvisational journeys.

Originally formed in 1989 as a trio with pianist Ethan Iverson, bassist Anderson, and drummer King, the band recorded a series of masterful recordings that balanced tongue-in-cheek irreverence with dauntingly accomplished musicianship.

After Iverson’s departure in 2017 and a short stint by pianist Orrin Evans, The Bad Plus was joined by Speed, a visionary saxophonist whose accomplices have included Jim Black, Tim Berne, and Craig Taborn, and Monder, a guitarist of a singular virtuosity whose resume runs the gamut from Brother Jack McDuff to David Bowie’s final masterwork Blackstar.

Over its evolution, The Bad Plus has developed a group concept and sound that makes for a thrilling ride without boundaries or preconceptions. They have had, in the words of DownBeat Magazine, “an inestimable impact on the modern jazz landscape.” Don’t miss this final chance to see them live!

Personnel: Chris Speed (tenor saxophone, clarinet); Ben Monder (guitar); Reid Anderson (bass); Dave King (drums)

events.title: Americans Without Borders
events.location: Clio’s Books, 353 Grand Avenue, Oakland, CA 94610, Oakland, CA
events.description: The hidden history of American radicals abroad · One night in 1940, a group of Stalinists opened fire on Leon Trotsky’s compound in Mexico City. In the end, the victim was not Trotsky, but his bodyguard: a young American named Sheldon Harte. For investigative journalist Julia Harte, the quest to uncover the truth about Sheldon—her father’s second cousin—was just the beginning of her discovery. Her new book, Americans Without Borders: The Radical Activists Who Fought for US Ideals Abroad While Facing Political Persecution at Home reveals the hidden two-hundred-year history of Americans who traveled abroad to join revolutionary liberation movements—and in return were labeled radicals by the U.S. government. The surprising stories Harte uncovers include those of Black veterans of the Spanish Civil War who helped launch the civil rights movement; the forgotten Native American contingent in Nicaragua’s Sandinista/Contra conflict; Elaine Mokhtefi’s work with the Algerian National Liberation Front; Melinda Paras and her organization of Filipinos against the repressive US-backed Marcos regime; and many more. Through meticulous research and on-the-ground reporting, Harte brings her subjects to life in deeply personal detail, exploring not only their heroic sides but also the tensions between their actions and ideals. Interrogating how and why activists were branded as threats by an expanding security state, Americans Without Borders asks what makes a ‘radical’. Join author Julia Harte for a conversation about the long history of transnational radicalism as an irrepressibly American tradition. She’ll be joined by journalist, writer, and producer Sonia Paul . Julia Harte is an investigative reporter in New York City. For the past decade, she has covered U.S. national affairs and the Justice Department for Reuters. Her writing has also appeared in publications including Harper's Magazine , The Nation , Slate , National Geographic , The Center for Public Integrity , and Lapham's Quarterly . Sonia Paul is an award-winning independent journalist, writer and producer who specializes in investigating how power hierarchies and transnational issues impact state systems and individual and community identities. Her stories have been published widely, in outlets like WIRED , Mother Jones , Harper’s Magazine , NPR, 99% Invisible and BBC World Service. She is also the host of a new podcast from Berkeley Social Sciences and a forthcoming podcast based on her reporting. Sonia is a Bay Area native and lives in Oakland. She is on Instagram @sonipaul.

events.title: SYLVIA ANDERSON FEAT DARREL WALLS AND MUSIC DIRECTOR CARL WHEELER
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Two Voices, One Purpose. A Night of Gospel Brilliance, Soul & Praise · Join us for an unforgettable night of Gospel, Soul, and Praise as we usher in the holiday season with the angelic voice of gospel singer-songwriter Sylvia Anderson and her anointed guest, Grammy Award winner Darrel Walls, gospel legend Derrick Hall, and the music direction and ministry of Carl Wheeler. An inspiring evening of deliverance, celebration, and worship you won’t want to miss. Presented by Sylvia Anderson & Mark Elliott of the A-list Musiq Circle - Your Bay Area Who's Who Entertainment network. With Special Guest Host TBA. A gifted gospel artist with an angelic voice and a heart devoted to ministry, Sylvia Anderson has spent over 40 years using her God-given talent to inspire, uplift, and spread the love of Jesus Christ. Born into a family rich in musical and spiritual heritage, her journey began at the tender age of five when she discovered her ability to sing. Guided by her father, a preacher and singer, and her mother, a vocalist, she was nurtured in a household where music and faith were inseparable. She first sang with the Coleman Sisters, under the influence of her father, Willie Coleman, and continued to grow musically, sharing her voice with groups such as Derrick Hall & Company and the Center of Hope Choir. Her remarkable gift has also led her to sing background for gospel greats, including Tramaine Hawkins and Nona Brown, and appear on BET’s renowned Bobby Jones Gospel Hour. A true musician, she’s sung in concerts, gospel festivals, weddings, homegoing services and private events, further enhancing her ability to minister through music. In addition to her musical journey, she has served faithfully in ministry and is currently a minister at Covenant Worship Center in Berkeley, California. Beyond the stage, she is deeply committed to serving her community. She holds a Bachelor’s degree in Theology and is the owner of a care home for children, as well as actively involved in foster care initiatives—demonstrating her passion for nurturing and uplifting the next generation. A woman of many roles, she is a devoted mother of three, a loving wife, grandmother, sister, and friend. For over 30 years, she has also worked as a professional hairstylist, touching lives both inside and outside the church, and retired after 33 years from the medical field. Rooted in Oakland, California, her life’s mission is simple yet powerful: to send God’s love through every song, every act of service, and every life she encounters. Her favorite song, “Because He Lives,” reflects the foundation of her faith and the message she carries wherever she goes. Darrel Walls is the eldest sibling and eldest member of The Walls Group, the acclaimed four-sibling group celebrated for their distinctive harmonies, musicianship, and progressive sound. A gifted vocalist, musician, and creative force, Darrel has long been an integral part of the group’s unmistakable musical identity. Stepping into his own as a solo artist, he recorded his debut solo project, Heart of Mine, with Grammy-winning artist and producer PJ Morton, earning the 2026 Grammy Award for Best Gospel Album. His breakout solo season has continued with three Stellar Award wins, including Artist of the Year and Contemporary Male Artist of the Year, while his single “ABLE” reached No. 1 on Billboard’s Gospel Airplay chart. His solo journey has further established him as one of gospel music’s standout voices. While continuing to bring his unmistakable sound to The Walls Group, Darrel is building an exciting solo legacy of his own.

In one of the most highly anticipated returns of the season, Jake Shimabukuro brings his joyful holiday classics program back to the Miner stage.

Widely recognized as “the Jimi Hendrix of the ukulele, Shimabukuro has created an international fanbase as a sensational performer whose concerts leave audiences awed, dazzled and delighted. Over the past two decades, he's become a one-man army advancing the ukulele cause, turning the four-string axe into a supremely pliable musical vehicle, capable of generating everything from power chord rock to sensuously swinging jazz. Strumming with a hummingbird blur, he coaxes an impossibly big sound out of the instrument through his intoxicating repertoire of pop tunes, American Songbook standards and lilting originals.

Shimabukuro has released a staggering 25 albums for the global and Japanese markets since his 2002 debut Sunday Morning, including his 2006 breakout U.S. hit Gently Weeps and his 2012 Alan Parsons-produced showstopper, Grand Ukulele. The success of these recordings leaves no doubt why fellow string renegades such as banjo star Béla Fleck, fiddle wizard Darol Anger, and cello virtuoso Yo-Yo Ma embrace Shimabukuro as one of their own.

He brings his ebullient virtuosity to these evenings of beloved holiday favorites, imbuing them with a feeling of festive warmth and a tropical vibe.

Personnel: Jake Shimabukuro (ukulele); Bassist TBA

events.title: Janet Thornburg's COGNITIVE DIVINE
events.location: San Francisco
events.description: (Please do not bring infants to the show) You think it’s hard to herd cats? Try getting seven sub-personalities to agree on anything! Wild Child, Rosie, and Mauve love living in San Francisco, but Raisin and Hannah want to go back to Colorado. When Cora soothes Raisin with cinnamon rolls, Hannah complains that sugar is bad for us. Hannah and Wild Child lock horns over Wild Child’s party behavior. Rosie wants to go shopping for clothes and skin-care products, but Mauve wants to spend the money on writers’ conferences and research for her novel. The conflicts never end, and the arguments create quite a din. All seven of Janet’s sub-personalities are delighted to have this opportunity to give their opinions of Janet’s life choices! Janet Thornburg (writer/performer) is a soloist whose solo show Cognitive Divine won the Best Full-Length Comedy award in the In Front of Your Eyes Festival 2026 at the Marsh. She has written and performed eight solo shows in San Francisco at venues including The Marsh, StageWerx Theatre, Theatre Rhinoceros, Theatre of Yugen, Venue Nine, Next Stage Theatre,Young Performers’ Theatre, and the Solo Mio Festival. Her multi-character play Dinner Roles was presented at the San Francisco Repertory Theatre, and her play Antony and Cleopatra Meet Godzilla enjoyed two runs at the Intersection Theatre. She holds an MFA in playwriting from San Francisco State University and an MFA in fiction from Warren Wilson College. Her fiction has been widely published in literary journals, and Rhubarb Pie , a collection of her short stories, was published by Thunderegg Press. For further information about her performances and publications, visit www.janetthornburg.com. Instagram: @jthornburg111 Sound design : Robert Perez Light and sound design : Raye Goh Special thanks to Steve Thornburg and Kuniko Shibata Thornburg for support from start to finish. events.title: Joyful Raven's TACTICAL FRIVOLITY
events.location: Berkeley
events.description: (Please do not bring infants to the show) Born into a radical theater company, Joyful Raven was tasked from the tender age of 5 with the daunting mission to save the world from impending doom… using theater. Forced into animal-print unitards and political positions long before she was a consenting adult, she never had a fighting chance at anything resembling a normal life. You think your parents were embarrassing? Did you have to sing about salmon sex on stage, in a unitard, at 12 years old… WITH your parents? I didn’t think so. In an attempt to heal her hippie trauma, she runs away from home to seek solace in the arms of a spiritual teacher… and accidentally finds herself in the yoga-to-fascism pipeline. Can she save herself? Can she save the world… using theater?! Blending standup, drag, storytelling, & clown, Raven takes audiences on a dystopian and hilarious romp through the looking glass. ACTOR : Joyful Raven is an award-winning actor, director, and “story midwife” known for her powerful and thought-provoking solo shows, where she tackles thorny social issues with humor, heart, and nuance. Born into an iconic political theater family, she has been devising original work for over 20 years. Her first solo comedy, Tales of a Sexual Tomboy , was dubbed “…one of the funniest shows now on display on Bay Area stages” by the SF Chronicle, won Best of the Fringe at the 2016 San Francisco International Fringe Festival, and enjoyed an Off-Broadway run in 2017. Her latest solo show, Breed or Bust , was nominated for Best Comedy at the 2022 Hollywood Fringe Festival, critically acclaimed at the 2023 Edinburgh Fringe, where it won an Offie (OffWestEnd Award), and went on to have an extended run at The Marsh, where it received a Critics’ Pick in the SF Chronicle. She co-founded the award-winning theater company Rococo Risqué and co-authored four plays for the Prize of Hope-winning company Human Nature. As an actor, she has appeared in numerous stage and film projects, including Odyssey Works, the film The Pursuit of Happyness alongside Will Smith, and Spring Awakening, directed by Stafford Arima. Joyful holds an MFA in Dramatic Art from the University of California, Davis, and teaches solo performance and storytelling at Berkeley Rep School of Theatre, The Marsh, and her own studio in Berkeley. Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/joyfulraven/ Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/joyful.raven DIRECTOR : Jael Weisman , a founding member of the Dell’Arte Players Co. and a multi-Obie-winning director, is a trailblazer in actor-based theater, directing acclaimed productions like “Whiteman Meets Bigfoot,” “Performance Anxiety,” and “Mad Love.” With Dell’Arte, his works have toured extensively in South America and Europe, earning him numerous Dramalogue Awards for Directing. Noteworthy projects include “The Dragon Lady’s Revenge,” which traveled to New York and was awarded an Obie, the American premiere of “Red Noses” at the San Diego Repertory Co., “Uncle Gunjiro’s Girlfriend” at the Adelaide Festival, and “Mermaid Meat” for the Berkeley Symphony Orchestra. He has collaborated with luminaries like Carlo Mazzone-Clementi and Joe Chaikin and worked with renowned Bay Area performance artists including Jeff Raz and Brenda Wong Aoki. In his early career, he worked with The San Francisco Mime Troupe, directing among other things “The Dragon Lady’s Revenge,” which was awarded an Obie. Weisman holds a BA from Reed College and an MFA from Carnegie Tech Lighting Design : Kiara Valderrama Show Photos : Cynthia Smalley It is with great love and a deep bow of gratitude that I roast by inimitable parents, Jane Lapiner and David Simpson and their theater company Human Nature. events.title: DEMOLA THE VIOLINIST
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Internationally known award-winning recording artist & multi-instrumentalist · Demola the Violinist returns to Yoshi’s Oakland with a holiday vibe that’s straight-up next level. This is where classical finesse meets street energy , flipping the season with bold beats, symphonic melodies, and that signature Demola swagger. The global phenomenon brings a dope fusion of Afrobeats , R&B , Hip Hop , and Soul —turning winter into a full-on cultural avalanche to kick off the Holiday season. From viral social media star to award-winning showman, Demola delivers a festive, high‑energy experience that never falls short of amazing. This isn’t just a concert. It’s a holiday “ turn-up ”, a sonic joyride , and a seasonal celebration with real Oakland flavor you don’t want to miss. Presented by Kim Pruitt of KP Entertainment Connections, Mark Elliot of the A-List Musiq Circle, with Special Guest Host TBA. DEMOLA the VIOLINIST BIO: Demola, known to fans as “Demola the Violinist,” is an internationally recognized musician, songwriter, multi-instrumentalist, record producer, and award-winning self-taught multi-genre violinist. Born in Lagos, Nigeria, Demola moved to the United States to pursue his solo music career, blending his love for Afrobeat, reggae, R&B, hip-hop, pop, and country into a sound that is distinctly his own. In 2024, Demola’s career reached new heights, fueled by his vibrant social media presence and viral performances. With over 6 million followers and millions of streams across Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube, his videos regularly attract millions of views, making him one of the most-followed and celebrated violinists worldwide. His performances captivate global audiences, and his fanbase continues to expand with each viral hit. This year, Demola launched his highly successful “One in a Million 2.0” tour, performing in over 20 cities and mesmerizing audiences with original songs like “ONE IN A MILLION,” “MBAPPE,” and “LOVA,” which have collectively amassed millions of streams. He also made waves with his feature on the song “FORGIVE OUR TRESPASSES,” showcasing viral Afrobeat across the US and performing at Coachella. A hometown hero in Houston, Texas, Demola, has performed the national anthem for major sports teams, including the Houston Astros, Rockets, Dynamo, and Texans, before crowds of up to 70,000 people. He has also shared the stage with country music star Jelly Roll, performing for 74,000 fans at the Houston Rodeo. Demola is a fan favorite on television as well, with appearances on Good Morning America Online, FOX 26 Houston, CultureMap Houston, 97.9 KBXX Houston, FOX 31 Denver, WGN-9 Chicago, Black News Channel, and many others. His innovative fusion of genres has made him one of the first artists of his kind, captivating listeners with the melodic beauty of his violin and proving that he is truly one in a million. Demola - Afrobeat & Hip-hop Violinist, Artist, Singer

events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: With its humor, candor, delightful illustrations, and (of course) a bit of implied profanity, Get Off That Screen! is a gift book for adults that will resonate with ANYONE trying to raise, educate, or connect with kids in this digital age: from parents, caregivers, and grandparents to teachers, coaches, and therapists—and every adult in between. Willow will be joined in conversation by San Francisco author Erin Gordon. More than just “a balm for our shared exasperation”, Get Off That Screen! includes an Afterword with practical guidelines from author and parenting/technology expert Katherine Martinko and an extensive Resources section with books, events, and organizations to help families enjoy screen-free time, together. Is your kid’s obsession with screens driving you nuts? Do you spend your days begging and bribing your kiddo to “ Get off that screen! ”? This book can’t eliminate screen addiction (including, ahem , your own). But it can help you vent your frustrations about raising kids in the digital age. Willow Older’s lighthearted approach to a serious problem will make you giggle and groan—and you’ll find tips for reducing your family’s screen time, too. “An all-too-relatable tribute to the challenge of prying kids—and ourselves!—off of screens.” —Catherine Price, #1 New York Times bestselling author of How to Break Up With Your Phone “Willow Older injects some much-needed humor and hope into an otherwise overwhelming topic.”— Katherine Martinko, author of Hold the Phone and Childhood Unplugged and creator of The Analog Family newsletter “Just what the doctor ordered for the screen-addicted generation.”— Zibby Owens, host of the “Totally Booked” podcast “This whimsical tale is a balm for our shared exasperation.”— Tiffany Shlain, artist, Emmy-nominated filmmaker, and author of 2 4/6: Giving up Screens One Day a Week to Get More Time, Creativity, and Connection “A Shel Silverstein-esque author for the digital age, Willow Older makes you laugh out loud and feel seen in the best of ways.”— Erin Gordon, author of PEEPS and Look What You Made Me Do Willow Older is an author, illustrator, speaker, and ghostwriter in Mill Valley. She’s the co-founder of Today I Noticed mindfulness and the co-author of Today I Noticed: A Little Book of Mindfulness that Will Change the Way You See the World (Blue Star Press, 2023). For that book, which is now in its third printing and has been translated into multiple languages, Willow and her co-author, Deborah Huber, were thrilled to hold their launch event in front of a large and enthusiastic crowd at Book Passage, where all 40+ books in stock sold out. Erin Gordon is a San Francisco author whose work spans fiction, memoir and contemporary romance. A Stanford-trained journalist, she brings decades of reporting and storytelling experience to her conversation with Willow Older. events.title: Steve Thomas - The Last Navigator
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: This richly illustrated lecture* will take us into a world of ocean navigation largely unknown to the West, a world in which the traditional navigator’s only directional tools are the stars, the ocean swells and the flight paths of birds. In 1983 and 1984 I spent eleven months on Satawal Island and in the Western Carolines as an apprentice to Mau Piailug, then one of the last paliuw, captains fully initiated in the Talk of Navigation, the closely guarded, ancient practices around reading the cosmos and the seas. I chronicled my experiences and the navigational techniques in the book The Last Navigator, first published in 1987, and a documentary film of the same title for PBS in 1988. Now some forty years on I have updated the stories with a new generation of Satawalese islanders and researchers in the revised and fully illustrated edition of The Last Navigator. *Original photographs and film footage, 1983-1987 The classic account of traditional Micronesian navigation and “the last navigator,” Mau Piailug, who fought to preserve it—now available in a revised edition illustrated in full color As a young man piloting a small sailboat across the Pacific, Steve Thomas developed a fascination with ancient methods of navigation. He learned that, for thousands of years, the peoples of Oceania had sailed unerringly across the Pacific without compass or charts, guided only by natural signs—stars, waves, and the flight paths of birds. In search of this secret knowledge, Thomas traveled to the tiny island of Satawal in Micronesia, home to Mau Piailug, one of the few surviving paliuw , or navigators. In The Last Navigator , Thomas tells how he convinced Piailug to accept him as his student and teach him the closely guarded Talk of Navigation. It is a remarkable book, offering at once a clear and precise account of Micronesian wayfinding and the moving story of one man trying to preserve his culture against the tide of modernity. Now, forty years after his original journey to study under Mau Piailug, Thomas has worked with a new generation of researchers, including natives of Satawal, to prepare this revised edition of The Last Navigator . All Satawalese words are rendered in the now-accepted orthography, and the islanders, originally identified by pseudonyms, appear under their true names. And throughout, Thomas has added a generous selection of color photographs from his time on Satawal, documenting the island, its people, and its seafaring culture. This result is a lasting tribute to the spirit of the Satawalese, and to the Talk of Navigation A fascinating exploration of a remoted archipelago and its seagoing people — Peter Matthiessen If you have any interest in the sea and navigation or in the impact of colonialism on indigenous cultures, or if you just enjoy a well-told story of adventure, then read on. — from the foreword by David Barrie [Thomas] is a dual explorer, simultaneously trying to rediscover an ancient system of sailing, using only nature’s navigational signals, and trying to find himself in the myth-made culture of Micronesia. . . . [This] is a travel book with a dream. — Los Angeles Times Book Review This is a story of adventure, and coming of age. It is also an important document, preserving an ancient oral tradition. — San Francisco Chronicle Steve Thomas is familiar to television viewers as the two-time Emmy award-winning host of This Old House, Renovation Nation, and Save Our History. But he is also an experienced home builder and sailor. Beginning in 1977, he sailed a 43-foot wooden sloop from England to San Francisco via the Panama Canal, Galapagos, Marquesas, and Hawaii. In the early 1980’s, he journeyed to the remote Micronesian island of Satawal to learn the ancient technique of star path navigation, an experience that resulted in this book as well as a documentary for the PBS series Adventure. events.title: MARTHA FREEMAN: KITTY VS. CHRISTMAS
events.location: Books Inc. Alameda, 1344 Park St, Alameda, CA 94501
events.description: Join Books Inc. Alameda for our First Saturday Storytime. This month we are thrilled to present author, Martha Freeman, reading and signing copies of her new book, Kitty vs. Christmas. About the book: Kitty is back—but that doesn't mean he's ready for the holidays! The most wonderful time of the year fills this finicky feline with dread. Can Santa help Kitty feel the Christmas spirit? Kitty is a good, nice kitty with a good, nice family who has everything he could ever want. He has his raggedy one-eyed mouse, breakfast at 7:00, supper at 7:00, and a so-cozy life that should never change. But to Kitty’s everlasting surprise and annoyance, things continue to change around him! So when the holiday season arrives, Kitty is not excited. He doesn’t like the itchy sweaters, his family doesn’t appreciate him singing along to Christmas carols, and he’s not even allowed to eat the cookies left right out in the open on Christmas Eve! So Kitty tangles the tinsel, wrecks the wreath, and messes up the mistletoe. Kitty doesn’t feel bad until he sees what a rough night Santa has had. As he and Santa show one another kindness, Kitty realizes that Christmas might not be so bad after all. Martha Freeman was born in Southern California shortly after the Big Bang. As the universe cooled and the Earth formed, Martha grew up and fought injustice, mostly with her pen but sometimes with her feet. Martha has worked as a newspaper reporter, copy editor, substitute teacher, college lecturer, advertising copywriter, and freelance magazine writer. In 1995, she published her first book for children, STINK BOMB MOM (not an autobiography). Subsequently, she has published 30 more books, most recently ZAP! a techno-thriller about a power blackout, and IF YOU'RE GOING TO A MARCH, the perfect how-and-why picturebook for kids on their way to a protest. Besides writing, Martha enjoys running, parallel parking, making pies, hiking and talking on the phone to her far-flung children.

events.title: Kirk Lombard's THE SHADOW STREAM In-Store Meet and Greet and Book Signing
events.location: Mrs. Dalloway's, 2904 College Ave, Berkeley, CA 94705
events.description: Kirk shares his new novel for young readers filled with brilliant storytelling, original writing, humor, and a forest filled with animals. Northern California author Kirk Lombard will be at Mrs. Dalloway's Bookstore chatting with his fans and signing copies of his book The Shadow Stream . He'll be at the store on Saturday, December 5 from 2:00 PM - 3:00 PM so come on down and join the fun! A throwback to family reads of yore, this epic follows a troubled boy and a host of hilariously vexed animals who must save a river before it’s dammed, so they can save themselves. Gabriel (“G” for short) is wasting away in the Abiddon County Juvenile Center when he’s introduced to the Shongunk River by his dying uncle. The river valley—trash-heaped but chock-full of mysteries and fish—wins G over. But, as G has learned, good things can’t last. The Shongunk is scheduled to be dammed by a local developer. In a matter of days, it will cease flowing, and all of the talkative creatures who live there in the river valley will be as homeless as G. Just as G decides it’s no time to accept his fate, so too do the animals. To inspire an uprising, a young trout is nominated to make a fateful journey up the river; a raccoon swears a violent oath against humans; and a newly sober buck leads his skittish flock out of harm’s way. Together with G, they show that good can triumph and that there is power in all of us, even the smallest minnow. KIRK LOMBARD is an author, angler, sustainable fishmonger, and tuba player who once worked inside the juvenile rehabilitation system. His first book, the award-winning Sea Forager’s Guide to the Northern California Coast , was described as “poetry” for fish by NPR. He lives in Half Moon Bay with his family, raising his children on herring and sea shanties.

events.title: Joyful Raven's TACTICAL FRIVOLITY
events.location: Berkeley
events.description: (Please do not bring infants to the show) Born into a radical theater company, Joyful Raven was tasked from the tender age of 5 with the daunting mission to save the world from impending doom… using theater. Forced into animal-print unitards and political positions long before she was a consenting adult, she never had a fighting chance at anything resembling a normal life. You think your parents were embarrassing? Did you have to sing about salmon sex on stage, in a unitard, at 12 years old… WITH your parents? I didn’t think so. In an attempt to heal her hippie trauma, she runs away from home to seek solace in the arms of a spiritual teacher… and accidentally finds herself in the yoga-to-fascism pipeline. Can she save herself? Can she save the world… using theater?! Blending standup, drag, storytelling, & clown, Raven takes audiences on a dystopian and hilarious romp through the looking glass. ACTOR : Joyful Raven is an award-winning actor, director, and “story midwife” known for her powerful and thought-provoking solo shows, where she tackles thorny social issues with humor, heart, and nuance. Born into an iconic political theater family, she has been devising original work for over 20 years. Her first solo comedy, Tales of a Sexual Tomboy , was dubbed “…one of the funniest shows now on display on Bay Area stages” by the SF Chronicle, won Best of the Fringe at the 2016 San Francisco International Fringe Festival, and enjoyed an Off-Broadway run in 2017. Her latest solo show, Breed or Bust , was nominated for Best Comedy at the 2022 Hollywood Fringe Festival, critically acclaimed at the 2023 Edinburgh Fringe, where it won an Offie (OffWestEnd Award), and went on to have an extended run at The Marsh, where it received a Critics’ Pick in the SF Chronicle. She co-founded the award-winning theater company Rococo Risqué and co-authored four plays for the Prize of Hope-winning company Human Nature. As an actor, she has appeared in numerous stage and film projects, including Odyssey Works, the film The Pursuit of Happyness alongside Will Smith, and Spring Awakening, directed by Stafford Arima. Joyful holds an MFA in Dramatic Art from the University of California, Davis, and teaches solo performance and storytelling at Berkeley Rep School of Theatre, The Marsh, and her own studio in Berkeley. Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/joyfulraven/ Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/joyful.raven DIRECTOR : Jael Weisman , a founding member of the Dell’Arte Players Co. and a multi-Obie-winning director, is a trailblazer in actor-based theater, directing acclaimed productions like “Whiteman Meets Bigfoot,” “Performance Anxiety,” and “Mad Love.” With Dell’Arte, his works have toured extensively in South America and Europe, earning him numerous Dramalogue Awards for Directing. Noteworthy projects include “The Dragon Lady’s Revenge,” which traveled to New York and was awarded an Obie, the American premiere of “Red Noses” at the San Diego Repertory Co., “Uncle Gunjiro’s Girlfriend” at the Adelaide Festival, and “Mermaid Meat” for the Berkeley Symphony Orchestra. He has collaborated with luminaries like Carlo Mazzone-Clementi and Joe Chaikin and worked with renowned Bay Area performance artists including Jeff Raz and Brenda Wong Aoki. In his early career, he worked with The San Francisco Mime Troupe, directing among other things “The Dragon Lady’s Revenge,” which was awarded an Obie. Weisman holds a BA from Reed College and an MFA from Carnegie Tech Lighting Design : Kiara Valderrama Show Photos : Cynthia Smalley It is with great love and a deep bow of gratitude that I roast by inimitable parents, Jane Lapiner and David Simpson and their theater company Human Nature. DEMOLA the VIOLINIST BIO: Demola, known to fans as “Demola the Violinist,” is an internationally recognized musician, songwriter, multi-instrumentalist, record producer, and award-winning self-taught multi-genre violinist. Born in Lagos, Nigeria, Demola moved to the United States to pursue his solo music career, blending his love for Afrobeat, reggae, R&B, hip-hop, pop, and country into a sound that is distinctly his own. In 2024, Demola’s career reached new heights, fueled by his vibrant social media presence and viral performances. With over 6 million followers and millions of streams across Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube, his videos regularly attract millions of views, making him one of the most-followed and celebrated violinists worldwide. His performances captivate global audiences, and his fanbase continues to expand with each viral hit. This year, Demola launched his highly successful “One in a Million 2.0” tour, performing in over 20 cities and mesmerizing audiences with original songs like “ONE IN A MILLION,” “MBAPPE,” and “LOVA,” which have collectively amassed millions of streams. He also made waves with his feature on the song “FORGIVE OUR TRESPASSES,” showcasing viral Afrobeat across the US and performing at Coachella. A hometown hero in Houston, Texas, Demola, has performed the national anthem for major sports teams, including the Houston Astros, Rockets, Dynamo, and Texans, before crowds of up to 70,000 people. He has also shared the stage with country music star Jelly Roll, performing for 74,000 fans at the Houston Rodeo. Demola is a fan favorite on television as well, with appearances on Good Morning America Online, FOX 26 Houston, CultureMap Houston, 97.9 KBXX Houston, FOX 31 Denver, WGN-9 Chicago, Black News Channel, and many others. His innovative fusion of genres has made him one of the first artists of his kind, captivating listeners with the melodic beauty of his violin and proving that he is truly one in a million. events.title: LIVE MUSIC: Dagmar Zuniga (Presented by THROWIN' BO'S)
events.location: 4-Star Theater, 2200 Clement St, San Francisco, CA 94121
events.description: Throwin’ Bo’s presents: Dagmar Zuniga Nicaraguan-American artist Dagmar Zuniga makes music that feels both intimate and expansive: songs drift like disrupted signals, carried by harmony, tape hiss, and a strong sense of touch. Her debut solo album in filth your mystery is kingdom / far smile peasant in yellow music — written and recorded in New York, Norway, and Athens, Georgia over a period of five years on her longtime companion, the Tascam 424 — was released by the People’s Coalition of Tandy on Bandcamp & YouTube in January 2025, accompanied by a small tape run that sold out instantly. The project quickly garnered over two hundred thousand views and the attention of artists such as Mount Eerie, who invited her to tour with them that summer. This year, what was once a jewel of tapped-in algorithms and message boards will meet the world at large, with in filth arriving digitally on March 4 , and physically on April 10 , via AD 93 . in filth is an atmospheric, devotional collage where one voice multiplies into a chorus of selves, sometimes delicate, sometimes severe; an effect created by Zuniga’s masterful layering of texture and complex harmonies. Synths glitter out like spears of sunlight from beneath clouds of moody, time-distorted guitars, and songs spin about themselves like tightly-wound music boxes, making use of a kind of hypnotic repetition, before melting apart into their components or slipping into the following track. Zuniga began recording to tape as a teenager, drawn to the physicality of the medium — how a tape recording is fragile, mutable, and alive. Though her ethereal sound may draw easy comparisons to other female pioneers of psychedelic folk, she is influenced just as much by the darker sounds of Syd Barrett and The Fall. Like Barrett, Zuniga is a painter, and she is interested not only in recording music but in creating a full, self-contained artistic universe: she creates her own artwork, merchandise, music videos, and bootleg tapes of new and unfinished music that she exclusively sells at live shows ( “If something is not material, it does not exist,” she insists). Her world has not gone unvisited, garnering her a monthly show on NTS Radio ‘World of Pain’, as well as a forthcoming appearance at Rewire Festival in April 2026. Though Zuniga’s work explores themes of solitude and suffering, the suffering in her songs is not borrowed or displayed; it is held, then opened outward through empathy — an exacting practice of attention that insists on shared ground. Solitude, in her work, is not withdrawal but a starting point for connection. Likewise, over time, her recording process has become increasingly communal, with in filth featuring musicians across the globe. Newer recordings widen the circle even more. For Zuniga, collaboration is a way to “find a place between worlds,” echoing Badiou’s idea of love as a vision refracted through the prism of difference. Meaning emerges there — in the space between voices, between artist and listener. “I hope my music helps people work through difficult experiences,” she says. “The same way it helps me.” Bandcamp | IG Support to be announced DOORS at 7:00PM | MUSIC at 8:00 PM Tickets

events.title: Amy Oppenheimer's LOOKING FOR JUSTICE
events.location: San Francisco
events.description: (Please do not bring infants to the show) A hippie, activist, lesbian, feminist, lawyer, judge’s search for identity & justice. The at times humorous and at times deadly serious show begins when Amy moves to Berkeley in the early 1970’s during second wave feminism. Amy finds her identity as a lesbian feminist, goes to law school to fight for women’s rights, represents coal miners and battered women in Appalachia and returns to California to open a lesbian feminist law practice. She is representing women who had been sexually harassed – pre-Anita Hill – but keeps seeing all sides of things, becomes an administrative judge and starts a law firm to do mediation and impartial investigations of harassment and discrimination. She adopts two children – both biracial – and experiences racism up close and personal. In the meantime, she can’t stop revisiting her first experience with the criminal justice system in 1970 when she accompanied a friend to a rape trial. Her (white) friend had been raped by a (Black) boyfriend. The friend wanted him to get help, rather than serve a decade in prison. This restorative justice solution was not an option. Amy wonders about her role in the verdict and if real justice is possible in an unjust world. Content Advisories: The content of this production includes topics and events that may be triggering to some people including sexual violence/rape, sexual harassment, racism and familial violence.

This is where classical finesse meets street energy , flipping the season with bold beats, symphonic melodies, and that signature Demola swagger. The global phenomenon brings a dope fusion of Afrobeats , R&B , Hip Hop , and Soul —turning winter into a full-on cultural avalanche to kick off the Holiday season. From viral social media star to award-winning showman, Demola delivers a festive, high‑energy experience that never falls short of amazing. This isn’t just a concert. It’s a holiday “ turn-up ”, a sonic joyride , and a seasonal celebration with real Oakland flavor you don’t want to miss. DEMOLA the VIOLINIST BIO: Demola, known to fans as “Demola the Violinist,” is an internationally recognized musician, songwriter, multi-instrumentalist, record producer, and award-winning self-taught multi-genre violinist. Born in Lagos, Nigeria, Demola moved to the United States to pursue his solo music career, blending his love for Afrobeat, reggae, R&B, hip-hop, pop, and country into a sound that is distinctly his own. In 2024, Demola’s career reached new heights, fueled by his vibrant social media presence and viral performances. With over 6 million followers and millions of streams across Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube, his videos regularly attract millions of views, making him one of the most-followed and celebrated violinists worldwide. His performances captivate global audiences, and his fanbase continues to expand with each viral hit. This year, Demola launched his highly successful “One in a Million 2.0” tour, performing in over 20 cities and mesmerizing audiences with original songs like “ONE IN A MILLION,” “MBAPPE,” and “LOVA,” which have collectively amassed millions of streams. He also made waves with his feature on the song “FORGIVE OUR TRESPASSES,” showcasing viral Afrobeat across the US and performing at Coachella. A hometown hero in Houston, Texas, Demola, has performed the national anthem for major sports teams, including the Houston Astros, Rockets, Dynamo, and Texans, before crowds of up to 70,000 people. events.title: Bookagami with Adrienne Biggs
events.location: Book Passage, Corte Madera Store 51 Tamal Vista Blvd Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: What is Bookagami? Book Folding is a global art genre. No glue, no scissors, no stress! Learn how to repurpose discarded (or favorite) books into beautiful, sculptural art with the award-winning Marin artist Adrienne Biggs, the originator behind Bookagami. This hands-on Bookagami workshop guides participants through the meditative and mindful practice of folding books into unique, creative, and sustainable art. Adrienne Biggs’ Bookagami art has captivated Marin . A 30-year Marin resident and former book publishing professional, Adrienne will introduce her unique approach—combining origami, altered books, and circular economy principles—to help every attendee fold up to three books into works of art. Workshop Highlights: Learn Bookagami techniques: Start with simple folds and progress to more complex forms, suitable for all skill levels. Embrace sustainability: Discover how book folding diverts unwanted books from the landfill and gives them renewed purpose. Connect and create: Enjoy a community atmosphere where creativity sparks joy and every fold is intentional yet also spontaneous. Take home your art: Finish the session with your handmade Bookagami sculptures to display at home or give as gifts, and the skills to keep folding. What to bring to the workshop: Newer paperbacks or hardcovers with minimum 1” spine (around 300 pages) work best. Books with words and books with images produce different results/color patterns, so you are encouraged to bring and try both at the workshop (see images below for examples). Book Passage can also supply you with books if needed. Meet Your Instructor Adrienne Biggs is an accomplished artist known for fostering creative inclinations within this community, while rescuing books from landfill (or a dusty bookshelf) by repurposing these common two-dimensional objects into three-dimensional works of art that people of all ages can enjoy, create, and share. Since 2024, she has created more than 600 unique “Bookagami” (as she calls them). Her Atlas, 1963: You Are Here won First Place Blue Ribbon at the 2024 Marin County Fair, and her Bug-a-Gami totem and her Stars, Stripes & Stories piece each won ribbons in 2025 and 2026. Past public art exhibits include two-month shows at Town Books in San Anselmo and at Marelli’s in downtown San Rafael; three month shows at the downtown San Rafael Public Library and at the Friends School in San Francisco; one-month show at ACCI Gallery in Berkeley; and various exhibits at ArtWorks Downtown in San Rafael. Her current solo show, Black White & Read All Over, is at Falkirk Cultural Center in San Rafael November 6 - December 15, 2026. Learn more at @IntoTheFoldBookagami on Instagram. What students are saying about Adrienne "Adrienne was so much fun, and I took home 3 lovely art projects and will make more on my own." Susan F. "Loved it! Adrienne was an excellent teacher. She told fun stories and was very motivating. I had three great examples I created and brought home...I am not crafty and Bookagami was easy to do and fun to learn." Diana S.

events.description: Three time GRAMMY® winning ensemble · Spanish Harlem Orchestra, the three-time GRAMMY® winning Salsa and Latin Jazz band, sets the gold standard for excellence in authentic, New York-style, hardcore salsa. Whether in a concert hall or at an outdoor jazz festival, there is no easing you in as they come at you full force, from start to finish. Their energy on stage and their rich sound and musical precision leave audiences mesmerized until the last note is played. With an unwavering respect for the music’s storied history, the ensemble’s thirteen world-class musicians and vocalists come together to create an unparalleled musical experience. For over 20 years, SHO has been dedicated to the sounds of the barrio (Spanish Harlem, NYC). Their music is characterized by the raw, organic, and vintage sound defined by the genre. They are on a mission to keep the musical legacy of salsa dura (hard salsa) alive and expand its audience to those who love great music, not just Latin music. Grounded in the past, while focused on the future, they strive to keep the music relevant, creating a unique and fresh approach. “As a leader and producer, my mission and vision are to represent the great history and legacy of this music that I’ve been blessed to be a part of my entire life,” reflects Hernández. “Our passion and commitment to this music is never-ending.” With this unyielding motivation, SHO’s GRAMMY® nominated 2022 release Imágenes Latinas saw the band exploring new dimensions but never deviating from its core belief. “As with all the new SHO recordings, the concept and sound are the same, but the playing of new songs, arrangements, and performances always aim to create a new magic for the listeners,” Hernández adds. SHO released their 9th studio album, Swing Forever , in 2024, further solidifying the group as “the leading light of the salsa reconstruction movement” ( Newsday ). With eight albums and six GRAMMY® nominations, this powerhouse orchestra is aware that it is crucial to continually push itself and raise the bar. events.title: Matt O'Hara with Rebecca Herman - The Flying Death
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: “Compulsively readable, well structured, historically informative, and entertainingly written. The Flying Death tells the story of how a modern-day miracle drug was born out of an Amazonian blowgun poison thanks to the efforts of a motley crew of fortune-seeking adventurers—a crew that included a handful of unscrupulous medical researchers, an obsessive White Russian émigré, and an American storyteller with big dreams.”—John Lee Anderson, author of Che: A Revolutionary Life Matt will be joined in conversation by Rebecca Herman, Associate Professor of History, U.C. Berkeley. In The Flying Death: Poison, Plunder, and the Quest for a Miracle Medicine in the Amazon (FSG; November 10, 2026), historian Matt O’Hara tells the story of a young, frail American explorer named Richard Gill, who traveled to the Amazon in the 1930s to open a tourist ranch. Instead, he stirred up an international hunt to harvest a local vine known as curare. As Gill and his rivals quickly realized, curare was both a dangerous poison used by local tribes in blow darts and a potential cure for numerous ailments, including multiple sclerosis and other motor diseases. Seeking to treat his own degenerative illness and make a fortune, Gill established connections with tribal leaders and pharmaceutical companies back home—even as his Russian-born rival, Boris Krukoff, sought to do the same. Navigating treacherous terrain and politics, Gill and Krukoff successfully created a veritable curare industrial complex. The plant became a key element in shock therapy treatments and, eventually, in anesthesia back in the United States. Gill and Krukoff’s rivalry and ethical compromises offer a timeless reflection on how personal ambition, competition, and obsession can shape—and sometimes distort—scientific and cultural progress. In this ethnobotanical adventure story, O’Hara deftly explores the intersections of indigenous knowledge, scientific exploration, and exploitation, and poses searching moral ​conundrums about the price of progress. And who pays it. “The Flying Death is as gripping as the exotic poison at its heart. Matt O’Hara is a master researcher who brews a tale at the frontiers of scientific discovery, with healthy doses of ambition and adventure mixed in. This is historical narrative nonfiction at its best.” —Mitchell Zuckoff, author of Lost in Shangri-La “Matt O’Hara has uncovered the thrilling true story of Richard Gill, a sickly American explorer who ventured into the Amazon in 1938—and ended up transforming medicine. Moving from jungle rivers and poison-masters to medical trials and corporate boardrooms, O’Hara offers a gripping, exciting, and deeply researched adventure story about ambition, exploitation, and the true cost of medical breakthroughs.”—Charles Duhigg, author of The Power of Habit “The Flying Death, Matt O’Hara’s brilliant tale of the South American poison curare, is a wild ride driven by courage, mystery, pharmaceutical wrongdoing, and Indigenous wisdom. The story will surprise you, infuriate you—and it will definitely make you smarter.” —Deborah Blum, author of The Poisoner’s Handbook “An unforgettable tale of medicine, ambition, greed, and the natural world, The Flying Death is a true page-turner. Matt O’Hara is a tenacious historian who writes with great skill and with a keen eye for human drama and injustice.”—Hector Tobar, author of Deep Down Dark Matt O’Hara is a professor of history at the University of California, Santa Cruz. He is the award-winning author of many journal articles and two books, The History of the Future in Colonial Mexico and A Flock Divided: Race, Religion, and Politics in Mexico, 1749–1857. Rebecca Herman is Associate Professor of History at UC Berkeley, where she teaches about environmental politics, US-Latin American relations, and modern Latin America. She is the author of Cooperating with the Colossus: A Social and Political History of US Military Bases in World War II Latin America and is currently at work on a book about anti-extractivism in Antarctica. Her first novel, The Outposters, will be published next summer by Cardinal. events.title: Build or Die
events.location: Clio's Books, 353 Grand Avenue, Oakland, CA 94610, Oakland, CA
events.description: Rebuilding Our Cities — And Our Democracy · Cities like New York, Los Angeles, and San Francisco are in crisis. Chronic housing shortages are driving countless middle-class and working-class households out of high-opportunity areas. Homelessness is skyrocketing. Cars continue to rule city streets, poisoning the climate and putting everyone’s health and safety at risk. And city governments, instead of rising to meet the challenge, are increasingly dysfunctional and unaccountable. Build or Die: How America Is Suffocating Its Cities and What to Do About It traces the history of a disaster a century in the making, detailing how shortsighted and reactionary policy decisions led to the interlocking crisis that threatens America’s great cities.Join Build or Die author Ned Resnikoff, California Assemblymember Buffy Wicks, and Economic Security Project co-founder Natalie Foster for a conversation about what ails America's great cities—and how we can revitalize both urban America and American democracy. Ned Resnikoff is an independent writer and urban policy analyst. His work has appeared in The New York Times , San Francisco Chronicle , The New Republic , The Nation , Dissent , and The Atlantic , among other publications. He writes Public Comment , an online newsletter about cities and democracy. Natalie Foster is author of The Guarantee: Inside the Fight For America’s Next Economy and co-founder and former President of Economic Security Project, an organization dedicated to building economic power for everyday Americans. She's a Senior Fellow at the Aspen Institute Future of Work Initiative.

events.title: SPANISH HARLEM ORCHESTRA
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Three time GRAMMY® winning ensemble · Spanish Harlem Orchestra, the three-time GRAMMY® winning Salsa and Latin Jazz band, sets the gold standard for excellence in authentic, New York-style, hardcore salsa. Whether in a concert hall or at an outdoor jazz festival, there is no easing you in as they come at you full force, from start to finish. Their energy on stage and their rich sound and musical precision leave audiences mesmerized until the last note is played. With an unwavering respect for the music’s storied history, the ensemble’s thirteen world-class musicians and vocalists come together to create an unparalleled musical experience. For over 20 years, SHO has been dedicated to the sounds of the barrio (Spanish Harlem, NYC). Their music is characterized by the raw, organic, and vintage sound defined by the genre. They are on a mission to keep the musical legacy of salsa dura (hard salsa) alive and expand its audience to those who love great music, not just Latin music. Grounded in the past, while focused on the future, they strive to keep the music relevant, creating a unique and fresh approach. “As a leader and producer, my mission and vision are to represent the great history and legacy of this music that I’ve been blessed to be a part of my entire life,” reflects Hernández. “Our passion and commitment to this music is never-ending.” With this unyielding motivation, SHO’s GRAMMY® nominated 2022 release Imágenes Latinas saw the band exploring new dimensions but never deviating from its core belief. “As with all the new SHO recordings, the concept and sound are the same, but the playing of new songs, arrangements, and performances always aim to create a new magic for the listeners,” Hernández adds. SHO released their 9th studio album, Swing Forever , in 2024, further solidifying the group as “the leading light of the salsa reconstruction movement” ( Newsday ). With eight albums and six GRAMMY® nominations, this powerhouse orchestra is aware that it is crucial to continually push itself and raise the bar. Their sixth album, entitled Anniversary, won the 2019 GRAMMY® Award for Best Tropical Album.

events.title: Death Café with Christine Comaford, End-of-Life Doula
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: EOLPeace is holding a community gathering at Book Passage to explore death and the dying process. We will follow the format of Death Café, which was created by Jon Underwood in London approx. 12 years ago. It is a gently moderated conversation where all experiences are welcome, and tea and cookies will be served. Each month we come together to explore the sacredness of our mortality through a new theme. We Follow The Death Cafe Guidelines: Confidentiality: Everything Shared Is Private Or Not For Attribution. Acceptance: We Welcome All Experiences And Only Give Advice If Asked. Respect: All Perspectives Are Honored. Sharing: Everyone Has An Opportunity To Speak. If you know anyone who has experienced a death recently, is supporting a loved one through the death process, and/or is simply curious to demystify death and explore what it means to them, all are welcome. We will have plenty of wonderful book recommendations about death and the grieving process on display and available for purchase at the meeting. Want email reminders? Visit www.eolpeace.com . Christine Comaford's Bio: For 25+ years Christine has had the honor to walk 60+ people through their death process. She views death as a graduation after a life well-lived. This guides the work she does with patients and their families to release fear and anxiety, regrets, guilt, shame, and to do their forgiveness work. Along the way, her patients complete unfinished business (usually around relationships and communication). The result is a peaceful death. Christine’s Experience: INELDA & EOLPC-TRAINED END OF LIFE DOULA EOLPC TRAINED PSYCHEDELIC CARE CERTIFIED REIKI MASTER CERTIFIED NEURO LINGUISTIC PROGRAMMING MASTER SHAMANIC & INDIGENOUS WISDOM PRACTITIONER AFFILIATED WITH UCSF PALLIATIVE CARE, BY THE BAY HEALTH AND ANX HOSPICE Christine Comaford - photo courtesy of self. Event details: This event will be hosted by EOLPeace at Book Passage's Corte Madera store. Free Admission / Open Seating For any questions regarding our events, please contact us at books@bookpassage.com .

events.title: DAVID BENOIT
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: In 1965, the first-ever “Peanuts” animated special took place. It was a landmark event, and it was the start of a tradition that would continue year after year. “A Charlie Brown Christmas” is a tradition enjoyed around the world by fans of all ages. Now, over 50 years later, Contemporary Jazz Piano Legend, David Benoit, along with distinguished Vocalist, Courtney Fortune, is paying tribute to this incredible piece of entertainment history, with a “ David Benoit Christmas Tribute to Charlie Brown With Special Guest Courtney Fortune”. This inspirational tribute concert features the classical music of Vince Guaraldi along with “Charlie Brown Christmas” originals from David Benoit, who took over the helm as music composer for the new Charlie Brown Christmas TV Specials more than a decade ago, as well as classics from David Benoit’s illustrious career as a multi- Grammy-nominated solo artist. The show also features the young voices of a local children’s choir, which serves as a wonderful way of getting the local community involved. The heart-warming show is sure to get the audience in that Christmas Spirit and bring out the‘kid’ in all of us this holiday season. Courtney Fortune is an acclaimed singer, songwriter, and performance coach. She has been recognized by the John Lennon Foundation, Glamour Magazine, and Genlux Magazine as "America's Next Big Jazz Singer” and has written and performed songs for Atlantic Records, Universal Music Group, Sony Japan, Disney, Cartoon Network, MTV, and ABC. She was named one of Glamour Magazine’s “Top 10 College Women” in 2009 and received the Brian Wilson Musical Achievement Award for her work in the songwriting field.

events.title: Marlon James: The Disappearers
events.location: Sydney Goldstein Theater, 275 Hayes St, San Francisco
events.description: $53 with code LITQUAKE5 Co-presented with City Arts & Lectures In his new novel The Disappearers, award-winning author Marlon James traces the lives of a group of gay men in 1980s Jamaica after they are attacked by a mob, leaving one of them dead and the rest with terrible physical and mental injuries. As each man attempts to heal, they must also decide how they will continue their lives after facing such horrible violence. Some choose to ignore the event, while others look for retribution. In the process, James unveils the compromises society demands of oppressed people if they want to survive. In conversation with founder of NPR’s award-winning podcast Code Switch Shereen Marisol Meraji. A limited number of tickets include a copy of The Disappearers.

EARLY SHOW · 6:30 PM · DOORS 5:15 PM LATE SHOW · 9:00 PM · DOORS 8:30 PM Admission: $55 - $85 Elvin Bishop went into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2015 as a founding guitarist of the Paul Butterfield Blues Band, which he joined in 1963 after a National Merit Scholarship took him to the University of Chicago to study physics. King. Two of his records drew Grammy nominations for Best Traditional Blues Album: the Big Fun Trio debut in 2017 and 100 Years of Blues with Charlie Musselwhite in 2020. events.title: Janet Thornburg's COGNITIVE DIVINE
events.location: San Francisco
events.description: (Please do not bring infants to the show) You think it’s hard to herd cats? Try getting seven sub-personalities to agree on anything! Wild Child, Rosie, and Mauve love living in San Francisco, but Raisin and Hannah want to go back to Colorado. When Cora soothes Raisin with cinnamon rolls, Hannah complains that sugar is bad for us. Hannah and Wild Child lock horns over Wild Child’s party behavior. Rosie wants to go shopping for clothes and skin-care products, but Mauve wants to spend the money on writers’ conferences and research for her novel. The conflicts never end, and the arguments create quite a din. All seven of Janet’s sub-personalities are delighted to have this opportunity to give their opinions of Janet’s life choices! Janet Thornburg (writer/performer) is a soloist whose solo show Cognitive Divine won the Best Full-Length Comedy award in the In Front of Your Eyes Festival 2026 at the Marsh. She has written and performed eight solo shows in San Francisco at venues including The Marsh, StageWerx Theatre, Theatre Rhinoceros, Theatre of Yugen, Venue Nine, Next Stage Theatre,Young Performers’ Theatre, and the Solo Mio Festival. Her multi-character play Dinner Roles was presented at the San Francisco Repertory Theatre, and her play Antony and Cleopatra Meet Godzilla enjoyed two runs at the Intersection Theatre. She holds an MFA in playwriting from San Francisco State University and an MFA in fiction from Warren Wilson College. Her fiction has been widely published in literary journals, and Rhubarb Pie , a collection of her short stories, was published by Thunderegg Press. For further information about her performances and publications, visit www.janetthornburg.com. Instagram: @jthornburg111 Sound design : Robert Perez Light and sound design : Raye Goh Special thanks to Steve Thornburg and Kuniko Shibata Thornburg for support from start to finish. events.description: In New York’s East Village, a group of young artists struggles to build lives, make art, and hold onto each other in the face of uncertainty. Over the course of a single year, friendships are tested, love is complicated, and every moment feels urgent. With an iconic score featuring “Seasons of Love,” “La Vie Bohème,” “Take Me or Leave Me,” and more, Jonathan Larson’s groundbreaking musical captures a generation living under the shadow of HIV/AIDS, where joy and loss exist side by side, and the question is not how long you have, but how you choose to spend it. Winner of the Tony Award for Best Musical and the Pulitzer Prize for Drama, Rent is an electrifying, deeply human story about connection, resilience, and living fully in the present.

events.title: CON FUNK SHUN
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Bay Area’s Legends of Funk & Soul 6th Annual Holiday Concert Rendition · All Aboard the LOVE TRAIN — a Bay Area-beloved holiday rendition of funk, soul, and pure celebration with CONFUNKSHUN . This season, let the groove bring you home as the legendary hitmakers return to Yoshi’s Oakland for their 6th annual Holiday Concert Series . It’s more than a show—it’s a soul-charged reunion , gift-wrapped in rhythm, nostalgia, and that signature Fun, Fun, Fun energy only Confunkshun can deliver. Get ready for a festive ride through: Timeless classics you know by heart Holiday gems from their 2024 album Home for Xmas A special first listen to unreleased tracks from their upcoming 2027 project, Smooth Jukebox Get ready for a night made for dancing , reminiscing , and straight vibing with the band that feels like family. As Confunkshun brings home a high-powered mix of holiday heat and signature funk—it’s a homecoming celebration built to move you, lift you, and light up your holiday spirit. And don’t miss the chance to grab limited-edition merchandise, CFS holiday CD jams —and CONFUNKSHUN’s 2027 Pre-released Smooth Juke Box T-Shirts. Presented by Mark Elliot & The A-List Musiq Circle, Your Bay Area's Who's Who Entertainment Network. Pre-Show VIP Q & A Meet & Greet with special guest host TBA. CONFUNKSHUN The R&B funk icon, Confunkshun, who has been pleasing fans for over 50 years, is at it again! After the success of Love’s Train being rerecorded by Silk Sonic (Bruno Mars and Anderson Paak) and reaching #1 on the charts, the band’s locomotive has once again rolled out with recent singles Text Me Tomorrow and Smooth from their highly anticipated 2024 spring album release, Smooth Jukebox. Initially known as Project Soul, the R&B funk icon group we now know as Confunkshun has been pleasing fans for over 50 years. Originating in Vallejo, CA, founding member Michael Cooper, along with high school classmates Louis McCall, Karl Fuller, Cedric Martin, Danny Thomas, Paul “Zebulan” Harrell, and newfound talent Felton Pilate, started this unprecedented music journey. Eventually, the group found a home in Memphis in the mid-'70s when they booked a performance backing Stax Recording Artist the Soul Children. Soon, they were recruited as the background band for Rufus Thomas for the Golden Globe-nominated Wattstax Benefit Concert/ Documentary. While in pursuit of a recording contract, the group adopted a new name inspired by the group NiteLiters’ song, Confunkshun. The newly renamed act attracted the attention of Mercury Records, and soon set funkateers around the world on fire with their debut album featuring their first single “Sho'Feels Good To Me.” Confunkshun went on to release a total of 11 albums and eight top ten Billboard hits, including the No. 1 hit single “Ffun”, “Chase Me”, “Shake & Dance”, “Baby I’m Hooked”, and more. Ironically, their biggest hit was an album cut that was never released as a single. The fan favorite, Love’s Train, propelled Confunkshun’s “To the Max” album to Gold Status. But it was 40 years later that supergroup Silk Sonic’s remake of the single took it to #1 on the charts, helping the duo (Bruno Mars & Anderson Paak) win a BET Album of the Year Award. In 2022, Michael Cooper and Felton Pilate were presented with Honorary Doctorates of Humane Letters from the Christian Bible Institute, with Confunkshun member Dr. Ron Moton earning his Ph.D. In 2018, Confunkshun can proudly claim to be one of the only R&B Funk bands with three doctoral members! Dr. Cooper and Dr. Pilate were also honored to receive the Presidential Lifetime Achievement Awards for their lifetime of service through music and more. This prestigious award has been awarded to a select few Americans to recognize over 4,000 hours of extraordinary service. Confunkshun’s current lineup includes three original members, Michael Cooper, Felton Pilate, and Karl Fuller, as well as the talents of Kurt “KC” Clayton, Ron Moton, Aaron Green, Rene Escovedo, and Brian LaTour. Additional support includes the service of long-time road manager and travel agent Steve Sullivan & Master of Ceremonies (Conductor), Clarence Isadore. They continue to mesmerize audiences with magnetic performances on their worldwide 2023 Smooth Jukebox Tour. The group is also a frequent favorite on the Soul Train Cruise and Tom Joyner Cruise, and will soon be on the upcoming Keith Sweat’s Sweatfest in the Dominican Republic. Their contribution to R&B music was recognized in 2014 with the National R&B Music Society Lifetime Achievement Award. Confunkshun’s catalog of hits remains on worldwide radio playlists and in the hearts of their dedicated fans. Con Funk Shun has produced several hits throughout their career. Some of their most popular songs include: 1. Ffun: This song topped the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1978. 2. Shake and Dance with Me: This song reached No. 5 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1978. 3. Chase Me: This song peaked at No. 4 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1979. 4. Got to Be Enough: This song reached No. 8 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1980. 5. Too Tight: This song peaked at No. 8 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1981. 6. Baby, I’m Hooked (Right into Your Love): This song reached No. 5 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1983. 7. Electric Lady: This song peaked at No. 4 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1985

events.title: Kenny Garrett
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
Coming up as a teen through the Duke Ellington Orchestra and serving a memorable five-year stint with the iconic Miles Davis, saxophone virtuoso and 2023 NEA Jazz Master Kenny Garrett is “one of the most admired alto saxophonists in jazz after Charlie Parker” (The New York Times). He returns to SFJAZZ with his latest ensemble.

A Detroit native, Garrett came of age in the 1980s and was grouped in with the so-called neo-traditionalist “Young Lions” of the era, but it was clear from the start that his adventurous spirit defied easy categorization. Beyond his work with Davis and the Ellington band, Garrett performed with trumpeters Woody Shaw and Freddie Hubbard before releasing his 1984 debut, Introducing Kenny Garrett, and joining one of the last iterations of Art Blakey’s vaunted Jazz Messengers.

Garrett’s extensive output as a leader established the saxophonist as a masterful composer and conceptualist, with standout sessions including 1990’s African Exchange Student, 1997’s Songbook, 2003’s Standard of Language, and the expansive, GRAMMY-nominated 2006 release Beyond the Wall.

Garrett received a GRAMMY nod for the 2009 all-star Five Peace Band Live with McBride, Chick Corea, and John McLaughlin, and his latest is the 2024 Mack Avenue release Who Killed AI?, an innovative electro-acoustic collaboration with keyboardist and producer Svoy.

Personnel: Kenny Garrett (alto saxophone, soprano saxophone, flute); Others TBA
