events.title: Author Storytime: Elsa's Chessboard and Story Power!
events.location: Black Bird Bookstore, 4033 Judah St, San Francisco, CA 94122
events.description: Jenny Andrus Children's Book Author and Librarian Elsa's Chessboard Elsa carries her chessboard everywhere, always ready for a game. When World War II forces her from Europe, can chess help make America home? Growing up in 1900s Vienna, Elsa watches her brothers play chess. “No girls!” they tell her when she first asks to learn; but she’s determined, and soon she’s such a pro that they give Elsa her very own special chessboard. From then on, Elsa plays chess whenever she can. When she grows up, she even meets her husband over games in the park. But when World War II grips Europe, the young Jewish family flees to America, where they find themselves surrounded by unfamiliar languages. Luckily, Elsa knows one language that can always bring people together: chess! Based on the life of author Jenny Andrus’s grandmother, with illustrations by award-winning artist Julie Downing, Elsa’s Chessboard is an inspiring and exciting tale, perfect for any reader who's ever found meaning in a special object. (2025)(co-author Simon Wildman chung, illustrated by Estefanía Razo; translated into Spanish as !El Poder de los Cuentos! by Cecilia Pópulus-Eudave); Ghost Writer (2024)(co-authored with Cecilia Pópulus-Eudave, illustrated by Estefanía Razo; in Spanish as Escritor Fantasma); Breath by Breath (2024)(illustrated by Estefanía Razo; translated into Spanish as Respiro a Respiro by Cecilia Pópulus-Eudave); Treasure Hunt (2022) (illustrated by Estefanía Razo; translated into Spanish as Búsqueda del Tesoro by Cecilia Pópulus-Eudave); and Brave in the Water (2021) (illustrated by Jenni Feidler-Aguilar; translated into Spanish as Valiente en el Agua by Cecilia Pópulus-Eudave), all from Lawley Publishing, and Miri’s Moving Day (2024)(co-authored with Adam Chang, illustrated by Dream Chen from Kar-Ben Publishing). events.title: Rhys Bowen - To Crown It All
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: Multi-award-winning mystery author Rhys Bowen presents her latest work in the acclaimed A Royal Spyness series, To Crown It All . Lady Georgiana Rannoch never expected to be more than a guest at the coronation of King George VI, but murder and some international intrigue make for a change of plans… One of the most daunting things about being related to the royal family but not being royalty myself is finding just the right ensemble for incredibly important events like the coronation. The process has become especially difficult as my maid has fallen ill and I am now relying on Queenie for everything—well almost everything. We do have a lovely new nanny with whom my son James is quite smitten. My concerns about gowns and Queenie-related disasters are put aside when I receive a worrisome letter from my mother. She seems anxious to see me and is missing her grandson-not at all like her! Darcy and I read between the lines only to discover a coded plea for help. We decide the best way to get Mummy away from Hitler and his cronies is to secure her an invitation to the coronation and have her stay at Eynsleigh along with our other guests for the big event. Two complications quickly arise. A stern member of the German government has arrived with Mummy who seems to be watching her-and our-every move. And then I unexpectedly find myself involved in the coronation ceremony at Westminster Abbey. Well, that solves my worry about what I should wear as I will be outfitted by Buckingham Palace for the festivities. But with a house full of visitors for the big event, Darcy receives word that the ceremony itself, and all of the royal attendees are under threat. And to make matters immeasurably worse, one of my esteemed house guests is found quite dead in their bed. Darcy and I must find a killer and prevent a terrible tragedy all while I do my best to avoid any embarrassing mishaps at the coronation, as quite literally, the world will be watching. Rhys Bowen , a New York Times bestselling author, has been nominated for every major award in mystery writing, including the Edgar®, and has won many, including both the Agatha and Anthony awards. She is also the author of the Molly Murphy Mysteries, set in turn-of-the-century New York, and the Constable Evans Mysteries, set in Wales, as well as two international bestselling stand-alone novels. She was born in England and now divides her time between Northern California and Arizona. events.title: LIVE MUSIC: June McDoom, Eliana Glass (Presented by THROWIN' BO'S)
events.location: 4-Star Theater, 2200 Clement St, San Francisco, CA 94121
events.description: Throwin’ Bo’s presents: June McDoom There is a hush most of us only knew as children, the warm drift between familiar household sounds and being carried to bed, a place that belongs to you and to some self you have not met yet. June McDoom's debut full-length, Follow the Light, lives in that dream space and then keeps walking, slipping out of time and waking somewhere new, barely familiar enough to feel like home yet wholly your own. She came up in a Jamaican household on the edge of the Florida Everglades, an existence built of extended family, communal care, bass and harmonics. Her father, a carpenter and a student of sound, built his own speakers and kept three sound systems going across as many rooms. His low end would rise through her bedroom floor like some wayward cat while she lay above it with folk records, finding harmonies that were new and hers alone. Two musics in one room. Lushness as past and premonition. She found folk on her own, somewhere between the cast recording of The Sound of Music and Simon and Garfunkel, while everyone around her called it sleepy music. She did not mind being the only one. The solitude let her fall for harmony first, before words, before anything else, and harmony is still the thing she reaches for. Generationally speaking, the music was already in the air. Her grandfather, Colin Smith, is a distinguished mento man who played banjo and guitar and built his own rumba boxes, worked to keep Jamaica's oldest acoustic folk form alive. Mento is the root of all of it: ska, rock steady, reggae, dub and everything after. He is the one who put a guitar in her hands. An inheritance, a gift and a map. Even her name is part of it, though she will tell you she landed on it more by feel than reason. She records as June McDoom, born Alyssa, June being a nickname one of her grandmothers, Joan, went by, a name she thought was cool to carry and simply liked the sound of. An etheric channel that reverberates all the same. A dub all its own. Made slowly and by hand with her longtime partner Evan Wright, Follow the Light lays the harmony of folk over the rhythm of dub, with Dionne Warwick, Minnie Riperton, Pentangle and the washed guitars of Cocteau Twins haunting its outer edges. Voice and guitar seeking each other out first, then everything else stacked across long days in the studio they keep at home, restraint kept on purpose. The lead single "Without You" is the whole method surfacing, split open and sparkling like a geode in a creek bed. Angelic heroics, and nothing less. At the heart is family. Her grandmother Aggie, the light behind "Memory," guiding still. And underneath, the quieter truth the record keeps: none of us are only one person, but a continuum of selves, the ones who shaped us and the ones we have yet to meet. Future you is an ancestor your current self gets to greet. Press play and the same invitation is yours: A few minutes out of time, a place that turns familiar the longer you stay until you surface somewhere new and find it was yours all along. Bandcamp | IG Eliana Glass Eliana Glass (b.1997) is a singer, pianist, and visual artist born in Australia, raised in Seattle, and based in New York. She is a graduate of the jazz program at The New School where she studied with such mentors as Andrew Cyrille, Ben Street, Kris Davis, and Jay Clayton. She also holds a degree in Visual Studies and Writing and works freely across multiple mediums. In the past year she has released her debut album, E, an album comprised primarily of piano and voice, via Shelter Press. Her work dedicates special attention to sparseness, voice, and her relationship to the piano, a lifelong entity since she was a kid. Bandcamp | IG DOORS at 7:00PM | MUSIC at 8:00 PM Tickets

events.title: Adam Shulman Trio plays 'A Charlie Brown Christmas'
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
A creative force on the San Francisco jazz scene for well more than a decade, pianist Shulman reprises his tribute to Bay Area jazz legend Vince Guaraldi and his soundtrack to Charles Schulz’s 1965 holiday classic, A Charlie Brown Christmas.

Among the most beloved holiday albums of all time, A Charlie Brown Christmas has been certified Triple Platinum with sales of over three million copies. The session was voted into the GRAMMY Hall of Fame in 2007 and was added to the Library of Congress’ National Recording Registry’s list of “culturally, historically, or aesthetically important” American recordings. The album includes a definitive version of the Peanuts theme song “Linus and Lucy” and a pair of originals now considered Christmas standards, “Christmas Time Is Here” and “Skating,” as well as new arrangements of classic holiday songs “O Tannenbaum” and “What Child is This,” among others.

A San Francisco native, Shulman studied music at UC Santa Cruz and soaked up bandstand wisdom from the late, beloved piano master Smith Dobson and work with Stefon Harris, Miguel Zenón, Luciana Souza, Paula West, Larry Coryell, and Bobby Hutcherson. He brings Guaraldi’s classic to life with a trio comprising several of the Bay Area’s finest musicians.

Personnel: Adam Shulman (piano); Others TBA

events.title: Amy Oppenheimer's LOOKING FOR JUSTICE
events.location: San Francisco
events.description: (Please do not bring infants to the show) A hippie, activist, lesbian, feminist, lawyer, judge’s search for identity & justice. The at times humorous and at times deadly serious show begins when Amy moves to Berkeley in the early 1970’s during second wave feminism. Amy finds her identity as a lesbian feminist, goes to law school to fight for women’s rights, represents coal miners and battered women in Appalachia and returns to California to open a lesbian feminist law practice. She is representing women who had been sexually harassed – pre-Anita Hill – but keeps seeing all sides of things, becomes an administrative judge and starts a law firm to do mediation and impartial investigations of harassment and discrimination. She adopts two children – both biracial – and experiences racism up close and personal. In the meantime, she can’t stop revisiting her first experience with the criminal justice system in 1970 when she accompanied a friend to a rape trial. Her (white) friend had been raped by a (Black) boyfriend. The friend wanted him to get help, rather than serve a decade in prison. This restorative justice solution was not an option. Amy wonders about her role in the verdict and if real justice is possible in an unjust world. Content Advisories: The content of this production includes topics and events that may be triggering to some people including sexual violence/rape, sexual harassment, racism and familial violence.

events.title: Nashville Honeymoon
events.location: Bird & Beckett Books & Records, 653 Chenery Street, San Francisco
events.description: Lynne Maes, rhythm guitar & vocals; Hank Maninger, lead guitar & vocals; Tim Wagar, bass guitar; Paul Revelli drums You’re in for two sets in honky tonk heaven. Mainstays of the Bay Area Americana scene, and the Bird & Beckett bandstand, for nearly a decade, Nashville Honeymoon has traversed country, rockabilly, bluegrass, and pop across four albums, writing songs that uplift the tangled mess of day-to-day life and investigate universal themes of love and loss – often at the same time. Their latest album, Sidewinder, is true to its title, offering a collection of songs that are grounded in classic country while edging into different sounds, genres, and themes that run through American pop music. This is some of the sweetest, sauciest, and most sincere country music you’ll ever hear. SUNDAY HAPPY HOUR! Grab your partner! Gather your kids! Call a friend! Come on down to the bookshop to get a bit better acquainted with your neighbors and just have a ball before the start of another long hard work week!

events.title: CON FUNK SHUN
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Bay Area’s Legends of Funk & Soul 6th Annual Holiday Concert Rendition · All Aboard the LOVE TRAIN — a Bay Area-beloved holiday rendition of funk, soul, and pure celebration with CONFUNKSHUN . This season, let the groove bring you home as the legendary hitmakers return to Yoshi’s Oakland for their 6th annual Holiday Concert Series . It’s more than a show—it’s a soul-charged reunion , gift-wrapped in rhythm, nostalgia, and that signature Fun, Fun, Fun energy only Confunkshun can deliver. Get ready for a festive ride through: Timeless classics you know by heart Holiday gems from their 2024 album Home for Xmas A special first listen to unreleased tracks from their upcoming 2027 project, Smooth Jukebox Get ready for a night made for dancing , reminiscing , and straight vibing with the band that feels like family. As Confunkshun brings home a high-powered mix of holiday heat and signature funk—it’s a homecoming celebration built to move you, lift you, and light up your holiday spirit. And don’t miss the chance to grab limited-edition merchandise, CFS holiday CD jams —and CONFUNKSHUN’s 2027 Pre-released Smooth Juke Box T-Shirts. Presented by Mark Elliot & The A-List Musiq Circle, Your Bay Area's Who's Who Entertainment Network. Pre-Show VIP Q & A Meet & Greet with special guest host TBA. CONFUNKSHUN The R&B funk icon, Confunkshun, who has been pleasing fans for over 50 years, is at it again! After the success of Love’s Train being rerecorded by Silk Sonic (Bruno Mars and Anderson Paak) and reaching #1 on the charts, the band’s locomotive has once again rolled out with recent singles Text Me Tomorrow and Smooth from their highly anticipated 2024 spring album release, Smooth Jukebox. Initially known as Project Soul, the R&B funk icon group we now know as Confunkshun has been pleasing fans for over 50 years. Originating in Vallejo, CA, founding member Michael Cooper, along with high school classmates Louis McCall, Karl Fuller, Cedric Martin, Danny Thomas, Paul “Zebulan” Harrell, and newfound talent Felton Pilate, started this unprecedented music journey. Eventually, the group found a home in Memphis in the mid-'70s when they booked a performance backing Stax Recording Artist the Soul Children. Soon, they were recruited as the background band for Rufus Thomas for the Golden Globe-nominated Wattstax Benefit Concert/ Documentary. While in pursuit of a recording contract, the group adopted a new name inspired by the group NiteLiters’ song, Confunkshun. The newly renamed act attracted the attention of Mercury Records, and soon set funkateers around the world on fire with their debut album featuring their first single “Sho'Feels Good To Me.” Confunkshun went on to release a total of 11 albums and eight top ten Billboard hits, including the No. 1 hit single “Ffun”, “Chase Me”, “Shake & Dance”, “Baby I’m Hooked”, and more. Ironically, their biggest hit was an album cut that was never released as a single. The fan favorite, Love’s Train, propelled Confunkshun’s “To the Max” album to Gold Status. But it was 40 years later that supergroup Silk Sonic’s remake of the single took it to #1 on the charts, helping the duo (Bruno Mars & Anderson Paak) win a BET Album of the Year Award. In 2022, Michael Cooper and Felton Pilate were presented with Honorary Doctorates of Humane Letters from the Christian Bible Institute, with Confunkshun member Dr. Ron Moton earning his Ph.D. In 2018, Confunkshun can proudly claim to be one of the only R&B Funk bands with three doctoral members! Dr. Cooper and Dr. Pilate were also honored to receive the Presidential Lifetime Achievement Awards for their lifetime of service through music and more. This prestigious award has been awarded to a select few Americans to recognize over 4,000 hours of extraordinary service. Confunkshun’s current lineup includes three original members, Michael Cooper, Felton Pilate, and Karl Fuller, as well as the talents of Kurt “KC” Clayton, Ron Moton, Aaron Green, Rene Escovedo, and Brian LaTour. Additional support includes the service of long-time road manager and travel agent Steve Sullivan & Master of Ceremonies (Conductor), Clarence Isadore. They continue to mesmerize audiences with magnetic performances on their worldwide 2023 Smooth Jukebox Tour. The group is also a frequent favorite on the Soul Train Cruise and Tom Joyner Cruise, and will soon be on the upcoming Keith Sweat’s Sweatfest in the Dominican Republic. Their contribution to R&B music was recognized in 2014 with the National R&B Music Society Lifetime Achievement Award. Confunkshun’s catalog of hits remains on worldwide radio playlists and in the hearts of their dedicated fans. Con Funk Shun has produced several hits throughout their career. Some of their most popular songs include: 1. Ffun: This song topped the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1978. 2. Shake and Dance with Me: This song reached No. 5 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1978. 3. Chase Me: This song peaked at No. 4 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1979. 4. Got to Be Enough: This song reached No. 8 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1980. 5. Too Tight: This song peaked at No. 8 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1981. 6. Baby, I’m Hooked (Right into Your Love): This song reached No. 5 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1983. 7. Electric Lady: This song peaked at No. 4 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1985

events.title: Song Circle with Amateur Music Network
events.location: Berkeley
events.description: October Theme: “Broadway and Show Tunes” There’s nothing that brings people together better than singing our favorite songs. It recalls summer nights around the campfire: someone strumming the guitar and all singing a mix of folk music, familiar songs we heard on the radio, and occasional new songs that someone shares. Nobody has to worry about whether you know the songs or can sing like a pro. This is our chance to share the joy of singing simply for the fun of it. Cary Sheldon is a singer, songwriter, and beloved Berkeley voice teacher with 30 years worth of grateful students. She has been playing and teaching in the Bay Area for the last 40 years. Her love for R & B music led her to be part of Zazu Pitts Memorial Orchestra in the 1980’s. Other affiliations include The Henry Kaiser Band, The Henriettas (a recreation of DeZurick sisters, a popular country music duo from the 1940’s), who appeared on Prairie Home Companion, and most recently her band DanceChant, a joyful community-inspired R&B band that encourages audience participation. She continues to be inspired by her love of singing in community. “Singing together with others is one of the greatest joys in my life.” Now in her 60’s, she returns to influences from her early life. Her grade school music teachers included John Langstaff, creator of the Christmas Revels, and the repertoire was based on the American folk tradition, including old English ballads, spirituals, freedom songs, and the popular folk and protest songs of the 1960’s. She hopes to inspire others to explore the depth of this material and rediscover the joy of community singing. Soprano Candace Johnson has led AMN’s Juneteenth Choral Celebration since its inception in 2020. The AMN community knows her through her commitment to the power of the Negro Spirituals tradition, but Candace has a deep connection to theater and to the music of the Broadway stage. A voice instructor at UC Berkeley for 17 years, in 2022 Candace also became the director of the University Gospel Choir. A lyric coloratura soprano, she crosses musical boundaries performing classical, jazz, musical theater, pop and gospel. She has sung on many stages, including Carnegie Hall and The Manhattan Center. Also a playwright and actress, Candace premiered her first one-woman show, Vox in a Box , in UC Berkeley’s Hertz Hall in 2018, which led to her becoming a resident solo artist at The Marsh theater (Berkeley/San Francisco). Candace has written and performed 5 full-length one-woman musicals. Her most recent show, Scat-ter Brain: The Music of ADHD , was commissioned by The Marsh in 2024 for its inaugural IFOYE festival of new works by women-identifying playwrights. Following an extended run, Scat-ter Brain was nominated by Broadway World SF for Best Solo Show of 2025. Please read our Health, Safety and COVID-19 Information Our commitment to our patrons

events.title: MIKE STERN BAND
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: FEAT. DENNIS CHAMBERS, DENNIS GWIZDALA, BOB FRANCESCHINI & LENI STERN · Legendary Guitarist Mike Stern On Tour! Mike Stern’s Debut Release With Mack Avenue Music Group/Artistry Music Features Collaborations With Christian McBride, Chris Potter, Antonio Sanchez, Dennis Chambers and Richard Bona Produced By The Late Jim Beard, Stern’s Longtime Collaborator and Friend Mike Stern's new album Echoes, And Other Songs marks his debut release on Mack Avenue Music Group/Artistry Music. Echoes delivers all the elements that longtime Stern fans want, and then some: the hook-filled rapid-fire bebop writing; the gorgeous melodic sensibility culled from African music, gospel and other influences; the breakneck improvisations that pepper hornlike bop virtuosity with rock fire. Along with the announcement, Stern has shared the lead single “Stuff Happens,” which features the 9-time Grammy Award winner Christian McBride . “It’s definitely got a Blues vibe, and it opens with a short but really wonderful solo from Christian McBride,” Stern says of the track. “He is definitely not only one of the greatest upright bass players ever, but he plays amazing electric bass. Of course, I knew that going into this project, so I asked him to play a lot of electric bass and he did that so beautifully on this tune. He played great on everything.” Stern has been celebrated for his versatile playing style since he first hit the scene in the 1970s, transcending genres by performing with Blood, Sweat & Tears, Miles Davis, Jaco Pastorius, The Brecker Brothers, David Sanborn, Béla Fleck, Yellowjackets and more. With Echoes and Other Songs, Stern brings together an all-star group of musicians, including Christian McBride, Chris Potter, Antonio Sanchez, Richard Bona & Dennis Chambers, for 11 brand-new originals that will captivate and unite guitar and jazz fans of all generations. This is Stern’s first release since the loss of longtime producer and keyboardist Jim Beard (who played on and produced the album), the closure of Stern’s beloved 55 Bar, and his 2016 injury, from which he continues to face physical hurdles. Echoes and Other Songs is a powerhouse document from one of the finest guitarists in jazz history, at a time in his career when he overcame immense physical struggles and experienced profound loss. In the sheer might of these performances, Echoes is a defiant record — not so much a victory lap as a call to arms. Echoes and Other Songs could be considered a loving farewell to Jim Beard, who passed away in March 2024. Beard acted as Stern’s go-to producer for over three decades, and as a favorite keyboardist for even longer. “I’m not exaggerating when I call Jim Beard a genius,” Stern says. “People would say, ‘You should change up your producer — you know, just mix it up.’ And I would say, ‘Why?’ Everybody loved Jim. He was just great at what he did — how he used technology, how he produced, how he mixed.” Stern goes on to describe Beard’s touch as a player. “Incredible.” He pauses. “Ridiculous… Everything he did was perfect. The records he came out with were amazing, but I think he could have done even more as a piano player.” In the end, though, Stern was most affected by Beard’s devotion as a friend. “When I had the blues,” he recalls, “when I felt low and wanted to talk to somebody, he’s one of the people I would reach out to. It would be short, but he would know exactly what I was talking about. It’s a heartbreaker.” Echoes also marks the first album Stern has released as a leader since the West Village jazz haunt 55 Bar closed its doors in 2022, a casualty of the pandemic. Stern’s regular gig there was legendary, enduring and advantageous; it was at 55 where Michael Brecker became interested in hiring the guitarist. His 55 residency also provided a physical-therapy regimen of sorts after Stern broke both of his humerus bones in 2016. He stumbled over construction materials on the street in New York and fell, and the aftermath included potentially career-ending nerve damage that threatened his picking hand. The road to recovery has been long, hard, and ongoing. Stern has had the abiding support of his wife, Leni, to help him, as well as godsends like Dr. Alton Barron, an orthopedic hand specialist recommended by a friend, fellow guitar master Wayne Krantz. Advised by another pal, the drummer Ray Levier, Stern came up with an efficient system for holding his pick, using wig glue and tape. “It was a challenge and a half,” Stern says, “and it still is, sometimes, just to accept it. It gets me really upset and frustrated because I used to play stuff with my fingers. I had to change certain things about my technique.” But Stern pushes on and rises above, as he has throughout his career — like when he rejoined Miles Davis’ band in 1985, having found sobriety. Throughout Echoes, you’d be hard-pressed to find a second in which Stern’s chops are less than sublime. In terms of expressivity, his flatpicking has no limitations. “I’m gonna keep trying with whatever I got,” Stern says. “You know I got to. Because I love it, and love means that some days you hate it; those two sides are on the same coin. But the love is definitely winning out.” Consider Mike Stern’s Echoes and Other Songs his love letter to jazz, to the guitar, to bandstand camaraderie, and to his own undefeated will. Echoes And Other Songs tracklist: 1. Connections 2. Echoes 3. Stuff Happens 4. Space Bar 5. I Hope So 6. Where’s Leo 7. Gospel Song 8. Crumbles 9. Curtis 10. Climate 11. Could Be For more information, please contact: Sonny Bailey-Lemansky ( sonny@missingpiecegroup.com ) Joe Sivick ( joe@missingpiecegroup.com ) Brett Loeb ( brett@missingpiecegroup.com ) at Missing Piece Group

events.title: Rent
events.location: San Francisco Playhouse, 450 Post St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description: In New York’s East Village, a group of young artists struggles to build lives, make art, and hold onto each other in the face of uncertainty. Over the course of a single year, friendships are tested, love is complicated, and every moment feels urgent. With an iconic score featuring “Seasons of Love,” “La Vie Bohème,” “Take Me or Leave Me,” and more, Jonathan Larson’s groundbreaking musical captures a generation living under the shadow of HIV/AIDS, where joy and loss exist side by side, and the question is not how long you have, but how you choose to spend it. Winner of the Tony Award for Best Musical and the Pulitzer Prize for Drama, Rent is an electrifying, deeply human story about connection, resilience, and living fully in the present.

The records he came out with were amazing, but I think he could have done even more as a piano player.” In the end, though, Stern was most affected by Beard’s devotion as a friend. “When I had the blues,” he recalls, “when I felt low and wanted to talk to somebody, he’s one of the people I would reach out to. It would be short, but he would know exactly what I was talking about. It’s a heartbreaker.” Echoes also marks the first album Stern has released as a leader since the West Village jazz haunt 55 Bar closed its doors in 2022, a casualty of the pandemic. Stern’s regular gig there was legendary, enduring and advantageous; it was at 55 where Michael Brecker became interested in hiring the guitarist. His 55 residency also provided a physical-therapy regimen of sorts after Stern broke both of his humerus bones in 2016. He stumbled over construction materials on the street in New York and fell, and the aftermath included potentially career-ending nerve damage that threatened his picking hand. The road to recovery has been long, hard, and ongoing. Stern has had the abiding support of his wife, Leni, to help him, as well as godsends like Dr. Alton Barron, an orthopedic hand specialist recommended by a friend, fellow guitar master Wayne Krantz. Advised by another pal, the drummer Ray Levier, Stern came up with an efficient system for holding his pick, using wig glue and tape. “It was a challenge and a half,” Stern says, “and it still is, sometimes, just to accept it. It gets me really upset and frustrated because I used to play stuff with my fingers. I had to change certain things about my technique.” But Stern pushes on and rises above, as he has throughout his career — like when he rejoined Miles Davis’ band in 1985, having found sobriety. Throughout Echoes, you’d be hard-pressed to find a second in which Stern’s chops are less than sublime. In terms of expressivity, his flatpicking has no limitations. “I’m gonna keep trying with whatever I got,” Stern says. “You know I got to. Because I love it, and love means that some days you hate it; those two sides are on the same coin. But the love is definitely winning out.” Consider Mike Stern’s Echoes and Other Songs his love letter to jazz, to the guitar, to bandstand camaraderie, and to his own undefeated will. events.title: Stella Cole
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
With the Del Sol Quartet

A preternaturally gifted artist who broke through to widespread fame through a viral TikTok video of her performance of the Harold Arlen and Yip Harburg classic “Over the Rainbow,” Illinois-born, New York-based vocalist Stella Cole is a wildly acclaimed and self-assured young jazz singer on the rise. For her first appearance on the Miner stage, she presents a soaring holiday-themed program of music with strings, accompanied by the Bay Area’s Del Sol Quartet.

Considering how the public first discovered Cole, it’s only fitting that the now 27-year-old found what would be her lifelong fascination with music while watching Judy Garland in The Wizard of Oz at age three.

While still a student at Northwestern during the COVID pandemic, Cole began posting impromptu videos of her singing, which immediately captured public attention.

Upon arriving in New York, Cole paid her dues before lining up higher profile gigs throughout the city incuding Birdland and Dizzy’s Club, and recording her eponymous 2023 debut album, produced by Matt Pierson (Jane Monheit, Pat Metheny).

Her career since then has been a whirlwind, touring the world as a solo act and with Postmodern Jukebox, and releasing her 2024 holiday EP Snow!, from which this performance will draw. Her latest album is the 2025 Decca session It’s Magic, featuring GRAMMY-winning pianist and arranger Alan Broadbent.

Personnel: Stella Cole (vocals); DEL SOL QUARTET; Benjamin Kreith (violin); Hyeyung Sol Yun (violin); Charlton Lee (viola); Kathryn Bates (cello)

events.title: Charm School with Lara Starr
events.location: Book Passage, Corte Madera Store 51 Tamal Vista Blvd Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: Learn to Make Resin Charms! Join us for this popular workshop where participants learn to make wearable charm keepsakes. What are resin charms? Little metal frames that you can fill with glitter, tiny gems, bits of paper ephemera, beads, leaves, or anything itty bitty! Perfect for capturing special memories from 2026 or making as gifts for loved ones. Instructor Lara Starr will provide all of the tools, supplies, and inspiration to make as many charms as you like during the three-hour workshop. You’re also welcome to bring little bits and bobs that are meaningful to you, such as an earring that has lost its mate, petals or tiny flowers, a ticket stub, a stamp from a special letter, or photo of a loved one. You'll graduate charm school with 5-7 unique mini-collage keepsakes! For ages 12 to adults. Meet Your Instructor Lara Starr is a publicist, cookbook author, former radio producer, Substacker, and semi-pro thrift shopper. A 25-year Marin resident, she’s mentored aspiring authors at Book Passage’s Path to Publishing Program. After making her first resin charm at Maker Faire, she couldn't wait to make more, and has been teaching Charm School workshops at private parties as well as at the Indie Alley, San Anselmo Recreation, and College of Marin Community Education. What students are saying about Lara: "(Lara) was very nice and explained things very well. She had an abundance of items for us to use and take with us. I got to take away quite a few gifts for people and myself. It was taught very coherently and it was an extremely creative outlet." Stephanie H. "(Lara) was warm, helpful and encouraging!" Anon. "This is a fun workshop to take with friends & family. My sister, niece, and I all enjoyed turning summer memories into charms we could keep and also give as gifts." Jen S.

events.description: In New York’s East Village, a group of young artists struggles to build lives, make art, and hold onto each other in the face of uncertainty. Over the course of a single year, friendships are tested, love is complicated, and every moment feels urgent. With an iconic score featuring “Seasons of Love,” “La Vie Bohème,” “Take Me or Leave Me,” and more, Jonathan Larson’s groundbreaking musical captures a generation living under the shadow of HIV/AIDS, where joy and loss exist side by side, and the question is not how long you have, but how you choose to spend it. Winner of the Tony Award for Best Musical and the Pulitzer Prize for Drama, Rent is an electrifying, deeply human story about connection, resilience, and living fully in the present.

events.title: The Queen's Cartoonists
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
Joining the two longstanding American traditions of animation and jazz, the remarkable New York-based ensemble The Queen’s Cartoonists performs the indelible music from animation’s golden age synchronized to screenings of classic cartoons from the 1930s-50s as well as gems from the present day for this family-friendly holiday concert.

Formed in 2015 and led by pianist Joel Pierson, who has collaborated with artists ranging from the New York Philharmonic and the Kronos Quartet to Linkin Park and Ke$ha, TQC boasts a multi-national cast of musicians hailing from Bulgaria, Japan, Australia, and the U.S. The Queens-based sextet recreate the exact soundtracks from the animated shorts that employ compositions from Jazz Age composers Raymond Scott, Carl Stalling, and Duke Ellington as well as opera and classical works by Mozart, Richard Strauss, and Rossini, in performances that blend stunning virtuosity with endless reserves of humor.

With an irreverent stage presence that incorporates hilarious anecdotes about the cartoons and composers along with stream-of-consciousness wit and deft physical comedy, the group breathes fresh life into these beloved shorts from the major animation studios of the early 20th century as well as more modern cult cartoons. Join us for this all-ages holiday experience like no other.

Personnel: Joel Pierson (piano); Drew Pitcher (woodwinds); Mark Phillips (woodwinds); Greg Hammontree (brass); TBA bass; Rossen Nedelchev (drums)

events.title: ROBERT GLASPER
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Jazz pianist bridging musical and artistic genres · Robert Glasper is the leader of a new sonic paradigm with a career that bridges musical and artistic genres. To date, he boasts 5 Grammy wins and 15 nominations across 9 categories, an Emmy Award for his song for Ava Duvernay’s critically hailed documentary “13th” with Common and Karriem Riggins, and a Peabody Award for his Composition of “Mr. Soul!”. His work and accolades bridge all aspects of the music business, from live touring to film scoring, composing and producing. Evolution is his hallmark. Glasper’s breakout crossover album Black Radio changed the face of the genre and set a new expectation for what popular music could be. The album won him the Grammy for Best R&B album and established him as the musician of choice for some of the world’s most iconic artists; notably playing keys throughout Kendrick Lamar's To Pimp A Butterfly, winning another Grammy for the elastic track “These Walls”. The ongoing Black Radio series has since become Glasper’s calling card, upholding a place at the heart of a trailblazing community: from long-time sonic brothers Mos Def and Bilal, to legends including Ledisi, Lupe Fiasco, Kanye West, Jill Scott, and Erykah Badu. Glasper’s eternal pursuit to further his sound has been consistent in challenging and transforming his creative horizons across the board. Whether producing a remix album with Kaytranda or as a bandleader, Robert consistently defies the limits of the genre. This is evident in a portfolio that ranges from his acoustic jazz trio, which simultaneously defies and elevates the traditional idiom by uniting it effortlessly with electronics from visionary DJ Jahi Sundance, to August Greene, a collaboration with Common + Karriem Riggins, to R+R=Now, a supergroup at the crossroads of hip-hop and Jazz. In the past year, Robert Glasper has released three diverse albums under his exclusive deal with Apple Music. The holiday album In December features artists such as Cynthia Erivo and Andra Day, while Let Go offers a calming, soulful experience that helps listeners find their center. Code Derivation merges jazz and hip-hop, with each track presented in two versions—one in jazz, and the other flipped by a producer. The track “Say Less” was flipped by Glasper’s son, Riley. Code Derivation has been nominated for a 2025 Grammy in the Best Alternative Jazz Album category. In addition to his musical accomplishments, Glasper hosted Black Radio Backstage for Tidal League, where he interviewed A-list guests like Affion Crockett, Thundercat, and Lalah Hathaway, alongside co-host Jahi Sundance. The festival he curates in Napa, The Black Radio Experience, celebrated its third year, and his legendary month-long residency at the Blue Note NYC marked its sixth season, featuring star-studded appearances from Dave Chappelle, Questlove, Marsha Ambrosius, and Andra Day, both on and off stage. Prior to a knockout 2024, in 2023 Glasper released Black Radio III and Black Radio III Supreme Edition on Loma Vista Records, with features ranging from Jennifer Hudson, Killer Mike, and the late Mac Miller. On screen, he created the original score for Run The World Season 2 and The Best Man television series. With boundless innovation and elite technique as his signature, it’s no surprise that Glasper has an avalanche of accolades, awards, and achievements to his name. Glasper is an artist at the heart of a moment - and a movement - to champion Black music, Black people, and the possibility of a better future. The hip-hop-head-nod ballad is a dedication to just that: the beauty and brilliance of a heritage that is as much Kendrick as it is Coltrane, and which seeks to empower and uplift with every offering. In his own words: “Black lives matter and so does black love; no one wants a life without love, but we have generations of people in our community who haven’t had the tools to actually be in healthy relationships. It seems like people are finally ready to open their eyes to systemic racism in this country, and if we’re going to talk about it, we have to also talk about how it affects our relationships — how we communicate, how we see ourselves, how we treat each other. It’s not always good, even though maybe it could be.” - Robert Glasper

events.title: Tribute to Eddie Palmieri & La Perfecta
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
To celebrate the legacy of the late pianist and composer Eddie Palmieri during the week that would have marked his 90th birthday, pianist and SFJAZZ Director of Education Rebeca Mauleón leads a truly all-star Latin jazz orchestra with special guest saxophonist David Sánchez as well as members of the San Francisco Conservatory of Music Latin Jazz Ensemble.

A Nuyorican innovator of salsa, Palmieri and his band La Perfecta brought the boogaloo to the Latin jazz sound in the 1960s and infused the modern jazz approach into the music over the course of his monumental career.

Mauleón considers Palmieri her “gateway” to serious Latin music and the Cuban icons that guided her own stellar trajectory. For this night, she honors his pioneering body of work and the major developments of the prime eras of his creative life with an ensemble of the greatest names on the local scene including flutist Chloe Scott Jones, saxophonist Melecio Magdaluyo, and Santana percussionist Karl Perazzo along with SFJAZZ Collective saxophonist Sánchez. An artist discovered by Palmieri while still living in Puerto Rico, Sánchez contributed to the maestro’s GRAMMY-winning 2005 Concord Picante release Listen Here! And his KUVO radio series Calienté! with Eddie Palmieri.

Personnel: Rebeca Mauleón (piano, vocals, music director); Chloe Scott Jones (flute); Melecio Magdaluyo (baritone sax); Mike Olmos (trumpet); Jeff Cressman (trombone); Obrayan Calderón (trombone); Ernesto Mazar-Kindelán (bass); Karl Perazzo (percussion & vocals); Jesús Diaz (percussion & vocals); Christian Pepín (percussion & vocals); Christelle Durandy (vocals); SPECIAL GUESTS; David Sánchez (tenor saxophone); Members of the San Francisco Conservatory of Music Latin Jazz Ensemble

events.title: Cyrus Chestnut plays 'A Charlie Brown Christmas'
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
“The best pianist of his generation” (Time Magazine), Cyrus Chestnut has established a career as a peerless soloist and torchbearer of the classic piano trio setting. He brings back a favorite of the holiday season, performing Bay Area jazz luminary Vince Guaraldi’s music from the beloved 1965 Charles Schultz animated classic A Charlie Brown Christmas.

A standout since his student days at Berklee, Chestnut spent formative years accompanying vocalese legend Jon Hendricks, anchoring the quintessential young lion quintet of Terence Blanchard and Donald Harrison, and touring with Wynton Marsalis. But he credits his early 1990s stint in vocal explorer Betty Carter’s band with radically expanding creative vision, appearing on her landmark 1992 late career Verve release It’s Not About the Melody. Since then, the pianist has racked up dozens of recording credits with jazz’s greatest names and 35 albums as a leader.

Chestnut’s performances of Guaraldi’s timeless score to the holiday classic appeared on his all-star 2000 Atlantic Records album Charlie Brown Christmas with the Boys Choir of Harlem and guests including the late Michael Brecker. For this date, Chestnut is joined by a terrific ensemble to help make your spirits bright.

Personnel: Cyrus Chestnut (piano); Others TBA

events.title: Norman Fischer - The Great Road
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: From beloved Zen teacher and poet Norman Fischer, a new collection of wise and surprising essays that explores what it means to dive fully into spiritual practice and to embody our deepest aspirations in every waking moment. In The Great Road , acclaimed Zen teacher and writer Norman Fischer explores what it means to make everyday life itself a spiritual practice. Inspired by the teachings of legendary Japanese Zen master Eihei Dogen, this wide-ranging collection of essays examines the philosophy of “continuous practice”—the idea that awakening is not separate from ordinary living, but discovered within it. Weaving Buddhist thought with literature, Western philosophy, and deeply personal reflection, Fischer brings Dogen’s teachings into conversation with figures such as Simone Weil and William Wordsworth, while drawing on his own decades among America’s most influential Zen practitioners. The result is a work that moves fluidly between the spiritual, philosophical, and literary, inviting readers into a richer understanding of attention, compassion, and human experience. At once intellectually expansive and deeply intimate, The Great Road offers a timely meditation on how to live with greater presence and meaning in a distracted world— revealing the extraordinary possibilities contained within ordinary life. “A true delight! Norman Fischer has long been one of the best interpreters of Zen Buddhism for the modern world. By illuminating the everyday relevance of Zen's most far-reaching teachings, Fischer gives us a book that is simultaneously thought-provoking, inspiring, and deeply hopeful.” —Adam Frank, author of Light of the Stars: Aliens Worlds and the Fate of the Earth “Repetition is central in Zen practice, offering us an opportunity to see with fresh eyes. That’s the relationship you will want with this book, returning to it again and again for new insights. Norman has given us a deep and accessible book. He invites us into continuous practice and the miracle of presence in everyday life.” —Frank Ostaseski, author of The Five Invitations: Discovering What Death Can Teach Us About Living Fully “The Great Road winds around a single question: what is our human life, really, and what are we supposed to do about it? ... Continuous practice is not particular to Dogen or to Zen. It is the form of any serious human life. As Fischer teaches us, continuous practice means closing the gap between one's deepest aspirations and one's ordinary speaking, thinking, and acting.” —Bonnie Nadzam, author of The Magpie Spoke to Me: How the Stories We Tell Shape Our World NORMAN FISCHER is a Zen teacher, poet, translator, and director of the Everyday Zen Foundation. A beloved figure in the Buddhist world, he is also well-known for his efforts at interreligious dialogue. His numerous books include The World Could Be Otherwise: Imagination and the Bodhisattva Path, What Is Zen?: Plain Talk for a Beginner’s Mind, and Training in Compassion: Zen Teachings on the Practice of Lojong. Event details: This event will be hosted by Book Passage at our Corte Madera store. Free Admission / Open Seating Following the presentation, there will be a signing line or a meet-and-greet. For any questions regarding our events, please contact us at books@bookpassage.com .

events.title: Christmas with the Count Basie Orchestra
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
Every performance by the Count Basie Orchestra is a jazz holiday celebrating a 90-year legacy so bountiful that a month-long residency could only scratch the surface. But a Christmas concert with the Basie Band takes the party to another level, delivering a Santa’s sled full of swing with a program of seasonal standards over an evening show and Sunday matinee.

Under the direction of trumpeter Scotty Barnhart since 2013, the orchestra staked a claim to the North Pole with 2015’s chart-topping A Very Swingin’ Basie Christmas!, the first Xmas album ever recorded by the Basie organization. The project featured special guests Ledisi, Johnny Mathis, Ellis Marsalis, and Carmen Bradford, the ebullient jazz and blues singer who continues to tour with the band. The orchestra followed up that celebratory project with a series of excellent albums, scoring GRAMMY Award nominations for 2018’s All About That Basie (with special guests Stevie Wonder, Jon Faddis, and Take 6) and 2022’s Live At Birdland, while winning a GRAMMY with 2023’s Basie Swings the Blues. For swing-loving jazz fans, there’s no better gift than a night with the Basie Orchestra.

The orchestra followed up that celebratory project with a series of excellent albums, scoring GRAMMY Award nominations for 2018’s All About That Basie (with special guests Stevie Wonder, Jon Faddis, and Take 6) and 2022’s Live At Birdland, while winning a GRAMMY with 2023’s Basie Swings the Blues. For swing-loving jazz fans, there’s no better gift than a night with the Basie Orchestra.

events.title: ROBERT GLASPER
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Jazz pianist bridging musical and artistic genres · Robert Glasper is the leader of a new sonic paradigm with a career that bridges musical and artistic genres. To date, he boasts 5 Grammy wins and 15 nominations across 9 categories, an Emmy Award for his song for Ava Duvernay’s critically hailed documentary “13th” with Common and Karriem Riggins, and a Peabody Award for his Composition of “Mr. Soul!”. His work and accolades bridge all aspects of the music business, from live touring to film scoring, composing and producing. Evolution is his hallmark. Glasper’s breakout crossover album Black Radio changed the face of the genre and set a new expectation for what popular music could be. The album won him the Grammy for Best R&B album and established him as the musician of choice for some of the world’s most iconic artists; notably playing keys throughout Kendrick Lamar's To Pimp A Butterfly, winning another Grammy for the elastic track “These Walls”. The ongoing Black Radio series has since become Glasper’s calling card, upholding a place at the heart of a trailblazing community: from long-time sonic brothers Mos Def and Bilal, to legends including Ledisi, Lupe Fiasco, Kanye West, Jill Scott, and Erykah Badu. Glasper’s eternal pursuit to further his sound has been consistent in challenging and transforming his creative horizons across the board. Whether producing a remix album with Kaytranda or as a bandleader, Robert consistently defies the limits of the genre. This is evident in a portfolio that ranges from his acoustic jazz trio, which simultaneously defies and elevates the traditional idiom by uniting it effortlessly with electronics from visionary DJ Jahi Sundance, to August Greene, a collaboration with Common + Karriem Riggins, to R+R=Now, a supergroup at the crossroads of hip-hop and Jazz. In the past year, Robert Glasper has released three diverse albums under his exclusive deal with Apple Music. The holiday album In December features artists such as Cynthia Erivo and Andra Day, while Let Go offers a calming, soulful experience that helps listeners find their center. Code Derivation merges jazz and hip-hop, with each track presented in two versions—one in jazz, and the other flipped by a producer. The track “Say Less” was flipped by Glasper’s son, Riley. Code Derivation has been nominated for a 2025 Grammy in the Best Alternative Jazz Album category. In addition to his musical accomplishments, Glasper hosted Black Radio Backstage for Tidal League, where he interviewed A-list guests like Affion Crockett, Thundercat, and Lalah Hathaway, alongside co-host Jahi Sundance. The festival he curates in Napa, The Black Radio Experience, celebrated its third year, and his legendary month-long residency at the Blue Note NYC marked its sixth season, featuring star-studded appearances from Dave Chappelle, Questlove, Marsha Ambrosius, and Andra Day, both on and off stage. Prior to a knockout 2024, in 2023 Glasper released Black Radio III and Black Radio III Supreme Edition on Loma Vista Records, with features ranging from Jennifer Hudson, Killer Mike, and the late Mac Miller. On screen, he created the original score for Run The World Season 2 and The Best Man television series. With boundless innovation and elite technique as his signature, it’s no surprise that Glasper has an avalanche of accolades, awards, and achievements to his name. Glasper is an artist at the heart of a moment - and a movement - to champion Black music, Black people, and the possibility of a better future. The hip-hop-head-nod ballad is a dedication to just that: the beauty and brilliance of a heritage that is as much Kendrick as it is Coltrane, and which seeks to empower and uplift with every offering. In his own words: “Black lives matter and so does black love; no one wants a life without love, but we have generations of people in our community who haven’t had the tools to actually be in healthy relationships. It seems like people are finally ready to open their eyes to systemic racism in this country, and if we’re going to talk about it, we have to also talk about how it affects our relationships — how we communicate, how we see ourselves, how we treat each other. It’s not always good, even though maybe it could be.” - Robert Glasper

events.title: MINDI ABAIR CHRISTMAS SHOW
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Be swept up in the joy of the season · PRE-SHOW WINE TASTING + MUSIC EXPERIENCE AVAILABLE HERE (SHOW TICKETS NOT INCLUDED) JOIN MINDI ABAIR AND FRIENDS FOR A MAGICAL NIGHT OF CHRISTMAS CLASSICS AND SMOOTH JAZZ HITS Mindi Abair’s I Can’t Wait For Christmas Tour is bringing the spirit of the holidays to audiences across the U.S. for an exciting, heartfelt season of music—now in its third year hosted by Mindi Abair. Joined by five exciting solo artists, expect Christmas classics you love, fresh original songs, and of course those moments that will make you laugh, tear up, and leave with your heart full of the Christmas spirit. Come early for the pre-show Wine and Jazz Tasting experience hosted by Mindi Abair and her husband Eric Guerra. Pouring their company’s www.WINEandJAZZ.com fine wines, Eric will walk the group through an informative wine-by-wine “taste like a sommelier” master class, while Mindi then pairs each wine style with a live performance song. During her remarkable 26-year recording career, Mindi Abair has garnered 2 GRAMMY nominations, recorded with some of the biggest names in music, and built a devoted following among jazz and blues audiences with her soaring melodies and powerhouse style. As co-founder of WineandJazz.com, she brings people around the world on intimate Wine & Jazz Adventures and hosts her annual Wine & Jazz New Year’s Eve in San Diego, CA. Rebecca Jade will move you. Named Smooth Jazz Network’s “Breakout Artist of the Year” and JazzTrax “Debut Artist of the Year” in 2022, she brings that rare mix of polish and raw emotion. She has toured extensively with Sheila E, shared the stage with Sir Elton John at the Academy Awards, and has been a regular featured artist on Dave Koz & Friends at Sea. She’s performed at Mindi Abair’s Wine & Jazz New Year’s Eve and Wine & Jazz Adventure in Sonoma, so the musical chemistry is already baked in. Andréa Lisa , the South African-born, New Zealand-raised singer, guitarist, composer, and producer, is a musical powerhouse – think the heart of Alicia Keys with the guitar sensibility of John Mayer. Her collaborations include Jonathan Butler, Kirk Whalum, and Kool & The Gang. She’s the artist who can melt a room with one lyric… then light it up with one solo. Xavier Gordon arrives as an exciting new voice on the jazz scene — pianist, songwriter, producer, and performer with a feel-good sound that hits hard live. He earned a GRAMMY nomination in 2018 for his production work and has toured extensively with Marcus Miller. Arthur Thompson , Mindi’s long-time drummer, is the heartbeat behind the music — a visionary artist with purpose as a drummer, vocalist, producer, author, and educator. He was voted 2023 “Breakout Artist of the Year” by the Smooth Jazz Network. And Darryl Williams brings smooth-jazz firepower. His debut album That Was Then earned praise from JazzTimes and national airplay on SiriusXM. He’s shared stages with heavy hitters like Dave Koz, Peter White, Gerald Albright, Jonathan Butler, and of course, Mindi Abair. This isn’t just another holiday show — it’s a night that will leave you energized, moved, and truly in tune with the joy of the season. Whether you come for the songs, the shared moments, or just to be swept up in the joy of the season, this night promises to stay with you long after the last note. For more info, visit mindiabair.com.

events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
with special guest

For more than a decade, GRAMMY Award-winning trumpeter Maurice "Mobetta" Brown has returned every winter to his hometown Chicago for his MOBETTA Holiday Jam. Now the charismatic horn player, rapper and producer is giving the rest of us a taste of an uproarious Mobetta holiday celebration.

With a sound that seamlessly encompasses jazz, hip-hop, funk, soul, and R&B, Brown was shaped by his long pre-Katrina residency in New Orleans, where he fully assimilated the Crescent City concept of social music. After the hurricane he ended up in New York City, where he’s thrived as a creative force, collaborating with Aretha Franklin, Lettuce, Santana, Tedeschi Trucks Band, Anderson .Paak & The Free Nationals, Harry Styles, Bruno Mars, and The Roots, among many others.

His horn arrangements and production work have appeared on GRAMMY-winning albums, Netflix documentaries, and Broadway, where he debuted alongside Dave Chappelle and Thundercat. Building on the irrepressible soul of his 2025 album Betta Days, Mobetta celebrates the season by weaving improvisation, storytelling, and groove into music that speaks to freedom, love, and transformation.

events.description: Step into the Spirit—Where Christmas Meets God's Promise · Back by overwhelming demand, Nzuri Soul returns to Yoshi's Oakland with the fourth installment of her beloved holiday tradition, Christmas in Egypt IV – The Gift. After selling out year after year, this unforgettable production has become one of the Bay Area's most anticipated Christmas concerts. More than a concert, The Gift is an extraordinary musical experience that reimagines the Christmas story through the beauty, mystery, and majesty of Egypt—the place where the Holy Family found refuge. Through breathtaking vocals, powerful storytelling, and soul-stirring music, Nzuri Soul invites audiences on a journey of faith, hope, and celebration. Whether you're experiencing Christmas in Egypt for the first time or returning to continue the tradition, prepare for an evening that will inspire your heart, lift your spirit, and leave you filled with the joy of the season. Presented by Nzuri Soul About Nzuri Soul Award-winning vocalist, songwriter, producer, and entertainer Nzuri Soul has become one of the Bay Area's premier live performers, captivating audiences with her powerful voice, heartfelt storytelling, and unforgettable stage presence. Born in Texas and raised in Oakland, California, Nzuri Soul effortlessly blends R&B, Soul, Gospel, Jazz, and Funk into a signature sound that is both timeless and refreshingly original. events.title: Marcus Shelby New Orchestra
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
Plays Duke Ellington’s Nutcracker Suite featuring Tiffany Austin

It’s a short walk from the SFJAZZ Center to the War Memorial Opera House, which is where the evening-length ballet The Nutcracker made its North America premiere in the winter of 1944. An immediate sensation, the production unleashed an army of Nutcrackers large and small that march across the country come the holidays, turning Tchaikovsky’s spirited score into an enchanting soundtrack for the season.

In 1960, at the urging of Billy Strayhorn, the Duke Ellington Orchestra recorded The Nutcracker Suite (Columbia), a brilliant jazz interpretation of Tchaikovsky’s music. While largely forgotten today, the popular album marked a watershed in one of American music’s most consequent and productive partnerships, as Ellington gave Strayhorn equal billing for the first time on the album’s cover.

For bassist, composer, and arranger Marcus Shelby, Ellington and Strayhorn’s Nutcracker Suite arrangements offer an ideal vehicle for his talent-laden New Orchestra, an ensemble he modeled after Ellington’s. Reveling in Tchaikovsky’s enduring melodies, Shelby’s band with guest vocalist Tiffany Austin breathes new life into a singular cultural fusion that gracefully marries the great Russian composer with the orchestral language of two nonpareil jazz innovators, and in addition, features original arrangements of holiday music and black spirituals.

Website Instagram YouTube   about Lavay Smith and Her Red Hot Skillet Lickers The band scales from eight pieces to sixteen when the room allows, and Miss Smith to You! followed on Fat Note in 2009. Smith is the fourth of five children of a jazz obsessed father, which is how a kid in Long Beach ended up knowing Bessie Smith and Fats Waller records by heart before she knew what to do with them. events.title: BONEY JAMES LIVE
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Celebrating NYE and his NEW album "Simple Man" · Boney James — A Simple Man Three decades into a career built on deep groove, melodic instinct and a saxophone voice unmistakably his own, Boney James is still finding new ground. On A Simple Man , his milestone 20th studio album, out October 2 via Concord Records, the multi-platinum saxophonist, composer and producer delivers one of his most personal records. James’ catalog has generated more than two billion on-demand streams in the United States. His honors include four GRAMMY nominations, three NAACP Image Award nominations, four RIAA Gold-certified records and a Soul Train Award. Billboard named him one of the Top 3 Contemporary Jazz Artists of the 2000s, and in 2024 he became the first artist to score 20 No. 1 singles on the Billboard Smooth Jazz chart. Recent collaborations have also earned him two Top 10 hits at Adult R&B. For James, A Simple Man reflects a growing desire to strip away distraction and focus on what matters most. “As I’ve gotten older, I’ve realized I don’t need a lot to make me happy,” he says. “I love making music and playing my saxophone.” That clarity runs through the new album. GRAMMY-winning vocalist Ledisi joins him on the warm contemporary R&B duet “I Belong To You,” while acclaimed trumpeter Marquis Hill appears on “Morocco” and legendary guitarist Larry Carlton guests on the Steely Dan-influenced “Storybook.” James also reimagines Ellington’s “In a Sentimental Mood” over a D’Angelo-inspired groove. James’ R&B foundation runs deep. He turned professional at 19 and spent his formative years touring with Morris Day, The Isley Brothers, Teena Marie and others before stepping forward with his 1992 debut, Trust . More than three decades later, he remains focused not on preserving a legacy, but on continuing to grow. On A Simple Man, James’s playing is warmer, deeper, and stronger than ever — and, 20 albums in, he is still making progress. And that may be the clearest expression of A Simple Man : an artist who, after more than three decades, knows more clearly than ever what matters.

events.title: Cimafunk
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
What better way to welcome the new year than with a blast of Cuban funk, courtesy of the man who invented the genre? Over the past decade, Cimafunk has forged a deeply soulful sound combining funk and hip-hop with rhythms from his native Cuba and other Afro-Caribbean traditions. Living in New Orleans since 2022, the dynamic vocalist dubbed his style “Afro-Cuban funk,” but that convenient label only hints at his breadth. Born in the eastern provincial capital of Pinar del Río, Erik Alejandro Iglesias Rodríguez took the first half of his stage moniker from the cimarróns, escaped slaves who lived in self-sustaining communities in colonial Cuba.

He often says that his music is about freedom, and he’s fully embraced an unfettered ethos collaborating with musicians from far and wide. Whether he’s working with Cuban legends Chucho Valdés, Gonzalo Rubalcaba, and Omaru Portuando, British-Jamaican dancehall star Stylo G or the Mothership captain George Clinton himself, Cimafunk has found the universal key to unleashing bodies on the dance floor.

Joined by his hard working band La Tribu, he’s recorded a series of celebrated albums, including his latest, the 2025 GRAMMY-nominated Pa' Tu Cuerpa. Returning after his showstopping performance at the 42nd San Francisco Jazz Festival in 2025, Cimafunk kicks off 2027 in spectacular style.

events.title: Avotcja & Modúpue: afro-latin jazz and poetry
events.location: Bird & Beckett Books & Records, 653 Chenery Street, San Francisco
events.description: AVOTCJA’s poetry is music and Avotcja’s music is poetry. Both are as hot as fire and as soothing as snow flakes. And in both she brings the best of her talent in Spanish and English. Listen to her. Read her. Enjoy her. Celebrate her.” • Camincha – Peruvian Poet/Novelist; & Pacifica Poet Laureate, 2017-2021. Poet / Playwright / Essayist / Fiction Writer / Multi-Percussionist / Photographer / Teacher, Avotcja is a Bay Area icon and is renowned for her group Modúpue. At Bird & Beckett tonight, Modúpue will be a quintet with Avotcja joined by violinist Sandi Poindexter , saxophonist Francis Wong , bassist Heshima Mark Williams and talking drum master Baba Ken Okolulo . Modúpue was named best jazz group of the year twice, in 2005 and again in 2010, by the Bay Area Blues Hall of Fame. Avotcja herself was named a “Jazz Hero” by the Jazz Journalists Association. Her radio shows on KPFA – Bebop, Cubop & the Musical Truth (Tuesdays, 8-10pm), and KPOO – La Verdad Musical (Fridays, noon-3pm), have been soul satisfying for decades, expressing the boundless joy she always finds in the music. As for her poetry, no one taps deeper wells of humanity than Avotcja! We love her more than we can express. Read here what Linda Tillery, Chuy Varela, Camincha, Greg Landau, Leslie Simon, Ishmael Reed, Lady Bianca, Elaine Cohen, Julian Carroll and Melanie Berzon have had to say in praise of Avotcja! The cover charge for the quintet tonight is $25 cash or venmo, payable at the door. College and high school students – $10. Grade school and younger, free. No one turned away for lack of funds. Wheelchair accessible. Bring your own beverages, but please eat out or at home before or after the show. Lots of good restaurants in the neighborhood, cafes, and grocers!

events.title: The Best Journey in the World: An Antarctic Story with Kim Stanley Robinson
events.location: Grace Cathedral, 1100 California St, San Francisco
events.description: FREE, $10-$15 suggested donation, $49 with signed book Co-presented with Grace Cathedral’s The Forum Interweaving memoir and good old fashioned ice adventure, Kim Stanley Robinson’s latest takes readers along on the journeys that have happened before and those that may never happen again. In May of 1911, Robert Scott and his men said goodbye to the sun and settled in for the long Antarctic winter. When the sun returned in September, they would try to become the first people to reach the South Pole. However, a week past the winter solstice, Scott’s second-in-command decided to take an impromptu sled trip. Chronicled by zoological assistant Apsley Cherry-Garrard, this side trip became The Worst Journey in the World, one of the best adventure books ever written. Robinson first read Cherry-Garrard’s book in his twenties and re-read it again in 1995, as preparation for a research trip to Antarctica for his Mars novels. It was a dream excursion: he traveled around the continent, by snowmobile and helicopter and airplane, and followed in their ill-fated footsteps. Doors at 7:00 PM.

events.title: Chris Botti
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
With his finely etched features and piercing green eyes, trumpeter Chris Botti combines matinee idol looks with the simmering lyricism of an expert balladeer” (The Mercury News).

A trumpeter with a sumptuous, enveloping tone, fluent phrasing, and sense of space, Botti became a masterly musician equally at home in the realms of jazz and pop. He honed his craft performing and recording with stars like Frank Sinatra, Buddy Rich, Paul Simon, Joni Mitchell, and Sting, who featured him on his Brand New Day tour and who was one the stellar artists on Botti’s chart-topping 2009 album Live in Boston.

Botti’s 2012 CD Impressions won the GRAMMY for Best Pop Instrumental Album, and he made his Blue Note Records debut in 2023 with Vol. 1, his first new recording in over a decade.

Stepping back from the lush orchestral arrangements of his recent work, Botti returns to an intimate, small group dynamic on the album, focusing on classic standards like “Old Folks,” “Blue in Green,” “Bewitched, Bothered, and Bewildered,” and “Someday My Prince Will Come,” among others. Produced by 16-time GRAMMY-winner David Foster, Vol. 1 features performances by violinist Joshua Bell, pianist Taylor Eigsti, guitarist Gilad Hekselman, and drummer Vinnie Colaiuta.

Botti’s SFJAZZ shows have become a New Years tradition and always sell out in advance.

Personnel: Chris Botti (trumpet); Others TBA

events.title: Song Circle with Amateur Music Network
events.location: Berkeley
events.description: October Theme: “Broadway and Show Tunes” There’s nothing that brings people together better than singing our favorite songs. It recalls summer nights around the campfire: someone strumming the guitar and all singing a mix of folk music, familiar songs we heard on the radio, and occasional new songs that someone shares. Nobody has to worry about whether you know the songs or can sing like a pro. This is our chance to share the joy of singing simply for the fun of it. Cary Sheldon is a singer, songwriter, and beloved Berkeley voice teacher with 30 years worth of grateful students. She has been playing and teaching in the Bay Area for the last 40 years. Her love for R & B music led her to be part of Zazu Pitts Memorial Orchestra in the 1980’s. Other affiliations include The Henry Kaiser Band, The Henriettas (a recreation of DeZurick sisters, a popular country music duo from the 1940’s), who appeared on Prairie Home Companion, and most recently her band DanceChant, a joyful community-inspired R&B band that encourages audience participation. She continues to be inspired by her love of singing in community. “Singing together with others is one of the greatest joys in my life.” Now in her 60’s, she returns to influences from her early life. Her grade school music teachers included John Langstaff, creator of the Christmas Revels, and the repertoire was based on the American folk tradition, including old English ballads, spirituals, freedom songs, and the popular folk and protest songs of the 1960’s. She hopes to inspire others to explore the depth of this material and rediscover the joy of community singing. Soprano Candace Johnson has led AMN’s Juneteenth Choral Celebration since its inception in 2020. The AMN community knows her through her commitment to the power of the Negro Spirituals tradition, but Candace has a deep connection to theater and to the music of the Broadway stage. A voice instructor at UC Berkeley for 17 years, in 2022 Candace also became the director of the University Gospel Choir. A lyric coloratura soprano, she crosses musical boundaries performing classical, jazz, musical theater, pop and gospel. She has sung on many stages, including Carnegie Hall and The Manhattan Center. Also a playwright and actress, Candace premiered her first one-woman show, Vox in a Box , in UC Berkeley’s Hertz Hall in 2018, which led to her becoming a resident solo artist at The Marsh theater (Berkeley/San Francisco). Candace has written and performed 5 full-length one-woman musicals. Her most recent show, Scat-ter Brain: The Music of ADHD , was commissioned by The Marsh in 2024 for its inaugural IFOYE festival of new works by women-identifying playwrights. Following an extended run, Scat-ter Brain was nominated by Broadway World SF for Best Solo Show of 2025. Please read our Health, Safety and COVID-19 Information Our commitment to our patrons

events.description: (Please do not bring infants to the show) Barbara has to clean out her oddball uncle’s house. He’s dead. Does she find his porn stash? Of course. Is that the strangest thing in there? Not by a long shot. Barbara explores family secrets from an unusual perspective. It’s about what happens when someone becomes the in-case-of-emergency person for the elephant in the family room. My Dead Uncle’s Porn Collection is about confronting the damage done by a dysfunctional family and coming through it with grace and humor. Yes, humor! So many aspects of the story are just ludicrous. You can’t make this stuff up! Following a career in business communication, Barbara discovered solo performance (like so many others) in David Ford’s class. What started as an attempt to blow off steam turned into two solo shows, (so far). She is a frequent performer at The Marsh and other Bay Area performance venue and has performed at The Marsh’s In Front of Your Eyes Festival, The PlayGround Free-Play Festival, The Binge Fringe Festival at Santa Monica Playhouse, Orlando International Theater Festival, Cincinnati Fringe, Tampa Fringe, Ooley Theater Women’s Wit & Wisdom Festival, Rogue Festival, Soaring Solos Stars Series and elsewhere, to laudatory reviews. events.title: ANA POPOVIC
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: One of the most dynamic forces in contemporary blues · Grace. Power. Drive. Meet the Queen of the Pack Some guitar players play the blues. Ana Popovic sets it on fire. An award-winning guitarist, singer, songwriter, and bandleader, Ana Popovic is a force of nature onstage. Blending smoking electric funk, fiery slide guitar, soulful vocals, jazz-infused instrumentals, and deep blues grooves, she has created a sound that is unmistakably her own. For more than 25 years, Popovic has relentlessly toured the world, continually pushing the boundaries of contemporary blues. Her music never stands still. She bends genres, challenges expectations, and reinvents herself with every record, while remaining deeply connected to the power, emotion, and freedom of the guitar. A ten-time Blues Music Award nominee, Popovic was the only female guitarist selected for the 2014-2018 Experience Hendrix all-star lineup, sharing the stage with legendary artists including Buddy Guy, Eric Johnson, and Kenny Wayne Shepherd. She has appeared on the covers of Vintage Guitar and Guitar Player and has shared headlining stages with B.B. King, Joe Bonamassa, Gary Clark Jr., Robben Ford, Keb' Mo', and many other major artists. Bruce Springsteen summed up her musicianship simply: "One helluva guitar player." Popovic's recordings have earned widespread critical and commercial recognition. Can You Stand the Heat and Unconditional were named Pick of the Week by USA Today and featured by NPR Music. Her album POWER reached #1 on the Billboard Blues Albums chart, marking another major milestone in her career. Albums including Like It On Top, Trilogy, Can You Stand the Heat, Unconditional, and Dance to the Rhythm have all appeared among Billboard's best-selling blues albums. Her international profile has also been reflected in numerous magazine covers, including Vintage Guitar (US), Guitar Player Gear Guide (US), Blues Music Magazine (US), Blues Magazine (France), American Blues Scene (US), and Blues Matters! (UK), among many others. POWER & FANTASTAFUNK POWER is a record about unity, friendship, resilience, and the strength we find in one another. Its striking cover-two hands, one black and one white, holding on to each other-captures the album's central message: connection and collective strength have the power to move the world forward. Recorded during one of the most challenging periods of Ana's life, POWER became a deeply personal expression of survival and a renewed faith in the transformative power of music. That same spirit inspired Popovic's FANTASTAFUNK, an explosive 11-piece big band launched in 2023. Bringing together funk, gospel, soul, and blues, FANTASTAFUNK expands her guitar-driven sound into a full-scale, high-energy live experience designed for major festival stages. DANCE TO THE RHYTHM In 2025, Popovic released DANCE TO THE RHYTHM, a vibrant celebration of perseverance, joy, gratitude, and a renewed love of life. Created with longtime collaborator Buthel, the ten-track album blends funk, soul, blues, and gospel into what Popovic calls her "ever-evolving gumbo of sound." Tracks such as "Dance to the Rhythm" and "Sho Nuff" push the electric guitar into infectious, dance-driven grooves, while songs including "Dwell on the Feeling" and "Sisters and Brothers" explore inclusiveness, resilience, faith, love, and the powerful connection between artist and audience. As Popovic puts it: "POWER was about survival. DANCE is about celebrating life-a second chance." Popovic writes for the stage-and that is where her music truly comes alive. Whether leading her powerful band or the FANTASTAFUNK big band, she delivers performances that are soulful, fearless, dynamic, and impossible to sit still through. Ana Popovic isn't just playing the blues. She's pushing it forward. She remains one of the most dynamic forces in the contemporary blues and beyond. Endlessly curious, fiercely committed, and always evolving, Ana Popovic is not simply carrying the blues into the future-she is helping redefine what the genre can become. When she's not on the road, Popovic divides her time between Los Angeles, California, and Detroit, Michigan. She is endorsed by Fender, D'Addario, Jim Dunlop, and DR Strings. 'Plainly and simply - the album is damn good. Selections such as "Worked Up.* "California Chase.* "Hurt So Good," and "Dwell On the Feeling" shine as a medium between the artist's Blues. Funk. and Soul meeting place, where her skills as a guitar virtuoso and her soul-nature converge naturally and brilliantly. "Highly recommended* is an understatement. GOLDMINE MAG (USA) ' Dance To The Rhythm' sees Ana Popovic at the top of her game; all the songs are fabulous, yet diverse. A lot of thought and passion has gone into this. An album that you will be going back to again and again. POWERPLAY MAG (UK)
