events.title: Kurt Rosenwinkel & Gerald Clayton
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
Two instrumentalists at the pinnacle of modern jazz meet for this inspired evening of duets.

“A jazz guitarist of glowing lyricism and graceful exposition” (NY Times), Kurt Rosenwinkel has staked out a singular position in jazz’s firmament as a player, composer and bandleader with a vast and supremely sophisticated harmonic vision and melodic sensibility. He made memorable contributions as part of Gary Burton’s star-making quartet as well as legendary drummer Paul Motian’s Electric Bebop Band and fellow rhythm master Brian Blade’s Fellowship Band, and has released a series of acclaimed albums including his 2001 Verve breakthrough The Next Step and his most recent sessions on his own Heartcore imprint.

Possessing an exquisite touch, astonishing technique, and a sound that somehow combines the dynamic finesse of Ahmad Jamal with the hurtling swing of Oscar Peterson, six-time GRAMMY nominee Gerald Clayton ranks among the very best pianists of his generation. Son of iconic bassist John Clayton, he’s recorded five highly regarded albums, and collaborated with artists including Roy Hargrove, Charles Lloyd, Diana Krall, Ambrose Akinmusire, and Terri Lyne Carrington. His third album for Blue Note, Ones & Twos, represents an innovative approach to acoustic jazz inspired by DJ culture.

Most recently, the pair have performed together to present material from Rosenwinkel’s 2023 duo album A Lovesome Thing.

Personnel: Kurt Rosenwinkel (guitar); Gerald Clayton (piano)

events.title: Emmaline: Sinatra, My Sweetheart
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
“A singer and songwriter possessing a smoky, jazz-infused, genre-fluid voice” (Broadway World), Emmaline returns for her Miner Auditorium debut with an evening dedicated to the music associated with Ol’ Blue Eyes, Frank Sinatra.

The Cincinnati native possesses a powerful, mellifluous voice and masterful skill on violin matched to a decidedly retro aesthetic and a beguiling gift for composition. She has received coverage in Rolling Stone and American Songwriter, opened for the legendary Chaka Khan, collaborated with funk icon Bootsy Collins, and headlined clubs all over the U.S.

The daughter of jazz pianist Russ Campbell and singer Julie Campbell, Emmaline was exposed to the work of Ella Fitzgerald, Sarah Vaughan, and Anita O’Day from childhood, and though her love of old movies and vintage fashion has informed her personal style, she is a true artist for the 21st century, accumulating over a half-million followers on social media for her homemade videos showcasing her songs.

Now based in Chicago, Emmaline has released a series of assured EPs and singles that blend the jazz tradition with soul, pop, and R&B. For this night, she embraces the timeless Sinatra songbook with the style and panache that has made her a sensation.

Personnel: Emmaline (vocals); Others TBA

events.title: Jeremy Pelt All-Star Quintet / Charles Altura
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
Terence Blanchard’s first UpSwing concert of 2027 is focused on a pair of California natives.

Bay Area-born guitarist Charles Altura is renowned for his work with Chick Corea, Stanley Clarke, Ambrose Akinmusire, Dayna Stephens, Thundercat, and Terence’s own E-Collective, with whom he has performed on the Miner stage. A two-time GRAMMY nominee for his work with Blanchard, Altura is among the most in-demand guitarists on the scene, balancing fiery fretboard acuity with a soulful, burnished tone. Beyond his work as a sideman, Altura leads several groups on the New York club circuit, including his new quintet with Ravi Coltrane and Milena Casado, and the Heart + Mind Quartet featuring a revolving cast of greats including SFJAZZ Collective members Matt Brewer and Kendrick Scott.

Trumpet great Jeremy Pelt is a veteran of 25 albums as a leader and work with Vincent Herring, Ralph Peterson Jr., Wayne Shorter, and the Mingus Big Band, with whom he established his career. The Los Angeles native was recognized as a rising master during his time at Boston’s Berklee College of Music and has recorded a remarkable series of releases since his 2002 debut. His newest HighNote album, Our Community Will Not Be Erased, is an embrace of the positive contributions of his neighborhood and community, featuring a powerful set of originals and a veteran band including pianist Orrin Evans, bassist Buster Williams, and drummer Lenny White.

events.title: Phoebe Thompson - Girls Our Age
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: Join us at Book Passage for an author event in celebration of Phoebe Thompson and her debut novel, Girls Our Age. Three women navigate their late twenties together in a bittersweet novel about female friendship, identity, and growing up—from the hope and promise of college to the realities that lie beyond. Lily, Ana, and Margot have been best friends ever since Hawthorne Res Life assigned them as roommates during their first year of college. Ten years later and Lily is planning her wedding to the endlessly supportive and entirely symmetrical Jack. Ana is a fourth-grade teacher at the prestigious Horizon Academy, alma mater of her long-term boyfriend, who’s finally asked her to move in. Margot is about to land a life-changing promotion at ad agency McQueen O’Doul. It all looks good from here. But when the three friends converge on Maine for the wedding, the real challenges they’ve been able to keep from each other begin to surface. It’s finally time to open up about the very private struggles they’ve hidden for too long and the risks they’ve taken to protect themselves, and those they love, from the truth. “Nostalgic, aching, and sharply observed, Girls Our Age is a story about the friendships that shape us, the lives we think everyone else is living, and the quiet heartbreak of realizing we only ever see the polished version. With tender precision, Phoebe Thompson reminds us that girlhood never really leaves us and that the people who knew us then often know us best now.” —Alissa DeRogatis, author of Call It What You Want “Girls Our Age is full of heart, tenderness, and characters who are so lifelike they might as well be my own friend group, with all the struggles, doubts, and aches of twentysomething adulthood. Thompson’s empathetic and riveting debut pulls on the heartstrings, will make you text your friends just to tell them how much you love them, and announces an exciting new voice in fiction.” —Isabel Banta, author of Honey “I see myself and my closest friends in the characters of Girls Our Age, an honest and gripping coming-of-age story about the ways that friendships bend and waver in your twenties, only to grow back stronger. I devoured this book, and I didn’t want to say goodbye to Lily, Margot, and Ana!” —Morgan Pager, author of The Art of Vanishing “Visceral and emotional, Girls our Age is a monument to the metamorphosis from girlhood to adulthood. In her unflinching debut, Phoebe Thompson renders all the intimate, hilarious, painful nuances that make friendship among girls of any age some of life’s most compelling subject matter.” —Courtney Preiss, author of Welcome Home, Caroline Kline Phoebe Thompson writes about female friendship, mothers and daughters, and money. She studied English literature at Bowdoin College, got her MFA in fiction at the University of Wisconsin–Madison, and runs a marketing agency in Brooklyn, New York. She grew up in Mill Valley, California. GIRLS OUR AGE is her debut. You can follow her on Instagram and TikTok: @phoebethompsonwrites Phoebe Thompson - photo courtesy of the publicist Event details: This event will be hosted by Book Passage at our Corte Madera store. Free Admission / Open Seating Following the presentation, there will be a signing line or a meet-and-greet. For any questions regarding our events, please contact us at books@bookpassage.com .

events.description: Event title ROCKY SHARMA — Solving Problems That Matter: A Product Explorer's™ Playbook for AI Product Builders Date and time NEW DATE: Monday, Jan. 18, 2027 — 5:30 PM Location Book Passage, Ferry Building, San Francisco Event description AI has made it cheap to build the wrong things. The book codifies the operating model Rocky built from leading the team responsible for the technology fitted onto the U.S. Army's bomb-disposal suit, Iron Man's helmet, in real life. The technician inside the suit was the alternative. His team ran 124 verbatim customer interviews with defense personnel, bomb-disposal operators, and experts, saving the Army $10 million, and kept those operators home with their families. Ten years later, that same operating discipline is what the book teaches senior product managers navigating the AI era. The counterargument to “ship faster with AI,” built for the era where code is cheap and judgment is scarce. The book teaches an original methodology: The 12 P's: the operating spine for Product Explorer™ - The identity that comes before Product Builder Triple Fit (product fit · executive fit · mission fit): The pass gate before any code commits Mission Steward: The executive altitude every senior product leader must reach before approves the budget Public recognition : Rocky's June 2026 Forbes column on the book's thesis: https://www.forbes.com/councils/forbesbusinesscouncil/2026/06/18/sequence-matters-in-product-management-be-a-product-explorer-first-a-product-builder-second/ 2016 Iron Man mission clip (Vimeo, 53 seconds): https://vimeo.com/162478948 This was featured on NBC Bay Area News. Advance praise (sample list) : Steve Blank (Stanford, creator of Lean LaunchPad), Alex Osterwalder (co-creator of the Business Model Canvas), Alex Dang (co-author of the global bestseller The Venture Mindset), Robert E. Siegel (Author of The Systems Leader and The Brains and the Brawns Company), Rich Mironov (Author of Money Stories), Prof. Hau Lee (Stanford, Inventor of Bullwhip Effect), Alan Smith (Co-founder of Strategyzer), several U.S. defense personnel and leaders from Silicon Valley. About the author Rocky Sharma created the Product Explorer™ Methodology: the Product Manager who thinks like an Executive, discovers like an Inventor, and pitches like an Operator, before becoming a Product Builder, connecting every decision to their executive's metrics. Stanford GSB alumnus. Forged on a Stanford × U.S. Army mission in 2016, applied at Home Depot Supply’s $1.3B eCommerce P&L and across 20+ years in Product. Thought Leader at Forbes. CEO & CPO of Procurement AI, Luxeo Platforms, and ProductLedCEO. Also CEO of ASCM Golden Gate at Berkeley. Event format Free admission, open seating. Signing line following the reading.

events.title: RISING - Irma Herrera's The ICEmen Cometh
events.location: Berkeley
events.description: (Please do not bring infants to the show) The ICEmen Cometh critiques the Trump Regime’s full-frontal attack on immigrants, and how the brutality and cruelty of ICE agents as they catch, detain, disappear, and deport people, is eroding the civil rights of everyone in the United States. Stories about earlier waves of anti-immigrant hysteria explain how white supremacy has shaped our nation’s immigration laws. Irma Herrera’s new play, The ICEmen Cometh, uses current events to examine the history of immigration and the racial attitudes that have controlled who is allowed entry into the United States. Her first solo show, Why Would I Mispronounce My Own Name? is a personal narrative with laugh-out-loud humor and a substantial dose of American history. Her characters show who is valued and seen as “Real Americans.” The play had a five-month run at The Marsh Theaters (both SF and Berkeley) and has been performed nationally. Before becoming a playwright and solo performer, Irma was a San Francisco-based civil rights lawyer and journalist for three-plus decades. Through her powerful plays, Irma urges audiences to confront the enduring power of xenophobia, racism, sexism, and other forms of prejudice, and to speak up for fairness and equality. events.title: Vijay Iyer & Wadada Leo Smith
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
We welcome the long-awaited return of a pair of master improvisers and long-term collaborators for a landmark evening of duets drawing on their two ECM Records albums, 2016’s A Cosmic Rhythm With Each Stroke and their 2025 follow-up, Defiant Life.

“One of the truly great jazz musicians of our time” (Stereophile), pianist and composer Vijay Iyer stretches the boundaries of jazz but has long reached beyond the music’s vocabulary. He was the recipient of the MacArthur Foundation’s “Genius Grant” in 2013 and his current trio with bassist Linda May Han Oh and drummer Tyshawn Sorey is among the most acclaimed small groups in modern jazz.

A lion of the avant-garde since his membership in Chicago’s AACM in the late 1960s, trumpeter and composer Wadada Leo Smith is in the midst of a spectacular late career creative burst. Over the past decade, the 2016 Doris Duke Artist Award-winner released nearly two-dozen albums, most notably 2012’s epic Pulitzer Prize finalist Ten Freedom Summers (Cuneiform), an orchestral four-disc project inspired by the civil rights movement.

2016’s A Cosmic Rhythm With Each Stroke took its title from a line in the diaries of Indian visual artist Nasreen Mohamed, and their follow-up for ECM, 2025’s Defiant Life, is devoted to the necessary resistance to state-sponsored violence, at home and abroad.

Personnel: Vijay Iyer (piano, Fender Rhodes); Wadada Leo Smith (trumpet)

events.location: Bird & Beckett Books & Records, 653 Chenery Street, San Francisco
events.description: The Lenny Carlson Music Collective is a unique chamber ensemble that performs Carlson’s original compositions along with standards. His musical directions converge in the genre of Americana, blending Jazz, pop, folk, and classical. A Los Angeles native and award-winning composer, Carlson has also been an accomplished jazz guitarist, producer, music professor and author. Since 2009, he has been resident composer for Jeff Sanford’s Cartoon Jazz Orchestra. The Collective’s premiere performance at Bird & Beckett on 1/22/27 will feature Kevin Gerzevitz, piano; Michelle Maruyama, violin; Carla Wilson, bassoon and Luke Kirley, tuba/euphonium. Kevin Gerzevitz’s compositions and arrangements will also be performed. Carlson’s recent discography includes the title and three additional selections on Jeff Sanford’s Playland at the Beach CD (2023), available on Spotify and Bandcamp; Down by the Riverside: Theme and Variations CD (2022) on Bandcamp; and Nothing Wrong (2019), a Cartoon Jazz CD comprised entirely of his compositions, on Bandcamp. Carlson’s suite Four Sketches for My Mother (2022) appears in the S.F. Public Library’s 2026 Bay Beats music collection. The Bird & Beckett performance will be streamed live on Bird & Beckett’s YouTube channel and Facebook page. The YouTube stream can be found at this link: https://www.youtube.com/@bird_beckett/streams

events.title: Eliane Elias Quartet
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
(JAN 22-23) Antônio Carlos Jobim Centennial Celebration
(JAN 24) The Art of Bossa Nova

“Ms. Elias is never more sumptuously at home than when she turns to bossa nova” (The New York Times). A superlative pianist and singer who combines the sensuous, sun-splashed melodicism of Brazil with the harmonic sophistication of New York City, GRAMMY winner Eliane Elias honors the centennial of Brazil’s greatest songwriter, Antônio Carlos Jobim on Friday and Saturday, followed by Sunday's concert devoted to the wildly popular Bossa Nova movement of the 1960s and beyond.

The São Paulo-born Elias made an immediate splash in New York when she settled there in 1981, becoming an original member of the seminal fusion band Steps Ahead with Mike Mainieri, Michael Brecker, Eddie Gomez, and Peter Erskine. Since that auspicious debut, Elias has been thriving as a bandleader, leading a series of telepathic and flexible ensembles able to navigate fire-breathing bebop and gentle sambas with equal aplomb. She has recorded a succession of wide-ranging sessions for Blue Note, Concord, and Candid encompassing jazz standards, solo piano, and the music of her homeland as well as tributes to influential icons Bill Evans and Chet Baker.

Through it all, Jobim has always been a bedrock part of her creative life, with his compositions finding their way into numerous albums including her masterful 2022 session Quietude that features seductive takes on “Só Tinha De Ser Com Você (This Love That I’ve Found)” and “Brigas Nunca Mais (No More Fighting).”

Personnel: Eliane Elias (piano, vocals); Others TBA

events.title: Christy Scott Cashman - What Happened in Beulah
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: A teenage girl uncovers the dark secrets of her Smoky Mountain town while searching for a missing classmate in this gripping coming-of-age mystery perfect for fans of Where the Crawdads Sing . Nestled in the foothills of the Smoky Mountains, Beulah has always seemed steady—rooted in tradition, shaped by generations, and slow to change. But in 1986, the ground has shifted, and no one feels that more than fifteen-year-old Barrett Childress Owens. Between her parents’ unraveling marriage and a school full of kids she can’t connect with, she feels invisible in her own hometown. When Lacy Gunderson, the captivating new girl everyone is curious about, suddenly vanishes, the town’s calm surface fractures. Search parties comb the woods. A police investigation begins. Rumors multiply. Families close ranks. And Barrett begins to sense how much the adults around her choose not to say. As Beulah clings to its usual rituals—including the annual Miss Kudzu pageant, which has shaped local girlhood for decades—Barrett is forced to navigate a community where loss lingers in the air and secrets are carefully kept. Her journey through the uncertainty reshapes her understanding of friendships, family, and the complex place she calls home. A rich coming-of-age story with a pulse of mystery and a budding romance, What Happened in Beulah explores the fault lines of a small town and the courage it takes to face the truths people would rather bury. Christy Scott Cashman is a mother, author, and active member of the literary and arts communities. She serves on the boards of directors of the Associates of the Boston Public Library and the American Film Institute and is the founder of YouthINK, a nonprofit mentorship program for young artists in the United States and Ireland. events.description: Join us for the Invention of Solitude Fiction Book Club. This month we will be discussing the novel, Taiwan Travelogue by Yang Shuang-Zi. About the book: WINNER OF THE 2024 NATIONAL BOOK AWARD FOR TRANSLATED LITERATURE WINNER OF THE 2026 INTERNATIONAL BOOKER PRIZE A bittersweet story of love between two women, nested in an artful exploration of language, history, and power May 1938. The young novelist Aoyama Chizuko has sailed from her home in Nagasaki, Japan, and arrived in Taiwan. She's been invited there by the Japanese government ruling the island, though she has no interest in their official banquets or imperialist agenda. Instead, Chizuko longs to experience real island life and to taste as much of its authentic cuisine as her famously monstrous appetite can bear. Soon a Taiwanese woman-who is younger even than she is, and who shares the characters of her name-is hired as her interpreter and makes her dreams come true. The charming, erudite, meticulous Chizuru arranges Chizuko's travels all over the Land of the South and also proves to be an exceptional cook. Over scenic train rides and braised pork rice, lively banter and winter melon tea, Chizuko grows infatuated with her companion and intent on drawing her closer. But something causes Chizuru to keep her distance. It's only after a heartbreaking separation that Chizuko begins to grasp what the "something" is. Disguised as a translation of a rediscovered text by a Japanese writer, this novel was a sensation on its first publication in Mandarin Chinese in 2020 and won Taiwan's highest literary honor, the Golden Tripod Award. Taiwan Travelogue unburies lost colonial histories and deftly reveals how power dynamics inflect our most intimate relationships.

events.title: Rent
events.location: San Francisco Playhouse, 450 Post St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description: In New York’s East Village, a group of young artists struggles to build lives, make art, and hold onto each other in the face of uncertainty. Over the course of a single year, friendships are tested, love is complicated, and every moment feels urgent. With an iconic score featuring “Seasons of Love,” “La Vie Bohème,” “Take Me or Leave Me,” and more, Jonathan Larson’s groundbreaking musical captures a generation living under the shadow of HIV/AIDS, where joy and loss exist side by side, and the question is not how long you have, but how you choose to spend it. Winner of the Tony Award for Best Musical and the Pulitzer Prize for Drama, Rent is an electrifying, deeply human story about connection, resilience, and living fully in the present.

events.title: Terence Blanchard
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
Trumpeter, composer, and SFJAZZ Executive Artistic Director Terence Blanchard kicks off the new year with this residency showcasing an exclusive program of music.

A savvy bandleader, celebrated film composer, brilliant jazz writer, and influential educator, the GRAMMY-winning New Orleans native is a major creative force in the modern jazz scene. A prodigious trumpeter, he cut his teeth as a member of drummer Art Blakey’s iconic ensemble The Jazz Messengers and has risen to become one of the most in-demand collaborators in jazz.

He has composed over 40 movie scores, including soundtracks for the majority of director Spike Lee’s work, making Blanchard the most prolific jazz artist working in film.

An active composer for opera, he presented a revised version of his Champion: An Opera in Jazz at SFJAZZ in February 2016, and his follow-up, Fire Shut Up in My Bones, became the first opera by a Black composer to be presented at New York’s Metropolitan Opera in 2021.

Blanchard was appointed SFJAZZ Executive Artistic Director in 2023 and was named an NEA Jazz Master in 2024.

Personnel: Eliane Elias (piano, vocals); Others TBA

events.title: Cécile McLorin Salvant
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
Three-time GRAMMY Winner Cécile McLorin Salvant is the “the most successful female jazz singer to emerge since the turn of the millennium” (JazzTimes). For this highly anticipated engagement, she brings music from her newest Nonesuch Records release Oh Snap, with her remarkable band featuring pianist Sullivan Fortner.

Possessing a deep, velvety voice, rhythmic poise, and a sublime feel for the blues, Salvant combines conservatory-honed technique with a beguiling gift for lyrical interpretation — a singular, inimitable talent that won her the 2010 Thelonious Monk International Vocals Competition and drew the attention of early collaborators Jacky Terrasson and Wynton Marsalis.

Since her 2013 American debut album, the GRAMMY-nominated WomanChild, Salvant’s profile has taken a meteoric course around the world.

Never one to rest on past triumphs, Salvant is always exploring new realms of expression, from reinterpreted 1980s pop classics to symphonic music and her original song cycle Ogresse, making each SFJAZZ residency into a journey of unexpected delights. The music from Oh Snap presents yet another new side to Salvant’s creativity, consisting of original songs recorded alone in her home and expanded with contributions from her regular collaborators Fortner, bassist Yasushi Nakaumura, and drummer Kyle Poole. Utilizing electronic instruments, loops, vocal effects, and layers of overdubs, Oh Snap takes Salvant’s singular gifts into exciting new territory.

Personnel: Cécile McLorin Salvant (vocals); Sullivan Fortner (piano); Others TBA

Never one to rest on past triumphs, Salvant is always exploring new realms of expression, from reinterpreted 1980s pop classics to symphonic music and her original song cycle Ogresse, making each SFJAZZ residency into a journey of unexpected delights. The music from Oh Snap presents yet another new side to Salvant’s creativity, consisting of original songs recorded alone in her home and expanded with contributions from her regular collaborators Fortner, bassist Yasushi Nakaumura, and drummer Kyle Poole. Utilizing electronic instruments, loops, vocal effects, and layers of overdubs, Oh Snap takes Salvant’s singular gifts into exciting new territory.

Personnel: Cécile McLorin Salvant (vocals); Sullivan Fortner (piano); Others TBA

events.title: Song Circle with Amateur Music Network
events.location: Berkeley
events.description: October Theme: “Broadway and Show Tunes” There’s nothing that brings people together better than singing our favorite songs. It recalls summer nights around the campfire: someone strumming the guitar and all singing a mix of folk music, familiar songs we heard on the radio, and occasional new songs that someone shares. Nobody has to worry about whether you know the songs or can sing like a pro. This is our chance to share the joy of singing simply for the fun of it. Cary Sheldon is a singer, songwriter, and beloved Berkeley voice teacher with 30 years worth of grateful students. She has been playing and teaching in the Bay Area for the last 40 years. Her love for R & B music led her to be part of Zazu Pitts Memorial Orchestra in the 1980’s. Other affiliations include The Henry Kaiser Band, The Henriettas (a recreation of DeZurick sisters, a popular country music duo from the 1940’s), who appeared on Prairie Home Companion, and most recently her band DanceChant, a joyful community-inspired R&B band that encourages audience participation. She continues to be inspired by her love of singing in community. “Singing together with others is one of the greatest joys in my life.” Now in her 60’s, she returns to influences from her early life. Her grade school music teachers included John Langstaff, creator of the Christmas Revels, and the repertoire was based on the American folk tradition, including old English ballads, spirituals, freedom songs, and the popular folk and protest songs of the 1960’s. She hopes to inspire others to explore the depth of this material and rediscover the joy of community singing. Soprano Candace Johnson has led AMN’s Juneteenth Choral Celebration since its inception in 2020. The AMN community knows her through her commitment to the power of the Negro Spirituals tradition, but Candace has a deep connection to theater and to the music of the Broadway stage. A voice instructor at UC Berkeley for 17 years, in 2022 Candace also became the director of the University Gospel Choir. A lyric coloratura soprano, she crosses musical boundaries performing classical, jazz, musical theater, pop and gospel. She has sung on many stages, including Carnegie Hall and The Manhattan Center. Also a playwright and actress, Candace premiered her first one-woman show, Vox in a Box , in UC Berkeley’s Hertz Hall in 2018, which led to her becoming a resident solo artist at The Marsh theater (Berkeley/San Francisco). Candace has written and performed 5 full-length one-woman musicals. Her most recent show, Scat-ter Brain: The Music of ADHD , was commissioned by The Marsh in 2024 for its inaugural IFOYE festival of new works by women-identifying playwrights. Following an extended run, Scat-ter Brain was nominated by Broadway World SF for Best Solo Show of 2025. Please read our Health, Safety and COVID-19 Information Our commitment to our patrons

events.title: Grace Hwang Lynch Author Talk • How to Cook Rice: On the Care and Feeding of an Immigrant Family
events.location: Omnivore Books on Food, 3885a Cesar Chavez St, San Francisco, CA 94131
events.description: Grace Hwang Lynch is a San Francisco Bay Area writer specializing in Asian American food and culture. Her writing has been published by outlets such as NPR, Eating Well, KQED, San Francisco Chronicle, and San Jose Mercury News and was a finalist for an IACP Food Writing award. Follow her on Instagram @gracehwanglynch. Linda Shiue, MD, Chef , is a Taiwanese American physician, professionally trained chef, and author of the award-winning cookbook, Spicebox Kitchen. She is the Director of Culinary Medicine and Lifestyle Medicine at Kaiser Permanente San Francisco, where she founded Thrive Kitchen, a teaching kitchen. You can connect with Dr. Shiue @spiceboxtravels. In How to Cook Rice: On the Care and Feeding of an Immigrant Family , Grace Hwang Lynch takes readers on a bittersweet journey as the firstborn daughter of Taiwanese immigrants learning to navigate the California suburbs, Asian American identity, and motherhood while exploring what love, food, and family mean in light of her generational roots. Through Grace’s stories and included recipes, these meals express what words cannot, prompting an examination of what love—and food—mean in an immigrant family.

events.title: Kenny Barron: Songbook
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
with special guest vocalists

Called “one of the top jazz pianists in the world” by The Los Angeles Times, Kenny Barron is a 2010 NEA Jazz Master, fourteen-time GRAMMY nominee, and former SFJAZZ Resident Artistic Director who helped define and extend the jazz tradition since his work with Dizzy Gillespie in the early ‘60s catapulted him into the spotlight. On these nights, Barron is joined by his trio with drummer Johnathan Blake and a bassist to be named soon, and a selection of very special guest vocalists, performing his original compositions from his 2025 Artwork Records album Songbook. This performance will also honor the legacy of bassist and longtime trio member Kiyoshi Kitagawa, who passed in April of 2026.

A seven-time recipient of Best Pianst by the Jazz Journalists Association and named to the DownBeat Jazz Hall of Fame in 2022, the Philadelphia-born Barron built his peerless reputation as a sideman with Freddie Hubbard, Yusef Lateef, Stan Getz, James Moody and Ron Carter.

He has recorded over 50 albums as a bandleader over his five-decade career, and his newest release for the Paris-based Artwork label, Songbook, fulfills a longtime goal to record an album of his original compositions with vocals. The session includes a stunning lineup of guests including his fellow 2026-27 Season performers Cécile McLorin Salvant and Kurt Elling along with Tyreek McDole, Ann Hampton Callaway, Jean Baylor, Kavita Shah, Ekep Nkwelle, and Catherine Russell.

Personnel: Kenny Barron (piano); TBA bass; Johnathan Blake (drums); Special Guest Vocalists TBA

events.title: Charlie Hunter & Ella Feingold Trio
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
It’s true that Berkeley-reared Charlie Hunter has long been a familiar presence on Bay Area stages. Even though he moved east decades ago and now resides in Greensboro, North Carolina, Hunter has maintained deep ties to his hometown.

But the inveterately inventive 7-string guitar wizard has never presented anything quite like his trio with fellow guitar explorer Ella Feingold. Based in Western Massachusetts, she’s a pioneer of inverted tuning, which facilitates unexpected harmonic structures and voicings inaccessible in standard tuning. Inspired by the dauntingly prolific songwriter, jazz musician, and conceptual artist Chris Weisman, this approach shapes her signature sound—blending lush chord inversions, walking basslines, and expressive melodic phrasing, which makes Feingold a capaciously creative foil for Hunter.

He’s hardly the only one seeking her out. She’s also been working with Meshell Ndegeocello, Bootsy Collins, and Erykah Badu (with whom she’s performed many times in the Bay Area). But it’s with Hunter that she’s defining her own musical identity. He’s carved out a major new role for himself over the past decade as a producer, and last year he released their debut album Different Strokes for Different Folks on his SideHustle label. Rooted in funk, jazz, soul and ambient textures, it’s a raw, spontaneous conversation between friends who find limitless new space to investigate deep in the pocket.

Personnel: Charlie Hunter (guitar); Ella Feingold (guitar); TBA drums

events.title: Matthew Whitaker
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
The remarkable keyboardist, multi-instrumentalist, composer, and arranger Matthew Whitaker is a torchbearer for a new generation of young musicians with boundless creativity. The GRAMMY-winning former prodigy has collaborated with Jon Batiste, Christian McBride, Regina Carter and Bootsy Collins, and has recorded four uplifting albums blending the soul and jazz traditions. His SFJAZZ debut follows the release of his latest album, On Their Shoulders: An Organ Tribute — a loving salute to the organists who have inspired him including Dr. Lonnie Smith, Charles Earland, Jimmy Smith, Elbernita Clark, and Joey DeFrancesco.

The Hackensack, New Jersey native received his first keyboard at three and made a splash at 10, opening the festivities for Stevie Wonder’s 2011 induction into the Apollo Theater Hall of Fame.

Whitaker released his debut album, Outta the Box, at 16, with guests including Christian McBride, James Carter, and Will Calhoun, and has worked widely in film and television, both onscreen and as a composer. A Juilliard graduate, he has performed with major orchestras around the world and at venues including Carnegie Hall and Lincoln Center. In 2026, he won a GRAMMY for his arranging work with the 8-Bit Big Band.

His fourth album, On Their Shoulders, was nominated for Outstanding Jazz Album at the 2025 NAACP Image Awards.

Personnel: Matthew Whitaker (keyboards); Others TBA

events.title: Mavis Staples
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
With a professional career spanning nearly seven decades, Mavis Staples is the greatest living gospel and soul singer — a five-time GRAMMY winner, a 2016 Kennedy Center honoree, a 1999 Rock and Roll Hall of Fame inductee, a Blues and Gospel Hall of Fame inductee, and recipient of the 2005 GRAMMY Lifetime Achievement Award whose soaring voice turned classic spirituals into joyous declarations of freedom.

Born in Chicago, Staples made her professional debut at age 10 with her legendary family band, The Staple Singers, singing on timeless songs that became chart topping hits and indelible anthems of the Civil Rights Movement. Her unforgettable performances on a string of classics including “Uncloudy Day,” “Some Truth To Tell,” “Freedom Highway,” “Respect Yourself,” “Why Am I Treated So Bad,” “I’ll Take You There,” and “Let’s Do It Again” have all become intrinsic parts of the American cultural fabric.

Staples has recorded 18 albums as a solo artist and led a career that includes a staggering number of highlights, from performing at John F. Kennedy’s inauguration and marching with Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. to collaborating with Bob Dylan, Prince, The Band, Wilco’s Jeff Tweedy, and countless others.

Her newest ANTI Records release, 2025’s Sad and Beautiful World, is her fourteenth album and won GRAMMYs for Best American Roots Performance and Best Americana Performance, and includes material by the likes of Leonard Cohen, Curtis Mayfield, Gillian Welch, and Tom Waits.

Staples received the SFJAZZ Lifetime Achievement Award at SFJAZZ Gala 2020.

events.title: WeBop at SFJAZZ: Gumbo Group
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Joe Henderson Lab
events.description:
Ages 3.5 - 5

ABOUT WEBOP AT SFJAZZ
We are thrilled to partner with our sister organization—Jazz at Lincoln Center—in launching the West Coast version of the acclaimed early childhood music education program, WeBop! The perfect preamble to our Family Matinee program and designed for youngsters between the ages 2-5 and their caregivers, WeBop at SFJAZZ is designed to introduce young children to jazz music and performance in a safe, welcoming and interactive setting. Classes are 45 minutes long and provide plenty of opportunities to learn, explore, and play.

ABOUT THIS CLASS
Musical activities for the Gumbo Group utilize dramatic play as a core learning element and provide opportunities for discovery and exploration through jazz. The multisensory nature of music—hearing, moving, touching, vocalizing—creates many entry points for children in this age group to be engaged and develop. They will learn to identify and repeat short musical patterns, explore important musical concepts—such as dynamics and tempo—through singing, listening, playing, and improvising with jazz tunes and stories.

events.title: LIVE MUSIC: @ (Presented by THROWIN' BO'S)
events.location: 4-Star Theater, 2200 Clement St, San Francisco, CA 94121
events.description: Throwin’ Bo’s presents: @ Songwriters Victoria Rose and Stone Filipczak are the creative force behind @, a singular duo whose inventive collaboration has reimagined psychedelic folk for a new generation. On Autosmile, their first album for 4AD, the pair expand on the acclaimed promise of their debut Mind Palace Music, blending timeless songwriting with adventurous arrangements, dense harmonies, and a playful spirit that constantly pushes beyond genre boundaries. Though now based in Philadelphia, Victoria and Stone continue their distinctive songwriting process: working independently before completing each other’s compositions. Recorded largely at home with a humble collection of equipment and enriched by contributions from close friends on cello, violin, and drums, Autosmile transforms lo-fi methods into something remarkably lush, immersive, and emotionally resonant. Across eleven songs, @ balance darkness and wonder with striking confidence. The album moves effortlessly between haunting folk textures, progressive flourishes, indie-pop hooks, and moments of cinematic beauty. Highlights include the expansive title track “Autosmile,” the nostalgic earworm “I Know You Are (But What Am I Thinking),” and the intricately arranged “Punish My Mind,” each exploring themes of change, self-reflection, loss, and acceptance through lyrics that remain deliberately open-ended and deeply relatable. Equal parts mysterious, virtuosic, and playful, Autosmile showcases @ at their most fully realized—an adventurous partnership capable of looking backward and forward at once. It is an album of contrasts: beauty and pain, humor and gravity, intimacy and ambition. In the face of uncertainty, @ offer curiosity, connection, and the possibility of transformation. events.title: Billy Childs Quartet
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
70th Birthday Celebration

A six-time GRAMMY winner, Pultizer Prize finalist, and 2009 Guggenheim Fellow, pianist and composer Billy Childs is an iconic artist whose innovative work bridges the jazz tradition and contemporary chamber music. His new Mack Avenue album Triumvirate was described as “truly magical” by JazzTimes, and for this special performance commemorating his 70th birthday, Childs performs with his quartet featuring former SFJAZZ Collective trumpeter Sean Jones.

The Los Angeles native began as a prodigy, performing professionally by his teens and making his professional debut in 1977 with the iconic trombonist J.J. Johnson. He spent six formative years as a sideman with trumpeter Freddie Hubbard in the 1970s and 80s and issued his debut album Midland in 1985.

From that notable start, Childs has released a series of GRAMMY-winning albums for the Windham Hill, Mack Avenue, and his own Lunacy label and lent his formidable arranging skills to work with Dianne Reeves, Gladys Knight, Sting, and Yo-Yo Ma.

His 2026 Mack Avenue album Triumvirate is a remarkably attuned trio release featuring former SFJAZZ Collective bassist Matt Penman and drummer Ari Hoenig and revisits favorites from Childs’s own songbook as well as singular takes on standards like Thelonious Monk’s “Ask Me Now.” This 70th birthday performance celebrates a legacy still very much in progress.

Personnel: Billy Childs (piano); Sean Jones (trumpet); Others TBA

events.title: Kandace Springs
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
“A bewitching amalgam of Dusty Springfield’s caliginous, cream-filled soulfulness and Nancy Wilson’s sensual sophistication, with distinct shades of Michael Jackson” (JazzTimes), the stunning soul jazz singer Kandace Springs presents favorites from her career and a selection of scintillating new material.

Springs first gained national attention with her 2014 self-titled EP, a hip-hop inflected project that led to performances on Jimmy Kimmel Live and The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, appearances at the Afropunk and Bonnaroo festivals, and an invitation to perform with Prince at Paisley Park for the 30th anniversary of Purple Rain. While elated by these opportunities, she started rethinking her musical direction and gravitated toward the jazz and soul-based sounds of her Nashville upbringing.

Her 2016 full-length debut Soul Eyes was produced by GRAMMY-winner Larry Klein and remains a defiant statement of purpose, embracing both her jazz credentials and pop experience with power and grace. Springs has become yet more artistically assured with each subsequent release.

Following her revelatory 2024 SRP Records debut Run Your Race comes her fifth and latest, 2025’s Lady in Satin, a loving tribute to the great Billie Holiday that revisits Lady Day’s same-named 1958 album and heartbreaking final statement with fresh arrangements, accompanied by Portugal’s remarkable Orquestra Clássica de Espinho.

Personnel: Kandace Springs (piano, vocals); Others TBA

events.title: Tyreek McDole / Isaiah Collier
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
Terence Blanchard’s curated series dedicated to artists deserving wider recognition continues in February with a pair of young artists who are poised to reach stratospheric heights as rising masters — vocalist Tyreek McDole and saxophonist Isaiah Collier.

Winner of the 2023 Sarah Vaughan International Jazz Vocal Competition, Florida-reared vocalist Tyreek McDole has earned his reputation as “a standout in the next generation of great jazz singers” (WBGO). His 2025 debut release for Artworks Records, Open Up Your Senses, features bold interpretations over its thirteen tracks ranging from a romantic approach to the 1933 Jerry Levinson standard “Under a Blanket of Blue” to an adventurous take on Pharoah Sanders’ “The Creator Has a Master Plan,” signaling McDole’s commitment to both jazz tradition and innovation.

An explosive young saxophonist, vocalist, composer, and bandleader, Isaiah Collier is a self-described “sonic scientist” at the forefront of the vibrantly creative Chicago scene. He's captured rapturous acclaim and a fervent following since the bow of his 2018 debut Return of the Black Emperor and has collaborated with legends including Wadada Leo Smith, channeling the churning, relentless energy of his hometown forebears the AACM and Art Ensemble of Chicago. His newest Division 81 recording, The Almighty, features appearances by fellow Chicago luminaries Corey Wilkes on trumpet and Fred Jackson Jr. on alto saxophone.

Personnel: TYREEK MCDOLE; Tyreek McDole (vocals); Others TBA; ISAIAH COLLIER; Isaiah Collier (tenor saxophone)

events.title: Sungazer
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
“A bundle of energy that expertly marries the organic and synthetic” (Everything is Noise), the electro-acoustic fusion juggernaut Sungazer is the brainchild of bass virtuoso Adam Neely and mind-bending drummer Shawn Crowder. Formed in 2014, the Brooklyn-based group brings together bewildering time signatures and 8-bit style EDM with masterful instrumental prowess on a range of material including tracks from their most recent album, Against the Fall of Night.

From the outset, Sungazer has challenged the boundaries separating jazz fusion, progressive rock, and electronic production, creating music that feels simultaneously cerebral and visceral. Neely’s elastic bass lines weave through Crowder’s hyper-detailed polyrhythms with astonishing precision, yet the duo never sacrifices groove for technicality. Instead, their compositions thrive on tension and release, balancing virtuosic complexity with infectious melodies and digitally inspired textures.

Against the Fall of Night represents the clearest realization of Sungazer’s artistic philosophy to date. Across the album, shimmering synthesizers collide with explosive drumming, while intricate rhythmic modulations transform each track into an unpredictable sonic journey. By combining internet-age electronic aesthetics with improvisational sophistication, the band has carved out a singular identity that continues reshaping expectations for contemporary instrumental music. Their fearless experimentation ensures fusion remains innovative, relevant, and resonant.

Personnel: Adam Neely (bass); Shawn Crowder (drums); Others TBA

events.title: Ambrose Akinmusire
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
With guests Bill Frisell and Herlin Riley

For the first of his two nights during the 2026-27 Season, Oakland-reared trumpet genius Ambrose Akimusire returns with Owl Song, the project he premiered at SFJAZZ in 2022 as a Resident Artistic Director with pioneering guitarist Bill Frisell and the iconic New Orleans drummer Herlin Riley.

The most distinctive trumpeter of our era, Akinmusire has come so far since his early days at Berkeley High School and his 2007 win at the Thelonious Monk International Trumpet Competition, building a career by transcending expectations at every turn. As The New York Times observed, “More than almost any other contemporary improviser, Mr. Akinmusire has invented a way of composing that’s unfixed from jazz’s stickiest conventions.”

Owl Song, Akinmusire’s eighth album and 2023 debut for Nonesuch Records, was recorded in the days following the world premiere performance at SFJAZZ and comprises a deeply felt series of intimate compositions emphasizing space and melodic beauty – aspects perfectly aligned with the aesthetic approaches of Frisell and Riley. Called “one of the most interesting recordings to come along in a very long time” by DownBeat, Owl Song was nominated for a GRAMMY for Best Instrumental Jazz Album and made numerous best-of-year lists in the press.

Personnel: Ambrose Akinmusire (trumpet); Bill Frisell (guitar); Herlin Riley (drums)

events.title: Ambrose Akinmusire Quartet
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
For his second night of the season, trumpeter Ambrose Akinmusire performs with his long-term working quartet including pianist Sam Harris, bassist Harish Raghavan, and drummer Justin Brown — the group with which he made his first SFJAZZ appearance as a leader in 2011.

To the jazz world, Akinmusire’s ascension from young Oakland-born trumpeter at Berkeley High School to one of the most important voices in jazz seemed shockingly brief. In truth, his trajectory has been a linear progression, starting in earnest with a touring opportunity from influential saxophonist and composer Steve Coleman while still in high school, and built on a foundation of study at the Manhattan School of Music and the Thelonious Monk Institute of Jazz at USC with Herbie Hancock, Wayne Shorter, and Terence Blanchard. After decamping to New York, Akinmusire built his résumé as a sideman with the likes of Vijay Iyer and Aaron Parks, and in 2007, won both the prestigious Carmine Caruso International Jazz Trumpet Solo Competition and the star-making Thelonious Monk International Trumpet Competition.

Since then, the trumpeter has been a whirlwind of activity but has always returned to this quartet as home base, heard most recently on 2020’s GRAMMY-nominated On the Tender Spot of Every Calloused Moment.

Personnel: Ambrose Akinmusire (trumpet); Sam Harris (piano); Harish Raghavan (bass); Justin Brown (drums)

events.title: Klezmatics
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
The GRAMMY-winning Jewish klezmer superstars celebrate 40 years of music with this performance of material from their new album, We Were Made For These Times — a powerful new body of work rooted in protest, hope, and resilience.

Formed in New York’s East Village in 1986, the Klezmatics led the resurgence of the nearly forgotten klezmer tradition and contemporized it with an irreverent dose of punk rock attitude, and since their inception, have been one of most visible faces of today’s Yiddish culture. Enduring a number of personnel changes over the past two decades, the band has revolved around original members Lorin Sklamberg on lead vocals and accordion, trumpeter/keyboardist Frank London and bassist Paul Morrissett. They have collaborated with violin virtuoso Itzhak Perlman, Pulitzer Prize winner Tony Kushner and Israeli vocalist Chava Alberstein, and have released a dozen diverse albums, including the GRAMMY-winning Wonder Wheel, their first session that set previously unused Woody Guthrie lyrics to their own original material. The band would expand their integration of Guthrie’s words to new compositions on their Happy Joyous Hanukkah and Happier Joyous Hanukkah projects that have been an SFJAZZ holiday tradition for many years.

Released on International Workers’ Day in 2026, We Were Made For These Times brings together Jewish, Black gospel, Latin American, Crimean Tatar, and avant-jazz voices, creating a shared musical language of solidarity for the world we are living in now.

Personnel: Lorin Sklamberg (lead vocals, accordion, guitar, piano); Matt Derriau (kaval, clarinet, saxophone); Lisa Gutkin (violin, vocals); Frank London (trumpet, keyboards); Paul Morrissett (bass, tsimbl); Richie Barshay (percussion)

events.title: Benny Green Trio
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
with Christian McBride and Carl Allen

Nobody plays straight-ahead modern jazz piano with more swinging joy and finesse than Benny Green, the one-time Berkeley High wunderkind who developed his leanly lyrical and propulsive playing in the star-making bands of singer Betty Carter, drummer Art Blakey, and bassist Ray Brown. With this performance, Green is joined by a historic rhythm section including bass great Christian McBride and the influential drummer Carl Allen — a supremely attuned trio who worked in the early 1990s with the legendary trumpeter Freddie Hubbard and recorded Green’s Blue Note sessions Greens (1991), Testifyin’!: Live at the Village Vanguard (1991), and That’s Right! (1992).

A successful bandleader for over 35 years, Green has released a string of fine records played on scores of dates with the likes of Etta Jones, Ralph Moore, and Milt Jackson. In 1993, the late great Oscar Peterson picked Green to receive Toronto’s Glenn Gould International Protégé Prize in Music and later recorded the dazzling Oscar & Benny album with him.

More than a bass superstar, Christian McBride has become a commanding force in American culture as an eight-time GRAMMY Award-winning bandleader and recording artist.

“One of the most prominent contemporary jazz drummers” (All Music Guide), Carl Allen was a protégé of the legendary Art Blakey and has amassed a staggering resume as a bandleader, sideman, and educator.

Personnel: Benny Green (piano); Christian McBride (bass); Carl Allen (drums)

events.title: Song Circle with Amateur Music Network
events.location: Berkeley
events.description: October Theme: “Broadway and Show Tunes” There’s nothing that brings people together better than singing our favorite songs. It recalls summer nights around the campfire: someone strumming the guitar and all singing a mix of folk music, familiar songs we heard on the radio, and occasional new songs that someone shares. Nobody has to worry about whether you know the songs or can sing like a pro. This is our chance to share the joy of singing simply for the fun of it. Cary Sheldon is a singer, songwriter, and beloved Berkeley voice teacher with 30 years worth of grateful students. She has been playing and teaching in the Bay Area for the last 40 years. Her love for R & B music led her to be part of Zazu Pitts Memorial Orchestra in the 1980’s. Other affiliations include The Henry Kaiser Band, The Henriettas (a recreation of DeZurick sisters, a popular country music duo from the 1940’s), who appeared on Prairie Home Companion, and most recently her band DanceChant, a joyful community-inspired R&B band that encourages audience participation. She continues to be inspired by her love of singing in community. “Singing together with others is one of the greatest joys in my life.” Now in her 60’s, she returns to influences from her early life. Her grade school music teachers included John Langstaff, creator of the Christmas Revels, and the repertoire was based on the American folk tradition, including old English ballads, spirituals, freedom songs, and the popular folk and protest songs of the 1960’s. She hopes to inspire others to explore the depth of this material and rediscover the joy of community singing. Soprano Candace Johnson has led AMN’s Juneteenth Choral Celebration since its inception in 2020. The AMN community knows her through her commitment to the power of the Negro Spirituals tradition, but Candace has a deep connection to theater and to the music of the Broadway stage. A voice instructor at UC Berkeley for 17 years, in 2022 Candace also became the director of the University Gospel Choir. A lyric coloratura soprano, she crosses musical boundaries performing classical, jazz, musical theater, pop and gospel. She has sung on many stages, including Carnegie Hall and The Manhattan Center. Also a playwright and actress, Candace premiered her first one-woman show, Vox in a Box , in UC Berkeley’s Hertz Hall in 2018, which led to her becoming a resident solo artist at The Marsh theater (Berkeley/San Francisco). Candace has written and performed 5 full-length one-woman musicals. Her most recent show, Scat-ter Brain: The Music of ADHD , was commissioned by The Marsh in 2024 for its inaugural IFOYE festival of new works by women-identifying playwrights. Following an extended run, Scat-ter Brain was nominated by Broadway World SF for Best Solo Show of 2025. Please read our Health, Safety and COVID-19 Information Our commitment to our patrons

events.title: Lucía
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
The electrifying young vocalist brings her signature blend of jazz, traditional Latin folk, and modern pop to SFJAZZ.

Weaned on the percussive sound of son jarocho while growing up in Veracruz, Lucía Gutierrez Rebolloso started performing in her family’s ensemble before enrolling in grade school. She’s carried her Mexican roots with her, but these days the Harlem-based vocalist, who records and performs under the single moniker Lucía, is one of the most sought-after young artists in jazz. Her 2022 victory at the prestigious Sarah Vaughan International Jazz Vocal Competition has fueled her rise. The first Mexican artist to win the event, she’s following in the ascending footsteps of previous winners Samara Joy (2019) and Jazzmeia Horn (2013).

Smitten with jazz as a teenager, Lucía loved the opportunities it provided for spontaneous invention. “As vocalists we are free to express ourselves and interact with the other band members, and to lead as well,” she says. Her eponymous 2025 debut album gives a good sense of her bilingual repertoire, from her captivating version of the traditional lament “La Llorona,” a song she grew up with in Veracruz, and “Cuando vuelva a tu lado” which became a major hit for Dinah Washington with the English lyric “What a Diff'rence a Day Makes,” to sensuous standards like “You Must Believe In Spring” and contemporary fare like Olivia Rodrigo’s “Lacy.”

Personnel: Lucía (vocals); Others TBA

events.title: Bria Skonberg Quintet
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
Juno award-winning trumpeter and vocalist Bria Skonberg is, in the words of The Wall Street Journal, “one of the most versatile and imposing musicians of her generation.”

An artist deeply committed to the New Orleans “hot jazz” tradition filtered through contemporary influences, the Chilliwack, British Columbia native began her musical life as a big band vocalist (doubling on trumpet) at age sixteen and studying with trumpeter and swing veteran Warren Vaché. Skonberg traveled the world with veteran guitarists Bucky Pizzarelli and Horward Alden, and since arriving in New York, her profile has risen steadily with a New York Bistro Award for Outstanding Jazz Artist and a Swing! Award bestowed by Jazz at Lincoln Center.

Her seventh and latest studio album, What it Means, is her first in five years and balances original compositions with classic material by Louis Armstrong, John Lennon, and Sidney Bechet. Recorded in New Orleans, the recording is steeped in the spirit of the Crescent City and features a remarkable assemblage of “local” talent including drummer Herlin Riley, guitarist Don Vappie, and sousaphonist and Preservation Hall director Ben Jaffe.

With a deep, melodious trumpet tone and a voice possessed of warmth and clarity, Bria Skonberg is an artist whose approach, steeped in the past, points the way to a vibrant future.

Personnel: Bria Skonberg (trumpet, vocals); Others TBA

events.title: Stella Heath: The Billie Holiday Project
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
w/ BHP Jazz Big Band

A versatile young vocalist and bandleader whose taste for classic jazz spans the 20s through the 40s, Stella Heath presents a special evening devoted to the life and music of the great Billie Holiday, accompanied by the BHP Big Band.

Born in Novato and raised in Petaluma, Heath began singing at eight and was inspired by the Billie Holiday records in her mother’s collection. She spent the last two years of high school at Michigan’s prestigious Interlochen Arts Academy before acting studies in New York and a career as a working Shakespearean actor that took her from Florida to Beijing and all points in between.

Upon returning to the Bay Area, Heath dove headlong into music, assembling a series of groups that would honor areas of early jazz that she wanted to explore and bring to audiences, from the Roma jazz of Django Reinhardt and the traditional jazz of the 1920s to the swing of the 30s and 40s and the Great American Songbook.

For this night, Heath celebrates the legacy of Lady Day — particularly her collaborations with pianist Teddy Wilson in the 1930s — through music, storytelling, and visuals that immerse the listeners in the era, placing the songs in historical context that gives the timeless music a still deeper meaning. Heath released her album dedicated to Holiday, For Billie, in 2026.

Personnel: Stella Heath (vocals); Others TBA

events.title: Carmen Lundy
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
A 2026 NEA Jazz Master, vocalist and composer Carmen Lundy is a bona fide giant in the music who first made her mark more than four decades ago and has led an incredibly influential career. She makes her first appearance on the Miner stage with this highly anticipated performance.

Championed by jazz giants like Geri Allen, Billy Childs, Bobby Watson and Walter Bishop Jr., Lundy is a renaissance woman whose creativity knows no bounds. A brilliant songwriter with several contemporary standards to her credit (“These Things You Are to Me”), she’s an actress, painter, bandleader, arranger and composer with an extensive book of finely wrought original songs.

On stage, she’s a riveting performer, utterly at ease and open to wherever the music needs to go. Already well-established on the New York scene in 1985 when Dr. Herb Wong’s Black Hawk label released her first album Good Morning Kiss, she’s recorded a stellar body of work since then for JVC, Arabesque and Justin Time (which reissued Good Morning Kiss in 2002).

Lundy has been running her own label Afrasia since 2005’s Jazz and the New Songbook: Live at the Madrid, and her two most recent albums, 2019’s Modern Ancestors and 2022’s Fade to Black, were each nominated for a GRAMMY.

Personnel: Carmen Lundy (vocals); Others TBA

events.title: 40 FINGERS
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Phenomenal quartet of guitarists · They are called 40 FINGERS, they are Italian and they are the phenomenal quartet of guitarists who, to the tune of millions of views, are conquering social networks all over the world (over 100 million views: https://www.youtube.com/@40Fingers) with their masterful reinterpretations and rearrangements of fa-mous rock and pop hits, film and TV series soundtracks, and an official endorsement such as that of Queen, who applauded and published on their website the “40 Fingers” version of Bohemian Rhapsody (official Queen website). They have also been acclaimed by numerous Italian and international music stars who have chosen them to duet together: from Andrea Bocelli to US singer Tory Kelly, and Andy Summers of The Police to revisit the band’s famous song “Bring on the Night”(https://bit.ly/40fingerspolice). Each with a strong musical history and a different background, the four musicians together explore new sonic universes in the name of fingerpicking, proposing a vast repertoire that starts with a reinterpretation for four guitars of rock and pop songs and ends with their own original compositions. The shared passion that the four of them have for the world of film and TV series and for their scores has also led them to try their hand at a series of original arrangements of famous soundtracks, including their “40 finger” version of the two main themes of John Williams' work on George Lucas' Star Wars saga, The Last of the Mohicans, a sensational Disney medley and the medley from Harry Potter, also including some of the themes written by the great John Williams. The stage is the natural home of 40 FINGERS. Accompanied by a highly spectacular visual production created by some of Europe's best light designers, they take the audience on a musical journey with no linguistic or geographical boundaries through their versions of Sultans of Swing, Africa, Sound of Silence, Bohemian Rhapsody, The Last of the Mohicans, Libertango and other tracks that span genres in a comprehensive way, uniting and thrilling all music lovers.

events.title: Meklit
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
Meklit Hadero is an Ethiopian-American vocalist, songwriter, and composer, known for her electric stage presence, innovative sound and vibrant cultural strategy. A fixture on the Bay Area and global scenes, she makes her return to the Miner stage for the first time in six years.

A 2019 Artist-in-Residence at Harvard University, she is a National Geographic Explorer and is co-founder and host of the podcast and concert series Movement.

A Piece of Infinity, the latest album by Meklit, was released in 2025 on Smithsonian Folkways Records. It has already received rave reviews by Bandcamp, The Guardian, and AfroPop Worldwide, and has been featured by NPR Music, NPR’s Weekend Edition and the Recording Academy’s GRAMMY Global Spin. This album is an invitation to think, to love, and to groove, reimagining folk tunes from a multitude of communities and cultures throughout Ethiopia into jazz-inflected fantasies imbued with warmth and reverence.

From songs of longing and love to children's riddles and original compositions, Meklit traverses expansive sonic ground that offers just a glimpse at the infinite complexity of Ethiopian culture. The album features guest appearances by harpist Brandee Younger and flutist Camille Thurman and was recorded at Women’s Audio Mission in San Francisco.

Personnel: Meklit (guitar, vocals); Others TBA

events.title: WeBop at SFJAZZ: Gumbo Group
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Joe Henderson Lab
events.description:
Ages 3.5 - 5

ABOUT WEBOP AT SFJAZZ
We are thrilled to partner with our sister organization—Jazz at Lincoln Center—in launching the West Coast version of the acclaimed early childhood music education program, WeBop! The perfect preamble to our Family Matinee program and designed for youngsters between the ages 2-5 and their caregivers, WeBop at SFJAZZ is designed to introduce young children to jazz music and performance in a safe, welcoming and interactive setting. Classes are 45 minutes long and provide plenty of opportunities to learn, explore, and play.

ABOUT THIS CLASS
Musical activities for the Gumbo Group utilize dramatic play as a core learning element and provide opportunities for discovery and exploration through jazz. The multisensory nature of music—hearing, moving, touching, vocalizing—creates many entry points for children in this age group to be engaged and develop. They will learn to identify and repeat short musical patterns, explore important musical concepts—such as dynamics and tempo—through singing, listening, playing, and improvising with jazz tunes and stories.

events.title: Dee Dee Bridgewater Quartet
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
A restless explorer who has collaborated with master musicians of Mali, interpreted the cabaret of Kurt Weill, and embraced the hard bop of Horace Silver, 2017 NEA Jazz Master Dee Dee Bridgewater brings a powerful new program she calls We Exist!, accompanied by a stellar rhythm section including pianist Alexis Lombre, bassist Liany Mateo, and drummer Shirazette Tinnin.

Since she first gained recognition in the early 1970s with the great Thad Jones/Mel Lewis Orchestra, Bridgewater has thrived wherever she’s landed, and this show stands as a revelatory statement of purpose. Built as a “rallying cry” that connects past and present struggles, the program reimagines songs of protest such as Nina Simone’s “Mississippi Goddam” and Roberta Flack’s “Trying Times,” tracing the ongoing fight for justice and equality.

Taking a cue from drummer and activist Max Roach’s landmark 1961 protest album We Insist!: Freedom Now Suite, the project confronts issues of racial oppression and civil rights while also championing female empowerment in a historically male-dominated jazz world. Bridgewater reinforces this message through an all-female ensemble, transforming the band itself into a living symbol of representation and change. It is a celebration of resilience, a platform for women in jazz, and a reminder—delivered with power and elegance—that music can still be a force for cultural and social transformation.

Personnel: Dee Dee Bridgewater (vocals); Alexis Lombre (piano); Liany Mateo (bass); Shirazette Tinnin (drums)

events.description:
Brazilian music and artistry have a long and storied relationship within American jazz. For this spring series, we amplify the eras and artists who shaped some of Brazil’s most enduring sounds—from the roots of samba to the global phenomenon of jazz-infused bossa nova and beyond. This spring we highlight a musical marriage that has stood the test of time and given us plenty of reason to sing, dance and rejoice.

Live music featuring special guests each week along with curated media playlists and Q&A make Discover Jazz the Bay Area’s favorite Thursday evening hang!

events.title: Edward Simon: When Dogs Howl
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
“One of the strongest pianists of his generation” (DownBeat), SFJAZZ Collective pianist Edward Simon brings his latest and most expansive project to the stage.

When Dogs Howl is an ambitious multidisciplinary project that blends jazz composition, Afro-Venezuelan percussion, dance, storytelling, and immersive video design into a unified performance experience. Created in collaboration with SFJAZZ and commissioned by the Creative Work Fund, the work centers on the journeys of Venezuelan refugees and migrants who travel thousands of miles across Latin America in search of safety, opportunity, and belonging.

Simon combines a jazz big band with traditional South American instruments and percussion, creating a sound world that merges contemporary improvisation with Venezuelan rhythmic traditions. Rather than presenting migration as abstract politics, the project emphasizes lived emotional experiences: displacement, resilience, memory, and reinvention. Its unique strength lies in how music, projected visuals, and movement interact to create a cinematic narrative atmosphere. When Dogs Howl reflects Simon’s long-standing commitment to socially engaged jazz and cross-cultural collaboration and further elevates his status as a visionary artist whose creativity continually pushes beyond borders, genres, and restrictions.

Personnel: Edward Simon (piano); Rafael Barata (drums); Others TBA

events.title: Flamenco Vivo Carlota Santana
events.location: Presidio Theatre, 99 Moraga Ave, San Francisco, CA 94129
events.description: Popular and innovative Flamenco Vivo Carlota Santana returns with Quinto Elemento (Fifth Element), an evening-length work by acclaimed choreographer Patricia Guerrero, winner of Spain’s National Dance Award, with an original score by Francis Gómez performed live. Featuring Flamenco Vivo’s world-renowned international cast of dancers and musicians, the work explores the invisible essence that connects all things. Guerrero is hailed by The New Yorker as “a master of tradition who dares to deconstruct the art form.”

events.title: Sasha Berliner Arts & Sciences
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
A gifted and award-winning vibraphonist, composer, and producer, San Francisco native Sasha Berliner presents the SFJAZZ premiere of her new electric band project Arts & Sciences and music from their debut EP for this homecoming performance.

Berliner began on drums at eight and attended the Oakland School for the Arts, studying with Howard Wiley and Dave Ellis before becoming a two-year member of the SFJAZZ High School All-Stars Orchestra, performing with the Monterey Jazz Festival Next Generation Jazz Orchestra and Stanford Jazz Workshops.

Now based in New York, Berliner was a student of Stefon Harris, Chris Dingman, and Matt Wilson at the New School and is an active bandleader, heading a series of superlative ensembles.

She has collaborated with Beck, Vijay Iyer, Terri Lyne Carrington, Ravi Coltrane, Nicholas Payton, Christian McBride, Tyshawn Sorey, and Cécile McLorin Salvant, and released her full-length debut album, Azalea, in 2019 — a recording that received a “Best New Release” nomination in the JazzTimes Readers’ Poll.

The youngest artist and first woman to win the DownBeat Critics’ Poll for Rising Star Vibraphonist, Berliner’s Arts & Sciences is a potent new dimension for a boundlessly creative voice in modern jazz.

Personnel: Sasha Berliner (vibraphone, MalletKAT, electronics); Others TBA

events.title: Gabi Hartmann / Samora & Elena Pinderhughes
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
The March installment of Terence Blanchard’s UpSwing series presents the Paris-based singer and songwriter Gabi Hartmann and the brother and sister duo of flutist Elena and keyboardist Samora Pinderhughes, highlighting the rising generation of jazz torchbearers.

Gaby Hartmann is an acclaimed vocalist who elegantly blends pop, jazz, soul, and world music, who takes audiences on “an enticing musical voyage that echoes the bossa nova sounds of Brazil, the Afropop of Miriam Makeba and the cool jazz of Norah Jones” (Montreal Gazette). Born in Paris in 1991, she studied ethnomusicology before captivating international audiences with her multilingual storytelling and velvet voice. Her self-titled debut earned praise and a Japan Golden Disc Award nomination, while performances alongside Melody Gardot elevated her profile. In 2025, Hartmann unveiled La Femme aux yeux de sel (The Woman with Eyes of Salt), an album steeped in intimacy.

Born in Berkeley and currently taking over the jazz world, Elena and Samora Pinderhughes have each made indelible marks on the global scene as bandleaders and collaborators.

Flutist Elena rose through the SFJAZZ High School All-Stars program to become one of the most in-demand musicians in jazz, working with Ambrose Akinmusire, Herbie Hancock, Chief Adjuah, Childish Gambino, Esperanza Spalding, and Milton Nascimento.

The award-winning pianist Samora Pinderhughes has ingeniously combined jazz, neo soul, and hip-gop, working with Common, Robert Glasper, Lalah Hathaway, and Sara Bareilles. His 2022 album Grief was listed among the best albums of the year by The New York Times and Bandcamp.

The pair recorded their first album together, Catch 22, in 2005 when they were 9 and 13 years old.

events.title: Annie & The Caldwells
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
Spend Easter Sunday with the group PopMatters calls “An unrepentantly soul-stirring sound capable of transcending time and place.”

Powerhouse vocalist Annie Caldwell and her husband, guitarist Willie Joe Caldwell, Sr., founded a family band to keep their children from performing in juke joints and blues clubs. But Annie & The Caldwells ended up following the kids, pouring gospel fervor into secular songs. Hailing from West Point, Mississippi, the septet delivers a glorious book of original tunes inspired by the Gap Band, Chaka Khan, Bootsy Collins and George Clinton, all filtered through their love of the golden age gospel groups like the Ward Singers and the Soul Stirrers.

For this Easter performance they’ll be drawing deeply from their critically acclaimed 2025 gospel album on David Byrne’s Luaka Bop label Can’t Lose (My Soul) — a masterpiece that PopMatters says “blends gospel fervor and deep grooves into a triumphant, soul-stirring album that reaches for transcendence.”

Combining soaring gospel harmonies with grit and street savvy, the songs summon the spirit back into the sound that gave birth to soul music.

Personnel: Annie Caldwell (vocals); Willie Joe Caldwell Sr. (guitar, vocals); Deborah Caldwell Moore (vocals); Anjessica Caldwell (vocals); Toni Rivers (vocals); Willie Joe Caldwell Jr. (bass); Abel Aquirius (drums)

events.title: Chris Potter Septet
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
“One of the most studied (and copied) saxophonists on the planet” (DownBeat), SFJAZZ Collective musical director Chris Potter is undoubtedly one of jazz’s leading lights and a highly engaged student of history. His newest album project, Alive With Ghosts Today, is a stirring set of compositions that explores the power and poignancy of abolitionist John Brown’s life and his 1859 raid on Harpers Ferry that preceded the American Civil War. Joining him on the Edition Records album, and for this performance, is a decidedly off-kilter septet that Potter describes as “a slightly unruly village band” including master guitarist Bill Frisell and a lineup featuring violin, clarinet, trombone, bass, and drums.

Drawing inspiration from gospel, blues, African music, and the wide vistas of Aaron Copland, Alive With Ghosts Today captures the spirit of the era during a period of deep fracture in the country, when the battle for slavery and freedom reached a boiling point that still resonates deeply within the collective American psyche.

An omnivorous artist who has fronted multiple ensembles and collaborated with a staggering list of music's greatest names, Chris Potter again expands upon his remarkable output with Alive With Ghosts Today — a project he approaches with heart and soul.

Of the project, Potter says, “It’s a story that holds the complexity and tragedy of America in one moment. It felt important to engage with it now.”

Personnel: Chris Potter (tenor and soprano saxophone); Bill Frisell (guitar); Others TBA

events.title: SONGWRITERS PRODUCTION SERIES W/ PABLO QUINTERO
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Joe Henderson lab
events.description:
This three-part series explores the intersection of songwriting and music production, helping songwriters build the skills to become full-fledged producers. Taught by songwriter and producer Pablo Quintero, each class is designed to function as a standalone creative experience, while also building progressively for students who attend all three. In every class, students engage in a mini song-creation process that integrates songwriting, beat-making, and production. Through collaborative, project-based learning, participants develop skills in lyric writing, melody and song structure, beat-making, software instruments, recording, and mixing.

events.title: Martin Luther McCoy
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
Cherished Bay Area vocalist and SFJAZZ Collective alumnus Martin Luther McCoy honors the timeless songs of the great Ray Charles with this return to SFJAZZ.

Rising to international attention for his work with The Roots, Cody ChesnuTT, Dave Matthews, Jill Scott, DJ Jazzy Jeff and Zion I, McCoy is perhaps best known for his on-screen role as the Jimi Hendrix inspired character “Jo-Jo” and his performance of George Harrison’s “While My Guitar Gently Weeps” in director Julie Taymor’s Oscar-nominated 2007 Beatles tribute film Across the Universe. He made a memorable appearance in comic megastar Dave Chappelle’s 2005 concert film Dave Chappelle’s Block Party, and was a highlighted artist during Chappelle’s 2014 SFJAZZ performances. McCoy was a vital part of the Collective’s 2019 salutes to Miles Davis’ In a Silent Way and Sly Stone’s Stand!, and in 2021, his original composition “Already Died For Her” was a perfect set-closing statement for the band’s season devoted to music reflecting the moment.

Steeped in gospel music from his childhood in the church, McCoy began songwriting at six, influenced by a mighty collection of iconic artists including Cooke, Bill Withers, and Parliament/Funkadelic.

For this show, McCoy brings a renewed vitality to Ray Charles’ classic blend of gospel and soul.

Personnel: Martin Luther McCoy (vocals); Others TBA
