events.title: Matt Brewer Quintet
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
SFJAZZ Collective bassist Matt Brewer has emerged as one of the most respected and versatile musicians of his generation, known for his deeply melodic playing, rhythmic sophistication, and broad collaborative range. For his night as part of the SFJAZZ Collective Spotlight Series, Brewer performs with his razor-sharp quintet, featuring Oakland-born trumpet phenom Ambrose Akinmusire and legendary pianist Gonzalo Rubalcaba.

Born in Oklahoma City and raised in Albuquerque in a family of musicians, Brewer studied at the Interlochen Arts Academy before joining the inaugural class of the Juilliard Jazz Program. Over the last two decades, he has built an extensive résumé performing and recording with artists including Vijay Iyer, Steve Coleman, Antonio Sánchez, and Gonzalo Rubalcaba.

Brewer’s quintet with Akinmusire and Rubalcaba highlights the bassist's compositional depth and interactive approach to improvisation. The group combines Rubalcaba’s harmonic brilliance and Akinmusire’s emotionally charged trumpet language with Brewer’s supple bass lines and expansive rhythmic concepts, resulting in music that is both adventurous and lyrical. Brewer’s leadership emphasizes collective interplay rather than virtuosity alone, reflecting his reputation as a musician equally valued for sensitivity, imagination, and ensemble cohesion.

Personnel: Matt Brewer (bass); Ambrose Akinmusire (trumpet); TBA saxophone; Gonzalo Rubalcaba (piano); TBA drums

With “a lush, honeyed baritone with just a hint of smoldering melancholy, at once sensual and brooding” (Pitchfork), the Indian-born, Fremont-raised vocalist Sid Sriram is a visionary artist who has melded his traditional Carnatic upbringing with the experience he gleaned as a stadium-filling superstar in India to forge a fresh approach to contemporary soul and R&B. He brings his singular gift to his first SFJAZZ appearance.

A graduate of Mission San Jose High School and Boston’s Berklee School of Music, Sriram applied his early experience an education in traditional South Indian Carnatic music to his renowned work as a composer and playback singer, collaborating with the likes of star director Mani Ratnam and composer A.R. Rahman and appearing on the soundtracks to over 200 films across Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, and Hindi cinema.

Now a resident of Chennai, Sriram released his debut album, Entropy, in 2019 — a worldwide hit blending his Carnatic background with elements of global pop, hip-hop, and modern soul.

His follow up for the American Def Jam label, 2023's Sidharth was made in partnership with producer Ryan Olson (Bon Iver, Lizzo) and features an appearance by Bon Iver frontman, singer, and songwriter Justin Vernon.

Personnel: Sid Sriram (vocals); Others TBA

events.title: Sam Gendel & Sam Wilkes
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
Saxophonist Sam Gendel and bassist Sam Wilkes are two of the defining figures of the contemporary Los Angeles jazz scene, known widely as members of drummer Louis Cole’s iconoclastic band Knower and for their groundbreaking duo project blending virtuosic instrumental playing with heavy electronic processing. A partnership at its most unpredictable in a live setting, they perform pieces from their newest album UNRELATED, and more.

Over the past decade, both musicians have helped redefine the language of modern jazz, shaping a distinctly West Coast sound that merges improvisation with ambient music, hip-hop, experimental electronics, and pop minimalism.

Gendel first emerged through his acclaimed solo recordings and collaborations with artists ranging from Moses Sumney to Vampire Weekend, developing a saxophone style that feels hauntingly intimate and radically unorthodox. Wilkes, meanwhile, has become one of the most sought-after bassists and producers of his generation, celebrated for his elastic grooves, adventurous harmonic sensibility, and deeply collaborative spirit.

First meeting at the USC Thornton School of Music, they have built a body of work that feels both deeply cerebral and emotionally immediate. Their latest music expands even further into abstraction and atmosphere, transforming fragments of melody and rhythm into immersive sonic environments. More than collaborators, Gendel and Wilkes have become architects of a new musical vocabulary, influencing a generation of improvisers across jazz and experimental music alike.

Personnel: Sam Gendel (alto saxophone, guitar, electronics); Sam Wilkes (bass, guitar, electronics)

events.title: Sona Jobarteh
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
“A griot for a new generation of West Africans” (BBC Radio), London-born kora virtuoso Sona Jobarteh is a pioneer of the 21-string African lute. Her return marks her debut on the Miner stage with two nights of spellbinding musicianship.

Jobarteh is the first female kora master to have emerged from an established family of West African griots, bucking a long-held hereditary tradition that restricted instruction on the instrument to males only. Starting as a prodigy, Jobarteh began studies with her brother, kora great Tunde Jegede, at age four and gave her first public performance on the instrument at London’s Jazz Café at five.

She deeply immersed herself in western classical music studies at London’s Royal College of Music, touring the world with her brother’s acclaimed ACM Ensemble as a teen and sharing the stage with Toumani Diabaté, Oumou Sangaré, and the BBC Symphony Orchestra. She composed the score to the 2010 documentary The Motherland, and has done extensive work for film, lending her soaring soprano to the soundtracks of Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom, The First Grader, and The History Channel’s 2016 miniseries Roots.

Her beguiling debut solo recording, Fasiya, showcased her skills as vocalist and multi-instrumentalist, and her follow-up for African Guild Records, Badinyaa Kumoo, was voted Best Album of 2022 by Songlines.

Personnel: Sam Gendel (alto saxophone, guitar, electronics); Sam Wilkes (bass, guitar, electronics)

events.title: Song Circle with Amateur Music Network
events.location: Berkeley
events.description: October Theme: “Broadway and Show Tunes” There’s nothing that brings people together better than singing our favorite songs. It recalls summer nights around the campfire: someone strumming the guitar and all singing a mix of folk music, familiar songs we heard on the radio, and occasional new songs that someone shares. Nobody has to worry about whether you know the songs or can sing like a pro. This is our chance to share the joy of singing simply for the fun of it. Cary Sheldon is a singer, songwriter, and beloved Berkeley voice teacher with 30 years worth of grateful students. She has been playing and teaching in the Bay Area for the last 40 years. Her love for R & B music led her to be part of Zazu Pitts Memorial Orchestra in the 1980’s. Other affiliations include The Henry Kaiser Band, The Henriettas (a recreation of DeZurick sisters, a popular country music duo from the 1940’s), who appeared on Prairie Home Companion, and most recently her band DanceChant, a joyful community-inspired R&B band that encourages audience participation. She continues to be inspired by her love of singing in community. “Singing together with others is one of the greatest joys in my life.” Now in her 60’s, she returns to influences from her early life. Her grade school music teachers included John Langstaff, creator of the Christmas Revels, and the repertoire was based on the American folk tradition, including old English ballads, spirituals, freedom songs, and the popular folk and protest songs of the 1960’s. She hopes to inspire others to explore the depth of this material and rediscover the joy of community singing. Soprano Candace Johnson has led AMN’s Juneteenth Choral Celebration since its inception in 2020. The AMN community knows her through her commitment to the power of the Negro Spirituals tradition, but Candace has a deep connection to theater and to the music of the Broadway stage. A voice instructor at UC Berkeley for 17 years, in 2022 Candace also became the director of the University Gospel Choir. A lyric coloratura soprano, she crosses musical boundaries performing classical, jazz, musical theater, pop and gospel. She has sung on many stages, including Carnegie Hall and The Manhattan Center. Also a playwright and actress, Candace premiered her first one-woman show, Vox in a Box , in UC Berkeley’s Hertz Hall in 2018, which led to her becoming a resident solo artist at The Marsh theater (Berkeley/San Francisco). Candace has written and performed 5 full-length one-woman musicals. Her most recent show, Scat-ter Brain: The Music of ADHD , was commissioned by The Marsh in 2024 for its inaugural IFOYE festival of new works by women-identifying playwrights. Following an extended run, Scat-ter Brain was nominated by Broadway World SF for Best Solo Show of 2025. Please read our Health, Safety and COVID-19 Information Our commitment to our patrons

events.title: Gilles Vonsattel Piano Recital
events.location: Presidio Theatre, 99 Moraga Ave, San Francisco, CA 94129
events.description: The extraordinary pianist Gilles Vonsattel offers a captivating look inside Beethoven becoming Beethoven as we know him, part of a series of special engagements in the Bay Area that see the stunningly original performer take on the composer’s complete piano sonata cycle. With this rare performance of four landmark piano sonatas presented in a single evening, Gilles Vonsattel hands us the keys to unlocking the psyche of a genius. Works to be performed – Sonata no. 1 in F Minor, Op. 2; Sonata No. 21 in C Major, Op. 53 “Waldstein”; Sonata No. 27 in E Minor, Op. 90; Sonata No. 28 in A Major, Op. 101. Presented in partnership with Music@Menlo and Stanford Live.

events.description:
SFJAZZ is proud to partner with the San Francisco Conservatory of Music and its Roots, Jazz & American Music (RJAM) program, linking a world-class conservatory to the award-winning SFJAZZ Center and its resident all-star ensemble, the SFJAZZ Collective.

Side-By-Side concerts pair select faculty from the Roots, Jazz and American Music (RJAM) program at The San Francisco Conservatory of Music with their young artist proteges. The stellar faculty cast includes the SFJAZZ Collective's Warren Wolf, David Sanchez, Edward Simon and Matt Brewer, along with luminaries Anthony Hervey, Matt Wilson, Helen Sung and many others.

events.title: Shabaka
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
In recent years, the most vital, inclusive, and innovative jazz scene on earth has shifted east across the Atlantic to London, and the figure that stands atop this revolution is Shabaka (formerly known as Shabaka Hutchings). The former leader of the heralded conglomerations Sons of Kemet, Shabaka and the Ancestors, and The Comet is Coming, Shabaka returns to SFJAZZ with music from his 2026 release Of the Earth — an innovative and adventurous solo recording that marks both his return to the saxophone and his immersion into electronic beats and loops that has opened new worlds for exploration.

A multi-faceted instrumentalist and composer whose influence has spread far beyond the U.K., the Birmingham-raised Hutchings spent the formative years of his youth in Barbados, an island rife with reminders of Britain’s colonial history, where the budding artist first picked up the saxophone and where the seeds of his creative aesthetic in the roots of the African diaspora were planted.

Bristling with raw energy and deep spiritual power, Of the Earth was inspired by the solo producer-auteur approach of the late D’Angelo and points to Shabaka’s vision for his future relationship with the instrument, allowing him to fully embrace new sonic realms and chart new expressive paths, each marked by resonances from the ancient past while feeling resolutely of the moment.

Personnel: Shabaka (tenor saxophone, flute, electronics)

events.title: The Comeuppance
events.location: A.C.T., 415 Geary St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description: When a group of millennial classmates meet to pregame for their twentieth high school reunion, everyone is nervous for the night ahead. As alcohol and weed help the self-declared “Multi-Ethnic Reject Group” let their guards down, they begin to reminisce and reveal how their lives have unfolded since graduation. Did their friendships stand the test of time? Why do they remember certain moments from their past differently? From Pulitzer Prize–winning and two-time Tony Award–winning playwright Branden Jacob-Jenkins ( Gloria ) comes a new profound tragicomedy about the reunion that awaits us all.

events.title: Joe Lovano: Paramount Quartet
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
w/ Julian Lage, Asante Santi Debriano, and Will Calhoun

An artist The Boston Globe accurately describes as “jazz royalty,” GRAMMY-winning saxophonist Joe Lovano showcases his latest ensemble for the second two nights of his 2026-27 Season residency — a masterful assemblage of virtuosos including guitar great Julian Lage, esteemed bassist Asante Santi Debriano, and Living Colour drummer Will Calhoun — performing music from Lovano’s new ECM Records release Paramount Quartet.

Cutting his professional teeth with the bands of Woody Herman and Mel Lewis, Lovano is the most acclaimed saxophonist and composer in modern jazz, leading over 40 albums and forging long-term partnerships with John Scofield and Paul Motian and collaborating with artists ranging from Jim Hall and McCoy Tyner to Abbey Lincoln and Elvin Jones.

The spark of the Paramount Quartet dates to a meeting with Debriano and Calhoun at a fundraiser for Puerto Rico hurricane relief in 2023 and adding Lage to the mix was a natural step, as the two had been talking about doing a project together for over two decades.

Consisting of all original compositions and a loving version of Wayne Shorter’s “Lady Day,” the album is possessed of a singular magic. As Lovano himself puts it, “There's a lot of magic that just kind of unfolds as we play. And the more we play, the more magical it becomes."

Personnel: Joe Lovano (tenor & soprano saxophone); Julian Lage (guitar); Asante Santi Debriano (bass); Will Calhoun (drums)

events.title: Alfredo Rodríguez Band
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
with Pedrito Martínez

Following his spectacular performance last season as part of Terence Blanchard’s UpSwing series, Cuban piano savant Alfredo Rodríguez returns with his powerful Afro-Cuban ensemble featuring the dynamic percussion master Pedrito Martínez for this evening of rhythmic fireworks.

After Quincy Jones first heard Alfredo Rodríguez at the Monteux Jazz Festival in 2006 the legendary producer guided his ascent as Rodríguez became one of Cuba’s most visible and creatively unfettered musicians. Based in Los Angeles since he defected in 2009, the pianist has released a series of increasingly expansive albums for Mack Avenue, incorporating sounds from South India, Argentina, Spain, the Middle East and beyond. His formidable technique and soulful approach was described by the Mercury News as “the way Monk might have sounded if he had been born in Chick Corea’s body and raised on a diet of Bach, Chopin and Stravinsky in a Havana conservatory.”

Released on his own Take Cover imprint, Rodriguez’s new album is a blistering collection of standards and covers called ¡Take Cover! that includes his takes on the music of Tito Puente, Henry Mancini, Stevie Wonder, The Eagles, Lalo Shifrin, and more.

Personnel: Alfredo Rodríguez (piano); Pedrito Martínez (percussion); Others TBA

events.title: J3PO / Joel Ross
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
The final season installment of Terence Blanchard’s wildly popular UpSwing concert series highlights a pair of instrumentalists forging singular careers guided by uncompromising artistic vision.

Los Angeles-based keyboardist and producer Julian Pollack, known widely as J3PO, is among the most exciting young artists on the scene. Raised in Berkeley, he was an award-winning member of the SFJAZZ High School All-Stars and appeared on Marian McPartland’s iconic Piano Jazz program on NPR at age 18. Since then, Pollack has emerged as a visionary force bridging jazz virtuosity with electronic production, hip-hop, and experimental sound design. He has worked with artists across jazz and contemporary music while developing a distinctive solo voice that positions him at the forefront of a new generation redefining jazz for the digital age.

Vibraphonist Joel Ross has earned widespread renown as the most remarkable young voice on his instrument. Since the 2019 release of Ross’ debut album Kingmaker on Blue Note, he’s quickly established himself as a triple threat with a far-reaching approach. A graduate of Stockton’s University of the Pacific, Ross went on to study jazz at The New School and was mentored by former SFJAZZ Collective vibraphonist Stefon Harris. His new Blue Note release, Gospel Music, is a sonic interpretation of the Biblical story and an exploration of faith, featuring an expanded sextet lineup of his Good Vibes band.

Personnel: J3PO; J3PO (keyboards); Others TBA; JOEL ROSS; Joel Ross (vibraphone); Others TBA

events.description: Sixteen-year-old Pi Patel sets out on a journey across the ocean with his family, only to find himself alone after a catastrophic shipwreck. Adrift on a lifeboat in the vast Pacific, he must learn to survive alongside a group of unlikely companions, including a hyena, a zebra, an orangutan, and a Bengal tiger. As the days stretch into weeks, reality and imagination begin to blur. Pi is pushed to his limits, confronting fear, faith, and the stories we tell ourselves to endure the unimaginable. Winner of five Olivier Awards including Best New Play, and hailed by The Guardian as “extraordinary and unmissable,” this breathtaking stage adaptation brings Yann Martel’s beloved novel to life through stunning visuals and groundbreaking puppetry. Life of Pi is a theatrical event about survival, belief, and the power of storytelling.

events.title: Emmet Cohen Quintet
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
Winner of the 2019 American Pianists Award and finalist in the 2011 Thelonious Monk International Piano Competition, virtuoso Emmet Cohen is among the most acclaimed pianists in jazz, known widely as a member of bass great Christian McBride’s Tip City and music director with vocal phenom Veronica Swift, along with his stellar work as a bandleader. He steps back on the Miner stage with his working quintet after his sold-out 2026 performance focused on the music of Miles Davis and John Coltrane in honor of their centennials.

The prodigious pianist started piano studies at three and released his 2011 debut In the Element while still enrolled at University of Florida’s Frost School of Music. He has accumulated nearly 20 major awards and honors over his career and created the acclaimed Masters Legacy Series of recordings and interviews in 2016 featuring collaboration with Ron Carter, Benny Golson, Albert “Tootie” Heath, George Coleman, and Houston Person.

Cohen has been a member of the bands led by drumming luminaries Herlin Riley and Ali Jackson and hosted the wildly popular YouTube series Live From Emmet’s Place with a procession of special guests.

Cohen has led 12 albums including his newest Mack Avenue release, 2024’s Vibe Provider.

Personnel: Emmet Cohen (piano); Others TBA

events.title: The Comeuppance
events.location: A.C.T., 415 Geary St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description: When a group of millennial classmates meet to pregame for their twentieth high school reunion, everyone is nervous for the night ahead. As alcohol and weed help the self-declared “Multi-Ethnic Reject Group” let their guards down, they begin to reminisce and reveal how their lives have unfolded since graduation. Did their friendships stand the test of time? Why do they remember certain moments from their past differently? From Pulitzer Prize–winning and two-time Tony Award–winning playwright Branden Jacob-Jenkins ( Gloria ) comes a new profound tragicomedy about the reunion that awaits us all.

events.title: Django Festival Allstars
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
with Special Guest

Pioneering Romani jazz guitarist Django Reinhardt lamented that he might be neglected by history, but today the ebulliently swinging “jazz manouche” sound he created with French violinist Stéphane Grappelli is more pervasive than ever. For this very special night, the leading purveyors of the style, the Django Festival Allstars, return to the Miner stage for a magical evening of hot jazz with a special guest to be named soon.

Featuring the guitar mastery of Samson Schmitt of the Schmitt clan, the first family of jazz manouche, the Django Festival All-Stars also includes accordionist and keyboardist Ludovic Beier, violinist Pierre Blanchard, and rhythm guitarist Francko Mehrstein — all of whom gained fame as part of the original band led by family patriarch Dorado Schmitt — joined by bassist Antonio Licusati. This assemblage of masters in the Roma jazz style are regular performers at the annual Django Reinhart Festival in Samois-sur-Seine, France and New York’s celebration at Birdland, which celebrates over a quarter century of music.

The group performs in support of their new Motéma Music release, Evolution, a hard-swinging collection of original compositions written and arranged by the members of the band. DownBeat magazine hailed the release as “(jazz manouche) for the 21st Century!”

Personnel: Samson Schmitt (guitar); Francko Mehrstein (guitar); Pierre Blanchard (violin); Ludovic Beier (accordion, keyboards); Antonio Licusati (bass); TBA vocals

events.title: Song Circle with Amateur Music Network
events.location: Berkeley
events.description: October Theme: “Broadway and Show Tunes” There’s nothing that brings people together better than singing our favorite songs. It recalls summer nights around the campfire: someone strumming the guitar and all singing a mix of folk music, familiar songs we heard on the radio, and occasional new songs that someone shares. Nobody has to worry about whether you know the songs or can sing like a pro. This is our chance to share the joy of singing simply for the fun of it. Cary Sheldon is a singer, songwriter, and beloved Berkeley voice teacher with 30 years worth of grateful students. She has been playing and teaching in the Bay Area for the last 40 years. Her love for R & B music led her to be part of Zazu Pitts Memorial Orchestra in the 1980’s. Other affiliations include The Henry Kaiser Band, The Henriettas (a recreation of DeZurick sisters, a popular country music duo from the 1940’s), who appeared on Prairie Home Companion, and most recently her band DanceChant, a joyful community-inspired R&B band that encourages audience participation. She continues to be inspired by her love of singing in community. “Singing together with others is one of the greatest joys in my life.” Now in her 60’s, she returns to influences from her early life. Her grade school music teachers included John Langstaff, creator of the Christmas Revels, and the repertoire was based on the American folk tradition, including old English ballads, spirituals, freedom songs, and the popular folk and protest songs of the 1960’s. She hopes to inspire others to explore the depth of this material and rediscover the joy of community singing. Soprano Candace Johnson has led AMN’s Juneteenth Choral Celebration since its inception in 2020. The AMN community knows her through her commitment to the power of the Negro Spirituals tradition, but Candace has a deep connection to theater and to the music of the Broadway stage. A voice instructor at UC Berkeley for 17 years, in 2022 Candace also became the director of the University Gospel Choir. A lyric coloratura soprano, she crosses musical boundaries performing classical, jazz, musical theater, pop and gospel. She has sung on many stages, including Carnegie Hall and The Manhattan Center. Also a playwright and actress, Candace premiered her first one-woman show, Vox in a Box , in UC Berkeley’s Hertz Hall in 2018, which led to her becoming a resident solo artist at The Marsh theater (Berkeley/San Francisco). Candace has written and performed 5 full-length one-woman musicals. Her most recent show, Scat-ter Brain: The Music of ADHD , was commissioned by The Marsh in 2024 for its inaugural IFOYE festival of new works by women-identifying playwrights. Following an extended run, Scat-ter Brain was nominated by Broadway World SF for Best Solo Show of 2025. Please read our Health, Safety and COVID-19 Information Our commitment to our patrons

events.title: Iraq, But Funny
events.location: A.C.T., 415 Geary St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description: This hilariously chaotic new play follows five generations of Assyrian women attempting to reclaim their story as it’s being narrated by some British guy (said British guy being played with sharp-elbowed satire by playwright Atra Asdou). Marching through time and space, this journey from the Ottoman Empire to modern-day USA portrays a gritty reality that’s playfully witty, filled with history, family, and dysfunction—it’s the zaniest history of the Middle East you ever did see!

events.title: Mark Lettieri & Purbayan Chatterjee
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
The inspired collaboration between Snarky Puppy guitarist Mark Lettieri and the virtuosic Indian sitar master Purbayan Chatterjee comes to the Miner Auditorium stage for one night, highlighting their shared spirit of exploration, improvisational telepathy, and quicksilver dexterity. They bring a night of spirited musical dialog, performing compositions from their 2026 GroundUP Music debut, Feathered Creatures, and more than a few surprises.

Mark Lettieri, renowned for his work with Snarky Puppy and The Fearless Flyers, has become one of contemporary instrumental music’s most inventive guitar voices. Raised in the Bay Area and seasoned in the Dallas music scene, Lettieri developed a style that merges funk precision, jazz sophistication, and rock intensity. A multi-GRAMMY winner with Snarky Puppy and a GRAMMY nominee for his solo release Deep: The Baritone Sessions, Vol. 2, he is celebrated for groove-driven compositions and fearless improvisation.

Purbayan Chatterjee stands among India’s foremost sitar maestros, carrying forward the Senia Maihar gharana tradition while expanding it into contemporary global music. Trained by legendary masters and honored with the Rashtrapati Award as a teenage prodigy, Chatterjee has built an international reputation through dazzling technique, emotional depth, and cross-cultural collaborations, as on his all-star 2021 album Unbounded featuring the late Zakir Hussain, drummer Antonio Sánchez, and Snarky Puppy leader Michael League.

Lettieri and Chatterjee’s new album Feathered Creatures promises a vivid meeting of rhythmic fire, lyrical beauty, and boundary-defying musical conversation.

Personnel: Mark Lettieri (guitar); Purbayan Chatterjee (sitar)

events.title: GoGo Penguin
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
The piano trio has been one of the most durable, beloved, and flexible formats in jazz history. Manchester-based GoGo Penguin turns this most venerable construct on its ear, infusing direct influences from contemporary electronic music and modern classical concepts into their singular ensemble approach that has earned well-deserved raves from all corners of the music world.

The band’s hypnotic, swirling grooves are acoustic adaptations of pieces composed with sequencing software, and rely as much on additive development and dynamic contrasts as improvisation, with pianist Chris Illingsworth’s powerful melodic statements anchored by Nick Blacka’s thunderous bass and the skittering break-beat rhythms of drummer Jon Scott.

The strength of their first two independent albums and magnetic live performances led to inclusion on Rolling Stone’s list of “20 Great New British Artists to Watch,” as well as a deal with Blue Note Records, who released their 2016 breakout, Man Made Object.

Fast forward to the present — the band are riding high from their eighth release, the 2025 XXIM Records album Necessary Fictions, which integrates a wider sonic spectrum through modular synthesizers, and have recently released the follow-up Call to the Void, a three-track EP that dives still deeper into electronic experimentation.

Pushing the jazz trio form in unprecedented new directions, GoGo Penguin truly sounds like nothing else on Earth.

Personnel: Chris Illingsworth (piano); Nick Blacka (bass); Jon Scott (drums)

events.title: Derek Gripper & Alam Khan
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
A pair of master musicians representing the diversity of string instrument traditions, Derek Gripper and Alam Khan unite for a project that dissolves musical borders and reimagines the possibilities of global acoustic music.

Gripper has earned international acclaim for his groundbreaking adaptations of West African kora music for solo guitar, a feat that led legendary kora master Toumani Diabaté to remark that Gripper had “taken the guitar to a new place.” His work bridges African classical traditions with jazz and contemporary composition, establishing him as one of the world’s most innovative guitarists.

Alam Khan, the son of the legendary sarod maestro Ali Akbar Khan, carries forward one of India’s most revered musical lineages. A master of the sarod and a gifted composer, Khan blends the rigor of Hindustani classical music with adventurous cross-cultural collaboration, earning respect across both traditional and contemporary music circles.

Together, Gripper and Khan engage in a transcendent musical conversation—an immersive journey through African, Indian, and contemporary sound worlds shaped by improvisation, technical brilliance, and deep cultural exchange.

Personnel: Derek Gripper (guitar); Alam Khan (sarod)

events.title: Music of Remembrance: Women in the Shadows
events.location: Presidio Theatre, 99 Moraga Ave, San Francisco, CA 94129
events.description: Women in the Shadows explores the inner worlds of women artists overshadowed by history. The featured work, composer Jake Heggie and librettist Gene Scheer’s Camille Claudel: Into the Fire, is a theatrical song cycle that traces the life of the brilliant French sculptor. The creators give Claudel a passionate voice, casting her as more than Auguste Rodin’s muse--a formidable artist in her own right. Mezzo-soprano Nikola Printz brings an intense musical and dramatic presence to the role, praised in the San Francisco Chronicle for performances that are “heartrending, musically resplendent . . . and thrillingly fierce.”

events.title: Poncho Sánchez & His Latin Band
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
Few artists embody the pulse of Latin jazz like Poncho Sánchez, a conguero whose hands seem to translate history into rhythm. He makes his first appearance at the SFJAZZ Center with this performance, joined by the latest iteration of his Latin Band.

Born in Texas and raised in Southern California, Sánchez emerged from a rich blend of Afro-Cuban traditions and bebop influences, eventually becoming one of the most influential percussionists in jazz. His early mentorship under vibraphonist Cal Tjader positioned him at the heart of a lineage that includes giants like Tito Puente and Mongo Santamaría—artists who helped define the genre he now carries forward.

With his band, Sánchez forged a sound that is both scholarly and electrifying: tight horn lines, driving congas, and an irresistible groove that merges jazz sophistication with street-level soul. Over decades and more than 20 albums, he has transformed Latin jazz into a living, evolving conversation, earning a GRAMMY and global acclaim.

His latest project, Poncho Sánchez & His Latin Jazz Band Live at the Belly Up Tavern, captures that vitality in real time. The album delivers fresh arrangements and the kinetic energy of a live performance, proving that Sánchez’s music is not archival—it is alive, urgent, and still expanding.

In every strike of the drum, Poncho Sánchez doesn’t just play Latin jazz—he sustains its heartbeat.

Personnel: Poncho Sánchez (congas); Others TBA

events.title: SFJAM: Free Community Jam Session: Sounds of Duke Ellington
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Joe Henderson Lab
events.description: These monthly open jam sessions provide a space for all Bay Area musicians to come together and perform in an inclusive, multigenerational setting. Each session features a musical director and curated repertoire. We invite musicians of all levels and ages to sign up, and each session is free and open to the public - no reservations or tickets needed to attend!

events.title: Caleb Teicher & Nic Gareiss
events.location: Presidio Theatre, 99 Moraga Ave, San Francisco, CA 94129
events.description: In Ear To The Ground, award-winning tap and swing dancer Caleb Teicher and celebrated percussive dancer Nic Gareiss draw on tap, swing, lindy hop, Appalachian clogging, and Irish step dance—braiding improvisation, song, and rhythm into a dynamic exchange of sound and movement. The result is an intimate, transportive performance that honors tradition while carving out a genre-defying percussive language all its own.

events.title: Chucho Valdés
events.location: SFJAZZ Center — Miner Auditorium
events.description:
The most influential figure in modern Afro-Cuban jazz for more than half a century, virtuoso pianist, composer and arranger Chucho Valdés celebrates his 85th Birthday with this week of special concerts.

The son of Cuban pianist Bebo Valdés, the winner of seven GRAMMYs and seven Latin GRAMMY Awards joined Armando Romeu’s celebrated Cuban Orchestra of Modern Music in 1967, a time when the communist government still considered American jazz anti-revolutionary. He was already recognized as the most formidable pianist of his generation when he launched Irakere in 1973 with a phenomenal cast that included saxophonist Paquito D’Rivera and trumpeter Arturo Sandoval.

Over the ensuing years, Valdés has concentrated on his career as a solo artist, recording over 25 albums and co-writing the landmark 2018 book Decoding Afro-Cuban Jazz in collaboration with SFJAZZ Director of Education Rebeca Mauleón. His staggering legacy was summed up by the Boston Globe, who lauded him for “an encyclopedic vocabulary of Afro-Cuban rhythms and an expansive palette that includes all manner of modern jazz as well as traditional classical repertoire.”

Most recently, Valdés has brought his Afro-Cuban Messengers, Irakere 50, and Royal Quartet projects to SFJAZZ, and for this 85th birthday celebration event, Valdés will be joined by a superlative lineup of musicians and special guests, ending the 2026-27 Season in grand fashion.

Personnel: Chucho Valdés (piano); Others TBA

events.description: Step Afrika! celebrates more than 30 years of critically acclaimed percussive performance with this groundbreaking program featuring new works alongside a performance shaped and refined through a long-standing collaboration in South Africa.

events.title: Life of Pi
events.location: San Francisco Playhouse, 450 Post St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description: Sixteen-year-old Pi Patel sets out on a journey across the ocean with his family, only to find himself alone after a catastrophic shipwreck. Adrift on a lifeboat in the vast Pacific, he must learn to survive alongside a group of unlikely companions, including a hyena, a zebra, an orangutan, and a Bengal tiger. Winner of five Olivier Awards including Best New Play, and hailed by The Guardian as “extraordinary and unmissable,” this breathtaking stage adaptation brings Yann Martel’s beloved novel to life through stunning visuals and groundbreaking puppetry. Life of Pi is a theatrical event about survival, belief, and the power of storytelling.

events.title: Song Circle with Amateur Music Network
events.location: Berkeley
events.description: October Theme: “Broadway and Show Tunes” There’s nothing that brings people together better than singing our favorite songs. It recalls summer nights around the campfire: someone strumming the guitar and all singing a mix of folk music, familiar songs we heard on the radio, and occasional new songs that someone shares. Nobody has to worry about whether you know the songs or can sing like a pro. This is our chance to share the joy of singing simply for the fun of it. Cary Sheldon is a singer, songwriter, and beloved Berkeley voice teacher with 30 years worth of grateful students. She has been playing and teaching in the Bay Area for the last 40 years. Her love for R & B music led her to be part of Zazu Pitts Memorial Orchestra in the 1980’s. Other affiliations include The Henry Kaiser Band, The Henriettas (a recreation of DeZurick sisters, a popular country music duo from the 1940’s), who appeared on Prairie Home Companion, and most recently her band DanceChant, a joyful community-inspired R&B band that encourages audience participation. She continues to be inspired by her love of singing in community. “Singing together with others is one of the greatest joys in my life.” Now in her 60’s, she returns to influences from her early life. Her grade school music teachers included John Langstaff, creator of the Christmas Revels, and the repertoire was based on the American folk tradition, including old English ballads, spirituals, freedom songs, and the popular folk and protest songs of the 1960’s. She hopes to inspire others to explore the depth of this material and rediscover the joy of community singing. Soprano Candace Johnson has led AMN’s Juneteenth Choral Celebration since its inception in 2020. The AMN community knows her through her commitment to the power of the Negro Spirituals tradition, but Candace has a deep connection to theater and to the music of the Broadway stage. A voice instructor at UC Berkeley for 17 years, in 2022 Candace also became the director of the University Gospel Choir. A lyric coloratura soprano, she crosses musical boundaries performing classical, jazz, musical theater, pop and gospel. She has sung on many stages, including Carnegie Hall and The Manhattan Center. Also a playwright and actress, Candace premiered her first one-woman show, Vox in a Box , in UC Berkeley’s Hertz Hall in 2018, which led to her becoming a resident solo artist at The Marsh theater (Berkeley/San Francisco). Candace has written and performed 5 full-length one-woman musicals. Her most recent show, Scat-ter Brain: The Music of ADHD , was commissioned by The Marsh in 2024 for its inaugural IFOYE festival of new works by women-identifying playwrights. Following an extended run, Scat-ter Brain was nominated by Broadway World SF for Best Solo Show of 2025. Please read our Health, Safety and COVID-19 Information Our commitment to our patrons

events.title: Life of Pi
events.location: San Francisco Playhouse, 450 Post St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description: Sixteen-year-old Pi Patel sets out on a journey across the ocean with his family, only to find himself alone after a catastrophic shipwreck. Adrift on a lifeboat in the vast Pacific, he must learn to survive alongside a group of unlikely companions, including a hyena, a zebra, an orangutan, and a Bengal tiger. As the days stretch into weeks, reality and imagination begin to blur. Pi is pushed to his limits, confronting fear, faith, and the stories we tell ourselves to endure the unimaginable. Winner of five Olivier Awards including Best New Play, and hailed by The Guardian as “extraordinary and unmissable,” this breathtaking stage adaptation brings Yann Martel’s beloved novel to life through stunning visuals and groundbreaking puppetry. Life of Pi is a theatrical event about survival, belief, and the power of storytelling.

events.title: Sweeney Todd: The Demon Barber of Fleet Street
events.location: San Francisco Playhouse, 450 Post St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description: Benjamin Barker returns to London a changed man. Now known as Sweeney Todd, the barber comes back to a city that took everything from him, driven by a single, consuming desire for revenge. Above Mrs. Lovett’s struggling pie shop, he sets up a new practice, and together they form a darkly ingenious partnership. As business begins to thrive, the line between justice and obsession starts to blur, with chilling consequences for all who cross their path. Winner of eight Tony Awards including Best Musical, Stephen Sondheim’s Sweeney Todd: The Demon Barber of Fleet Street is a thrilling and unforgettable tale of vengeance, morality, and the cost of losing one’s humanity.

events.title: Sweeney Todd: The Demon Barber of Fleet Street
events.location: San Francisco Playhouse, 450 Post St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description: Benjamin Barker returns to London a changed man. Now known as Sweeney Todd, the barber comes back to a city that took everything from him, driven by a single, consuming desire for revenge. Above Mrs. Lovett’s struggling pie shop, he sets up a new practice, and together they form a darkly ingenious partnership. As business begins to thrive, the line between justice and obsession starts to blur, with chilling consequences for all who cross their path. Winner of eight Tony Awards including Best Musical, Stephen Sondheim’s Sweeney Todd: The Demon Barber of Fleet Street is a thrilling and unforgettable tale of vengeance, morality, and the cost of losing one’s humanity.
